#### 7. CSRF, rate limiting, session cookies

**CSRF.** All 120 `/api/v1` routes pass `csrf=False`, but this is a no-op: CSRF validation lives only in `HttpDispatcher.dispatch` for `type='http'` routes (the one such route here, `/api/v1/forms/media/<path:key>`, is GET-only, which is never CSRF-checked) (`src/odoo/http.py:2448-2456`). `Json2Dispatcher` has no CSRF check at all. What actually protects these routes from cross-site abuse is the CORS allow-list plus, for a browser, the fact that a cross-site request cannot read the response. A same-site form POST cannot reach a json2 route because json2 requires `application/json` or an empty body (`src/odoo/http.py:2603-2605`), which a simple HTML form cannot produce.

**Rate limiting. THIS CHANGED IN 19.0.3.22.0 - the paragraph below used to say "none is implemented".** `assessments_be_v2` now overrides `res.users._assert_can_auth` (`models/res_users.py`), so the brute-force bucket is this addon's, not Odoo's:

- **The bucket is keyed on the LOGIN being attempted**, not on `remote_addr`. Odoo's own bucket is per-IP, and on this deployment every candidate reaches Odoo as one of two ingress addresses (the NLB and the Istio sidecar have already replaced the client IP), so five failures from one candidate froze sign-in for a 753-candidate cohort - 3,668 refusals in seven minutes on 2026-09-17. The mitigation at the time was to switch protection off entirely (`base.login_cooldown_after = 0`).
- **A second, far looser per-IP bucket** still catches one host spraying many accounts. Its ceiling is `base.login_cooldown_after * res.users._BE_IP_CEILING_MULTIPLIER` (20x), which a real cohort behind two ingress IPs never reaches.
- **The per-IP counter is a ROLLING WINDOW, and a successful sign-in does NOT clear it.** A success clears only the candidate's own login key. Clearing the shared address on any success would have meant credential spraying was never limited at all - the sprayer need only wait for somebody to sign in. The counter is instead reset when the last failure is older than `base.login_cooldown_duration`, which is the same window `_on_login_cooldown` already reads it through, so the stored number means "failures in the last window", not "failures ever".
- **Policy is still Odoo's.** The threshold is `base.login_cooldown_after`, the recency test is `res.users._on_login_cooldown`, and `0` still disables the feature entirely.
- The dict is bounded at `_BE_MAX_TRACKED_FAILURES` (4096) and evicts its oldest half when full, because keying on the login makes it unbounded in a way Odoo's per-IP version is not - a spray script trying random addresses would otherwise exhaust the worker.
- Buckets live in `registry._be_login_failures` and are per-worker, not shared, exactly as Odoo's `registry._login_failures` is.

`res.users._be_login_cooldown_key(login, source)` is the ONE predicate that decides whether an attempt is currently refused; it returns the offending key (`("login", ...)` or `("ip", ...)`) or `None`. Both the limiter and `api_auth_gateway` ask it, so the two cannot drift.

**A rate-limited caller on the GATEWAY route is now told so.** `POST /api/v1/auth_token` (`api_auth_gateway/controllers/main.py`) classifies its `AccessDenied` through `_is_rate_limited`, which checks Odoo's own `registry._login_failures` AND asks `res.users._be_login_cooldown_key`. When either says yes it answers **429** with `Retry-After` (`base.login_cooldown_duration`, clamped to 1-3600s) and the message *"Too many sign-in attempts from this network. Wait a minute and try again - your password is not the problem."* The header is load-bearing: the Flutter client treats 429 as retryable, so without it one refusal became up to five retries at the worst possible moment.

**`assessments_be_v2`'s own `auth.py` route is unchanged and still rewrites the cooldown to "Wrong login or password"** with code `invalid_credentials` (`auth.py:53-57`). The Flutter client calls the gateway route first and only falls back to `/api/v1/auth/session` on a 404, so in practice callers get the 429; a direct caller of the module route still gets the misleading 401. The docstring claim at `auth.py:35-37` that "login rate limiting all behave identically to the web client" remains true of the mechanism, not of the message.

**Session cookie.** `_save_session` sets `session_id` with `httponly=True` and `max_age=get_session_max_inactivity(env)` and nothing else - no `Secure`, no `SameSite` (`src/odoo/http.py::set_cookie`; `set_cookie` defaults `secure=False, samesite=None` at `src/odoo/http.py:1740`). Two consequences:

- Modern browsers default a cookie with no `SameSite` to Lax, so the cookie is not sent on cross-*site* requests. A Flutter web build served from a different registrable domain than Odoo cannot use the cookie path at all, no matter how correct the CORS headers are. In dev, `localhost:8100` → `localhost:7070` is same-site (ports are not part of a site for cookies), so this failure appears only on a real deployment. UNKNOWN: whether the production reverse proxy rewrites `Set-Cookie` to add `SameSite=None; Secure` - nothing in this repo does it.
- The cookie is issued on responses to bearer-only clients too, because `cookie_sid != sess.sid` whenever the client sends no cookie (`src/odoo/http.py:2142`). The client explicitly refuses to capture it on non-2xx responses, because doing so made the router treat a rejected login as signed in (`ethara-assessment-fe/lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:245-260`).

#### 8. Failure modes a developer will actually hit

| Symptom | Cause | Exact text / status |
|---|---|---|
| Browser console: CORS error, no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, while `curl` returns 200 | Origin not in `assessments_be_v2.cors_origins`, and not localhost-in-dev | No CORS headers, only `Vary: Origin` (`ir_http.py:364-376`). The server log shows a normal 200 |
| Preflight passes but the request is blocked | Client authenticates with an `access-token` header rather than `Authorization` | The wrapper's `Allow-Headers` omits it (`ir_http.py:382-385`) |
| Localhost refused | This backend's `web.base.url` is NOT a localhost host, the server is not in `--dev`, and `cors_allow_localhost` is unset. Usual cause: a shared box on a real hostname being pointed at from a local build - that is exactly what the parameter is for | `_localhost_origins()` returns `set()` |
| Domain added in Settings, still refused, no restart done | The negative-lookup refresh should cover this; if it did not, `_refresh_cors_cache` failed | `WARNING ... Could not refresh the CORS origin cache; a newly configured origin will be refused until restart` (`ir_http.py:298-301`) |
| 401 on every call after ~100 hours | Bearer token expired; adoption is silent | `{"ok": false, "code": "session_expired", "message": "Your session has expired. Sign in again."}` at 401 (`ir_http.py:568-575`) |
| 401 immediately after a correct password | MFA is enabled on the account | `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "mfa_required", "message": "This account needs multi-factor authentication. Sign in through the web portal."}}` at 401 (`auth.py:64-66`) |
| "Login failed. Please check your credentials." for a right password, from an en-GB (or other uninstalled-language) browser; `Invalid language code: en_GB` in the log | Fixed in 19.0.3.23.0 by `_auth_method_none` / `_use_installed_lang` (section 2). If the log line comes back, that fix is not running | The absence of "Invalid language code" in the log is the only sign it works; the swap is not logged |
| 429 on sign-in with a correct password | Login cooldown - the per-login bucket, or the 20x-looser per-IP bucket, in `registry._be_login_failures` | `{"message": "Too many sign-in attempts from this network. Wait a minute and try again - your password is not the problem.", "status_code": 429}` with a `Retry-After` header, from `/api/v1/auth_token` (`api_auth_gateway/controllers/main.py::auth_token`) |
| "Wrong login or password" for a password that is right | Same cooldown, but reached through the MODULE route rather than the gateway | `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "invalid_credentials", "message": "Wrong login or password"}}` at 401 (`auth.py:56-57`), with the real reason only in the server log. `auth.py` was deliberately left alone in 19.0.3.22.0; the client reaches the gateway route first |
| Filters or `limit` in the query string are ignored | json2 reads only the body | Defaults apply: limit 40, clamped to 200 (`common.py::limit`, `262-266`) |
| A 400 with an Odoo traceback in the body instead of the envelope | Malformed JSON, 404, or 405 - all raised before `@api_endpoint` and not `SessionExpiredException`, so `_handle_error` passes them to stock | `{"name": ..., "message": ..., "arguments": ..., "context": ..., "debug": "<traceback>"}` (`src/odoo/http.py:465-475`) |
| On `--dev=werkzeug`, the session-expired envelope never appears | `_update_served_exception` bubbles non-jsonrpc exceptions to the werkzeug debugger before `_handle_error` is consulted | `src/odoo/http.py:2302-2307` |
| Signing out leaves the app still able to call the API | Bearer token not revoked by `/api/v1/auth/logout` | See section 6 |

---

- `ADMIN_MEDIA_PREFIX` (`ir_http.py::ADMIN_MEDIA_PREFIX`, used at `:165`) has no caller in the Flutter client. `resolveMediaUrl` is referenced only from the exam stimulus and video widgets (`ethara-assessment-fe/lib/assessment/screens/exam/stimulus.dart:194`, `video_plate_web.dart:72`), which serve candidate token routes, and the single `Image.network` call passes no headers. A browser `<img>` cannot send `Authorization` anyway, and those routes declare no `cors`, so a credentialed cross-origin `fetch` of them cannot pass preflight either. The mechanism described at `ir_http.py:148-160` is in place but nothing currently drives it. UNKNOWN: whether a non-web (mobile/desktop) build of the client requests these URLs with headers.
- `custom_addons/analytics/models/ir_http.py`, cited at `ir_http.py:18`, does not exist.
- `save_session=True` on `auth.py:29` is the default for every route except `auth='bearer'` (`src/odoo/http.py:784-785`), so it is redundant.
- `csrf=False` on all 120 `/api/v1` routes is inert under json2 (section 7).
- The `"api.access_token" not in request.env` guard at `ir_http.py:524` describes a "cookie-only" fallback that the hard manifest dependency now makes unreachable.
- `find_one_or_create_token` (`api_auth_gateway/models/access_token.py::find_one_or_create_token`) computes and then discards a reusable token whenever `create=True`, so `api.access_token` grows by one row per login with no vacuum. Not this addon's code, but it is the store `_adopt_gateway_token` searches on every request.
- `access_token.py::has_expired` holds a commented-out duplicate of `has_expired`.


## 1.3 Shared helpers and access guards

Source file: `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/common.py` (327 lines, read in full). It is imported first by `controllers/api/__init__.py:14` because the other four controller modules bind its decorators at import time. Every symbol in it is module-level; there is no class.

#### Module-level constants

`API_TYPE` is `json2`, Odoo 19's plain-JSON dispatcher. The stated consequence (`common.py:19-22`) is that the **query string is ignored**: all filter/paging arguments must travel in the JSON body, which is why list endpoints accept both GET (no body, defaults apply) and POST (body with filters).

#### Authorisation guards

There are four group guards in this file plus one record guard and two token guards. All of them **return** an envelope; none raise. A caller that forgets to return the guard's value would silently continue - the record guard is the only one exposed to that mistake, and all 8 call sites use the `denied = ...; if denied: return denied` shape.

Each group guard tests exactly ONE group, the LOWEST one that should pass. `has_group` resolves through `implied_ids` and the chain is Admin -> Manager -> Candidate, so no guard enumerates roles and a higher rung is admitted for free.

Counts below are DECORATOR SITES (`grep -rc "@require_x" controllers/api/*.py`), which is what you can re-derive in one command. Every `/api/v1` decorator declares exactly one path; only the legacy redirects outside `/api/v1` declare several.

| Guard | Tests | Refusal message | Sites | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `require_manager` | `GROUP_MANAGER` (Admin) | "Assessment Admin access required" | 77 | write 52, admin 16, forms 6, task_templates 3 |
| `require_staff` | alias of the above | same | 10 | admin 8, task_templates 1, write 1 |
| `require_operator` | `GROUP_MANAGER_RESTRICTED` (Manager) | "Assessment Manager access required" | 16 | admin 15, forms 1 |
| `require_candidate` | `GROUP_CANDIDATE` | "Assessment access is not enabled for this account" | 4 | candidate 4 |

**FAIL CLOSED IS THE DESIGN, and it is worth stating why.** Every route keeps `require_manager` unless it was deliberately opted DOWN to `require_operator`. The inverse - pointing the default gate at Manager and raising the sensitive routes one at a time - makes every route nobody thought about a privilege leak. This way an overlooked route gives a read-only Manager a visible 403, which is a bug report.

`require_operator` is a **"this route is a read" marker, not a "a Manager may do this" marker.** All 16 of its routes are GET and mutate nothing. Assessments and Form Studio are therefore visible-but-read-only to a Manager rather than half-writable: `/api/v1/assessments` is `require_operator`, while `/api/v1/assessments/create` and `.../update` are not.

#### 1.3a The three rungs, and the ACL rows that make them work

`security/etp_assessment_security.xml` declares three groups in one privilege ("Assessment v2 Access"), so the user form shows a single dropdown reading **No / Candidate / Manager / Admin**. "No" is the privilege placeholder, not a record.

| XML id | Label | Sequence | Implies |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group_assessment_candidate` | Candidate | 10 | `base.group_user` - candidates are INTERNAL accounts |
| `group_assessment_manager_restricted` | Manager | 20 | Candidate |
| `group_assessment_manager` | **Admin** | 30 | Manager, `hr_recruitment.group_hr_recruitment_user` |

**The xmlid `group_assessment_manager` is labelled "Admin" on purpose.** It has always been the full-power group and ~40 sites point at it - 25 ACL rows, 3 record rules, 10 menus, 8 code guards and two views. Keeping it means the relabel needs no membership migration: everyone who is an admin today stays one. Repurposing the xmlid for the new read-only role would have silently converted all 40 of those into restricted grants.

**Holding a group is not the same as being able to read.** Odoo checks TWO independent things: the route guard asks `has_group`, and the ORM asks `ir.model.access`. The read-only Manager shipped with the first and not the second, and the result was a role that could sign in, was offered a console, and returned 403 on every screen in it:

```
403 {"code":"forbidden","message":"You are not allowed to access 'Assessment'
     (assessments.be) records. This operation is allowed for the following
     groups: - Assessment v2 Access/Admin ..."}
```

`ir.model.access.csv` now carries **15 `1,0,0,0` rows** for `group_assessment_manager_restricted`, one per model any `require_operator` route reads. Fourteen are this addon's own models. The fifteenth is **`hr.applicant`**, which this addon does not own: `assessments.be.evaluator_ids` is a Many2many to it, so the roster - and therefore both the assessment list and the assessment detail payload - cannot be serialized without read on it.

**That row must stay a bare ACL row.** Granting `hr.applicant` by implying one of hr_recruitment's groups instead looks tidier and is wrong both ways round:

- `group_hr_recruitment_user` carries write, create and unlink on applicants plus the whole Recruitment menu. A read-only role would be able to edit and delete candidate records.
- `group_hr_recruitment_interviewer` looks harmless but drags in the **"Applicant Interviewer" record rule**, domain `['|', ('job_id.interviewer_ids','in',user.id), ('interviewer_ids','in',user.id)]`. A Manager would then get 200 on every route and see an EMPTY roster on every launched assessment, with nothing on screen to explain it. That is worse than the 403, because it looks like data.

A bare ACL row attaches no record rule, so the only rule left on `hr.applicant` is Odoo's global multi-company one.

`tests/test_a_read_only_manager_can_actually_read.py` (11 tests) pins all of this, and it is the only test file in the addon that acts as a REAL user: `self.env(user=manager)` clears `env.su`, and `check_access` begins `if not self.env.su`. Every other access test in the suite runs as superuser or against a `_FakeRequest` built on `self.env`, which is why 1,691 green tests did not see the missing rows. Remove the 15 rows and that file reports 2 failures and 3 errors naming every affected model; verified by doing exactly that.

#### 1.3b The client half: a Manager must not be OFFERED an Admin route

Found the same way as the ACL hole - by signing in as one - and it is the same class of bug one layer up. **The console gated its write buttons on `Portal`, and `Portal` is binary.** There are two shells, the operator console and the candidate surface, and a read-only Manager belongs in the console, so `portal == Portal.admin` was true for them. Every screen on their rail therefore drew its full Admin toolbar: "New Assessment", per-row Archive, the bank importer, tag Normalize/Merge, Form Studio New/Import/Delete, Re-score. All Admin-only server-side. **A dead button is worse than a missing one**, because the reader cannot tell a permission from a bug - and the account card told them they were an "Admin", which is the label they would have quoted in the report.

The gate is `AppStore.can(Capability.x)`, fed by the `capabilities` array on the session payload, so what the console hides and what the API refuses come from ONE server-side fact rather than two hand-maintained lists. A Manager holds no capability at all - "read-only" is exactly "holds nothing that changes anything".

| Layer | Rule |
|---|---|
| Route (`assessment_section.dart::_isAuthoringOrPlatform`) | A Manager naming `GeneratorList`, `GeneratorDetail`, `ReviewQueue`, `SettingsAdmin`, `StartHere`, `NewAssessment` or `FormDesigner` lands on the Dashboard, not a 403 page. Covers deep links and stale history, which a hidden button does not. |
| Affordance | Each control is wrapped in `can(...)`. The slot COLLAPSES; a disabled control invites the reader to work out what would enable it, and nothing will. |
| Reading | Never gated. Notices, counts, roster chips, invite-failure reasons, the whole audit trail: a Manager is often the person being asked why a mark has not arrived, so the diagnosis stays and only the recovery goes. |
| Request | `_ifAdmin` (generators, settings) plus a gate on `_loadDraftsInBackground`. All three are Admin-only lists fetched on every console load, so without this each sign-in filed three 403s. |
| Label | `AccessRole.label` and `AccessRole.canDo`, never `Portal.label`. Three sites on the Account screen and one on the rail card read the binary and said "Admin"; the ledger breadcrumb asserted `Crumb('Admin')` on a screen a Manager can open. |

`FormDesigner` is route-guarded rather than made read-only on purpose: it AUTOSAVES, so a Manager would fire a 403 per keystroke, and it holds ~30 write affordances. A Manager reads a form through the `FormPreview` sheet instead - the Forms tab row tap branches on the capability.

Pinned by `test/assessment/manager_sees_no_write_affordance_test.dart` (21 tests). Every Manager assertion is `findsNothing`, so each one is paired with an Admin assertion that the same finder DOES match - otherwise a renamed button would make the file pass while proving nothing.

**`record_read_guard`** - **per record**, not per path (`common.py::record_read_guard`). This is the only guard that consults `ir.model.access` and `ir.rule`:

```python
    try:
        record.check_access("read")
    except AccessError:
        return fail("forbidden", "You may not read this record", status=403)
    return None
```

Its docstring states the exact hole it closes (`common.py:186-193`): `browse(id)` touches no database and `.exists()` is a bare `SELECT id`, so neither passes through an ACL or record rule; a route that then reads related rows under `sudo()` never reads a single field as the caller. The two admin call sites repeat the same reasoning inline and both mark the guard as "the ONLY line in this route that consults a record rule" (`admin.py:1384-1388`, `admin.py:1490-1494` - the chatter and email routes, whose subsequent searches run `sudo()`). The ORM's own `AccessError` text is swallowed on purpose so the refusal does not disclose the model, record ids or the granting groups.

**Route coverage of the group guards** (counted from decorator occurrences):

The four guards above cover 107 decorator sites. The paths carrying **no** group guard are 30, and each has a different reason: `auth.py` session/login (6) run before anybody has a role; `candidate.py`'s exam routes (6) are gated on the access token and an identity match instead; the media proxies (6) are `<img>`/`<video>` targets that carry no credential and gate inside the handler; `health` and `ready` (2) are load-balancer probes; the legacy redirect paths (9) only 301/302 to the Flutter client; and the Form Studio media route (1) serves published form assets.

Of the 120 `/api/v1` routes, **114** declare `auth="user"` and **6** declare `auth="public"`, re-counted per decorator by AST for `19.0.3.23.0` (unchanged from `19.0.3.22.0`). (The 11 August figures were counted from literals in aggregate rather than per route, which is why they summed to more than the route total.) The addon's 17 non-API paths - 9 legacy redirects, 6 media, 2 health probes - are counted separately; see section 1.1.

**Token guards for the candidate/exam surface.** `candidate.py` uses none of the group decorators; the equivalent gate is `is_assigned_candidate` / `may_view_attempt` plus its own `_write_guard`:

- `is_assigned_candidate(evaluator)` (`common.py::is_assigned_candidate`) resolves `evaluator._candidate_user()` and requires `request.env.user.id == candidate_user.id`. Every mutating exam route must gate on this and not merely on possession of the token, because a Manager previewing an exam holds the token too (`common.py:306-308`).
- `may_view_attempt(evaluator)` (`common.py::may_view_attempt`) is the read equivalent: the bound candidate always may; when the attempt has **no** resolvable candidate user, `request.env.user._be_is_staff()` is accepted - that is the preview path. Everyone else is refused. It used to test `has_group(GROUP_MANAGER)`, i.e. Admin only, which predates the Manager rung and so excluded the exact role preview was written for.
- `candidate.py::_write_guard` composes these into `_write_guard`, whose ordering is: unknown token -> `fail("invalid_token", ..., 404)`; not the assigned candidate -> `fail("wrong_candidate", ..., 403)`; attempt locked -> `fail("attempt_locked", ..., 409)`.

**Relationship to `api_auth_gateway`.** `common.py:106-119` states plainly that none of this addon's routes are registered as `api.role.endpoint` rows and that nothing here passes through the gateway decorator; the gateway reads an `access_token` header, while these routes are `auth="user"` and adopt an `Authorization: Bearer` token in `models/ir_http.py:_adopt_gateway_token` (`ir_http.py:497-538`), then gate on the decorators above. The claim in that docstring that this "looks like 78 unauthorized endpoints" is stale - there are 113 `/api/v1` decorators today.

#### Pagination

`paging()` (`common.py::paging`):

```python
    limit = int_arg("limit", DEFAULT_LIMIT) or DEFAULT_LIMIT
    offset = max(0, int_arg("offset", 0))
    return max(1, min(limit, MAX_LIMIT)), offset
```

| Aspect | Value |
|---|---|
| Body parameter names | `limit`, `offset` (JSON body only - query string is ignored, `common.py:19-22`) |
| Default limit | 40 (`DEFAULT_LIMIT`) |
| Maximum limit | 200 (`MAX_LIMIT`), hard-clamped |
| Minimum limit | 1 - a negative limit becomes 1 via `max(1, min(limit, MAX_LIMIT))` |
| `limit=0` | Falls back to `DEFAULT_LIMIT` because of the `or DEFAULT_LIMIT` |
| Offset | Floored at 0; no ceiling |

Page envelope, from `paged` (`common.py::paged`):

```json
{"ok": true, "data": [ ...rows... ],
 "meta": {"total": <int>, "limit": <int>, "offset": <int>, "has_more": <bool>}}
```

`has_more` is `(offset + len(rows)) < total` - computed from the returned row count, not from `limit`, so it stays correct on a short final page.

One route bypasses `paging()` and clamps itself: the leaderboard uses `limit = max(1, min(int_arg("limit", 10) or 10, MAX_LIMIT))` (`admin.py:1244`) - default 10, same 200 ceiling.

#### Search / filter / sort

`common.py` contains **no** search, filter, sort or domain-building helper. Domains are assembled inline per route in `admin.py`, from the `str_arg`/`bool_arg`/`int_arg`/`id_list_arg` readers. Two small filter helpers exist locally in `admin.py` and are shared only between that file's own routes:

| Helper | Where | Body params read | Domain built | Order |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_attempt_filters` | `admin.py::_attempt_filters` | `state`, `result`, `released_only`, `flagged_only` | `state =`, `result =`, `results_released = True`, and for `flagged_only` the OR chain `integrity_alert = True` / `score_outlier = True` / `scoring_error_flag != False` | - |
| `_attempt_page` | `admin.py::_attempt_page` | `limit`, `offset` via `paging()` | - | `create_date desc` |
| `_email_domain` | `admin.py::_email_domain` | `state`, validated against `self.EMAIL_STATES` | `[("state", "=", state)]` or `[]` | - |
| `_email_page` | `admin.py::_email_page` | `limit`, `offset` via `paging()`; searches `mail.mail` under `sudo()` | - | `id desc` (documented at `admin.py:1437-1440`: `date` belongs to `mail.message` via `_inherits` and cannot be an ORDER BY target on the queried table) |

Representative inline domains and their sort orders, for reference: assessments `name ilike` + `state` ordered `create_date desc` (`admin.py:52-64`); generators `name ilike` + `state` + `tag_ids in` ordered `create_date desc` (`admin.py:519-534`); drafts ordered `id` (`admin.py::state`); bank questions ordered `sequence, id` (`admin.py::prefix`, `746`); tags `name/display ilike` + `prefix` ordered `name` (`admin.py:786-796`); responses (`admin.py:809-841`) and AI usage (`admin.py:1321-1340`) ordered `create_date desc`. `_email_domain` returns a `(domain, error)` pair where exactly one is meaningful, and an unknown state yields `fail("bad_state", ..., status=400)`.

#### Limits and caps

| Constant | Value | Defined | Enforced at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEFAULT_LIMIT` | 40 | `common.py::DEFAULT_LIMIT` | `paging()` |
| `MAX_LIMIT` | 200 | `common.py::MAX_LIMIT` | `paging()`, `admin.py:1244` |
| `MAX_EXPORT_BYTES` | 20 MiB | `common.py::MAX_EXPORT_BYTES` | `write.py:_export` (`write.py:1339-1349`) -> `fail("export_too_large", ..., status=413, bytes=len(content), limit=MAX_EXPORT_BYTES)` |
| `_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | 25 MiB | `write.py::_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` - **not** in common.py | write.py upload routes, through `write.py::_too_large`, which sizes the base64 text BEFORE decoding (round 3, A-224); the CSV routes pass their own 25 MiB constants (`_MAX_CANDIDATE_CSV_BYTES`, `simple_import.MAX_CSV_BYTES`, the bank wizard's `_MAX_CSV_BYTES`) |
| `ANSWER_GRACE_SECONDS` | 10 | `controllers/api/candidate.py` | `/exam/<token>/answer` and `/violation`: how late after the deadline an answer is still kept (round 3; 1.6 Time limits) |
| `MAX_SCORING_SHARDS` | 4 (= the shard crons in `data/cron.xml`) | `constants.py` - **not** in common.py | `SETTING_RANGES["scoring_shards"]` (the settings write route, the Odoo form, the pre-deploy check) and the model's shard count. No route imports it any more: `/attempts/<id>/rescore` stopped taking the shard's advisory lock when it stopped grading inline |
| `MAX_SCORING_PARALLEL_CALLS` | 8 | `constants.py` | `SETTING_RANGES["scoring_parallel_calls"]` = (1, 8, default 4): judge calls one lane keeps in flight. New in 19.0.3.23.0 |

The rationale recorded for `MAX_EXPORT_BYTES` is that peak memory is roughly three times the file (file + base64 + the JSON copy), so 20 MB is about 60 MB of transient worker memory (`common.py:50-53`). Candidate free-text answers are truncated rather than rejected by caps declared locally in `candidate.py:30-34`.

#### Error helpers - what the client receives

Controllers never `raise` for a 4xx; they `return fail(...)`. `fail` builds a real `Response` via `request.make_json_response(payload, status=status)` (`common.py:83`) because the json2 dispatcher passes a `Response` through untouched but JSON-encodes a plain dict at status 200 (`common.py:74-79`).

Body shape:

```json
{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "<machine code>", "message": "<human text>"}, ...extra}
```

`code` is the branch contract; `message` may be reworded at any time (`common.py:70-73`). Extras land at the **top level**, siblings of `error`, not inside it - `bytes` and `limit` on `export_too_large` (`write.py:1348-1349`) and `meta` on `paged` are the examples.

`api_endpoint` (`common.py::api_endpoint`) converts anything that leaks out of a route:

| Caught | Envelope `code` | HTTP status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AccessDenied`, `AccessError` | `forbidden` (message = `str(exc)` or "Access denied") | 403 | `common.py::api_endpoint` |
| `UserError`, `ValidationError` | `rejected`, message forwarded **verbatim** (deliberate, user-facing domain refusals), after `cr.rollback()` | 422 | `common.py::api_endpoint` |
| A `UserError` carrying `code` (`RescoreRefused`) | its own `code`: `stopping`, `being_graded`, `spend_limit`, `erased`, `archived`, `released_confirm_required`, `released_results` (Reset to Draft, round 3), `not_on_attempt` | its `http_status`: 409, or 422 for `not_on_attempt` | `common.py::api_endpoint`, `models/assessment.py::RescoreRefused` |
| `SerializationFailure`, `TransactionRollbackError` | re-raised, never converted | - | `common.py:142-143` |
| Any other `Exception` | `server_error`, "Unexpected server error" | 500 | `common.py:132-152` |

Two details worth carrying forward. First, the serialization-failure re-raise is load-bearing: Postgres aborts the whole transaction, Odoo's `service.model.retrying` replays the request only if the exception reaches the top, and converting it here both defeats the retry and leaves the cursor dead so the serializer building the very response fails with `InFailedSqlTransaction` - recorded as the cause of a permanent 500 on `extract_tags` (`common.py:133-141`). Second, the generic handler calls `request.env.cr.rollback()` **before** building the envelope so `fail(...)` and Odoo's end-of-request flush run on a usable cursor (`common.py:146-151`), with the rollback itself wrapped in a bare `except` that never masks the original error.

Status codes actually used across the four controllers: 400 (18), 401 (2), 403 (7), 404 (53), 409 (17), 413 (3), 422 (41), 500 (1), 501 (1). The most common codes are `not_found` (50), `invalid` (26), `forbidden` (4).

Authentication failures never reach `api_endpoint` because they are raised by the dispatcher before any controller method runs; `models/ir_http.py:_handle_error` (`ir_http.py:549-585`) answers `http.SessionExpiredException` with 401 instead of 403, on the stated grounds that 401 tells a client to obtain credentials while 403 says "you may never".

#### Things that look wrong, dead, or contradictory

1. **Two different error body shapes.** `fail` nests under `error` (`common.py:81`), but `ir_http._handle_error` emits `{"ok": false, "code": "session_expired", "message": ...}` with `code` and `message` at the **top level** (`ir_http.py:569-573`). A client that branches on `error.code` will not find `session_expired`. This is a real contract split, not a stylistic one.
2. **`body()` has no external callers.** It exists only to serve the five readers in the same file. Not dead, but not a shared helper in practice.
3. **`int_arg` swallows an explicit zero.** `int(body().get(name, default) or default)` (`common.py:222`) means a JSON `0` is falsy and returns `default`. `int_arg("limit", 40)` with `"limit": 0` yields 40, not 0. Any future call site with a non-zero default and a meaningful 0 value would be wrong.
4. **`bool_arg` ignores its default on an explicit JSON `null`.** `raw = body().get(name, default)`; if the key is present with value `null`, control reaches `bool(None)` -> `False`, discarding a `default=True` (`common.py::bool_arg`). `write.py:1345`'s `bool_arg("archive", True)` relies on the key being absent, not null.
5. **`id_list_arg` accepts booleans.** `isinstance(True, int)` is true in Python, so `{"ids": true}` returns `[1]` (`common.py::id_list_arg`). `id_list_arg_strict` refuses them; the three routes where a wrong id list widens a paid or irreversible action use it.
6. **`require_staff`'s Manager branch is dead** given `implied_ids` (see the group table above).
7. **`float_arg` does not exist** but `tools/contract_audit.py:43` lists it in `READERS = {"arg", "str_arg", "int_arg", "bool_arg", "float_arg", "id_list_arg"}`. Either a leftover or an anticipated helper; the audit tool will simply never match it. The opposite gap matters more: `id_list_arg_strict` (19.0.3.23.0) is NOT in that set, so the audit reports the three keys read through it (`evaluator_ids` on `/release` and `/scoring/queue`, `question_ids` on `/attempts/*/rescore`) as unread and exits 1 - the 3 false positives in the headline facts.
8. **Stale endpoint count** in the `api_endpoint` docstring: "78 unauthorized endpoints" (`common.py`) vs 120 today. It was already stale at 84 in the 11 August edition.
9. **RESOLVED since 11 August.** `controllers/api/__init__.py` used to say the API "lives INSIDE etp_assessment_pro rather than in a separate addon", contradicting the manifest. It now says it lives inside `assessments_be_v2` because every route reads or writes THIS module's own models and calls THIS module's own `action_*` methods - which, after the fork, is simply true.
10. **`API_METHODS` is inconsistently applied.** admin/candidate/auth import it; write.py spells its method lists literally, so the "one constant so the whole surface can be moved in a single edit" intent (`common.py:15-17`) does not hold for the 49 routes in `write.py`.


## 1.4 Admin and read routes

All 39 routes live in one controller class, `EtpAssessmentApiAdmin` (`custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/admin.py::EtpAssessmentApiAdmin`). Every one is declared `type=API_TYPE` (`"json2"`, `controllers/api/common.py:36`), `auth="user"`, `csrf=False`, `cors="*"`, and is wrapped by `@api_endpoint` (envelope + exception mapping, `common.py:99`) plus exactly one of `@require_manager`, `@require_staff` (its alias) or `@require_operator` (15 read-only routes here that a Manager may call).

`Methods` below is the literal `methods=` on the route. `API_METHODS` is `["GET", "POST"]` (`common.py::API_METHODS`). Under the json2 dispatcher `request.params = self.jsonrequest | args` - the JSON body merged with the path parameters, query string never read (`src/odoo/http.py:2605-2617`, documented at `common.py:19-22`). **A GET therefore carries no filters and no paging at all**: every listed param below must travel in a JSON body with `Content-Type: application/json`, so a GET on any list route always returns the unfiltered first page (limit 40).

Source column line numbers are all in `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/admin.py`.

The Role column is the route's guard (re-derived from the decorators for 19.0.3.23.0): **Admin** is `require_manager` (and its alias `require_staff`), **Manager (read-only) or Admin** is `require_operator` - see 1.3 for the three rungs. Earlier editions wrote "staff" and "manager" here, from before the ladder.

#### Non-obvious behaviour and side effects

- **`/launch` is a mutation registered for GET.** It carries `methods=API_METHODS`, unlike every other state-changing route here, which are POST-only. It is safe only because `confirm` can only arrive in a body and json2 discards the query string, so a GET is always a dry run (admin.py:82, admin.py:107).
- **`_launch_gates` never short-circuits** (admin.py::_launch_gates). It re-implements the eight preconditions of `action_start` (`models/assessment.py::action_start`) as independent verdicts, then adds a ninth row, `grading_keys`, which is a WARNING and never blocks: `passed` is always true, `warning` is true when a graded question has no usable answer key (`scoring.lacks_answer_key`), and the reason names up to 10 such questions - their answers are graded against the task alone and flagged `no_answer_key`. The pool query (active, not retired, media present, narrowed by the shortlist) is copied from that method, so it can drift if `action_start` changes; `answer_keys` asks the model instead (`question._keyless_reason`), so that gate cannot. The first gate is `duration` (at least 2 minutes). When no generator is set, gates 5-8 (`questions_available`, `question_limit`, `answer_keys`, `reviewed_rubrics`) are emitted as failed with the reason `"Cannot check: no question generator selected."` and the function returns early (admin.py:146-160). The `reviewed_rubrics` gate reports `passed: True` with the label suffixed `"(not required)"` when `require_reviewed_rubric` is off (admin.py:219-222), so a client that only reads `passed` cannot tell an enforced pass from a skipped check.
- **`/release` reports what the action did, and skips a candidate being graded.** Both branches call the model (`action_release_results` for named ids, `action_confirm_release` for the cohort - `action_release_all_results` is the Odoo button, which opens the counted confirm dialog first) and take `released_count` / `skipped_count` from its `release` counts. A candidate a grading lane holds right now is not released: writing that row would hand the lane a SerializationFailure and its paid results would be bought again. `candidates` lists only the rows this call flipped (not the skipped, not earlier releases), and any skip adds `notice: {kind: "warning", title, message, is_warning: true}` - "Released N result(s). M candidate(s) being graded right now were not released - try again in a minute." - which both app builds toast in place of their fixed "Result released". `still_grading_count` counts released rows with `subjective_pending`, a warning, not a block. The strict parser closes the hole where an unreadable `evaluator_ids` fell through to the whole-cohort branch; an id past a float (`1e400`) is 422, not 500. Pinned by `tests/test_the_release_route_releases_what_it_says.py`.
- **`/assign` creates `hr.applicant` rows under `sudo()`** (admin.py::applicant, admin.py:386). An assessment Manager with no recruitment rights can create applicants through this route. Existing applicants are matched by `email_from` `=ilike` and get their `partner_name` backfilled if empty (admin.py:379-384) - a write to a record the caller did not name.
- **A typed-in `/assign` row must be a real address** (round 3, A-222). Every `candidates` row with both a name and an email goes through `candidate_row_error` (`models/hr_applicant.py`: strict `email_normalize`, name up to 200 characters) before anything is written; one bad row refuses the whole request with 422 `invalid` naming each bad row. A row missing its name or email is still skipped, as before. The candidate CSV import uses the same check (2.1 §11).
- **`_provision_late_candidates`** (admin.py::_provision_late_candidates) is the only place in this file that reimplements part of a lifecycle action rather than calling it. It draws from `assessment.question_ids` (the launch snapshot), falling back to a live generator query and *writing that back* onto `question_ids` if the snapshot is empty. **Every late candidate gets a copy of the cohort's one shared set** - "Same questions for everybody" is retired and `same_questions_for_all` is no longer read - taken from the **oldest** attempt that holds a paper (a bare roster row or a `"[]"` paper is skipped), shuffled unless `preserve_question_order` is set. When nobody holds a paper yet, it draws once and the rest of the batch copies that draw. A candidate is **refused, not provisioned**, when the cohort's set lost questions since launch (archived, media gone - the peers sat them, so a copy would be shorter), or when there is no shared set and the pool cannot fill `question_limit`; refusals come back as `not_provisioned` and a chatter line names who and why. Returns `(ids, refusals)`, `([], [])` when there is nobody new or no pool (it used to 500 on a running paper). It creates evaluators under `sudo()` with `invite_state: "queued"` and posts a chatter line with the number of questions actually given. `access_token` is not passed but the field defaults to a fresh uuid4 (`models/assessment.py::access_token`), so late attempts do get a working link.
- **`/drafts/<id>/approve` gates on authoring warnings** derived from `has_revealing_option` / `has_source_reference` (admin.py:643-652). `/drafts/<id>/deny` cannot store its reason on the draft - there is no field - so it posts it to the *generator's* chatter, HTML-escaped (admin.py:686-692). The reason is echoed back in the response but is not retrievable per draft afterwards.
- **`/bank?servable_only=true` pages in Python, not SQL** (admin.py:735-743). It runs an **unlimited** search over the matching bank rows, filters them with `_has_required_images`/`_has_required_videos` (Python guards, not columns), then slices. On a large bank this loads the whole result set per request. It also hard-codes `("active", "=", True)`, which silently contradicts `include_archived` when both are sent.
- **`/responses` accepts `llm_state` or `scoring_state` for the same field** (admin.py::llm_state). `question_type` is filtered via `question_id.question_type` because the response-side field is a non-stored related (`models/assessment.py::question_type`).
- **The exam access token is exposed by exactly one route**: `/attempts/<id>` passes `with_link=True` when the caller is a Manager (admin.py:895-897). `S.evaluator_admin_row` defaults `with_link=False`, so no list route leaks it (`controllers/api/serializers.py:706`).
- **`record_read_guard` is applied only to `/chatter/...` and `/emails/<kind>/<id>`** (admin.py:1388, admin.py:1494), because those two are the only routes whose payload is built entirely under `sudo()`. Everywhere else the serializer reads fields as the calling user, so record rules fire naturally and an `AccessError` becomes a 403 through `api_endpoint`. Note the resulting status asymmetry: a record hidden by a record rule returns 404 from `browse().exists()` on some paths and 403 on others.
- **`/emails` (global) is Manager-only and lists assessment mail only** (round 3, A-226): its domain is prefixed with `ASSESSMENT_MAIL` (`mail_message_id.model` in the chatter allow-list's three models, the same records `emails_for_record` reads), so a password reset or another module's mail is never listed. The record-scoped variant is staff-readable (admin.py:1510-1525 vs admin.py::mail). Both search under `sudo()` because upstream grants `mail.mail` only to `base.group_system` (admin.py:1445-1452). `failure_reason` is regex-masked to strip `/pro_assessment/<token>` before it leaves (`serializers.py:1290-1294`).
- **`/emails/<id>/cancel` cancels only assessment mail** (round 3, A-227): it searches the id inside `ASSESSMENT_MAIL`, so any other mail (a password reset included) is 404 `not_found`, as a missing id is. Then Manager plus `state in ("outgoing", "exception")`.
- **The chatter allow-list is deliberately not a free `model` param** (admin.py:1343-1352) and is reused by the email route. Its message-type filter is `["comment", "notification"]` (admin.py:1401). The inline comment says `notification` is "the module's own audit line", but `_log_activity` actually posts with `message_type="comment"` and subtype `mail.mt_note` (`models/assessment.py::_log_activity`). The comment is wrong about which type carries the audit; the allow-list still admits both, so behaviour is correct.

#### Attempts / evaluators listing

Two routes share one filter builder and one pager, by design (admin.py:270-303):

| Filter | Body key | Domain leaf |
|---|---|---|
| lifecycle state | `state` | `("state", "=", v)`; empty or `all` = no term; `scored` / `score_pending` = the answer-level domain below (`_state_domain`) |
| pass/fail | `result` | `("result", "=", v)` |
| released only | `released_only` (bool) | `("results_released", "=", True)` |
| review queue | `flagged_only` (bool) | `OR(integrity_alert, score_outlier, scoring_error_flag != False)` |
| assessment scope | `assessment_id` (only on `/attempts`) | `("assessment_id", "=", v)` |

**"Scored" and "Score Pending" are defined on ANSWERS, not on the attempt's `llm_state`** (W8; an objective-only attempt is never rolled up and keeps `pending` for ever). Score Pending = submitted with at least one answer that needs the grader and is not scored (queued, never queued, in flight, partial, failed, error, cancelled, archived paper); Scored = every other submitted attempt, so the two always add up to Submitted. A queued re-score leaves the old mark in place, so it keeps the candidate in Scored. The domain is the evaluator's own `_answers_scored_domain`, shared with the "Scored X/Y" line and `awaiting_scoring_count`, so the chips and the line agree. `/candidates` returns `meta.counts` keyed by every value `state` accepts (`all`, each attempt state, `scored`, `score_pending`), counted under every OTHER filter so a chip says what pressing it would list - in two queries whatever the cohort's size (a grouped read by state, then one count of Score Pending; Scored is the difference). Pinned by `tests/test_scored_and_score_pending_split_the_submitted.py`.

`meta.counts.pass` / `meta.counts.fail` (W5.5) are the Passed / Failed chips: the request key `result` (`pass` / `fail` / `pending`, any other value ignored) is AND-ed with `state`, and the two counts take every filter except their own `result` (as the state chips leave out only `state`), so pressing Failed never hides Passed and a pressed state narrows both - one more grouped read by `result`. Pinned by `tests/test_the_candidates_table_counts_passed_and_failed.py`.

`flagged_only` is built as `["|", "|", a, b, c]` (admin.py:289-292) - correct prefix notation for a three-way OR, ANDed with the preceding leaves. `scoring_error_flag` is a stored Char computed to `"!"` or `False` (`models/assessment.py:984-994`), so `!= False` resolves to `IS NOT NULL`.

Paging is offset-based over an ORM `search_count` + `search`, ordered `create_date desc`, under the caller's own record rules - no `sudo()` (admin.py:295-303). There is no cursor/keyset paging, so a listing that changes underneath a paging client can skip or repeat rows. `/attempts` exists specifically to replace one-request-per-assessment polling (admin.py:310-322); note that `flagged_only` on `/responses` means something narrower - `integrity_alert` alone (admin.py:836-837) - despite the shared name, which is exactly the cross-screen divergence `_attempt_filters` was written to prevent.

#### The scoring lane

- **`/scoring` (read)** defines the pipeline by `response_ids.needs_llm = True` rather than by the evaluator's `llm_state`, because the evaluator selection has no `not_needed` value (`models/assessment.py::llm_state`), so an all-objective paper would otherwise sit in `pending` forever (admin.py:1021-1034). The filter is applied to the four *waiting* lanes only - `pending`, `scoring`, `partial`, `failed` - while `scored` and `error` are counted raw (admin.py::error). All six lane names match the model's selection exactly, and `partial` is genuinely reachable (`models/assessment.py:1340-1343`). The six lanes come from one grouped read (the waiting lanes under the subjective filter, `scored` and `error` raw), and the 50-row errored `search` runs only when something is errored. **`queued` is what a lane would pick up**: one count over the drainer's own predicate (`_scoring_queue_domain`: `scoring_requested` and `llm_state` in `pending`/`partial`/`failed`, paper active and not cancelled, attempt not erased). It used to count `scoring_requested` in any state, and that flag is never cleared after a good score (prod read 2102 queued beside 2103 scored). The drainer-health verdict is computed once and handed to the phase compute through the context, so the cron check runs once per request. The route is written for polling. The reply also carries `phase` and `summary` (`null` / `""` unless scoped to one assessment) and `drainer` (`stalled`, cron counts, `reason`), which the dashboard's grader banner reads.
- **`/scoring/queue`** never grades inline: both branches only set `scoring_requested` / `llm_state = "pending"`. The reply is the action's own `{queued, skipped}`: a candidate a lane is grading right now is left to it (rewriting the row would make the lane's paid result collide and hide it from Kill), and for named ids an erased attempt is skipped too. The assessment branch calls `action_llm_score_all`, which **raises `UserError` when nothing is pending** - so "nothing to queue" surfaces as a 422 `rejected`, not a 200 with `queued: 0`. A paper whose Kill is still stopping is 409 `stopping` and a cancelled paper 422 `rejected`, with nothing written. `evaluator_ids` goes through the strict parser with `empty_ok=True`, because both app builds send `evaluator_ids: []` alongside `assessment_id`; unreadable ids are 422 `invalid`. The `evaluator_ids` branch is not scoped to any assessment; arbitrary ids are accepted and the ORM write is the only authorization.
- **`/scoring/requeue_errored`** is the only reset path (INVARIANT 5). It takes `evaluator_ids` or an `assessment_id` (a whole paper's stuck candidates). A candidate a lane is grading and an erased attempt are left alone (`action_reset_failed_scoring`); `answers_reset` says how many answers were actually reset. With `evaluator_ids` (the org-wide Responses sweep) the candidates of a cancelled paper, or of one whose Kill is still stopping, are dropped and counted in `skipped` instead of refusing the whole list (round 3, RV4-01); an `assessment_id` call on such a paper is still refused (409 `stopping`, 422 `rejected`).
- **`/attempts/<id>/rescore` queues; it never grades** (19.0.3.23.0, W6 - `docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 3 §3.8). It refuses anything not `submitted` (409), reads `question_ids` with the strict parser, and calls `action_rescore_individually`, which writes a fresh `rescore_request_key` on exactly the chosen answers (a failed or errored one also gets a fresh attempt budget). The lane that owns the candidate grades keyed answers first on its next tick; a scored answer keeps its mark unless the new grade succeeds. No web worker waits on Vertex, and the old shard advisory lock, the `pg_advisory_unlock_all()` and the 409 `scoring_busy` are gone with the inline grading. Refusals write nothing: `spend_limit` (daily or per-candidate cap reached; the per-minute limit is not a refusal, the key simply waits), `erased`, `archived` (queueing would lower the archive's stop flag), `stopping`, `being_graded` (with or without `question_ids`: "come back in a minute", never "nothing to re-score"), `released_confirm_required` (a mark the candidate can already see moves only with `confirm: true`, as `/scoring/requeue_errored` asks for `force`), and 422 `not_on_attempt`. A cancelled paper is 422 `rejected`. The chatter records who asked, for which answers, and the mark each had.
- **`/kill_scoring`** reports what the click stopped, from the settle itself - not the paper's lifetime `cancelled` tally. The action parks queued candidates no running lane holds, drops the paper's queued re-score requests (a killed re-score is not graded on the next tick), and leaves the flag raised while a lane is mid-call, so the candidate being graded stops at its next call (`held_count`). While the flag is up and a lane still holds a candidate (phase `stopping`), every route that queues grading answers 409 `stopping` before writing anything; Odoo hides those buttons and Flutter disables them. Once the lane lets go, the first click that actually queues something withdraws the kill.

#### Analytics and dashboard routes

| Route | Aggregated server-side | Left to the client |
|---|---|---|
| `/analytics` | `totals` (assigned/submitted/decided/passed/failed/awaiting, `avg_score`, `pass_rate`, `completion_rate` - all rounded to 1dp), `flags` (4 counts), `by_assessment` per-assessment rollup for the 25 newest assessments | any charting, any time series (none is returned), any assessment beyond the newest 25 |
| `/leaderboard` | full ranking: two `_read_group`s on the DB, tie-break `(avg, passed, attempts)` descending, sliced to `limit` | nothing - rows arrive pre-ranked with `rank` set |
| `/budget` | today's spend, per-operation spend/tokens (sorted desc), remaining, `capped` boolean, lifetime spend and call count | nothing beyond formatting |
| `/scoring` | six lane counts, queued count, config knobs, 50 most recent errored attempts | any grouping of the errored list |

`/analytics` also sends `totals.in_progress` / `totals.not_started` (attempt state `in_progress` / `pending`, so `assigned = not_started + in_progress + submitted`) and `flags.needs_review` (DISTINCT attempts with `integrity_alert`, `score_outlier` or `is_violated`), W5.2; every older key is unchanged.

The two aggregation routes take opposite approaches and the contrast is deliberate but uneven:

- `/leaderboard` aggregates **on the database** with `Evaluator._read_group` over `[state=submitted]`, one grouped read for count/avg/max and a second for the pass count (admin.py:2358-2376). Release is not a filter on who is ranked or on attempts/avg/best (the board must agree with the score distribution beside it), but the second read adds `results_released=True`, so a row's `passed` counts released passes only, the same rule as the analytics pass-rate tile. Note it is `require_manager` - the only read-only listing in the file that is not staff-readable.
- `/analytics` does the opposite: `everyone = Evaluator.search(domain)` with **no limit** (admin.py:1146) and then filters and sums in Python over the whole recordset. With `assessment_id` omitted this loads every evaluator the caller may read into memory on every call. `by_assessment` then walks up to 25 assessments, reading `assessment_evaluator_ids` on each (admin.py:1157-1174). Precomputed stored counters (`submitted_count`, `awaiting_scoring_count`, `releasable_count`) are used for three of the columns but `decided`/`passed`/`avg_score` are recomputed in Python from the cohort.
- `/analytics` applies no `record_read_guard` to a supplied `assessment_id`; reading the x2many on a rule-hidden assessment raises `AccessError`, which `api_endpoint` turns into a 403 (`common.py::api_endpoint`).

#### Dead, duplicated, or unreachable

- **Unused imports/module state.** `import logging` (admin.py:16) and `_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (admin.py:37) are never referenced anywhere in the file - this module never logs.
- **Duplicated launch validation.** `_launch_gates` (admin.py::_launch_gates) duplicates `action_start`'s eight checks. The answer-key check is no longer one of the copies - both sides ask `question._keyless_reason` - but the pool filter and the other gates are. Intentional per the docstring, but it is a real fork that must be kept in sync by hand.
- **Duplicated candidate provisioning.** `_provision_late_candidates` (admin.py::_provision_late_candidates) re-implements the per-candidate half of `action_start` (`models/assessment.py::action_start`) - copy the shared set, shuffle, create, queue invite - contradicting this file's own house rule in the module docstring (admin.py:2-13). There is no upstream action for "add a candidate to a running assessment", so the fork appears unavoidable; it is still a fork.
- **RESOLVED in 19.0.3.23.0: `/assessments/<id>` no longer appends `candidates`.** It used to add every attempt, unpaged, beside `roster` and `questions` - 904 KB of a 1 MB payload on a 750-candidate paper. The attempts are paged through `/candidates`. `S.assessment_detail` still embeds a full `bank_question_row` per selected question (1.7 §7 item 6).
- **Stale docstring cross-reference.** `email_cancel`'s docstring points at `/attempts/<id>/resend` (admin.py:1537), which is not in this file - it lives in `controllers/api/write.py:1225`. Accurate, just not local.
- **Comment/code mismatch** on the chatter message-type allow-list, described above (admin.py:1394-1397 vs `models/assessment.py:75`).
- **No route path in this file collides with `write.py`, `candidate.py`, or `auth.py`.** The `<int:...>` converters keep `/assessments/create`, `/bank/import` and `/generators/create` (all in `write.py`) from shadowing the detail routes here.
- **UNKNOWN: whether the `partial` and `failed` evaluator lanes are ever surfaced to a client.** They are reachable in the model, and `/scoring` counts them, but nothing in this file treats them differently from `pending` - only `error` drives `needs_manual_requeue` (admin.py::error).
- **UNKNOWN: `/ledger` reads `assessments.be.llm.usage` as the calling user (admin.py:1320) while `/budget` reads the same model under `sudo()` (admin.py:1279).** Both are Manager-gated, so whether `/ledger` returns rows at all depends on the ACL for that model, which I did not read.


## 1.5 Write routes and their invariants

All paths below live in `assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/write.py`, on the single controller class `EtpAssessmentApiWrite` (write.py::EtpAssessmentApiWrite) - except the last subsection, "Form Studio's own routes", which covers `controllers/api/forms.py` and says so again where it starts. Every route is `type="json2"` (`API_TYPE`, common.py::API_TYPE), `auth="user"`, `csrf=False`, `cors="*"`. Paths in citations are relative to `custom_addons/`.

Two facts govern everything else in this file:

- `fail()` **returns** a `Response`, it does not raise (common.py::fail). Nothing rolls back when a route returns a failure envelope, so any write that happened before the `return fail(...)` is committed at end of request. This is the mechanism behind the partial-apply cases listed at the end.
- `api_endpoint` (common.py::api_endpoint) converts leaked exceptions: `AccessDenied`/`AccessError` to 403, `UserError`/`ValidationError` (and their subclasses, including `MissingError`) to 422 `rejected` after `cr.rollback()` - or to the exception's own `code` and `http_status` when it carries one (`RescoreRefused`) - `SerializationFailure`/`TransactionRollbackError` re-raised for Odoo's retry, everything else to 500 `server_error` after `cr.rollback()`. A route's own `return fail(...)` does **not** roll back; the import routes therefore call `cr.rollback()` before each `import_failed` themselves.

#### Route table

| Path | Methods | Role | Body params | Effect | Returns | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/v1/assessments/create` | POST | manager | `name` (required) + any `ASSESSMENT_FIELDS` key | `assessments.be.create(values)`; `state` cannot be set because it is absent from the allow-list. A `max_violations` that is absent, `null` or `""` takes the field default 5 (round 3, A-074), not `_picked`'s 0 ("end on the first violation"); a `violation_action` that is absent, `null` or `""` takes the field default `log_only` rather than `""`, which the required Selection refuses | `S.assessment_detail` | write.py:406-424 |

| `/api/v1/assessments/<int:assessment_id>/cancel` | POST | manager | none | `record.action_cancel()` | `S.assessment_detail` | write.py:518-536 |

Over 25 MB is 413 `too_large` ("That image is N MB. The limit is 25 MB."), checked before decoding | `S.draft_detail` | write.py:966-1014 |
