The table holds 35 of `write.py`'s **53** routes; 19.0.3.23.0 adds and removes none. 19.0.3.24.0 adds three (56): `/generators/<id>/cancel_tag_extract`, `/generators/<id>/retry_failed_images`, `/drafts/<id>/retry_images` (see 5.0a). Not tabled here, all `require_manager` unless noted: `/assessments/<id>/archive` and `/delete` (see 2.2 §3.11a), `/assessments/<id>/candidates/import`, `/attempts/<id>/flag` (Part 5, D1), `/bank/<id>/delete`, `/bank/<id>/restore`, `/bank/delete`, `/bank/archive` (12 Oct 2026: `{ids, archive}` writes `retired` only and erases nothing; the bank's Archive used to call `/bank/delete`. Delete on a question with history now also sets `deleted`: out of Archived, listed under the app's Show deleted, never restorable, its papers, answers and scores untouched), `/bank/<id>/studio_item/save`, `/bank/template` and `/bank/template/json` (4.1), `/generators/<id>/cancel_generation`, `/generators/<id>/delete`, `/generators/delete`, `/generators/import`, `/generators/template`, `/tags/import`, `/tags/template`, `/settings/service_account`; and `task_templates.py`'s four (`/task_templates`, `require_staff`; `/task_templates/save`, `/draft`, `/delete`). Read each one's docstring. The Role column above predates the access ladder: "manager" and "staff" both mean Admin today (1.3).

`record_read_guard` (the caller's own ACL/record rules, common.py::record_read_guard) is applied on only six of them: generator archive (write.py:742), bank update (942), the three exports (1373, 1392, 1412) and chatter post (1483). Every other route relies on `require_manager` alone plus `browse().exists()`, which is a bare `SELECT id` enforcing nothing.

#### Field allow-lists

The module docstring (write.py:12-17) states the rule: nothing is passed to `create`/`write` wholesale; a field not named in a constant cannot be written. `_picked` (write.py::_picked) does the copying and omits keys the caller did not send, so a partial update touches only what it named.

**`ASSESSMENT_FIELDS`** (`write.py::ASSESSMENT_FIELDS`), **21** members, re-counted for 19.0.3.23.0: `name` (str), `generator_id` (int), `question_limit` (int), `duration_minutes` (int), `results_release` (str), `subjective_threshold` (float), `pass_threshold` (float, Q20), `start_date` (str), `end_date` (str), `rule_block_tab_switch`, `rule_block_copy_paste`, `rule_block_right_click`, `rule_block_devtools`, `rule_watermark`, `rule_fullscreen`, `rule_webcam` (all bool), `max_violations` (int), `violation_action` (str), `llm_auto_score` (bool), `require_reviewed_rubric` (bool), `question_ids` (ids). `state`, `results_released` and `score` are deliberately absent.

Four members earlier editions listed are **gone**: `require_justification_image_comparison` (removed with the `image_ab` blend - see 2.2 §3.1), `require_objective_justification`, `rule_block_screenshot`, and - since 19.0.3.23.0 - **`same_questions_for_all`**: "Same questions for everybody" is retired, every paper is one shared set, and the column stays with nothing reading it (`docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 4 §4.3). A payload still sending any of them has the key dropped silently, which is the allow-list's normal behaviour for an unknown key - so an older app that still sends it is ignored, not refused.

**`POST_DRAFT_FIELDS`** (`write.py::POST_DRAFT_FIELDS`), **17** members, re-counted for 19.0.3.23.0, the subset still editable once `state != "draft"`: `subjective_threshold`, `pass_threshold` (Q20), `duration_minutes`, `question_limit`, the seven `rule_*` flags, `max_violations`, `violation_action`, `llm_auto_score`, `require_reviewed_rubric`, `results_release`, and **`name`** - added in 19.0.3.22.0 on the grounds that a rename is not a change to the exam, and the title was otherwise editable only for as long as nobody had sat the paper. **`question_limit` is listed so the SAME value passes, not so it can change**: older apps save the whole settings object, and a changed count after launch is 422 `locked_after_launch` ("Every candidate sits the question set drawn at launch") - late candidates copy the set already drawn, so a new count would reach nobody. `shuffle_questions` is NOT here: `_apply_shuffle_alias` folds it onto `preserve_question_order` BEFORE the draft gate runs, so the draw order is refused on a running assessment by this one set. That is the server behaviour the Flutter Config tab's `_drawRo` now mirrors. The asymmetry the 11 August edition flagged is resolved: the field it named is no longer in `ASSESSMENT_FIELDS` either.

`subjective_threshold` and `pass_threshold` being post-draft editable is load-bearing, not incidental. Every earned mark is derived live from `llm_raw_100` and the subjective threshold, and Pass/Fail from the marks and the pass threshold, so moving either re-decides a whole cohort's results **with no re-scoring and no LLM spend**. Section 2.2 §3.9.

`pass_threshold` on `assessment_create` and `assessment_update` must be 1-100, else 422 `invalid` ("pass_threshold must be between 1 and 100."), from one helper, `write.py::_bad_pass_threshold`. 0 is refused too: "not set" is only ever the state of an assessment made before the field. A sent value that is not a number (`"abc"`, `"70%"`) is 422 `invalid` ("pass_threshold must be a number between 1 and 100."); it used to answer 200 and save nothing (round 3). `null` or `""` still means "not sent". The model enforces the same range on create and write (`_refuse_bad_pass_threshold`), and a create that leaves the key out is seeded from the Settings default (2.1 §2). The Flutter New Assessment form always sends it.

**`GENERATOR_FIELDS`** (write.py::GENERATOR_FIELDS), 5 members: `name` (str), `source_text` (str), `sop_title` (str), `sop_summary` (str), `sop_question_count` (int). `question_count_mode` is deliberately excluded because it is computed from `sop_question_count`.

**`DRAFT_FIELDS`** (write.py::DRAFT_FIELDS), 14 members: `name`, `question_prompt`, `description`, `question_type`, `difficulty` (str), `time_minutes` (int), `official_reasoning` (str), and the seven rubric fields `ak_ideal_answer`, `ak_mandatory_elements`, `ak_penalty_rules`, `ak_scoring_guide`, `ak_checklist`, `ak_constraints`, `ak_pass_condition` (all str, computed-with-inverse on the model, prompt.py:1943-1966).

**`BANK_FIELDS`** (write.py::BANK_FIELDS), 9 members: `name`, `prompt`, `description`, `difficulty` (str), `time_minutes` (int), `sequence` (int), `official_reasoning` (str), `rubric_reviewed` (bool), `active` (bool). `question_type` is **not** writable on a bank question, unlike on a draft.

**`SETTINGS`** (`write.py::SETTINGS`), now **38** keys (re-counted by AST for 19.0.3.27.0, `answers_flush_seconds`, `redis_url` and `cron_lock_mode` included; `paper_prefetch`, a strict bool, added after it), all `ir.config_parameter` names under the `assessments_be_v2.` prefix; the caller sends the part after the dot. Four governance floats (`score_outlier_sigma`, `pii_retention_days`, `daily_llm_cap_usd`, `per_evaluator_llm_cap_usd`), the model/location strings (including `thinking_level`), the S3 strings, and the five scoring knobs (`scoring_shards`, `scoring_parallel_calls`, `scoring_tick_limit`, `scoring_batch_size`, `llm_max_attempts`). `scoring_parallel_calls` (new in 19.0.3.23.0) is range-checked 1-8 from `constants.SETTING_RANGES`, and 0 means "unset, use the default 4", as for the other bounded integers; each lane runs the lower of it and what `db_maxconn` allows. The cache switch `scoring_cache` and the verdict gate `verdict_requires_current_prompt` are deliberately NOT here: they are system parameters only (switch table: `docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 0 §0.5 J). Two keys are Selection-backed and are checked against an exact value list by `write.py::_SETTING_CHOICES`: `video_default_duration_s` and, since 19.0.3.22.0, **`thinking_level`** (`model_catalog.THINKING_LEVELS` - `LOW`/`MEDIUM`/`HIGH`, plus `""` to clear the override). Without that entry a lowercase `"medium"` - which the runtime resolver accepts and upper-cases - saved 200 and then raised `Wrong value for ... 'medium'` on the next open of the Settings page for **any** app. `thinking_level` is also now READABLE on `GET /api/v1/settings` under `models.thinking_level`; it was write-only, so the console could set it and never show what it had set. `write.py::SECRETS` adds three WRITE-ONLY keys (`vertex_api_key`, `vertex_access_token`, `s3_secret_key`) that never come back from `/api/v1/settings`, which reports each as a boolean - omitting one leaves the stored value alone, so a Save from a form showing "set" cannot wipe a credential it could not display. `pass_threshold` was in this list on 11 August, was read by nothing, and has been removed. Its successor, since Q20, is **`default_pass_threshold`** (int): it only seeds a NEW assessment's `pass_threshold`, never an existing one, and is range-checked 1-100 (422 otherwise). Section 4.2 has the full table.

**`CHATTER_MODELS`** (write.py::CHATTER_MODELS), 3 entries: `assessment` -> `assessments.be`, `generator` -> `assessments.be.prompt`, `attempt` -> `assessments.be.evaluator`.

**`_RESOURCE_CATEGORIES`** (write.py::_RESOURCE_CATEGORIES): `sop`, `reference`, `sample`, `golden`, `vendor`, `client`, `other`. Mirrors the model's own selection. Note the model defaults to `other` while the route defaults to `sop` (write.py:630). Since 2026-09-29 golden and sample questions are ONE list: a `golden` upload is stored as `sample`, accepts every sample format (pdf, docx, txt, md, markdown, csv, html, json, xml, images) and is no longer refused; `init()` on `assessments.be.prompt.resource` moves existing `golden` rows to `sample` on `-u`. `golden` stays in the selection only so old rows and old clients still parse.

Fields written **outside** any allow-list, i.e. exceptions to the stated rule: `options_json` and `correct_answer_json` in draft update (write.py:892-895), `allowed_question_type_ids` (583), `active` in archive (748), `upload_image`/`upload_slot` (1008), `upload_video`/`upload_video_filename`/`upload_video_slot` (1654-1656), `source_url` on the image (1613), and the whole `question_dimension_ids` tree via `_sync_dimensions` (231).

`_picked` type coercion has asymmetric failure behaviour worth knowing:

| kind | helper | value that cannot be parsed | key sent as `null` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `int` | `int_arg(name, 0)` | **silently written as 0** | written as 0 |
| `float` | `_number` | **key skipped entirely** (write.py:86-88) | key skipped |
| `bool` | `bool_arg(name)` | `bool(raw)` | written as `False` |
| `ids` | `id_list_arg` | non-int items dropped | `(6,0,[])`, i.e. clears the relation |
| `str` | `str_arg(name)` | n/a, `str()` always succeeds, value is stripped | written as `""` |

`question_limit: "abc"` therefore silently sets 0, which the model documents as "all questions" (assessment.py:108-112), and `duration_minutes: "abc"` silently sets 0, which is "no limit" (assessment.py:123-127). The float path was deliberately made to skip instead (comment at write.py:86-87); the int path was not.

#### Validation rules and refusals

Assessments:

| Rule | Message | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name must be non-empty on create | "A name is required" | 422 | write.py:419 |
| Assessment must exist (update/cancel/reset/resend_all/exports) | "Assessment not found" | 404 | write.py:476, 533, 548, 1254, 1370, 1390 |
| Non-draft assessment, fields outside `POST_DRAFT_FIELDS` | "Only a draft assessment can be edited. This one is %s. These cannot change now: %s." | 409 `not_draft` | write.py::POST_DRAFT_FIELDS |
| Non-draft assessment, `question_limit` different from the stored one | "The number of questions cannot change after launch. Every candidate sits the question set drawn at launch." | 422 `locked_after_launch` | write.py::assessment_update |
| `pass_threshold` outside 1-100 on create or update, 0 included (Q20) | "pass_threshold must be between 1 and 100." | 422 `invalid` | write.py::_bad_pass_threshold (assessment_create, assessment_update) |
| `pass_threshold` sent but not a number (round 3) | "pass_threshold must be a number between 1 and 100." | 422 `invalid` | write.py::_bad_pass_threshold |
| Reset to Draft on a paper with released results, without `confirm_released: true` (round 3, A-040) | "N candidate(s) on '<name>' can already see their released results. Reset to Draft would permanently erase them. Nothing was deleted - confirm it on purpose to go ahead." | 409 `released_results` | models/assessment.py::action_reset_draft |

Generators and resources:

| Rule | Message | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generator must exist | "Generator not found" | 404 | write.py:124, 571, 626, 691, 709, 740, 1035 |
| Unknown question-type codes | "Unknown question type(s): %s" | 422 | write.py:580-581 |
| Generator name required on create | "A name is required" | 422 | write.py:593 |
| Resource filename required | "A file name is required" | 422 | write.py:632 |
| Resource content required | "File content is required" | 422 | write.py:634 |
| Category not in `_RESOURCE_CATEGORIES` | "category must be one of: %s" | 422 | write.py::_RESOURCE_CATEGORIES |
| Content not valid base64 | "content must be base64" | 422 | write.py:646 |
| Decoded file empty | "The file is empty" | 422 | write.py:649 |
| File over 25 MB (`_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`), sized from the base64 length before decoding (round 3, A-224) | "That file is %.1f MB. The limit is %d MB." | 413 `too_large` | write.py::_too_large |
| Resource not on this generator | "Resource not found" | 404 | write.py:696 |
| SOP-spending action with no source (`resource_ids` empty and `source_text` blank) | caller-supplied: "Attach an SOP document before extracting tags" / "...before generating questions" | 409 `no_source` | write.py:125-126, 760, 775 |
| Action method missing on the model | "This deployment of the assessment module does not provide '%s'." | 501 `not_supported` | write.py:133-139 |
| Similarity ranking with no `mapping_json` | "Extract this generator's skills first - ranking compares what was extracted, and nothing has been yet." | 409 `not_extracted` | write.py:1042-1047 |

The SOP readiness test deliberately uses `resource_ids or source_text` rather than the computed `sop_resource_ids`, so a generator whose only document is filed as `reference` or `vendor` is still accepted (write.py:114-120).

Drafts:

| Rule | Message | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft must exist | "Draft not found" | 404 | write.py:355, 855, 992 |
| Draft already decided | "This draft has already been %s; edit the bank question instead." | 409 `already_decided` | write.py:857-859 |
| `options` not a list | "options must be a list of strings" | 422 | write.py::options |
| `_draft_action` guard failed (retry_video only) | "This draft has no failed clips to retry." | 409 `not_applicable` | write.py:357, 1073 |
| Image missing | "Attach an image first" | 400 `no_image` | write.py:996 |
| Image not base64 | "Image is not valid base64" | 400 `bad_image` | write.py:1005 |
| Image over 25 MB, checked before decoding (round 3, A-224) | "That image is %.1f MB. The limit is %d MB." | 413 `too_large` | write.py::_too_large |

**Answer-key validation, draft side** (`answer_key_problem`, write.py::answer_key_problem). A pure predicate returning a sentence, deliberately not an HTTP envelope so it can be unit-tested without a request context; `assessments_be_v2/tests/test_api_invariants.py:397-421` exercises it directly. It runs only when `question_type in ("mcq","msq","image_ab")`; every other type is unvalidated and returns `None`. Rules in order:

1. fewer than 2 options -> `"A %s question needs at least two options"` (write.py:286)
2. no non-blank correct value -> `"Nothing is marked correct, so the question could never be scored"` (write.py:290-291)
3. a correct value that is not one of the options -> `"The correct answer %r is not one of the options"` (write.py:294). This is the rule the docstring calls the important one, because the key is stored as the option's **text** (write.py:277-282).
4. `mcq` with more than one correct -> `"A single-answer question cannot have %d correct options"` (write.py:296-297)

The route wraps whichever sentence comes back as a 422 `invalid` (write.py:891). The check runs on a **merged** view: `options` falls back to the stored `options_json`, `correct_answer` falls back to the stored `correct_answer_json` (write.py:879-887), and `question_type` uses the incoming value if the same request is changing it (write.py::options). `loads_list`/`loads_any` (write.py::loads_any) tolerate empty or malformed JSON columns by returning `[]` / `""`.

Note the draft's answer key is `options_json` + `correct_answer_json`, **not** the `answer_dimension_ids` tree; the long comment at write.py:863-873 says the dimension rows exist on the model (prompt.py::answer_dimension_ids) but are not populated for generated drafts and are not what `draft_detail` serializes. The bank question receives the dimension tree at approval time.

**Answer-key validation, bank side** (`_check_answer_key`, write.py::_check_answer_key). Also runs only for `mcq`/`msq`/`image_ab`:

1. no rows at all -> `"A %s question needs at least one answer axis"` (write.py:312-314)
2. an axis with fewer than 2 options -> `"Axis %r needs at least two options"` (write.py:319-322)
3. an axis with no `is_correct` option -> `"Axis %r has no correct option, so the question could never be scored"` (write.py:324-328)
4. `mcq` axis with more than one correct -> `"A single-answer question cannot have %d correct options"` (write.py:330-332)

All 422 `invalid`. For `image_label`, `image_prompt`, `video_prompt` and `subjective_rubric`, `dimensions` is applied with no answer-key check at all, so `dimensions: []` on a labelling question silently deletes its whole key (subject only to the option-in-use guard below).

**Option deletion rules** (`_sync_dimensions`, write.py::_sync_dimensions and `_refuse_used_options`, write.py::_refuse_used_options). `rows` is treated as the client's complete intended answer key, read-modify-write like a form: a row with an `id` updates, a row without one creates, anything absent is deleted.

- Every axis needs a name (`row["name"]` or `row["label"]`) -> `"Every answer axis needs a name"`, 422 (write.py:182)
- Every option needs text -> `"Every option needs text"`, 422 (write.py:192)
- An axis `id` not on this question -> `"Answer axis %s is not on this question"`, 404 (write.py:209-211)
- Deleting an option a candidate selected -> `"Cannot remove the option %r: a candidate has already selected it, and deleting it would rewrite their submitted answer. Edit its text instead, or retire the whole question."`, 409 `option_in_use` (write.py:244-249). The check is a `sudo()` search on `assessments.be.response.line.selected_option_id` (write.py:239-240). The column really is `ondelete="restrict"` (assessment.py:2347-2351), so the database would refuse anyway; this converts an `IntegrityError` into a sentence.

The guard runs twice: once per surviving dimension for options dropped from it (write.py:212-215), and once over all option lines of dimensions being dropped whole (write.py:225-228). Changing `is_correct` on an already-answered question is explicitly allowed and re-decides those marks (write.py:931-935). A rename re-scores nothing (12 Oct): Odoo marks every answer for re-scoring on ANY command through the question's dimension relation, and on any write of `is_correct`, changed or not, and editors send the whole key with every save. Before, a one-word rename on a question sat 3,700 times mid-exam took about 50 s and Odoo's last serialization retry. So `_sync_dimensions` writes changed dimension and option rows directly (creates and deletes still go through the relation), and `assessments.be.question.dimension.option.write` drops an unchanged `is_correct` (`tests/test_renaming_an_option_rescores_nothing.py`, through `bank_update`).

`protect_answers` is a parameter but `_sync_dimensions` has exactly one caller, `bank_update`, which always passes `True` (write.py:958-960). The `dim_field`/`dim_model` parameterisation exists for a draft path (write.py:156-158) that is never taken. `dim_model` is misnamed: it holds a **field name** (`"name"` for bank, `"label"` for draft), not a model name (write.py:183).

Bank media:

| Rule | Message | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Question must exist | "Question not found" | 404 | write.py:940, 1576, 1603, 1635 |
| No `slot == "single"` image (detect) | "This question has no single-slot image to detect on." | 422 `no_image` | write.py:1580-1582 |
| No `slot == "single"` image (capture) | "This question has no single-slot image to capture into." | 422 `no_image` | write.py:1607-1609 |
| `UserError` from `action_detect_now` / `action_capture_url` / `action_apply_uploaded_video` | the action's own text | 422 `refused` | write.py:1586, 1617, 1660 |
| Video content missing | "content is required" | 422 | write.py:1639 |
| Video content not base64 | "content is not valid base64" | 422 | write.py:1648 |
| Video over 25 MB, checked before decoding (round 3) | "That clip is %.1f MB. The limit is %d MB." | 413 `too_large` | write.py::_too_large |

Tags, invitations, settings:

| Rule | Message | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Merge missing ids | "target_id and source_ids are both required" | 422 | write.py:1175-1177 |
| Merge target or sources not found | "No such tag" | 404 | write.py:1183 |
| Merge target listed as a source | "A tag cannot be merged into itself" | 422 | write.py:1185-1186 |
| Normalize with no generator ids | "generator_ids is required - normalising re-extracts each generator and calls the LLM" | 422 | write.py:1209-1212 |
| Normalize generators not found | "No such generator" | 404 | write.py:1216 |
| Attempt not found | "No such attempt" | 404 | write.py:1240, 1410 |
| Setting value not a number | "%s must be a number" | 422 | write.py:1303 |
| Setting value negative | "%s cannot be negative" | 422 | write.py:1306 |
| `default_pass_threshold` outside 1-100 (Q20) | "default_pass_threshold must be between 1 and 100." | 422 `invalid` | write.py::settings_update |

`settings_update` is the only route in the file that validates the entire payload before writing anything (write.py:1286-1292 explains why: `fail()` returns rather than raises, so a mid-loop refusal used to leave earlier keys committed, with which ones survived depending on dict ordering). Outside the ranged keys (`constants.SETTING_RANGES`, and `default_pass_threshold` 1-100) there is no upper bound on a setting value.

#### Chatter routes

One route, `/api/v1/chatter/<string:kind>/<int:record_id>/post` (write.py:1453). It is the only `require_staff` route in the file; everything else is `require_manager`.

- `kind` must be a key of `CHATTER_MODELS`. Anything else: `"Unknown record kind '%s'. Expected one of: %s."`, 400 `bad_kind` (write.py:1472-1475). A free `model` parameter is deliberately not offered (write.py::model).
- Record must exist -> `"Record not found"`, 404 (write.py:1478).
- `record_read_guard` runs (write.py:1483-1485), because `browse().exists()` enforces no ACL and no `ir.rule`, and an Evaluator's record rule (`etp_assessment_record_rules.xml`) restricts them to their own attempts.
- `hasattr(record, "message_post")` is checked (write.py:1494). `assessments.be.evaluator` does **not** inherit `mail.thread` (assessment.py:859-862; only `assessments.be` at assessment.py:45 and `assessments.be.prompt` at prompt.py:66 do), so `kind="attempt"` always refuses with `"An attempt keeps a history but cannot take new notes. Comment on the assessment instead."`, 422 `not_supported`. The `a`/`an` article is picked from the first letter of `kind` (write.py::kind).
- `body` required -> `"A message needs a body."`, 400 (write.py:1504).
- `post_kind` (not `kind`, which is consumed by the path parameter, see the comment at write.py:1506-1510) must be `"note"` or `"message"` -> otherwise `"post_kind must be 'note' or 'message'."`, 400 (write.py:1512-1514). `note` maps to `mail.mt_note` (internal), `message` to `mail.mt_comment` (notifies followers).
- Messages land on the record's own `mail.thread`, i.e. `mail.message` rows against `assessments.be` or `assessments.be.prompt`, posted with `message_type="comment"`. They are therefore visible in Odoo's own chatter, which is the stated intent (write.py:1522-1524).
- Attachments: `attachments` is a list of `{name, content}` dicts. `data:` prefixes are stripped, non-dict rows and empty `content` rows are skipped, bad base64 -> `"%r is not valid base64."`, 400 `bad_attachment` (write.py::content). **Counted and sized before anything is decoded** (round 3, A-224): more than 10 non-empty files -> `"Attach at most 10 files to one note."`, 422 `too_many`; a file over 25 MB -> 413 `too_large` naming it (write.py::_too_large). They are passed as `attachments=[(filename, bytes)]` to `message_post`, which is the parameter `mail.thread` expects (`src/addons/mail/models/mail_thread.py:2176-2183`).

**Defect in the chatter body handling.** write.py:1520 reads:

```python
safe = html_escape(body).replace("\n", "<br/>")
```

`html_escape` returns a `markupsafe.Markup`, and `Markup.replace` escapes its arguments. The replacement `"<br/>"` becomes `&lt;br/&gt;`, so a multi-line note is stored as `line1&lt;br/&gt;line2` and renders the literal characters `<br/>` to the reader instead of a line break. Verified against the installed markupsafe. The XSS escaping of the operator's own text does work; only the newline conversion is broken. The fix is to wrap the replacement in `Markup`, which `admin.py:19` already imports for other purposes but this file does not.

#### Import routes

One route, `/api/v1/bank/import` (write.py:1095). It delegates rather than reimplementing, so the API cannot create questions the backend would reject (write.py:1102-1105).

- `dry_run: true` is refused up front: `"The module's importer has no dry-run mode. Import into a scratch generator to preview."`, 400 `not_supported` (write.py:1119-1122). Neither importer honours it, so accepting-and-ignoring would silently commit.
- **The file lane** (`content`, alias `file` / `csv`: base64, a `data:` prefix allowed) is the one a client should use. It hands the bytes to the same `assessments.be.bank.import.wizard.run_import` the Odoo back office uses, so both surfaces accept the same three formats and make the same records from the same file. Not base64: 422 `invalid`. Over 25 MB (the wizard's `_MAX_CSV_BYTES`, JSON files included): 413 `too_large`, before decoding. The route passes `confirm_native_restore` to `run_import`, so a native export restores into the live bank here as the file's shape says; in the Odoo dialog only the "Restore into the bank" button sends that flag (4.1).
- **The `payload` lane follows the same detected-format rule since 19.0.3.23.0 (W9, `docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 4 §4.4).** The shape decides, not a flag: `bank_import_wizard.harness_payload` (a list of `{id, instruction, fields, ...}`, or `{questions: [...]}` without the native sentinel) -> `import_bank_harness(harness, generator_id=..., generator_name=...)`, which files review DRAFTS in Pending Approvals; `native_payload` (the `assessments_be_bank` sentinel plus a `questions` list, which only `question._export_native` writes) -> `import_bank_native`, restored straight into the live bank - the one exemption from "drafts first", because a round-trip restores questions already approved here. Anything else is 422 `invalid_json_shape`, naming both shapes and `GET /api/v1/bank/template/json`. `native` is accepted and ignored, and `source_tag` is no longer read. This route never calls `import_bank`, which would put unreviewed JSON straight into the live bank - the old `question_bank`-shaped body that did exactly that is now refused. Pinned by `tests/test_a_json_payload_import_follows_the_file_rule.py`.
- Any exception from an importer is converted to 422 `import_failed` with `str(exc)` passed through verbatim, so the row-specific message survives. **The route rolls back first** (19.0.3.23.0): `fail()` does not raise, so without it the rows made before the failure were committed - in the live bank, for a native restore - while the caller was told nothing was imported. The tag and generator CSV imports (`_run_simple_import`) do the same. Pinned by `tests/test_a_failed_import_leaves_nothing_behind.py`.
- The importers are called under `sudo()`, after `require_manager`.
- **`/assessments/<id>/candidates/import`** (not tabled above) takes the candidate CSV as base64 `content` (alias `file` / `csv`). Over 25 MB (`_MAX_CANDIDATE_CSV_BYTES`) is 413 `too_large` before decoding. It runs `action_import_candidates_csv`, which checks EVERY row (name and email present, `candidate_row_error`) before it creates anything, so one bad row refuses the whole file (round 3, A-222); the route rolls back and answers 400 `invalid` with the importer's row-by-row message ("CSV import completed with errors: Row N: ..."). It used to pass that message as the error code.

#### Export

CSV is the only server-side format. Three builders, all in `assessments_be_v2/services/export.py`, all returning `(filename, bytes)`: `responses_csv` (line 20), `results_csv` (line 61), `candidate_template_csv` (line 80). There is no XLSX, PDF or JSON export path in this file. Bytes ride back base64-encoded under `content`, with `mimetype: "text/csv"`; nothing is persisted server-side (write.py::content).

Size cap: `MAX_EXPORT_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024` (common.py:53), enforced in `_export` (write.py::_export) against the raw CSV length. Over the cap: `"This export is %.1f MB, over the %d MB limit. Export a single candidate, or narrow the assessment."`, 413 `export_too_large`, with `bytes` and `limit` as extra envelope keys. The stated reason is that peak memory is roughly three times the file size (CSV + base64 + the JSON copy).

Gaps:

- `/api/v1/candidates/template` builds its own envelope at write.py:1435-1439 and never calls `_export`, so it is uncapped. In practice the template is two sample rows, so this is harmless today, but it is a divergence.
- The cap is applied only after the whole CSV has been built in memory. The refusal prevents the base64 and JSON copies, not the build itself.
- Outside this file but affecting what these routes return: `responses_csv` builds `ev_by_applicant` keyed by `ev.applicant_id.id` (services/export.py::ev_by_applicant) and then looks up with `app_id = r.evaluator_id.id` (line 52). The keys are applicant ids and the lookups are evaluator ids, so the per-candidate summary rows are dropped except where the two ids coincide. Flagging it here because the whole-assessment export route depends on it.

#### Write paths that mutate without a guard, or can partially apply

1. **`bank_update` partially applies.** `record.write(values)` runs at write.py:955-956, then `_sync_dimensions` at 958. If the dimension sync refuses (`option_in_use` 409, `invalid` 422, or `not_found` 404), the function returns a `fail()` envelope, which does not raise and does not roll back. The scalar edits (title, prompt, difficulty, `active`, ...) are committed while the caller is told the request failed. This is exactly the failure mode `settings_update` documents having fixed (write.py:1286-1292). Ordering the validation before the write, or raising instead of returning, would close it.

2. **`_sync_dimensions` writes an option id it never checks belongs to the question.** The dimension id is verified against `existing` and 404s if foreign (write.py:207-211), but the option ids are not verified against `dim.option_line_ids`: any `id` on an option row becomes `(1, int(oid), ovals)` (write.py::existing). Odoo's one2many `write` handles `Command.UPDATE` as `comodel.browse(command[1]).write(command[2])` with no membership test (`src/odoo/orm/fields_relational.py::browse`). A manager can therefore rewrite the `name`, `is_correct` and `sequence` of an option belonging to a **different** bank question by passing its id inside a valid dimension row. Since scoring reads the live key, that silently re-decides marks on an unrelated question. The candidate answer path does check option ownership (`candidate.py:620-628`); this write path does not.

3. **Dropping a whole dimension checks only its options, not the dimension reference.** `response.line.question_dimension_id` is `required=True, ondelete="restrict"` (assessment.py::selected_option_id), the same restriction as `selected_option_id`, but `_refuse_used_options` only searches `selected_option_id` (write.py:239-240). Both live write paths always set both fields together (candidate.py:625-628, portal.py:961-964), so in practice the option search covers it. A response line with a null `selected_option_id` (the field is not `required`) would slip past the guard and hit a raw `IntegrityError`, which `api_endpoint` turns into a 500 rather than the intended sentence.

4. **`generator_question_types` treats an absent key as "clear everything".** A bare POST with no `codes` produces an empty recordset, empty `missing`, and writes `(6, 0, [])` (write.py:573-583), wiping the generator's allowed question types. `_picked`'s stated invariant is the opposite (write.py:69-75: an absent key must never be treated as a value). Same effect for `codes: []` and `codes: null`. Related: `codes` is iterated directly, so a caller sending the string `"mcq"` iterates its characters and gets `"Unknown question type(s): c, m, q"`, unlike `id_list_arg` which tolerates a comma string (common.py::id_list_arg).

5. **`tag_merge`'s `target_id` is not the surviving tag.** The route names a target, refuses self-merge, and returns `S.tag_row(target)` as if that record survived. `action_merge_tags` picks the survivor itself, by highest `usage_count` with a name tiebreak, and unlinks everything else (`models/tag.py:64-85`). When a source has more usages than the named target, the target is deleted, and `S.tag_row(target)` then reads a deleted record, raising `MissingError` (a `UserError` subclass, `src/odoo/exceptions.py:99`) which `api_endpoint` converts to a 422 `rejected` **after the merge has already been applied**. `{"merged": len(sources)}` also counts the caller's source list rather than the losers the action actually merged.

6. **`assessment_resend_all` reports a count it did not verify.** It returns `len(record.assessment_evaluator_ids)` (write.py:1257), but `action_requeue_invitation` only touches records whose `invite_state != "sent"` (assessment.py::action_requeue_invitation). Every already-sent invite is counted as requeued. `attempt_resend` has the same underlying behaviour with no count: resending to a candidate whose invite is already `sent` is a silent no-op returning 200 with the row unchanged, which contradicts the route's stated purpose of retrying a bounced address (write.py:1232-1235).

7. **RESOLVED (round 3, A-224): `draft_apply_image` has a size limit.** Every upload route now calls `write.py::_too_large`, which sizes the file from its base64 length (`len * 3 // 4`) before decoding and answers 413 `too_large` ("X is N MB. The limit is M MB."): the resource, image, video, chatter-attachment, bank-import file, candidate CSV and tag/generator CSV (`_run_simple_import`) routes, all at 25 MB. The service-account key upload has its own 64K-character ceiling (`_MAX_SETTING_CHARS`, 422 `invalid`), also checked before decoding. `/forms/media` was already sized before decoding.

8. **The "cleared on failure" comment at write.py:985-988 only holds for `UserError`.** `record.write({"upload_image": False})` at write.py:1012 runs, then the exception is re-raised. For a `UserError`/`ValidationError`, `api_endpoint` returns 422 without rolling back, so the clear persists as intended. For any other exception, `api_endpoint` calls `cr.rollback()` (common.py:149), which discards the clear **and** the original staging write, leaving the record at its pre-request state. Different outcome from the one described, though not a worse one. `upload_slot` is never cleared in either case.

9. **`bank_question_apply_video` stages without cleanup.** `upload_video`, `upload_video_filename` and `upload_video_slot` are assigned directly (write.py:1654-1656), each triggering a write. If `action_apply_uploaded_video` raises `UserError`, the route returns 422 (write.py:1659-1660) with no rollback and no clearing, so the rejected clip stays parked on the record and the next press of the button applies it. This is the exact failure `draft_apply_image` was written to avoid, and the two routes disagree. It also writes the base64 string `content` rather than a re-encode of the decoded `raw`, unlike the resource route which re-encodes precisely so stray whitespace cannot reach the field (write.py::raw).

10. **Selection fields are written as free strings, so bad values are 500s rather than 422s.** `question_type` and `difficulty` (DRAFT_FIELDS), `violation_action` and `results_release` (ASSESSMENT_FIELDS), and `slot` on the video route are all typed `"str"` and passed through unchecked. An unknown value raises `ValueError` inside the ORM, which is neither `UserError` nor `AccessError`, so `api_endpoint` returns 500 `server_error`. `_RESOURCE_CATEGORIES` shows the pattern the file uses elsewhere (write.py::_RESOURCE_CATEGORIES: mirror the selection locally so an unknown value is a readable 422); it was not applied to these. `upload_video_slot` in particular is a three-value Selection (`reference`/`output`/`single`, question.py::upload_video_slot) while the route accepts any lowercased string (write.py:1653). Same class of problem for `start_date`/`end_date`, which are `Datetime` on the model (assessment.py::end_date) but typed `"str"` here: a malformed date string is a 500.
11. **`results_release` has exactly one valid value.** The model selection is `[("manual", ...)]` only (assessment.py::results_release), yet the field is writable in both `ASSESSMENT_FIELDS` and `POST_DRAFT_FIELDS`. Any value other than `"manual"` is a 500 per the point above; `"manual"` is a no-op. The field is effectively dead in the API surface.

12. **RESOLVED: the `subjective_threshold` comment now matches the model.** It used to say "0.0-1.0"; it now says the field is on a 0-100 percentage-point scale (default 70.0) and that `0.7` is a 0.7% pass bar every candidate clears, which is what `_check_subjective_threshold` enforces (`"Subjective Pass Threshold must be between 0 and 100"`). The rest of the block comment at write.py:428-434 (that `write()` decides inline-vs-cron recompute) is accurate, matching assessment.py::write.

13. **`/api/v1/generators/<id>/extract_structures` is dead.** `action_extract_structures` exists nowhere in the repository; the only occurrences of the string are the four in write.py itself. The route is permanently a 501. The `getattr` fallback in `_sop_action` (write.py::_sop_action) was written for it and is doing its job, but no build in this tree provides the method.

14. **`draft_update` stores the correct answer unstripped while storing options stripped.** `merged_options` is stripped at write.py::merged_options and stored at 892; `merged_correct` is stored raw at 894. Validation compares stripped values (`wanted` at write.py::wanted), so `correct_answer: ["  Alpha  "]` with option `"Alpha"` passes and then persists `"  Alpha  "` against a stored option of `"Alpha"`. Since the key is matched by text, this produces a question that validates clean and scores nobody correct, which is the precise defect `answer_key_problem` exists to prevent (write.py:277-282).

15. **`_sync_dimensions` casts ids and sequences with bare `int()`.** `int(row.get("sequence") or 10)` (write.py:183), `int(oid)` (200-201), `int(dim_id)` (207, 217-218) and `int(opt.get("sequence") or 10)` (196). A non-numeric value raises `ValueError` -> 500 `server_error`, where every neighbouring input error in the same function is a 422.

16. **`draft_apply_image`, `draft_retry_video` and `draft_rebuild_answer_key` have no state guard.** `draft_update` refuses unless `state == "draft"` (write.py:856-859), but the three action routes will happily operate on an approved or denied draft. Only `retry_video` has a guard, and it is on `video_state`, not `state`.

17. **Read guards are applied inconsistently.** Six routes call `record_read_guard`; twenty-nine do not (see the note under the route table). Every ungated route is `require_manager`, and the shipped record rules give managers `[(1,'=',1)]` on the models involved (`security/etp_assessment_record_rules.xml`), so there is no exploitable gap today. It is a latent one: the guard is what enforces `ir.model.access` and `ir.rule`, and any future rule narrowing manager visibility would be bypassed on those twenty-nine routes.

18. **Untested validation.** `answer_key_problem` was deliberately made a pure predicate so it could be unit-tested, and it is (`assessments_be_v2/tests/test_api_invariants.py:397-421`). `_check_answer_key` and `_sync_dimensions` - which carry the option-deletion rules, the cross-question write in item 2 and the partial-apply in item 1 - have no references anywhere outside write.py.


#### Form Studio's own routes (`forms.py`), and the share-link importer

**Different file, so read the scope line above again:** the eight routes here live in
`assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/forms.py` (683 lines), not `write.py`. They were undocumented
in every earlier edition of this file, which is why they are written out in full.

| Path | Methods | Role | Body params | Effect | Returns | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/v1/forms` | GET+POST | staff | `search`, `limit`, `offset` | `search_count` + `search` on `etp.studio.form`, `title ilike` | `paged([_row(r)])` | forms.py:50-61 |
| `/api/v1/forms/save` | GET+POST | manager | `form` (the whole document) | one upsert on `client_uid`; creates on first save | `_row(rec)` | forms.py:65-106 |
| `/api/v1/forms/delete` | GET+POST | manager | `id` (the `client_uid`) | `unlink()`; deleting what is already gone returns `{deleted: false}` and **200** | `{deleted: bool}` | forms.py:108-123 |
| `/api/v1/forms/publish` | GET+POST | manager | `id` | `rec.publish_to_assessment()` - generator + draft assessment + bank questions. Repeatable; every surface says "Publish" / "Published" (it said "Send" / "Sent" before 19.0.3.23.0) | the publish result, or 422 `unpublishable` with `problems` ("The form is not ready to publish: ...") | forms.py:125-154 |
| `/api/v1/forms/template/json` | GET+POST | manager | - | renders one blank item of every `constants.FORM_ITEM_KINDS` kind - no ORM, no read of any form, so the cost is constant | `{filename, mimetype, content}`, `content` base64 | forms.py:184-216 |
| `/api/v1/forms/media` | GET+POST | manager | `data` (base64), `name`, `content_type` | `_store_form_media` | `{url, key, ...}` | forms.py:161-189 |
| `/api/v1/forms/media/presign` | GET+POST | manager | `name`, `content_type`, `size` | mints an S3 POST policy for `form_studio/<uuid4>/` at the bucket root (`presigned_post(..., under_folder=False)`), pinned to that type and size | `{upload: {url, fields, prefix, expires_at}, key}` | forms.py:263-299 |
| `/api/v1/forms/media/complete` | GET+POST | manager | `key` (the one presign returned) | `head_object` must find it, at most 100 MB, with an allowed `ContentType`; a refused object is deleted | same as `/forms/media`, or 400 `bad_key` / `unsupported_type`, 404 `not_found`, 413 `too_large` | forms.py:301-350 |
| `/api/v1/forms/media/import` | GET+POST | manager | `url` (max 2048) | fetches a share link's bytes and stores them as our own media | `{url, key, imported_bytes, content_type}` | forms.py:264-354 |
| `/api/v1/forms/media/<path:key>` | GET | **public** | - | streams the object back from the resolved bucket | raw bytes | forms.py:587-613 |

`/forms/save` is deliberately one whole-document upsert rather than a per-field PATCH, because
the designer does not edit per field and a PATCH surface would have to be kept in sync with a
client that never produces one (forms.py:2-8). The document is capped at
`MAX_STRUCTURE_BYTES = 512 KB` (`models/studio_form.py:36`), measured on the serialised
`sections` before the write (forms.py::sections).

`/forms/media/<key>` is the one **`auth="public"`** route in this file. It is not a directory
read: the key must start with `form_studio/` and must not contain `..` (forms.py:590), every key
carries a uuid4, and the response is `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable` precisely
because the uuid makes each URL name one immutable object. It resolves its bucket through
`s3_service.storage_target` - the same resolver the upload writes through, and resolving it
independently on each side is exactly how a read once ended up looking in a different bucket
from the write (forms.py:594-597).

**Direct-to-S3 upload, the allow-list, and audio (Week 2).** `/forms/media/presign` then
`/forms/media/complete` let the browser POST the file straight to S3; the key is
`form_studio/<uuid4>/<safe name>.<ext of the type>`, at the bucket root because the proxy and
`object_key_from_url` only read `form_studio/...` there. `complete` accepts only that key shape,
so it can never touch (or delete) an object the base64 route or the importer stored. One
allow-list (`forms.py::UPLOAD_TYPES`, from `MEDIA_MIME`) gates presign, complete AND the base64
`/forms/media` route, which used to take any type: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif,
video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime, audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/mp4, audio/ogg, audio/aac,
audio/flac (`constants.AUDIO_MIME_BY_EXT`); the importer also accepts `audio/*`. Audio rides the
`videoBlock` ("Video") and lands on `question.video` like a clip; the stored
`question.video.media_kind` (`video` / `audio`, from the url or filename extension) reaches the
candidate as `kind` on each `videos[]` entry of `question_media()`.

##### `/api/v1/forms/media/import`: what it does, and why it is shaped this way

An examiner pastes the URL Drive gave them - `https://drive.google.com/file/d/<id>/view`. That
is the **viewer page**: it answers `text/html`, nothing can decode it, and the designer draws a
dead plate. This route fetches the real bytes once and hands back a `/api/v1/forms/media/...`
URL, after which the media is this app's own - the same storage the Upload button uses
(forms.py:269-276).

**Copying rather than rewriting the link is the point.** Drive does serve a direct URL that
renders, but a share link is the wrong dependency for an exam whatever its shape: the owner can
move or unshare the file mid-sitting, Drive rate-limits a cohort all loading the same image, and
a link that works for candidates is public to anyone holding it (forms.py:277-282).

**The host allow-list is the security boundary, and it is checked before any request is made.**
A route that fetches whatever URL a caller names is an SSRF primitive; on EKS it reaches the
instance metadata service and hands back IAM credentials. Two allow-lists do the work, both
anchored on the **whole host** so that `drive.google.com.evil.test` and
`evil.test/?u=drive.google.com` are refused - a substring test on `"drive.google.com"` passes
both:

| Constant | What it holds | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `_DRIVE_URL_PATTERNS` | the two Drive shapes: `/file/d/<id>` and `open`/`uc?...id=<id>`, id `[\w-]{10,}` | forms.py::_DRIVE_URL_PATTERNS |
| `_SHARE_URL_PATTERNS` | `(pattern, query param)` pairs for Dropbox `/s/` and `/scl/` (`dl=1`), `dl.dropboxusercontent.com` (none needed), `1drv.ms` and `onedrive.live.com` (`download=1`), and SharePoint `:i:` / `:v:` shares on any tenant (`download=1`) | forms.py::_SHARE_URL_PATTERNS |
| `_REDIRECT_HOST_SUFFIXES` | the 11 hosts a supported link may **redirect** to | forms.py::_REDIRECT_HOST_SUFFIXES |

`_import_fetch_url` (forms.py::_import_fetch_url) is the single decision: Drive links become
`uc?export=download&id=<id>&confirm=t` (`confirm=t` skips the interstitial Drive shows for
larger files, which would otherwise arrive as HTML and be rejected as "not a media file" - true,
but for the wrong reason and unactionable), and every other supported host gets its download
parameter applied through `_with_param` (forms.py::_with_param). **`_with_param` replaces rather than
appends**, because a Dropbox share link arrives carrying `?dl=0` and appending `&dl=1` leaves the
host free to honour the first one. `None` from `_import_fetch_url` means the route refuses
before making any request: 400 `unsupported_source`, naming the four supported sources and
pointing at Upload (forms.py:300-307).

**Every redirect hop is re-checked, by hand.** `_fetch_share_link` (forms.py::_fetch_share_link) calls
`requests.get(..., allow_redirects=False)` in a loop bounded by `MAX_IMPORT_REDIRECTS = 5`
(forms.py:201 - Drive alone takes two hops). This is not a stylistic choice. Every one of these
hosts answers a share URL with a 302 to a **separate content domain** - Drive's own
`uc?export=download` has always redirected to `*.googleusercontent.com` - so following redirects
automatically meant the allow-listed host chose the final destination, and the allow-list stopped
deciding anything after hop zero. An open redirect on any of them (or a compromised one) handed
this route back the fetch-anything primitive. Per hop, in order:

1. `net_guard.is_safe_url(url)` resolves the name and refuses private, loopback, link-local,
   reserved, multicast and NAT64-wrapped addresses plus the metadata hostnames
   (`services/net_guard.py:118`), so a hop cannot point inward directly or by DNS rebinding.
   Refusal is 400 `unsupported_source`.
2. `requests.get(..., timeout=IMPORT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=20, stream=True, allow_redirects=False)`.
   A `RequestException` is 502 `fetch_failed` with the exception text.
3. A status in `_REDIRECT_STATUSES = {301, 302, 303, 307, 308}` (forms.py:471) is a hop.
   **The status code is tested, not `resp.is_redirect`**: that property is `False` for a 3xx
   carrying no `Location`, which left the empty-`Location` guard below it unreachable and dropped
   such a response through to the success path, where the 302 body then failed the content-type
   gate and the examiner was told their file "is not an image or video" - untrue and
   unactionable. Pinned by
   `tests/test_drive_media_import.py::TestFetchShareLinkFollowsHopsByHand`, whose fake response
   deliberately does not define `is_redirect` so the code cannot regress to reading it.
4. An empty `Location` is 502 `fetch_failed` ("redirected without saying where"). Otherwise the
   hop is `urljoin`-ed (relative `Location`s are normal on these hosts) and checked against
   `_redirect_host_allowed` (forms.py::_redirect_host_allowed), which matches `host == suffix or host.endswith("." + suffix)` - never a substring. A refusal names the host it refused, at 400.
5. A non-`ok` final status is 502 `fetch_failed` ("that host answered N"). Running out of hops is
   502 ("redirected too many times").

**The content type is the permission check.** A file that is not shared answers **200 with a
sign-in page**, not a 403, so the only way to tell "private" from "fine" is that the bytes are
HTML. Anything not `image/*` or `video/*` is 422 `not_media`, naming the type that came back and
saying to check the file is shared as "Anyone with the link" (forms.py:314-327). The same gate
exists on the publish side in `_fetch_media_b64` (`models/studio_form.py::_fetch_media_b64`), because
publish fetches designer URLs too and `resp.ok` alone let a web page be stored as a question's
image with nobody told.

**The size cap is enforced while reading, not from `Content-Length`.** `MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` is set
equal to the Upload button's `MAX_MEDIA_BYTES` (100 MB, forms.py:159, 197) deliberately: a clip
an examiner could upload by hand must not be refused because they pasted its link instead.
Bytes are accumulated in 64 KB chunks with the running total checked each time (forms.py:329-341)
- trusting the header would let a lying `Content-Length` stream unbounded bytes into memory.
Over the cap is 413 `too_large`; zero bytes is 422 `not_media`.

Storage goes through `_store_form_media` (forms.py::_store_form_media), shared with the Upload button rather
than copied, because both must agree on the bucket prefix, the key shape and the storage order:
`studio_form._fetch_s3_object` reads those keys back at publish time, and a second copy that
drifted by one prefix would make publish silently fall back to a link-only image for every
question carrying imported media. The extension comes from `_EXT_BY_CONTENT_TYPE` (forms.py::_EXT_BY_CONTENT_TYPE),
defaulting to `bin`.

Tests: `tests/test_drive_media_import.py` (41 tests, 5 classes) covers `_drive_file_id`,
`_import_fetch_url` per host, every SSRF refusal re-asserted against `_import_fetch_url`,
`_with_param`, `_redirect_host_allowed`, and the hop loop with a fake transport that asserts
`allow_redirects` is `False` and that an off-list hop is **never requested**.
`tests/test_publish_media_classification.py` (17 tests) covers the classifier and the publish-side
content-type gate.

Known gaps in this route, stated rather than fixed:

- **`1drv.com` had to be added to `_REDIRECT_HOST_SUFFIXES` separately.** OneDrive personal
  serves the actual bytes from a *third* domain: `1drv.ms` -> `onedrive.live.com` ->
  `*.files.1drv.com`. That is a different registrable domain, so listing `1drv.ms` does not
  cover it, and without the entry every OneDrive import failed at the last hop. Any future host
  added to `_SHARE_URL_PATTERNS` needs its content domain traced the same way; the pattern
  list and the redirect list are not derivable from one another.
- **The stored filename is always `drive-import.<ext>`** (forms.py:352), including for a Dropbox
  or SharePoint import. Cosmetic - the key carries a uuid4 and nothing reads the name - but the
  word is now wrong for three of the four sources.
- **The empty-body message still says "Google Drive returned an empty file"** (forms.py:344),
  reachable from any of the four hosts.
- **`net_guard`'s DNS answers are cached for 30 seconds** (`_DNS_CACHE_TTL_S`,
  `services/net_guard.py:39`), so the resolve-then-fetch pair is not atomic. A TOCTOU rebind
  inside that window is theoretically possible; the redirect allow-list is what makes it
  uninteresting, since the attacker would have to control a name under one of the 11 hosts.


## 1.6 Candidate and exam routes

Paths below are relative to the `ethara-etp` repo root. The two files in scope are `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/candidate.py` (770 lines, 10 routes) and `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/services/export.py` (87 lines, 0 routes).

### Candidate/exam routes

All 11 routes are declared with `type=API_TYPE`, `csrf=False`, `cors="*"`. `API_TYPE == "json2"` and `API_METHODS == ["GET", "POST"]` (`custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/common.py:36`, `:40`). The json2 dispatcher merges the JSON body with path params into `request.params` and **ignores the query string** (`common.py:19-22`, `:211-213`) - so every parameter listed in the table below must travel in the JSON body, never as `?q=3`.

| Path | Methods | Auth | Params | Effect | Returns | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `/api/v1/me/dashboard` | GET, POST | `user` | none | Same search, then `S.candidate_dashboard(attempts)` | `ok({applicant, kpis})`; both `null` for a non-candidate | `candidate.py:88-107` |
| `/api/v1/me/analytics` | GET, POST | `user` | none | Same search, then `S.candidate_analytics(attempts)` | `ok({applicant, analytics})`; non-candidate gets `applicant:null` and `S.empty_candidate_analytics()` (zeros, never `null`) | `candidate.py:109-138` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/state` | GET, POST | **`public`** | `token` (path); `q` (body, 1-based question index, optional) | Read-mostly gate resolution. **Side effect:** an attempt past its deadline is auto-submitted here (`candidate.py:199`) | `ok({outcome, ..., answers_batch: true, answers_flush_seconds: 60})` where `outcome` is one of the 7 gate constants; shape from `S.exam_state_envelope`. `answers_batch` (`ANSWERS_BATCH_FLAG`, set by `_advertises_batch`) is on every successful reply in every state: this server has `/answers/batch`. `answers_flush_seconds` (set by the same decorator) is the seconds the client waits between batches: setting `assessments_be_v2.answers_flush_seconds`, clamped to 15-300, unset or 0 = 60. `paper_prefetch: true` (`PAPER_PREFETCH_FLAG`, same decorator) only while the setting `assessments_be_v2.paper_prefetch` is on, absent otherwise: the client may fetch `/paper` once and move between questions with no request | `candidate.py:144-208` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/begin` | **POST only** | `user` | `token` | Stamps `started_at` only if unset; flips `state` `pending`→`in_progress`. Idempotent | `ok(<question envelope>)` (the same shape `state` returns for `outcome:"question"`), plus `answers_batch: true`, `answers_flush_seconds` and (setting on) `paper_prefetch: true` as on `/state` | `candidate.py:210-230` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/answer` | **POST only** | `user` | `question_id` (req), `justification`, `selected_option_ids`, `label_answers`, `nav`; or `{question_id, cleared: true, updated_at?, session_key?, nav?}` to empty the answer (see the body-key table) | Creates or updates one `assessments.be.response` and calls `action_submit()` on it; flips attempt to `in_progress` | `ok({saved:true, next:{...}})`, or `ok({saved:true, next:null, review:{...}})` at the end of the paper. Plus `cleared: true` on a clear. Plus `concurrent: true` (absent otherwise) when THIS request stored nothing because a sibling won the question's first INSERT, which under write-behind may hold older content: `saved` stays true for older clients, and a current client re-sends. Inside the 10 s grace after the deadline the answer is stored only when the request carries no `session_key` or the attempt's current one (a request sent under a key the tab has since replaced is not stored: 409 `time_expired`, `answer_saved:false`, the sitting settled) | `candidate.py:232-276` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/answers/batch` | **POST only** | `user` | `answers:[{question_id, selected_option_ids, justification, label_answers, clip_answers? (a transcription), updated_at?}]`, or an item `{question_id, cleared: true, updated_at?}` that empties the answer exactly as `/answer`'s `cleared` (at most 200, `BATCH_MAX_ANSWERS`), `submit` (bool), `force` (bool); send `session_key` too, as on every write, or a replaced tab's batch is not refused | Many answers in one transaction (Week 3, Task 12). Each item goes through `_record_response_values`, the same rules as `/answer`; a refused item never blocks the others, but an item that RAISES rolls the whole batch back (500, or 422 for a UserError). Create-or-update on the (attempt, question) unique index, so a retried batch writes nothing. ONE flush for the batch: a 6-answer batch is 14 writes (an INSERT per answer and per option line, one UPDATE of the answers, one of the attempt). **Ordering (session-scoped):** `updated_at` is the client's ms-since-epoch edit time; the client keeps it monotonic only inside ONE session (one tab's `session_key`), so it is compared only there. Each stored answer keeps the stamp and session of the save on record (`client_updated_at`, a Float because Odoo's Integer is int4, and `client_session_key`). A save is `stale` (acknowledged `{accepted:true, reason:"stale"}`, nothing written, audited `stale`) ONLY when the request carries a `session_key` equal to the stored one AND its `updated_at` is strictly older than the stored stamp. Every other save (no session key, a different session such as a tab takeover or another device, no stamp, an equal or newer stamp) goes through as before and REPLACES both, so another tab's or device's clock never decides. This cannot lock an answer AS LONG AS the client keeps its stamp monotonic for the life of a session key, ACROSS RELOADS (the runner persists a high-water mark for this); a client that breaks the rule (a reload restarting its clock lower under the same key) is recovered by a new session key (a new tab) or by one unstamped save, both of which replace the stamp. A stamp outside 1..1e14 (NaN, negative, 1e300, a 400-digit integer) is read as absent. A held draft over a SUBMITTED answer stores nothing and stamps nothing. `/answer` applies the same rule to its body (`updated_at` plus `session_key`; a stale one answers `saved:true`). The client must send `updated_at` on `/answer` too: an unstamped save replaces the stamp with none, after which an older retried item from that session would win. **Known gap:** two FIRST saves of one question racing each other resolve by insert order (the loser folds in as `concurrent`, `_CONCURRENT_SAVE`), not by stamp. The client batches only when `/state` or `/begin` carried `answers_batch: true` (cross-origin, a server without this route fails the preflight as a transport error, indistinguishable from an overloaded load balancer's 503, so it never guesses from errors). Returns no `next` question and no `evidence_upload`: the snapshot policy refreshes only through `/state`, `/begin` and `/answer`'s `next`. Past the deadline it behaves as `/answer`: items inside the 10 s grace are saved, the attempt is settled, 409 `time_expired` with `answer_saved` and `results`; `answer_saved` is true when an item was accepted OR the batch carried no items (nothing sent means nothing lost: the empty final `submit:true` of a timed-out candidate must not read as a late change), false when every item sent was refused or arrived after the grace. Inside the grace (where `_write_guard` skips the session check) items are stored only when the request carries no `session_key` or the attempt's current one; under any other key each item is `{accepted:false, reason:"session_replaced"}`, nothing is stored, and the sitting is still settled (`_session_is_current`). `submit:true` then runs `/submit` exactly (`_submit_attempt`, `force` included). On a CLOSED paper (not `in_progress`, e.g. marked Done): without `submit` 409 `assessment_closed`; with `submit` the items are skipped and the reply is exactly `/submit`'s on that paper (which has no closed check), plus `results: []`, so an untimed paper can still be handed in | `ok({results:[{question_id, accepted, reason}]})`, `reason` one of `saved`, `cleared` (19.0.3.27.0, `accepted: true`), `concurrent`, `stale`, `unknown_question`, `not_in_paper`, `incomplete_answer`, `held_draft` (prose kept as a draft, not submitted), `missing_question`; with `submit:true` the `/submit` payload plus `results` (409 `incomplete_attempt` carries `results` too, and the answers stay saved) | `candidate.py::exam_answers_batch` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/review` | GET, POST | `user` | `token` | Read-only pre-submit checklist. No marks, no correctness. `answered` and `answered_count` are `_is_answered` (a cleared answer is not answered) | `ok({rows:[{index,question_id,name,answered}], answered_count, total_questions, unanswered:[ids], deadline, server_now})` | `candidate.py:278-315` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/paper` | GET, POST | `user` | `token`; send `session_key` (and the SEB proof) as on `/review` | Whole-paper prefetch (approved 7 Oct, OFF by default). 404 `prefetch_off` unless `assessments_be_v2.paper_prefetch` is on. Guarded exactly as `/review` (`_write_guard`: Candidate group, assigned candidate, not locked, SEB, begun, current session) and read-only: it claims no session. Also 409 `assessment_closed` (paper not `in_progress`) and 409 `time_expired` (past the deadline; a read settles nothing), where `/state` would serve no question. Every question of `_live_order` (the candidate's own, possibly shuffled, order), each built by `S.question_for_candidate` exactly as `/state?q=N` builds it (deep-equal, tested), so no answer key and the Redis question cache serves the whole paper in one pipelined round trip when on (`serializers.paper_content`); each carries `index`, `total` and the saved `answer`. One `paper.fetch` audit line (`count`) replaces the per-question `question.view` lines. Cost on a 10-question paper: 17 SQL statements cache off or cold, 11 warm, against 158 for ten `/state?q=N` moves. The client holds it in memory only, never in IndexedDB, and asks only after `/state` or `/begin` said `paper_prefetch: true` AND `answers_batch: true`; any failure keeps per-question navigation for that sitting. Since moves no longer re-issue the AI-proctoring `evidence_upload`, the client renews it itself: 5 minutes before its `expires_at` (only when it expires before the deadline, so never on a timed paper), one `/paper` (it checks the session and never claims it, so a replaced tab is refused and stands down), adopting the fresh `evidence_upload` and the fresh questions (local edits still win); 404 drops the held paper (unticking the setting is a working rollback: moves ask the server again and bring the policy), 409 ends the sitting through the completion path; retried once a minute on any other failure; never once the sitting is closed or stood down. The client also drops the held paper when the sitting ends (confirmed submit, completion) and whenever the attempt is rebuilt (`loadExamByToken`, the candidate list reload), fetching it again on the next `/state` | `ok({questions:[<question as /state?q=N>], answered_question_ids, total, evidence_upload?})` | `candidate.py::exam_paper` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/submit` | **POST only** | `user` | `force` (bool-ish) | Calls `evaluator._auto_submit_expired(blank_reason=...)`: fills placeholder responses, sets `state="submitted"`, `is_locked=True`, and flips the assessment to `done` when all evaluators are submitted | `ok({submitted:true, already:bool, result:<candidate_result>})`; `already:true` short-circuits with no `result` key | `candidate.py:317-368` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/violation` | **POST only** | `user` | `reason` (str, truncated to 240) | Past the deadline: counts nothing and answers 409 `time_expired` (settling the attempt as `expired` only after the 10 s grace). Otherwise dedups a same-reason burst inside 1.2s, then bumps `violation_count` with raw SQL; under Auto-submit may end the attempt at the cap | `ok({recorded, violation_count, max_violations, violation_action, attempt_ended, violation_limit_breached})` | `candidate.py:370-398` |
| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/review-flag` | **POST only** | `user` | `reason` (str, truncated to 240) | Eye-movement pilot (19.0.3.27.0). Appends `{reason, at}` to the attempt's `review_flags` in one SQL UPDATE; the same reason within 30 s and anything past 50 flags are dropped inside that statement. NEVER counted: `violation_count`, `violation_log`, `is_violated`, the violation limit and auto-submit are untouched. Same write guard as `/violation` (a replaced session is refused); 409 `gaze_review_off` when the paper lacks `rule_gaze_review`, 409 `time_expired` past the deadline. Admin payloads carry `review_flags`; the `flagged_only` filter ignores them. Erase and PII purge clear them with `violation_log`.
