| `/api/v1/exam/<string:token>/answers` | GET, POST | `user` | `token` | Post-release answer review, including the answer key | `ok({assessment:{id,name}, result, rows:[S.released_answer_review_row]})` | `candidate.py:400-437` |

Failure envelopes (`{"ok":false,"error":{"code","message"}}` at a real HTTP status, `common.py:69-83`) emitted by this file:

| code | status | Raised by |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_token` | 404 | `_write_guard` (`candidate.py::_write_guard`), `exam_answers` (`:495`) |
| `wrong_candidate` | 403 | `_write_guard` (`:453`), `exam_answers` (`:495`) |
| `attempt_locked` | 409 | `_write_guard` (`:548`) |
| `assessment_closed` | 409 | `exam_begin` (`:224`), `exam_answer` (`:260`), `exam_answers_batch` without `submit` (with `submit` a closed paper submits as `/submit` does) |
| `time_expired` | 409, plus `answer_saved` (bool) | `exam_answer` - an answer landing within `ANSWER_GRACE_SECONDS` (10) of the deadline is saved BEFORE the deadline is enforced, a later one is not stored; the attempt is settled either way, and the message says whether that last answer was kept. `exam_violation` - past the deadline, always `answer_saved: false`; see Time limits |
| `missing_question` | 400 | `exam_answer` (`:257`) |
| `incomplete_answer` | 422 | `exam_answer` (`:261`) |
| `incomplete_attempt` | 409, plus `unanswered:[ids]` | `exam_submit` (`:408`), `exam_answers_batch` with `submit:true` (plus `results`) |
| `invalid_answers` / `too_many_answers` | 400 / 413 | `exam_answers_batch`: `answers` is not a list / holds more than 200 items |
| `not_released` | 403 | `exam_answers` (`:495`) |
| `forbidden` / `rejected` / `server_error` | 403 / 422 / 500 | `@api_endpoint` catch-all (`common.py::api_endpoint`). Its ERROR line (500) and WARNING line (503 `busy`) carry `evaluator_id=<attempt id>` on every exam route, never the token: `evaluator_from_token` leaves the id on the request (`common.request_evaluator_id`). The pre-dispatch load-shed warning (`load_shed.py`) redacts the token out of the path it logs |

#### The token model

There are **two unrelated tokens** in play, and confusing them is the main trap in this file.

1. **The exam access token** - the `<string:token>` path segment. It is `assessments.be.evaluator.access_token`, a `uuid4` string defaulted per attempt row, indexed, `copy=False` (`custom_addons/etp_assessment_pro/models/assessment.py:899-901`). One token = one candidate's sitting of one assessment. It is resolved by `evaluator_from_token` - a plain `sudo().search([("access_token","=",token)], limit=1)` (`common.py::evaluator_from_token`). It is also the capability for media: question image/video URLs are built as `/assessments_be/exam/qimage|qvideo/<token>/<id>` and served by this addon's own `controllers/exam_media.py`. The invitation email sends the app's FRONT DOOR (`candidate_home_url`), not a token deep link; `candidate_link` is the deep link and always resolves to `<app origin>/exam/<token>` since 19.0.3.19.0 (`models/assessment_api.py::_candidate_link_for`).

2. **The API bearer token** - `api.access_token` from the `api_auth_gateway` module, sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` or an `access-token` / `x-access-token` header. `ir_http._adopt_gateway_token` resolves it to a `res.users` and calls `request.update_env(user=…)` (`custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/models/ir_http.py::_adopt_gateway_token`). This is what satisfies `auth="user"`; it is hooked into both `_auth_method_user` (`ir_http.py::_auth_method_user`) and `_auth_method_public` (`ir_http.py::_auth_method_public`). The public hook exists specifically so `/exam/<token>/state` sees the real user rather than the public user.

So the exam token alone authenticates **nothing**. It only names an attempt. Identity comes from the session cookie or the bearer token.

Auth levels: `/exam/<token>/state` is the only `auth="public"` route in the file (`candidate.py:145`) - deliberately, so an unauthenticated visitor gets `outcome:"login_required"` rather than a 401 they cannot interpret. Every other route is `auth="user"`; an unauthenticated call is rejected by the dispatcher before the controller body runs, and is formatted by `ir_http._handle_error` (`ir_http.py::_handle_error+`), not by `@api_endpoint`.

What stops candidate A reading candidate B's paper, given B's token:

- **Read gate:** `may_view_attempt(evaluator)` (`common.py::may_view_attempt`). It calls `evaluator._candidate_user()`; if that resolves a user, only that exact `res.users.id` passes. If it resolves nothing (an applicant with no portal user at all), an assessment **Manager** passes instead - this is the deliberate preview path.
- **Write gate:** `is_assigned_candidate(evaluator)` (`common.py::is_assigned_candidate`) - same resolution, but no manager fallback. `_write_guard` (`candidate.py::_write_guard`) applies it in a fixed order: unknown token → 404, not-your-attempt → 403, already locked → 409. Every mutating route (`begin`, `answer`, `review`, `submit`, `violation`) calls it. A manager holding a token is therefore read-only, which is what the `preview: true` flag in the state envelope tells the client (`candidate.py:173`).
- **Question scope:** even the assigned candidate can only answer question ids inside their own frozen `question_order` (`candidate.py:646-649`), and only option ids that belong to a dimension of that question (`_selected_option_lines`, `candidate.py::_selected_option_lines`).
- **Identity resolution itself** is `_candidate_user()` (`models/assessment.py::_candidate_user`): `applicant.candidate_user_id` → user matching `applicant.partner_id` → user whose `login` matches `applicant.email_from` case-insensitively, but **only if that user is not internal** (an explicit fix noted as "Security (M-1)" in that method).
- `exam_answers` does **not** use `_write_guard`; it uses `may_view_attempt` plus an explicit `finished and results_released` check (`candidate.py::_write_guard`), so a locked attempt can still be read there.

Gaps worth knowing:

- `resolve_applicant` (`common.py::resolve_applicant`), which backs the three `/me/*` routes, has the *same* `login == email_from` fallback but **without** the non-internal restriction that `_candidate_user` carries. An internal user whose login equals an applicant's `email_from` will resolve to that applicant and see their attempts on `/me/assessments`. This is an inconsistency between the two identity resolvers, not an obvious exploit path, but it is real.
- The exam token is a bare uuid4 in a URL path with no expiry and no rotation on submit. Its confidentiality only matters for media URLs and for the manager preview path, since every state-changing route re-checks the logged-in user.

#### The exam lifecycle over the wire

The client never decides for itself whether the exam is open - `/state` is described in-file as "the ONLY navigation authority for the runner" (`candidate.py:150-151`). The 7 outcomes are constants at `candidate.py:40-46`.

1. **Open link.** The candidate lands on `<app_base>/exam/<token>`. The client calls `POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/state` (body may carry `{"q": <1-based index>}` to jump to a specific question).

2. **Gate.** The response is `data.outcome`, one of:

| `outcome` | Condition | Extra keys |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid` | token resolves to nothing (`:157-159`) | none; no `assessment`/`attempt` block either |
| `login_required` | `request.env.user._is_public()` (`:160-161`) | none |
| `wrong_candidate` | `may_view_attempt` false (`:162-167`) | `expected_candidate` (applicant brief), `current_user` (login) |
| `complete` | `is_locked` or `state == "submitted"` (`:175-181`) | `preview`, `result`, `can_review_answers` |
| `closed` | assessment `state != "in_progress"` (`:182-186`) | `preview`, `reason` |
| `instructions` | no `started_at` yet (`:187-195`) | `preview`, `instructions:{duration_minutes,total_questions,question_limit}` |
| `complete` (expired variant) | `is_time_expired()` - **auto-submits first** (`:196-206`) | `preview`, `expired:true`, `result`, `can_review_answers` |
| `question` | everything else (`:653-654`) | `preview`, `question`, `answered_question_ids`, `progress_percent` |

  Branch order is load-bearing: a submitted attempt reads `complete` even after its assessment closes.

  Every outcome except `invalid`, `login_required`, `wrong_candidate` and `seb_required` also carries the common blocks from `S.exam_state_envelope`: `assessment:{id,name,state,duration_minutes,rules,max_violations,violation_action,pass_threshold}`, `attempt:{id,state,is_locked,started_at,deadline,server_now,submitted_at,total_questions,answered_count,results_released,violation_count,violation_limit_breached,violation_reason,is_violated,auto_submitted,auto_submit_reason}`, and `rules` (the proctoring policy, `S.proctoring_rules`) repeated as a top-level sibling.

3. **Fetch paper.** From `instructions`, the client calls `POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/begin`. That stamps `started_at` (which is what the deadline is computed from) and returns the same `question` envelope. Re-calling never re-stamps (`candidate.py:226-227`).

  The `question` object is built by `S.question_for_candidate` (`serializers.py::question_for_candidate`): `{id, index, total, name, prompt, description, question_type, time_minutes, requires_justification, dimensions:[{id,name,sequence,options:[{id,name}]}], images:[{id,slot,label,url,annotated_url}], videos:[{id,slot,label,url,poster_url,duration_s,has_audio}], label_boxes:[int | {number, box_2d}], answer:{answered, selected_option_ids, justification, label_answers}}`. Option objects deliberately have no `is_correct` key at all (`serializers.py:391-399`).

  Which question you get when no `q` is supplied, or one that does not read as a position in the paper (out of range, `inf`, `nan`, `1e400` - an `OverflowError` was a 500 before 19.0.3.23.0): the first item in the live order that has no submitted response, else item 1 (`candidate.py::_question_payload`; pinned by `tests/test_an_unreadable_question_number_is_ignored.py`). `label_boxes` for `image_label` comes from the image's `detections_json`, falling back to a count derived from the answer key; never labels. When EVERY detected marker carries a `box_2d`, the list is `{number, box_2d}` pairs so the app draws the author's numbered regions itself; with any geometry missing it degrades to plain numbers (`candidate.py::_label_boxes`). The L-2 gate that briefly withheld that geometry for object-mode questions was reverted before 19.0.3.23.0 shipped (owner decision Q1): it left 4 of the 6 prod labelling questions with no markers at all.

4. **Answer.** `POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/answer` per question - see the next subsection for body keys. The response is either `{"saved":true,"next":{<question envelope>}}` or, at the end, `{"saved":true,"next":null,"review":{…}}`. Note the asymmetry: the `review` key exists only in the terminal branch (`candidate.py:271-276`).

  `nav` controls where you land: `"next"` (default), `"prev"`, or `"review"` (`_next_index`, `candidate.py::_next_index`). `nav:"review"` means "save this answer, THEN show the checklist" and is why saving and navigating are one call.

5. **Review.** `POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/review` returns `{rows, answered_count, total_questions, unanswered, deadline}`. `rows[i]` is `{index, question_id, name, answered}` - no marks and no correctness. The docstring at `candidate.py:290-306` records that this route previously used the post-release row builder and thereby leaked the answer key to in-progress candidates; that is fixed, and the builder is now named `released_answer_review_row` so it cannot be picked up generically (`serializers.py:525-536`).

6. **Submit.** `POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/submit`. Refuses with `incomplete_attempt` (409, plus `unanswered:[ids]`) while questions are unanswered, unless time has expired or `force` is truthy. Returns `{submitted, already, result}`. The `result` block reports `awaiting_results` until a human sets `results_released` - submitting releases nothing (`serializers.py:167-197`).

7. **Post-release review.** `POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/answers`, gated on **both** finished and `results_released`. Rows carry `chosen`, `correct` (option names for mcq/msq), `verdict`, and for a scored subjective answer a raw 0-1 grader score (`serializers.py:525-580+`).

#### Answer submission - exact body keys

`POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/answer`. Everything is read from the JSON body via the helpers in `common.py:216-259`.

| Key | Type | Read by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question_id` | int | `int_arg`, `candidate.py::question_id` | Required. Missing/0 → `missing_question` 400. Must be present in the attempt's frozen `question_order`, else the save silently fails into `incomplete_answer` 422 (`:646-649`) |
| `justification` | string | `str_arg`, `candidate.py::justification` | **Truncated** to 8000 chars, never rejected (`_JUSTIFICATION_MAX_LEN`, `candidate.py::_JUSTIFICATION_MAX_LEN`) |
| `selected_option_ids` | list of ints | `id_list_arg`, `candidate.py:617` | Tolerates a bare int or a comma-separated string. Ids not belonging to a dimension of this question are dropped silently; duplicates are deduped (`:609-630`) |
| `label_answers` | JSON **object**, e.g. `{"1":"rotor","2":"stator"}` | `arg` then `_collect_label_answers`, `candidate.py::_collect_label_answers` | Only consulted for `image_label`. Non-dict → ignored entirely. Keys must be digit strings; non-digit keys dropped. Values trimmed to 500 chars; empty values dropped. Serialized to JSON and stored in the shared `justification` column |
| `nav` | `"next"` \| `"prev"` \| `"review"` | `str_arg("nav","next")`, `candidate.py::nav` | Any unrecognised value behaves as `"next"` |
| `cleared` | bool (optional) | `bool_arg`, `candidate.py::_answer_values` | 19.0.3.27.0. `true` empties the answer (`_clear_response`): its option lines, text and label answers are removed, `cleared` is set, the row goes back to `draft` (neither graded nor counted) and its grade is dropped in the same UPDATE (`llm_state` `not_needed`, `llm_raw_100` 0, and the grader's `llm_feedback`, `llm_verdict`, `llm_reasoning`, `llm_deductions_json`, `llm_credit_json`, `label_box_scores_json`, `llm_judge_model` blanked, and a transcription's `clip_answers_json`, `llm_critical_count` and `llm_minor_count` with them); a grade landing later is not stored (`scoring._store_scored` skips a `cleared` row) and settlement zeroes `llm_raw_100` on it again. Any content sent beside it is ignored. Same stale rule and stamp as a save. No row yet: a cleared row is INSERTED (draft, empty, carrying the clear's stamp and session), through the same savepoint and unique-index fold as a first save, so an OLDER first save from the same session landing after it is `stale`; from another session the last write wins. Reply `{saved: true, cleared: true}` (a stale clear answers as a stale save, without `cleared`); audit outcome `cleared`. A later real answer refills the same row (`cleared` back to `False`). Writes: 2 (no row yet, or a text answer), 3 for an answer holding options (their DELETE); a repeated clear writes nothing |
| `updated_at` | number, ms since epoch (optional) | `candidate.py::_answer_values` | The client's edit time, stored as `response.client_updated_at` with the request's `session_key` as `client_session_key`. Older than the stored stamp FROM THE SAME SESSION: nothing is written and the save is reported as stored (`stale` in `/answers/batch`). Any other case saves and replaces both. Outside 1..1e14, a bool or unreadable: read as absent. Same rule on batch items; see the `/answers/batch` row |

Per question type, what must be present for the answer to be accepted (`_record_response`, `candidate.py::_record_response`):

| `question_type` | Required body keys | Behaviour if missing |
|---|---|---|
| `mcq`, `msq`, `image_ab` | `selected_option_ids` (at least one valid id) | `incomplete_answer` 422. `justification` is optional and stored if sent |
| `subjective_rubric`, `video_prompt` | `justification` (non-empty after strip) | `incomplete_answer` 422 |
| `image_prompt` | `justification`; **plus** `selected_option_ids` if the question has dimensions | Missing text → 422 outright. Text present but options missing on a dimensioned question → the text is saved as a **draft** and the call still returns 422 (`gate_incomplete`, `:832-835`, `:699-700`, `:707-710`) |
| `image_label` | `label_answers` (preferred) or `justification`; plus `selected_option_ids` if the question has dimensions | Same as `image_prompt`. If `label_answers` is absent or not a dict, a raw `justification` string is stored instead - which is **not** the JSON shape scoring reads back |
| anything else | none | No validation at all; whatever is sent is stored and submitted |

Precise trap, as the task framing implies: sending label text under `justification` for an `image_label` question stores a plain string where scoring expects a JSON map, and sending `selected_option_ids` as `{"1": 12}` instead of `[12]` yields an empty list (`id_list_arg` returns `[]` for a dict, `common.py:254`) and therefore a 422 on mcq/msq. Sending options as `"12,13"` does work.

Re-answering: an existing response is rewritten in place - old option lines are unlinked and replaced (`_update_response`, `candidate.py::_update_response`). If it was already submitted and it has text (or is `image_ab`), subjective scoring is re-queued; the model dedups on a hash of the text so unchanged text is not re-graded.

Concurrency: `Response.create` runs inside a savepoint and catches `IntegrityError` from the `(evaluator, question)` unique index, re-searching and folding into the winner (`candidate.py:689-698`).

**`require_objective_justification` is GONE as of 25 August.** The 11 August edition recorded it as surfaced in the state envelope but enforced nowhere on the server. It has since been removed from the model, from the write allow-lists and from `exam_state_envelope`; `serializers.py::proctoring_rules` emits eleven keys and none of them is it. A client still sending it has the key dropped silently.

Note also that the API's option key (`selected_option_ids`, one flat list) differs from the upstream portal's wire format (one `dimension_<id>` form field per dimension, `custom_addons/etp_assessment_pro/controllers/portal.py:935-948`). The two front ends do not share a payload shape.

#### Time limits and expiry

- **Where the deadline comes from:** `deadline_datetime` is a **stored compute** on the evaluator: `started_at + timedelta(minutes=assessment.duration_minutes)`, and `False` when `started_at` is unset or `duration_minutes <= 0` (`custom_addons/etp_assessment_pro/models/assessment.py:1774-1783`). A `duration_minutes` of 0 therefore means an **unlimited** sitting: `is_time_expired()` returns `False` whenever `deadline_datetime` is falsy (`assessment.py::deadline_datetime`).
- **Where the clock starts:** `/begin` stamps `started_at` (`candidate.py:226-227`). It is guarded against re-stamping because that would silently grant extra time on every reconnect.
- **Who tells the client:** `attempt.deadline` in every state envelope (`serializers.py:513`), `deadline` in the `/review` payload (`candidate.py:314`), and `deadline` in each `/me/assessments` row (`serializers.py:218`). **Every payload that carries `deadline` also carries `server_now`** (round 3), the server's clock in the same format: `data.attempt.server_now` in the exam envelope (state, begin/resume, the next question after `/answer`), top-level `server_now` on `/review`, and per row in `/me/assessments`. The app counts down on the device clock plus the offset (`Attempt.clockOffset` = `server_now` minus the device clock at parse time; under 2 s is treated as zero, `models.dart::_clockOffset`, because `server_now` is whole seconds with no latency correction), so a device clock that is really off cannot count past the grace window; without `server_now` the offset is zero, the old behaviour. The app reads it from the attempt payloads only, not from `/review`. All timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC with a `Z` suffix (`serializers.py:51-60`); the API never emits local time.
- **Who enforces it:** the server, at four points - `/state` (`candidate.py:196-206`), `/answer` (`:249-253`), `/violation`, and `/submit`'s decision on whether to allow an incomplete paper (`:337`). Enforcement is always the same call, `evaluator.sudo()._auto_submit_expired()`.
- **The grace window** (round 3, MT3-01/MT3-02): `ANSWER_GRACE_SECONDS = 10` (`controllers/api/candidate.py`). An `/answer` within 10 s of the deadline is stored (the runner's last autosave or Next can be in flight at zero); a later one is not stored and gets 409 `time_expired` with `answer_saved: false` ("... your last answer arrived after the deadline and was not saved."); both settle the attempt. A `/violation` past the deadline is never counted and always answers 409 `time_expired`, `answer_saved: false`: within the grace it does NOT settle ("Your time has expired."), so the client can still flush its pending answer and let `/answer` settle - the app awaits `flushAnswers()` on this 409 before it completes; past the grace it settles the attempt as `expired` ("Your time has expired; the attempt was submitted."). So a candidate who leaves fullscreen or the tab after time-up is recorded as ended on the clock, never as a proctoring auto-submit.
- **What settling does:** `_auto_submit_expired` (`assessment.py::_auto_submit_expired`) creates a submitted placeholder response for every unanswered question in `question_order` (or promotes an existing draft), writes `state="submitted", is_locked=True`, and flips the assessment to `done` once every evaluator is submitted. The placeholder text is `blank_reason`, defaulting to `"[Auto-submitted: time expired]"`. `exam_submit` passes `"[Submitted with unanswered questions]"` when a `force`d submit happens with time remaining (`candidate.py:358-360`), and `_record_violation` passes `"[Auto-submitted: proctoring violation (<reason>)]"` (`candidate.py:767-769`), so the audit trail and the CSV export name the real cause.
- **Backstop:** `_cron_expire_stale_attempts` (`assessment.py::_cron_expire_stale_attempts+`) sweeps abandoned attempts, so a candidate who closes the app is settled without a live request.
- **What the candidate is told at time-up (19.0.3.23.0 app, Q12).** The app reads `time_expired` + `answer_saved` on every path that meets the deadline - Next, autosave, the deadline buzzer and submit - and says one thing: "Time's up - your answers are saved." (plus a neutral note when `answer_saved` is false, never a red "not saved": the server still settles and grades a held draft). No time-out is blamed on proctoring any more. My Assessments and My Performance show "Ended on the clock" and the time used out of the limit. Since round 3 the app stops the proctor watch at its own time-up, flushes pending autosaves once there and then sends no more saves, and treats a 409 from `/violation` as ended on the clock (it first awaits `flushAnswers()`, and says "saved" only if every pending save was kept); for `answer_saved: false` it says "Your last change reached us after the deadline, so it may not count." Flutter detail is in Part 3.
- **The placeholders never reach the candidate as an answer.** On the post-release review (`/exam/<token>/answers`) an auto-submitted response shows an empty `justification` and the verdict "Not answered" ("No Grade" only for a subjective one that carries picks or labels but no grade) - before 19.0.3.23.0 a timed-out MCQ read "Incorrect" for a question the candidate never saw, and the placeholder text showed under "Your answer" (`serializers.py::released_answer_review_row`).
- **Not enforced:** `question.time_minutes` is serialized to the client (`serializers.py:473`) but no per-question timer exists on the server.
- **Gap:** `/begin` does not check `is_time_expired()`. An attempt whose deadline has passed but which has not yet been settled is not `is_locked`, so `_write_guard` lets it through and `/begin` hands back a live question envelope. The client only learns the truth on the next `/answer` (409 `time_expired`) or `/state` (`outcome:"complete"`). `/review` likewise does not check expiry (`/violation` does since round 3, above).

#### Proctoring / violations

One route: `POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/violation`, body `{"reason": "<text>"}` (defaults to `"Unknown violation"`, truncated to 240 chars, `candidate.py:385-386`). Behaviour is in `_record_violation` (`candidate.py::_record_violation`):

- **Dedup:** a repeat of the *same* `reason` within 1.2 seconds of the stored `violation_datetime` returns `recorded:false` and does not increment. Two genuinely different reasons back-to-back both count. The rationale given is that one physical action (tab switch while fullscreen) fires several client events, each of which beacons.
- **Counting:** ONE raw SQL statement per violation (`models/assessment.py::_record_violation`) - `UPDATE assessments_be_evaluator SET violation_count = COALESCE(violation_count,0)+1, violation_log = … || entry, is_violated = TRUE, violation_reason, violation_datetime, write_uid, write_date … RETURNING violation_count` - so simultaneous beacons cannot lose an increment or a log entry. Pending ORM values for the row are flushed first and the cache is invalidated after. Until Week 3 (Task 12) the three latest-violation fields followed as a separate ORM write, two UPDATEs of the attempt row per beacon (pinned: `test_one_violation_is_one_update`).
- **The rule (owner's final wording, 25 Sep 2026: "The violation cap must auto-submit at the limit (only for auto-submit but not for log-only) and tell the candidate and admin why. Log only never ends the paper, even at the cap."; A-074 and L-107 are this one flow):** under `violation_action == "auto_submit"` the attempt is settled once the new count reaches `max_violations`; `max_violations` of 0 and of 1 both mean "end on the first violation" - 0 does **not** mean unlimited. Under `"log_only"` the exam is **never** ended, at any cap (the owner's own case, Log only with a cap of 20, is pinned by `test_owners_case_log_only_cap_20_never_ends`): every violation is recorded and listed. **In both modes** a reached limit sets `violation_limit_breached = true`, a non-stored compute on the evaluator (`_compute_violation_limit_breached`): cap > 0 means count >= cap; cap 0 means the first violation under Auto-submit and never under Log only (no limit there). The flag is sent on admin rows (`flags.violation_limit_breached`), the exam envelope (`data.attempt.violation_limit_breached`), the `/violation` reply and `/me/assessments` rows (`proctoring.violation_limit_breached`). The admin sees a red "Violation Limit Breached" label in both modes (Flutter attempt, candidate and response detail; Odoo "Limit Breached" list column on the roster and the attempt list, and a "Violation limit breached" badge on the attempt form). The candidate is told too: under Log only on the exam screen (the exam continues) and on the completion screen; under Auto-submit on the completion screen ("The exam ended there, and the attempt is marked Violation Limit Breached for the organiser."). New papers start at Log only with `max_violations` 5 (model defaults `violation_action='log_only'`, `max_violations=5`; the API create falls back to both when a value is missing, `null` or `""`; both New Assessment forms); existing papers keep their saved values, and the admin can change them. The Odoo field `max_violations` is labelled "Violation Limit" (was "Violations Allowed Before Auto-Submit"). A violation beaconed after the deadline is not counted (Time limits, above).
- **Response:** `{recorded, violation_count, max_violations, violation_action, attempt_ended, violation_limit_breached}`. `attempt_ended` is just `bool(is_locked)` re-read after invalidation (`candidate.py:388-397`).
- The policy the client should enforce locally is delivered as `rules` in every state envelope: `tab_switch`, `copy_paste`, `right_click`, `devtools`, `screenshot`, `fullscreen`, `webcam`, `watermark`, `watermark_label`, `max_violations`, `violation_action`, `violation_count` (`serializers.py:362-389`).
- Violations are advisory for scoring - they can end an attempt but never change a mark (comment at `candidate.py:395-396`).
- Once auto-submit fires, the attempt is locked, so any further beacon from the same client gets `attempt_locked` 409 from `_write_guard`, not a 200.
- **AI proctoring** (`rule_ai_proctor`, "AI proctoring (face and phone detection, camera snapshots)", default off, Week 2): face and phone detection runs in the candidate's browser on the webcam feed, so the rule needs `rule_webcam` (`_check_ai_proctor_needs_webcam` refuses it otherwise). Sent as `rules.ai_proctor`, right after `webcam`. Each AI rule posts an ordinary violation whose `reason` starts `AI: ` (`AI: phone detected`, `AI: no face for 5s`, `AI: more than one face`, `AI: left the frame`), so dedup, the cap and the reason-keyed `violation_tally` treat it like any other.
- **Evidence upload** (`services/evidence.py::upload_policy`): with both rules on and the attempt open, every question served (`/begin`, `/state`, `/answer`'s `next`, all through `_question_payload`) and the `/state` instructions envelope carry `evidence_upload: {url, fields, prefix, expires_at, max_bytes: 400000, content_type: "image/jpeg"}`, a `presigned_post` for `proctoring/<dbname>/<evaluator_id>/` (under `s3_folder`). Expiry: deadline + 30 min once started, else duration + 60 min, floor 60 s. The app posts `<epoch_ms>_<rule>.jpg` there. Omitted when the rule is off, the attempt is locked or submitted, for a manager's preview, or when storage is not configured (`presigned_post` logs the warning; the exam call still answers 200).
- **Evidence route:** `GET /api/v1/attempts/<id>/evidence` (Manager or Admin, `record_read_guard`) lists that prefix (at most 5 pages = 5000 keys, newest 500 kept): `{items: [{key, url (presigned GET, 900 s), at (ISO from the file name, null if unparsable), rule (from the file name, "" unless it matches `[\w-]{1,64}`), size}], count, prefix}, storage}` (`storage` is `"ok"` or `"not_configured"`), newest first by S3 `LastModified` (the name's time is the client's); empty list for an erased attempt (`pii_anonymized`); with no storage target a 200 empty list with `storage: "not_configured"` (never touches boto; not an error, so no 5xx), 502 `s3_failed` on an S3 error. **Erasure:** `_anonymize_pii` (Erase Candidate Data, `/attempts/<id>/erase`, the retention cron) calls `evidence.purge_evidence`, which deletes the whole prefix with `delete_objects` (one call per listed page of up to 1000 keys); S3 errors are logged and never stop the erasure. Tests: `test_an_ai_proctored_exam_gets_an_upload_policy.py`, `test_an_admin_sees_proctoring_evidence.py`.

#### Locked mode: Require Safe Exam Browser (added 2026-09-30, unreleased)

A browser page cannot stop a candidate using the rest of the computer; Safe Exam Browser (SEB, free, Windows/macOS/iPadOS) can. `assessments.be.rule_require_seb` (default off) locks a paper to SEB, enforced on the server. Plan and ceilings: `ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 11.

- **Settings and proof** (`services/seb.py`): `settings(evaluator)` is the one source for both the `.seb` file and the check - start page = the attempt's `candidate_link`, `quitURL` = that + `/quit`, `hashedQuitPassword` = SHA-256 of `seb_quit_password`, camera allowed, one display. `config_key()` is SEB's Config Key (Moodle's port; matches both Moodle test vectors). The app sends `seb_url` (the page URL SEB loaded) and `seb_key` (`SafeExamBrowser.security.configKey`) in every exam call body; `proof_ok` requires `seb_url` to start with the attempt's link and `seb_key == sha256(seb_url + config_key)`. The JS API is used because SEB for macOS never sends the `X-SafeExamBrowser-*` headers and SEB for Windows sends them only to the page's own host.
- **Where it bites** (`candidate.py::_seb_blocks`): `/state` answers the 8th outcome `seb_required` (before `login_required`, with no evaluator blocks, only `seb:{launch_url, download_url, quit_url}`), and `_write_guard` answers 403 `seb_required` for begin/answer/review/submit/violation. Not locked: rule off, a submitted or locked attempt, a paper not `in_progress`, a manager's preview or a wrong signed-in account (their own gates answer). While the rule is on every evaluator envelope carries the `seb` links block.
- **The file:** `GET /api/v1/exam/<token>/seb-config` (`type="http"`, public, the token is the capability) returns the plist as `application/seb`; 404 when the rule is off. `launch_url` is that route with `https` -> `sebs` (`seb.links`, base = `get_base_url()`).
- **Quit password:** random `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx` default, `copy=False`, required while the rule is on (`_check_seb_quit_password`), admin-only (`assessment_detail.seb_quit_password`), never in a candidate payload. Changing it mid-sitting changes the Config Key: candidates inside SEB must relaunch from the link.
- **Not gated:** question media routes (`exam_media.py`).
- Test: `tests/test_a_locked_exam_opens_only_in_seb.py`.

#### `services/export.py`

`services/export.py` is 328 lines and `services/export_api.py` is 125; neither declares a route or a model. Both are now owned by this addon. `export.py` builds an `ir.attachment` and returns an Odoo `ir.actions.act_url` download action, which is what the back-office buttons need; `export_api.py` is the API twin that returns raw bytes instead, and it IMPORTS `export.py`'s column lists and row builders (`RESPONSES_COLUMNS`, `RESULTS_COLUMNS`, `_response_row`, `_summary_row`, `_write_csv`, `results_rows`) rather than restating them. Two implementations of an export would drift, and the export is the artefact people file against an audit. Note `export_api.py`'s own docstring still calls `export.py` "upstream's" - a fork-point word that no longer means another module.

Three public functions, each returning a `(filename, bytes)` tuple:

| Function | Signature | What it builds |
|---|---|---|
| `responses_csv` | `(assessment, evaluator=None)` | Every answer on the assessment, or one candidate's when `evaluator` is passed. Columns = upstream `RESPONSES_COLUMNS` (37 columns, `services/export.py::RESPONSES_COLUMNS`). Filename `<assessment.name>_responses.csv`, or `<assessment.name>_<candidate_name_underscored>_responses.csv` |
| `results_csv` | `(assessment)` | One row per candidate, ranked by `score_percent` desc then name. Columns = upstream `RESULTS_COLUMNS` (30 columns, `services/export.py::RESULTS_COLUMNS`; the four after `Flag Remarks` are the time analysis and the last three the per-candidate roster facts, see "Results CSV" under the manual flag). Filename `<assessment.name>_results.csv` |
| `candidate_template_csv` | `()` | The candidate import template. Columns `["name","email"]` with two sample rows (John Doe / Jane Smith). Filename `candidate_import_template.csv` (`export.py:73-87`) |

Row ordering in `responses_csv` is `(candidate name, question sequence, response id)` (`export.py:34-38`). In the per-candidate mode a single `_summary_row(evaluator)` scorecard row is emitted first, then the answers. In whole-assessment mode a summary row is injected ahead of each candidate's first answer, keyed off `response.evaluator_id` - which is an `hr.applicant`, not an evaluator (`models/assessment.py::applicant`) - matched against `{ev.applicant_id.id: ev}` (`export.py:46-57`). The local names `app_id` / `ev_by_applicant` are correct despite reading confusingly.

**Who calls it:** only `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/write.py`, via four manager-only routes. Nothing in `candidate.py` touches it - a candidate cannot download their own CSV through any route in scope.

| Route | Function called | Guards |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/v1/assessments/<int:assessment_id>/export/responses` | `responses_csv(record)` | `@require_manager` + `record_read_guard` (`write.py:1356-1378`) |
| `/api/v1/assessments/<int:assessment_id>/export/results` | `results_csv(record)` | `@require_manager` + `record_read_guard` (`write.py:1380-1398`) |
| `/api/v1/attempts/<int:evaluator_id>/export/responses` | `responses_csv(record.assessment_id, evaluator=record)` | `@require_manager` + `record_read_guard` (`write.py:1400-1419`) |
| `/api/v1/candidates/template` | `candidate_template_csv()` | `@require_manager` only (`write.py:1421-1438`) |

The bytes are then base64-encoded into `{filename, mimetype:"text/csv", content}` by `write.py:_export` (`write.py:1339-1355`), which refuses anything over `MAX_EXPORT_BYTES` (20 MB) with `export_too_large` 413 - the note there is that base64 plus the JSON copy makes peak memory roughly three times the file size. `candidate_import_template` bypasses `_export` and does its own base64 inline (`write.py:1435-1438`), so it is not size-checked; at two sample rows that does not matter.

Two things to be aware of in `export.py`:

- It imports three **underscore-private** names from upstream (`_response_row`, `_summary_row`, `_write_csv`) at module import time (`export.py::_write_csv`). An upstream rename breaks this module at load, not at call time.
- Filenames interpolate `assessment.name` and the candidate's `partner_name` with no sanitisation beyond replacing spaces in the candidate name (`export.py:28-33`, `:66`). A name containing `/`, a quote or a newline lands verbatim in the JSON `filename` field the client uses to write a file.

#### Things that look wrong, dead, or half-finished

- **`progress_percent` can exceed 100.** `_answered_question_ids` searches all submitted responses for the attempt with no restriction to the live order (`candidate.py::_answered_question_ids`), while the denominator is `len(order)` (`candidate.py:539-540`). If a question is removed from the assessment after being answered, `answered` still counts it. `_review_payload.answered_count` has the identical property (`candidate.py:577-586`). `_unanswered_question_ids` is unaffected because it iterates the live order (`:584-586`).
- **Dead conditional.** `int(100.0 * len(answered) / len(order)) if order else 0` at `candidate.py:539-540` - `_question_payload` already returned at `:507-509` when `order` is empty, so the `if order` branch is unreachable.
- **422 on a successful partial save.** For an `image_prompt`/`image_label` question that also carries dimensions, sending only text persists the text as a draft and still answers `incomplete_answer` 422 (`candidate.py:669-672`, `:699-700`, `:707-710`). The status code says nothing was stored; something was. A client that retries the whole payload is fine; a client that treats 422 as "discard local state" loses nothing either, but the semantics are misleading.
- **`buckets[item["state"]]` is an unguarded dict index** (`candidate.py:81`). Safe today only because `S.attempt_bucket` provably returns one of the five keys (`serializers.py::attempt_bucket`); a sixth bucket added there would 500 this route.
- **`/me/dashboard` and `/me/analytics` disagree on the empty case** by design - the former returns `kpis: null`, the latter returns a zeroed structure (`candidate.py:100` vs `:128-131`). The docstring at `:120-124` explains the divergence, but a client hitting both still needs two shapes.
- **`submit` response shape varies.** The `already: true` branch returns no `result` key (`candidate.py:335`), while the normal branch does (`:361-368`).
- **`_label_boxes`' count fallback runs inside a bare `except Exception`** that logs and returns `[]` (`candidate.py::_label_boxes`). Both helpers are this addon's own now (`services/labelling.py::ideal_labels_count`, `services/scoring.py::_image_label_key`; the old `portal._ideal_labels_count` import went with `portal.py`), but if either moves, label questions still silently render with no per-box inputs rather than failing loudly.
- **`_next_index` on `nav:"prev"` at question 1** returns `max(1, 0) == 1`, i.e. it re-serves the same question rather than signalling "no previous" (`candidate.py:498-499`). Benign, but the client cannot distinguish "went back" from "stayed".
- **The two identity resolvers differ**, as noted above: `_candidate_user` excludes internal users from the login/email fallback, `resolve_applicant` does not (`common.py:286-289` vs `models/assessment.py:889-896`).
- **No longer unknown: the app sends `q`.** `ApiClient.examState(token, q:)` (`ethara-assessment-fe/lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart`) passes the 1-based position so the runner can move between questions without saving; `tests/test_an_unreadable_question_number_is_ignored.py` covers the route's side.
- UNKNOWN: whether `image_ab` is intended to be gradable without a `justification`. It is excluded from `_SUBJECTIVE_TYPES` (`serializers.py::_SUBJECTIVE_TYPES`) so no text is required, yet `_update_response` special-cases it to re-queue subjective scoring on edit (`candidate.py:715-716`), implying it does have a subjective component.


## 1.7 Serialisers: the wire contract

All paths below are relative to `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/`. The file under discussion is `serializers.py` (2,289 lines); route files are `auth.py`, `candidate.py`, `admin.py`, `write.py`, `forms.py`, `task_templates.py`, and shared helpers live in `common.py`. Upstream model paths are given as `models/...` relative to `custom_addons/`.

Every serialiser returns a plain `dict` (one exception, noted). Nothing here writes the HTTP envelope - that is `ok()` / `paged()` / `fail()` in `common.py::fail`, `common.py:86`, `common.py:69`, which wrap the serialiser output as `{"ok": true, "data": <payload>}` (plus `meta` for paged lists).

##### `assessment_row` / `assessment_detail` - what 19.0.3.23.0 changed

- `assessment_row` adds `scoring_scored` (int), `scoring_candidates` (int) and `scoring_finished_at` (iso): the "Scored N/M on <date> IST" line, read off the model's non-stored `scoring_scored_count` / `scoring_candidate_count` / `scoring_finished_at`. Idle (or with no saved tally): the live counts. While a run is going: the tally saved when that run was requested (`scoring_last_*`, written only when a value changes), until the live marks are newer and have caught up with it - so a forced re-grade, which resets marks, does not count backwards. Scored is counted by answers, as the chips are.
- `assessment_row` adds `pass_threshold` (float, Q20): the EFFECTIVE bar, `_effective_pass_threshold()` - the assessment's own pass threshold, or its subjective threshold while that is not set, so never 0 for an assessment made before Q20. `assessment_detail` inherits it. 26 keys in all since `launched_at`.
- `assessment_detail` no longer emits `same_questions_for_all` (retired).
- `/assessments/<id>` no longer appends `candidates` (1.4).
- `assessment_row` (so `assessment_detail` too) adds `launched_at` (iso, W5.1): the stored `assessments.be.launched_at`, stamped by every `action_start` (cleared by Reset to Draft); a launched row without a stamp falls back to `start_date`, a draft sends `null`. Needs the manifest bump + `-u`. Pinned by `tests/test_an_assessment_remembers_when_it_was_launched.py`.

##### `response_row` - `rescore_requested`

`response_row` adds `rescore_requested` (bool, `bool(response.rescore_request_key)`): a re-score is queued for this answer and the mark shown is still the current one until the new grade succeeds. The Flutter answer page shows "Re-score queued" from it (`response_detail_screen.dart`).

| `videos[]` | list | `{id, slot, label, url, poster_url, duration_s:float, has_audio:bool}` |

| `answer.answered` | bool | **computed**: `response.state == "submitted"`; a draft-state saved response reads `false` |
| `answer.selected_option_ids` | list[int] | |
| `answer.justification` | string | forced to `""` for `image_label` when the stored JSON parses (465) |

##### Question cache (Redis, W3 R1, built OFF)

`question_for_candidate` is split in two: `question_content` (name, prompt,
description, section title, type, time, `requires_justification`, dimensions
with options, label boxes, image and video asset ids and kinds: the same for
every candidate) and the per-candidate rest built fresh on every call (`id`,
`index`, `total`, the token's media URLs from `_media_urls`, and `answer`,
always read from Postgres). Only the content goes through
`services/question_cache.py`; the output is byte-identical with the cache on or
off (`tests/test_a_question_is_served_from_the_cache.py`). Only a call that
passes `label_boxes` (`/state`, `/begin`, `/answer` via `_question_payload`)
uses the cache: the boxes are not in the key, so a call without them builds
and never caches.

- **Switch.** Env `REDIS_URL`; if unset, system parameter
  `assessments_be_v2.redis_url` (Settings > Scoring > "Question cache Redis
  URL", and the settings API). Empty = off = the code that ran before: no
  client is created. Production sets the env var; the field is for local and
  stage rigs (`redis://localhost:6379/0`, docker `etp-redis`).
  `GET /api/v1/settings` reports `question_cache: {enabled, source: env |
  setting | "", target: scheme://host:port/db, reachable}`, never the URL
  itself (it can carry a password). `reachable` is a live PING from the
  server that answered (False also while it backs off after an error): the
  check that proves the pods reach Redis after `REDIS_URL` is set. Saving
  `redis_url` through `/api/v1/settings/update` answers `redis_url: true`,
  never the value; the Odoo field is masked (`password="True"`).
- **Client.** redis-py 5 (`src/requirements.txt` `redis>=5,<6`, manifest
  `external_dependencies`): one client per process per URL, 100 ms connect and
  read timeouts, no retries, no pool cap (a prefork worker holds one
  connection; a cap of 4 made a threaded server's 5th concurrent request an
  error and, with the back-off, the cache off). Query options in the URL override
  these (that is how `?ssl_cert_reqs=none` reaches a self-signed TLS server,
  e.g. the DevOps dev Redis); do not put timeouts or pool sizes in it.
- **Key.** `{dbname}:q:{question_id}:{write_date ISO}:{code}`, TTL 24 h.
  `code` is 8 hex of a hash of the files that build the content
  (`_BUILDER_FILES`, `constants.py` included), computed at import, so a
  deploy that changes the content's shape or derivation starts on fresh keys
  instead of serving the old code's content. Content over 256 KB is not
  cached (an empty marker is stored so nobody waits for it). A stored value
  that is not a JSON object holding every key of `serializers.CONTENT_KEYS`
  is a miss, rebuilt and overwritten (a hit missing a key would be a 500 for
  every candidate until the TTL).
- **Invalidation.** None needed: an edit makes a new key. The question's own
  writes move `write_date`; its dimensions, options, images (label boxes
  included) and videos inherit `assessments.be.question.cache.touch`
  (`models/question.py`), which bumps the question's `write_date` on create,
  write and unlink. A write of only bookkeeping (`_cache_quiet_fields`: the
  image's `detection_attempts`, the detect cron's retry counter) does not.
  A candidate's answer does not touch the question.
- **Single flight.** A miss takes `SET {key}:build NX EX 30`; a loser polls
  every 20 ms for up to 200 ms, then builds itself. The holder deletes the
  lock after its fill, and when its build raises.
- **Fallback.** Any Redis error or timeout (or an import or URL error):
  WARNING `question cache: Redis failed, serving from Postgres` at most once a
  minute per process, and that call builds from Postgres. Never a 500. The
  process then leaves Redis alone for `BACKOFF_SECONDS` (10), so a dead,
  black-holed or misconfigured Redis costs one 100 ms timeout per process
  every 10 s, not one per question (measured before the back-off: +100-150 ms
  on every request and +2.2 s per 20-question `/paper`). An unreadable URL is
  logged by exception type only: urllib quotes the URL text, password
  included, in its message.
- **Whole paper.** `/paper` reads every question in ONE pipelined round trip
  (`question_cache.fetch_many` via `serializers.paper_content`), then fills
  what was missing in one more; no single flight there, the launch warm-up
  fills the paper first.
- **Warm.** `action_start` builds every question of the paper inside a
  savepoint and sets them in one pipeline (one round trip); any failure, a
  database error included, is the one warning and the launch goes on. Log
  line `question cache: warmed N question(s)`.
- **Effect, measured** (one `/answer` that returns the next mcq, empty ORM
  cache): 35 SQL statements with the cache off, 35 cold (a miss), 32 warm (a
  hit); 4 writes in all three. A hit still reads the question row (the key
  needs `write_date`) and every per-candidate row.
- **Watch it.** `docker exec etp-redis redis-cli monitor` (local) shows the
  `GET`, `SET ... NX EX 30`, `SET ... EX 86400` and `DEL ...:build` per
  question;
  `redis-cli --scan --pattern '<db>:q:*'` lists what is held.
- **Rollback.** Unset the URL (env var, or empty the setting). Nothing in
  Postgres depends on Redis; deleting the keys is optional.
- **Production rules (12 Oct test campaign).** Redis must sit a few ms from
  the pods: the DevOps dev Redis at about 25 ms from a laptop made every exam
  request about 22 ms slower and cut saturated throughput 25-40%, while a
  TLS Redis on the same machine was neutral. Measured gain: about 7.5% fewer
  SQL statements per sitting (`/begin` 31 to 25, `/answer` 43 to 40,
  `/state` 24 to 18), not faster requests on an idle database. First
  rollout: set `REDIS_URL` only once every pod runs this code (older pods do
  not version a question on an option or media edit). Never point a
  production-derived copy at a shared Redis (real prompts would sit there for
  24 h). Anyone who can write to the Redis can change what candidates see:
  production Redis is private to the backend pods.

Presence, not prose - the list computes quality warnings from what a row carries, and carried neither, so every subjective question showed "No rubric" over a record holding one. Booleans because this is a paged list and the rubric is a whole checklist (1779-1782) |

**`designer_kind`: why one string was the whole of "question type is not rightly mapped".**

`question_type` is a closed set of seven **scoring** primitives, so `dropdown`, `linearScale`,
`rating` and `multipleChoice` all store as `mcq` - correctly, because all four are marked
identically. That makes the type unable to NAME the control, and this row carried no `dimensions`
at all, so the client had nothing else to read: every Form Studio question published from the
designer reported itself as "Objective - MCQ" on an assessment's Selected Questions tab and as
"MCQ" in the generator's question list, whatever the examiner actually drew. Annotation and
prompt-writing looked right only because they happen to own distinct `question_type` codes.

The signal already existed and was already trusted elsewhere:
`assessments.be.question.dimension.input_kind` (`models/question_dimension.py:16`), a `Char`
holding the Form Studio kind the examiner drew for that axis, written by `_sync_dimensions` and
by `studio_form._item_spec` (`models/studio_form.py::_item_spec`), and sent to the candidate by
`question_dimension` (`serializers.py::question_dimension`) since it existed. What was missing was the admin
lane. Three sites now carry it:

| Site | Shape | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `bank_question_row` | one scalar, `designer_kind` | serializers.py::bank_question_row |
| `bank_question_detail` -> `dimensions[]` | `input_kind` per axis | serializers.py::bank_question_detail |
| `draft_dimensions` | `input_kind` per axis, from the row (1378) or from the spec's `kind` (1407) | serializers.py::draft_dimensions |

**A scalar on the row and not the axis tree, deliberately.** The list shape is read by the bank
screen and by Selected Questions, and the bank list clamps at 200 rows; embedding every axis and
every option on every row to recover one string would multiply the payload for a field that is
the same on every axis of a question anyway. It is read off the **first axis that names one** - a
grid stamps its kind on every row and they always agree, and a single-axis question has exactly
one.

**Client side:** `Question.designerKindHint` parses `designer_kind`
(`lib/assessment/domain/models.dart:1580`), and `Question.designerKind` (`:886`) reads the hint
first, then falls back to the axes' `inputKind`, then to null - because a LIST payload has only
the scalar and a DRAFT has only the axes, so both have to be read or the same question would name
its control on one screen and not on another. `taskLabel` (`:914`) is the resolution order the
badges use: the examiner's template name, then the designer kind, then the engine type. The kind
string must match a `FormItemKind` enum name exactly (`lib/assessment/domain/form_models.dart:34`,
15 values); an unmatched string falls through to `type`, so an unknown kind degrades to the old
behaviour rather than throwing. Pinned by
`tests/test_designer_kind_reaches_admin_lists.py` on the server side.

**Empty is normal**, on two kinds of question: one the model wrote freely from an SOP (never drawn
in a designer), and one authored before the field existed. Both fall back to `question_type`.

##### `response_row` / `response_audit` - **re-derived 25 August**

**33 keys (32 re-counted by AST for 19.0.3.23.0, plus `justification_preview` in round 3), and six of them are new with component
scoring.** Emitted unconditionally, in source order (note `label_answers` is first):

`label_answers`, `id`, `assessment_id`, `evaluator_id`, `candidate`, `question_id`,
`question_name`, `question_type`, `tags`, `state` (`draft`/`submitted`), `auto_submitted`,
`answer_summary`, `justification_preview` (string, round 3: the written answer on one line, first
200 characters plus "..." when cut; `""` when there is no text, for a labelling answer's boxes, or
once the attempt is erased - `answer_summary` is built from option picks only), `has_objective`, `needs_llm`, `score` (int), `max_score` (int),
**`final_mark`** (float), **`final_max`** (int), **`mcq_mark`** (float),
**`objective_marks_max`** (int), **`raw_score`** (float), **`raw_max`** (int), `llm_state`,
`llm_error` (string, the grader's error text only when `llm_state` is `error`/`failed`),
`llm_raw_100` (float), `rescore_requested` (bool, new in 19.0.3.23.0), `llm_score` (int),
`llm_max_score` (int), `llm_passed` (bool), `subjective_result` (`pass`/`fail`/`""`),
`integrity_alert` (bool), `create_date` (iso).

Read the marks as PAIRS. `final_mark` over `final_max` is what the question earned over what it
was worth; `mcq_mark` over `objective_marks_max` is the objective half of the same, and
`mcq_mark` is **a COUNT of sub-questions, not a percentage** despite the name; `raw_score` over
`raw_max` is the ungated quality over the LLM-graded components only, and `raw_max` is 0 for a
purely objective question, which is the client's signal to omit the raw entirely rather than
render 0. Section 2.1 #4 has the rule.

Two scoring fields on the model are **NOT emitted here**: `label_fraction` and
`label_box_scores_json`. Neither appears anywhere in `serializers.py`, and the Flutter client
parses neither. The per-box detail is admin-only and reachable only through
`response_audit.grading.result`, the raw judge object.

`justification` is also NOT emitted by `response_row`: `split_label_answers` is called on the
way in and only the `label_answers` half survives. `justification` appears in `response_audit`
alone.

Audit adds, in order: `justification`, `correct_summary` (a rendering of the key), `lines[]` =
`{id, dimension_id, dimension_name, selected_option_id:int|null, selected_option_name:string,
is_correct:bool}`, then:

- `grading` = `{gate, profile, verdict, feedback, reasoning, reference_answer, rubric_source,
  judge_model}` (strings), `attempts` (int), `key_closeness`, `sop_coverage` (float),
  `clarity`, `ai_confidence`, `verdict_consistency` (strings), `deductions[]` / `credit[]`
  (`score_lines`), `golden_claims` (list), `flags` (list), `result` (object).
- `subscores` = `{ab_mcq_pct, ab_final_pct, ab_verdict_pct, ab_justification_pct,
  label_coverage_pct, label_correctness_pct}` - all float, all `or 0.0`. **Every one of these
  six is DISPLAY ONLY and none decides a mark.** `ab_final_pct` is the justification's raw
  alone now that nothing is blended into it; `label_coverage_pct` is a reporting figure since
  an unattempted box scores 0 on its own; `label_correctness_pct` is the ungated mean of the
  box raws, while the mark comes from how many boxes individually cleared the threshold.

`score_lines` row shape: `{reason:string, evidence:string}`, plus `points:int|null` **only when
the source entry has a non-`None` `points`**. The key is conditionally present, so a client must
use a null-safe lookup. Rows with an empty reason AND an empty evidence are dropped.

##### `released_answer_review_row` - the candidate's own marks

The post-release per-answer shape, and **the only serialiser that carries `marks_earned` /
`marks_available`**. Keys in order: `index`, `question_id`, `name`, `prompt`, `question_type`,
`images`, `videos`, `label_boxes`, `chosen`, `correct`, `justification`, `label_answers`,
`verdict`, `kind`, `score_raw`, **`marks_earned`**, **`marks_available`**, `tags`, `feedback`,
`score_verdict`, `deductions`, `credit`.

- `marks_earned` = `round(response.final_mark or 0.0, 2)`, or 0 with no response.
- `marks_available` = `response.final_max`, falling back to `question._component_counts()[0]`
  **when there is no response at all** - so an unopened question still shows what it was worth
  rather than 0, which is the same principle as the paper denominator.
- `feedback`, `score_verdict`, `deductions` and `credit` are each gated on
  `scored_subjective = bool(response and qtype not in ("mcq","msq") and response.llm_state ==
  "scored")`, else `""`/`""`/`[]`/`[]`.
- **`score_verdict` has a second gate (19.0.3.23.0): it is sent only when it was written under
  the grading instructions in force** (`_verdict_is_for_current_instructions`:
  `response.llm_prompt_version == scoring.current_scoring_prompt_version()`, today
  `bundled:785826a5`). Every verdict written before was addressed to an admin and may name
  profiles, caps or point arithmetic; an answer with no recorded version is never current. A
  withheld verdict is `""` (the key is never dropped, and the app shows it only when non-empty).
  The switch is `assessments_be_v2.verdict_requires_current_prompt`: unset = ON; `0`, `false`,
  `no` or `off` shows every verdict again without a deploy - a product decision, never a deploy
  step. If the check itself fails it withholds, logging one WARNING line without a traceback.
  Pinned by `tests/test_a_candidate_reads_only_todays_verdict.py`.
- **An auto-submitted placeholder is not the candidate's answer.** When `response.auto_submitted`,
  `justification` is `""` (the client then says "You did not answer this question.") and, for
  mcq/msq, `verdict` is "Not answered" / `info` ahead of the score comparisons - before
  19.0.3.23.0 a timed-out MCQ scored 0 against its `max_score` and read "Incorrect".
- `correct` is `[]` unless the type is mcq/msq; `score_raw` is `None` unless the subjective
  branch scored.

**The answer-key gate on this function is on the CALLER, not in the function.** It emits the
right option names and a live verdict; the docstring says "CALLER MUST HAVE CHECKED
`results_released`". It was renamed from `answer_review_row` after a pre-submit checklist
picked it up on the generic name.

Note the client side: on `AnswerSheetRow`, `marksEarned` is parsed **only when `released`** and
is null otherwise, while `marksAvailable` is parsed ungated and **defaults to 1, never 0**,
because it is used as a divisor.

|---|---|---|
| `index` | int | passed in |
| `question_id` | int | |
| `name` | string | **computed fallback** `question.name or "Question %s" % index` |
| `prompt` | string | **computed fallback** `prompt or name or ""` |
| `question_type` | string | |
| `chosen[]` | list[string] | option *names* selected |
| `correct[]` | list[string] | option *names* that are correct - **populated only for mcq/msq** (546-549); `[]` otherwise |
| `justification` | string | `""` for an auto-submitted placeholder |
| `verdict` | string | one of `"Not answered"`, `"Correct"`, `"Partly correct (N of M)"`, `"Incorrect"` (mcq/msq) or `"Not answered"`, `"Passed"`, `"Failed"`, `"No Grade"`, `"Awaiting grading"` (subjective). An auto-submitted placeholder reads `"Not answered"` on every type (its justification is blanked first); an auto-submitted subjective answer that still carries picks or labels but no grade reads `"No Grade"` - it is never sent to the grader |
| `kind` | `"info"`\|`"pass"`\|`"partial"`\|`"fail"` | `partial` goes with "Partly correct" |
| `score_raw` | float \| null | 0-1 decimal, 3 dp; null unless the subjective answer is `llm_state == "scored"` |
| `feedback` | string | `""` unless `scored_subjective` |
| `score_verdict` | string | `""` unless `scored_subjective` **and** written under the current grading instructions (the verdict gate, default ON) |
| `deductions[]` | list | `[]` unless `scored_subjective` |
| `credit[]` | list | `[]` unless `scored_subjective` |

##### `exam_state_envelope` (636)

| Key | Type | Presence |
|---|---|---|
| `outcome` | string | always. One of `invalid`, `login_required`, `wrong_candidate`, `closed`, `instructions`, `question`, `complete` (`candidate.py:40-46`) |
| `assessment` | `{id, name, state, duration_minutes, rules, max_violations, violation_action, pass_threshold}` | **only when `evaluator is not None`**. `pass_threshold` is the candidate's stored `evaluator.pass_threshold`, else the assessment's effective pass threshold (Q20). `rules` is the same object emitted as a top-level sibling, and `max_violations` / `violation_action` are hoisted out of it as well, so each appears twice |
| `attempt` | `{id, state, is_locked, started_at, deadline, server_now, submitted_at, total_questions, answered_count, results_released, violation_count, violation_limit_breached, ...}` (the full list is in 1.6) | **only when `evaluator is not None`**. `server_now` (round 3) is the server's clock beside `deadline`, so the runner can count down on server time |
| `rules` | `proctoring_rules` output | **only when `evaluator is not None`** |
| (arbitrary) | any | `extra` is merged verbatim at 521 |

Extras actually injected by callers: `expected_candidate`, `current_user` (`candidate.py::preview`), `preview`, `result`, `can_review_answers`, `reason`, `instructions`, `expired`, `question`, `answered_question_ids`, `progress_percent`.

##### `proctoring_rules` (437)

`tab_switch`, `copy_paste`, `right_click`, `devtools`, `screenshot`, `fullscreen`, `webcam`, `watermark` (all bool), `watermark_label` (string - **computed** by joining the applicant's name and email with two spaces, 368-374, empty when no evaluator or `rule_watermark` is off), `max_violations` (int), `violation_action` (string, `"log_only"` fallback), `violation_count` (int, **0 when called without an evaluator**).

`assessment_detail` calls it with `evaluator=None` (701), so on the admin surface `watermark_label` is always `""` and `violation_count` always `0`.

#### 3. The answer-key safety story

**Structural - the key has no representation in the shape.** No `if` protects these; there is nothing to forget to strip.

| Serialiser | Where | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `question_option` | 392-399 | Returns exactly `{"id", "name"}`. `is_correct` is never read |
| `question_dimension` | 402-409 | Options come only through `question_option` |
| `question_for_candidate` | 446-488 | The returned literal contains no `is_correct`, `grading_json`, `subjective_rubric_json`, `solution_json`, `covers_elements_json`, `official_reasoning` or `correct_answer`. Verified key-by-key against the dict at 466-488 |
| `candidate_result` | 167-196 | Emits marks, verdict, pending counts; no per-question content |
| `attempt`, `candidate_dashboard`, `candidate_analytics` | 199, 239, 285 | No question or option content of any kind |
| `bank_question_row` | 1016-1067 | Carries only *flags about* the key (`has_valid_key`, `has_answer_key`, `warnings.*`), never its content. This matters because `assessment_detail` embeds it (697-700) |
| `exam_state_envelope` | 491-522 | Own keys carry no answer content; but see the caveat below |

**Conditional - the key exists in the shape and its content is decided by an `if`.**

| Serialiser | Key | The condition | What it is NOT gated on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `released_answer_review_row` (525) | `correct` | `qtype in ("mcq","msq")` (546) | **Nothing in this function checks `results_released` or `state`.** The name is documentation, not enforcement |
| `released_answer_review_row` | `verdict`, `kind` | derived from `response.max_score` / `response.score` (551-554), which are stored computes that settle when the answer is saved | same |
| `released_answer_review_row` | `feedback`, `score_verdict`, `deductions`, `credit` | `scored_subjective` = `response and qtype not in ("mcq","msq") and llm_state == "scored"` (569-571); `score_verdict` also needs `_verdict_is_for_current_instructions` | not release state |
| `candidate_result` (167) | all 5 score keys | `bucket in ("completed","closed") and evaluator.results_released` (176) | - |
| `evaluator_admin_row` (706) | `access_token`, `candidate_link` | `with_link` argument, default `False` (769) | - |
| `email_row` (1296) | `body_html` | `include_body` argument, default `False` (1342) | - |

`released_answer_review_row` has exactly one caller: `candidate.py:429`, inside `/api/v1/exam/<token>/answers`, which checks `finished = is_locked or state == "submitted"` **and** `results_released` before building rows (`candidate.py:417-421`). The pre-submit checklist route `/exam/<token>/review` uses `candidate.py:_review_payload` (575-589) instead, which emits `{index, question_id, name, answered}` per row and has no correctness representation. The docstring at 525-540 records that this function was previously reachable from the pre-submit path under a generic name; `assessments_be_v2/tests/test_api_invariants.py` pins it.

**Admin-only shapes that carry the key by design.** All are reachable only through routes decorated `@require_staff` (Evaluator or Manager, `common.py:167`) or `@require_manager` (`common.py:156`):

| Serialiser | The key material | Routes |
|---|---|---|
| `draft_detail` (986) | `answer_key.*` (7 free-text fields), `correct_answer`, `rubric`, `solution`, `official_reasoning` | `/drafts/<id>` (staff), `/drafts/<id>/update`, `/drafts/<id>/apply_image` (manager) |
| `bank_question_detail` (1070) | `dimensions[].options[].is_correct` (1082), `official_reasoning`, `subjective_rubric`, `grading`, `solution`, `images[].annotated_admin_url` (1097) | `/bank/<id>` (staff), `/responses/<e>/<q>` (staff), `/drafts/<id>/approve` and 4 write routes (manager) |
| `response_audit` (1166) | `correct_summary`, `lines[].is_correct` (1185), `grading.reference_answer`, `grading.golden_claims` | `/responses/<e>/<q>` (staff), `/attempts/<id>` (staff) |

No candidate route (`candidate.py`, all `@api_endpoint` only) calls any of these three.

**One caveat that is not a clean structural guarantee** (superseded: since 19.0.3.24.0 `question_media` emits `annotated_url` only when an overlay exists, `annotated_is_worker_safe` allows it and the question's one overlay is the baked picture, `serializers.serves_baked_overlay`; the 2 September text follows). `question_media` (412) emits `annotated_url` for **every** image, unconditionally (429), including defect-annotation questions where the overlay *is* the answer key. The comment at 427-428 states the media route decides whether to serve it. That is true: the exam media route (`controllers/exam_media.py`) computes `annotated = bool(kw.get("annotated")) and media_stream.annotated_is_worker_safe(image.question_id)`, and `controllers/media_stream.py::annotated_is_worker_safe` returns `False` for anything that is not an `image_label` in `ui`/`dense`/`dense_boxes` detection mode or a live-DOM capture. So the URL is safe **only because a second module enforces it, and it degrades silently** - a candidate client requesting `?annotated=1` on a defect question gets a 200 with the plain image, not a 404. The safety here is not in this file.

**A second caveat**: `exam_state_envelope` merges `extra` verbatim (`payload.update(extra)`, 521). Its own keys are safe, but it provides no schema for what a caller injects. Today the only injections are the ones listed above; nothing in the function constrains a future caller from injecting key material.

#### 4. Naming convention

Every emitted key in this file is lowercase `snake_case`. There is no camelCase and no `PascalCase` anywhere. The following are consistent-with-`snake_case` but inconsistent *with each other*, and are the likely source of client-side confusion:

| Break | Where | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `uid` instead of `user_id` | 118 | The same object uses the `_id` suffix for `partner_id` and `applicant_id` (122, 127) |
| Four spellings for "percentage" | throughout | `score_percent` (737), `progress.percent` (216), `pass_rate` / `avg_score` / `best_score` (279, 275, 276 - percentages with no suffix at all), `*_pct` (1210-1215), `llm_raw_100` (1155 - the scale in the name) |
| Three spellings for a duration unit | | `duration_minutes` (218), `video_seconds` (1231), `duration_s` (440, 1113) |
| Three orderings of "raw" | | `raw_result` (739), `score_raw` (586), `llm_raw_score` (backing `score_raw`), `llm_raw_100` (1155) |
| `evaluator_id` means two different records | 1141 vs `models/assessment.py::evaluator_id` | On the wire, `response_row.evaluator_id` is `response.assessment_evaluator_id.id` - the **attempt**. On the model, `response.evaluator_id` is an `hr.applicant` - the **candidate** - and it surfaces on the wire as `candidate` (1143). The same name means opposite things in the API and the DB |
| `id` is not the row's own id | 819-820 | `similarity_row.id` is `pair.target_id.id` (the other generator); the pair's own id is `pair_id` |
| `state` means three unrelated things | 210, 728, 1046 | `attempt.state` = a 5-value candidate bucket; `evaluator_admin_row.state` = the raw 3-value model Selection; `bank_question_row.state` = a hardcoded literal string |
| `result` is polymorphic | 229 vs 740 vs 190 | `attempt.result` is an **object**; `evaluator_admin_row.result` and `candidate_result.result` are **strings** |
| `score_marks` is polymorphic | 264 vs 301 | `candidate_dashboard.breakdown[].score_marks` is a **string** (`"4 / 10"`); `candidate_analytics.per_assessment[].score_marks` is an **int** (earned marks only, with `total_marks` alongside). Same key, two types, two endpoints |

#### 6. Keys a client might expect but does not get

| Missing from | Key a client is likely to look for | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `exam_state_envelope` for `invalid` / `login_required` / `wrong_candidate` | `assessment`, `attempt`, `rules` | The docstring at 493-495 claims "Every outcome carries the same top-level shape so the client ... never has to probe for optional keys". **That is not what the code does**: 498-519 only add those three keys when `evaluator is not None`, and `candidate.py:159,161,163` all pass no evaluator. A client that reads `payload["attempt"]` on an `invalid` outcome raises |
| `attempt` (199) | `assessment_state`, `question_limit`, `attempt_number`, any score percentage | The client cannot explain *why* a bucket is `closed` vs `upcoming` without the assessment state |
| `candidate_result` unreleased shape | `score_marks`, `result`, `verdict`, `subjective_pending` | Deliberate (176-181). A client must branch on `released` before reading any score key, not null-check |
| `question_for_candidate` | `deadline`, `time_remaining`, server clock | Only `exam_state_envelope.attempt.deadline` has it; the runner must keep the envelope around |
| `question_for_candidate` | `sequence`, `marks`/`points` per question | No per-question weight is exposed to the candidate |
| `question_option` (392) | `sequence` | Options arrive pre-sorted (408) but carry no ordering field, so a client that re-sorts or re-keys loses the order. `bank_question_detail` *does* emit option `sequence` (1081) - asymmetric with the candidate shape |
| `assessment_row` (621) | `description`, `subjective_threshold`, `results_release`, `question_ids` (`pass_threshold` IS on the row since Q20) | Only `assessment_detail` has the policy block. `/api/v1/attempts/<id>` used to embed the ROW and so had neither the threshold nor the questions its own per-question grid joins on; it now embeds `assessment_detail` (`admin.py::assessment_detail`) |
| `evaluator_admin_row` without `with_link` | `access_token`, `candidate_link` | Intentional (713-720). A list screen cannot render a copy-link button; it must open the detail route |
| `evaluator_admin_row` | `question_order`, `response_count` | |
| `bank_question_row` / `_detail` | `tags`, `create_date`, `write_date` | Bank rows cannot be filtered by tag client-side |
| `bank_question_detail.images[]` | a candidate-facing `url` | Only `admin_url` / `annotated_admin_url`; the token-scoped URL exists only in `question_media` |
| `resource_row` (908) | download URL, `mimetype`, original filename | `file_size` is present but there is no way to fetch the file through this API |
| `draft_row` / `draft_detail` | `create_date`, `write_date`, `sequence` | The review queue has no client-side recency sort key |
| `response_row` | `question_prompt`, `submitted_at`, `write_date`, `justification`, `label_fraction`, `label_box_scores_json` | Only `create_date`. `justification` is stripped by `split_label_answers` and appears in `response_audit` only; the two labelling fields are not serialised anywhere |
| `response_audit` | `llm_raw_score` (the 0-1 grader score), `objective_score` / `objective_max` | `llm_raw_100` is present on the row; the 0-1 form appears only as `score_raw` in the candidate review row |
| `chatter_row` | `author_id` | Only the display-name string (1258), so a client cannot key or link by author |
| `email_row` | plaintext `body`, `mail_message_id` | `id` is the `mail.mail` id; a client correlating with `/chatter` (which returns `mail.message` ids) has no join key |
| `tag_row` | `active` | |
| `usage_row` | `assessment_id` | Spend can be attributed to a generator or an attempt, never directly to an assessment |
| `leaderboard_row` | applicant email or any contact field | |
| `session_user` | group list, token, expiry | |
| `similarity_row` | `source_id` | The row names its target but not its source generator |
| `candidate_dashboard` | attempts in the `closed` bucket | `completed` filters on `state == "completed"` only (247), so a released attempt bucketed `closed` appears in `/me/assessments` with a score but contributes nothing to `taken` / `scored` / `awaiting`. Reachable because `action_release_results` on the evaluator model has no state filter (`models/assessment.py:1740-1742`); the API release route does filter on `submitted` (`admin.py:243,255`), so this is only reachable from Odoo's own UI |
