#### 7. Things that look wrong, dead, or half-finished

1. **The module docstring's central claim is not true of the codebase.** Lines 4-5 state serialization "lives here and NOWHERE else". At least five route handlers build response shapes inline: `/api/v1/analytics` (`admin.py:1165-1199` - `totals`, `flags`, `by_assessment` rows), `/api/v1/scoring` (`admin.py:1007-1068`), `/api/v1/budget`, `/api/v1/settings`, and `candidate.py:_review_payload` (575-589). `admin.py:_launch_gates` uses `launch_gate` for rows but assembles the gate list itself.

2. **`exam_state_envelope`'s uniform-shape docstring contradicts its code** (see the table above, 493-519).

3. **`released_answer_review_row` carries no internal gate.** Its safety is entirely nominal - the function name and the docstring. A new caller that does not replicate `candidate.py:417-421` reintroduces the exact leak documented at 530-536. The `correct` key would be structurally safe only if the function split into two shapes; it did not.

4. **`iso()` will produce a malformed string for a `Date` field.** `fields.Datetime.to_string` on a date-only value yields `"2026-08-11"` with no space, so the `.replace(" ","T")` is a no-op and the result is `"2026-08-11Z"`. Every field currently passed to `iso()` is a `Datetime` (verified against `models/*.py`), so this is latent, not live.

5. **`_attachment_bytes` (926) issues one `ir.attachment` search per resource under `sudo()`**, inside `resource_row`, inside `generator_detail`'s `tabs.resources` loop (902). A generator with N resources costs N extra queries on every generator detail read - including the 8 `write.py` routes that return `generator_detail`. The bare `except Exception` at 941 will also swallow a genuine DB error as `file_size: 0`.

6. **`assessment_detail` embeds a full `bank_question_row` per selected question** (697-700), and each row does three `len()` calls over o2m fields (1060-1062). An assessment with many questions makes `/api/v1/assessments/<id>` proportionally expensive; there is no lighter question shape.

7. **`bank_question_row.state` is a hardcoded string** (1046). It is correct for bank questions today, but it means the wire shape carries a field that can never disagree with reality and can never be filtered on server-side. The comment (1034-1045) documents the client bug it was added to fix.

8. **`candidate_analytics.per_assessment[].released` is hardcoded `True`** (307) and the comment admits it is always true. It is a shape-stability placeholder, not data.

9. **`candidate_result`'s `"closed"` allowance (176) is nearly unreachable through this API.** Release always filters on `state == "submitted"` (`admin.py:243,255`), and a submitted attempt buckets as `"completed"` on the first branch of `attempt_bucket` (156). The branch only fires for attempts released through Odoo's UI.

10. **Percentages do reach candidates**, despite the framing in the module docstring. `/api/v1/me/dashboard` returns `avg_score`, `best_score`, `pass_rate` and `breakdown[].score_pct` (270-282), and `/api/v1/me/analytics` returns `pass_rate`, `avg_score`, `best_score` (309-317). The invariant that actually holds is narrower and precise: the stored `score_percent` **field** never leaves on a candidate route; the percentages that do leave are recomputed from the marks string by `marks_pair` (253-257). The docstring at 239-246 and 288-292 says so, but the shorter claim at 11-12 reads as broader than the code.

11. **`chatter_row` always emits raw `body_html`** (1262), while `email_row` makes it opt-in and manager-only (1342, with the rationale at 1305-1309). The chatter route closes the same leak a different way - by filtering `message_type` to `["comment","notification"]` (`admin.py:1400-1404`) - so invitation bodies never reach `chatter_row`. The two mechanisms are inconsistent, and `chatter_row` itself has no defence if a caller passes it an `email_outgoing` message.

12. **`_PORTAL_LINK_RE` masks only `failure_reason`** (1319). If a token ever appears in `subject` or in an opted-in `body_html`, neither is masked.

13. **`generator_detail`'s four `getattr` reads (873-878)** encode a hard dependency on optional upstream fields. Two default to `""`/`0`, but `structure_extract_state` defaults to `""` in the `getattr` and is then `or "idle"` - so a missing field reads as `"idle"`, indistinguishable from a present field that is genuinely idle.

14. **`score_lines` emits `points` conditionally** (606-611), so consumers of `deductions` / `credit` see a key that is sometimes absent, sometimes `int`, sometimes `null`.

15. **UNKNOWN: whether any client actually consumes `attempt.token`.** The key is emitted on `/api/v1/me/assessments` (207) and is the candidate's own credential, which is defensible, but I could not determine from this repository whether the Flutter client needs it or whether it could be dropped. The frontend lives in a separate repository (`/Users/cj/Developer/ethara/ethara-assessment-fe`), which was not in scope for this section.

16. **UNKNOWN: the exact JSON types inside `generator_detail.tabs.*`, `draft_detail`'s `loads()` keys, and `response_audit.grading.{golden_claims,flags,result}`.** These are `Text` columns parsed at read time; the fallback determines the type only on empty or unparseable input. Nothing in this file or the models constrains the stored shape, so a client cannot rely on `rubric` being an object or `skills` being a list.


## 1.8 Backend tests and tooling

#### The test module

#### `contract_audit.py` in detail

Purpose (`tools/contract_audit.py:1-21`): three shipped bugs of this class - `person_ids`/`applicant_ids`, `dry_run`/`confirm`, `option_ids`/`selected_option_ids` - none of which raised an error, because an unread key is silence, not a 400.

**Server side (Python, via `ast`, not regex).** `FileIndex` (line 76) parses every `*.py` under `controllers/api/` and walks it twice:

1. Pass one collects module- and class-level constants: any `Name = <dict/set/list/tuple of string literals>` becomes `consts[NAME] = {keys}` (lines 91-97, `_string_keys` at 65). Two passes exist so an allow-list defined below the handler that uses it still resolves.
2. Pass two indexes every `FunctionDef` (`_index_function`, line 122). For each function it records:
   - **reads** from three patterns: any reference to a known constant by `NAME` or `self.NAME` (`_const_keys`, 102) - this is how `_picked(ASSESSMENT_FIELDS)` at `controllers/api/write.py::_picked` is resolved; a call to one of `arg, str_arg, int_arg, bool_arg, float_arg, id_list_arg` with a string literal first argument (`READERS`, line 38); and `X.get("literal")` where `X` is one of `kw, kwargs, params, payload, vals, body` or a call to one of those names, so `body().get("x")` counts (`_is_payload_get`, 110, `PAYLOAD_NAMES`, 82).
   - **calls**: every other call, keyed by `func.id` for a bare name or `func.attr` for `self._helper(...)`.
   - **routes**: decorators whose `func.attr == "route"`, taking string constants from the decorator args, including a list of paths (lines 147-156).
3. `resolve(fn)` (158) unions a function's own reads with the reads of every same-file function it calls, recursively, with a `seen` set for cycles. This is what catches `/exam/<t>/answer`, whose `justification`, `label_answers` and `selected_option_ids` are read inside `_record_response` / `_collect_label_answers` / `_selected_option_lines`, not in the handler.

The docstring (lines 49-63) states the previous regex version produced 9 false findings out of 12, which is why the shell wrapper had degenerated into grepping for five hardcoded names.

**Client side (Dart, via regex).** `tools/contract_audit.py:209` matches `_call('<path>', <String, dynamic>{...})` with `re.S`, then pulls keys with `re.findall(r"'([a-z_0-9]+)'\s*:", body)`. The `,?` before the closing paren is load-bearing: `dart format` emits a trailing comma on multi-line calls, and without tolerating it the optional group could not close, so `(.*?)` backtracked across the newline into the *next* method's map and attributed its keys to the wrong path - a confident, wrong FAIL. Because keys are found by a regex over the map body, only lowercase-alphanumeric-underscore literal keys are seen; a computed or interpolated key is invisible. UNKNOWN: whether the client has any such call sites.

**Path normalisation** (`route_key`, line 41): strips the query string, replaces `<...>` (Odoo converters) and `$var` / `${var}` (Dart interpolation) with `*`, strips a trailing slash. So `/api/v1/assessments/<int:assessment_id>/launch` and `/api/v1/assessments/${id}/launch` compare equal.

**Exclusions.** `UNIVERSAL = {limit, offset, db, context, search, order}` (line 35) is added to every route's read set. Paths declared by `api_auth_gateway/controllers/*.py` are collected as `foreign` and skipped entirely (lines 182-194) - their *paths* are known so they do not report as "no matching route", but their keys are not audited.

**Exit contract as written**: 0 = clean; 1 = at least one route receives keys nothing reads (with a per-route printout of sent-but-ignored vs actually-read); 2 = either side could not be read. A path the client calls that no route declares prints `?  <path>  (no matching route found)` and does **not** fail (lines 220-224).

**Defect - the exit-2 contract is not implemented.** All three "exit 2" sites use `sys.exit(f"2: …")` (lines 172, 174, 197). Python's `sys.exit` with a non-integer prints the string to stderr and exits **1**. Verified: `ETP_FE_CLIENT=/tmp/does-not-exist.dart python3 tools/contract_audit.py` prints `2: no Dart client at …` and returns `EXIT=1`. Consequently `verify.sh:97-102` never reaches its `2) skp` branch and reports `FAIL the client sends keys no route reads` whenever the Dart checkout is simply missing - which is exactly the "silently wrong" failure the script's own docstring was written to prevent.

#### `e2e_pipeline.py` steps, in order

Preamble: `_env.require_local_or_explicit()` (line 21), admin token minted at line 74, marker `PROBE = "ZZPIPE"`. Every step goes through `step(n, name, ok, detail)` (57), which appends to `FAILURES`; the script exits `1 if FAILURES else 0` (363).

| Step | Where | Call | Asserted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 93 | `POST /api/v1/generators/create` | a generator id came back; hard `sys.exit(1)` if not |
| 2 | 104 | `POST /api/v1/generators/{id}/resources` with base64 SOP text, `category: "sop"` | `ok is not False`. The SOP must be an attached resource - `source_text` alone does not satisfy `/generate` |
| 3 | 114 | `POST /api/v1/generators/{id}/generate` (timeout 600) | `ok is not False`. Generation is queued, not inline: returning immediately is success |
| 4 | 121-135 | Poll `/generators/{id}` and `/drafts` every 10 s, up to 60 times (~10 min) | at least one draft appeared; hard exit 1 otherwise. Breaks early if `sop_gen_state` is `failed`/`error` |
| 5 | 141 | `POST /drafts/{id}/approve` with `acknowledge_warnings: true` for each draft | at least one approval succeeded |
| 6 | 150 | `POST /api/v1/bank` | at least one bank row matches this generator (via `generator.id`, guarded against a null `generator`) or the `ZZPIPE` marker |
| 7 | 164 | `POST /assessments/create` (`question_limit` clamped to 1..3, `duration_minutes: 30`, `subjective_threshold: 60.0`) | an id came back; hard exit 1 otherwise |
| 8 | 178 | `POST /assessments/{id}/assign` with `candidates: [{name, email}]` | `ok is not False` |
| 9 | 189 | `GET/POST /assessments/{id}` | the roster is non-empty |
| 10 | 197 | `POST /assessments/{id}/launch` twice: bare (dry run) then `{"confirm": true}` | `data.launched` is truthy. `confirm` is the real flag; a dry run is the default (`controllers/api/admin.py::launched`) |
| 11 | 205 | `POST /assessments/{id}/candidates`, then `/attempts/{id}` per row | an attempt exists and an `access_token` was obtained. List rows deliberately omit the token (`serializers.py:706-771`); the detail route adds it for a Manager |
| 12 | 234 | Candidate signs in (`_tok(CANDIDATE_LOGIN, CANDIDATE_PASSWORD)`), `POST /exam/{t}/state` | `ok is not False`. Every call from here down runs as the candidate |
| 13 | 237 | `POST /exam/{t}/begin` | `ok is not False` and a question came back. `begin` resumes at the current position, not question 1 |
| 14 | 279-312 | Answer loop, then a sweep loop, then `POST /api/v1/responses` with `evaluator_id` | `answered >= total_q`, counted from the **server's** response rows, not a local tally |
| 15 | 314 | `POST /exam/{t}/submit` | `ok is not False`, **or** the error message contains "already submitted" - answering the last item auto-submits, so that is the success path |
| 16 | 324-334 | Poll `/attempts/{id}` every 10 s, up to 30 times (5 min) | `result` reached `pass` or `fail` |
| 17 | 340 | `POST /assessments/{id}/release` with `evaluator_ids: [id]` | `ok is not False`. There is no `/attempts/<id>/release` route; that 404s into the website HTML handler |
| 18 | 345 | `POST /api/v1/analytics` | `totals.assigned > 0` (`controllers/api/admin.py:1176`) |
| 19 | 352 | `POST /api/v1/chatter/assessment/{id}` | `ok is not False`. `assessment` is a valid kind (`admin.py::assessment`) |

Two things about step 14 worth knowing. The main loop (282-290) terminates after **one** answer: `answer_one` returns `data["next"]`, and `/exam/<t>/answer` sets `next` to a full `_question_payload` **envelope** (`controllers/api/candidate.py:273-276`, `serializers.py:491`), which has no top-level `id` - so `current.get("id")` is `None` on the second iteration and the `while` exits. The sweep loop underneath (296-304) is what actually answers the rest, by re-calling `/begin` (which resumes at the first unanswered item) up to `total_q` times. The step still passes because the count comes from `/api/v1/responses`.

#### `e2e_exam.py` - does it assert, and do its keys match the route?

**It asserts, but only in some places.** It has a `die()` helper (line 93) that prints and `sys.exit(1)`. Steps that assert: 1 create (138), 2 assign (148), 3 launch preflight + gates + confirm (159, 164, 169), token presence (189), begin (215), answering (269-271 - "only N of M answers were accepted"), 5 submit (276), 6 scoring queue (284) and settle-within-420 s (303) and not-in-error (305), 7 release (312) and per-candidate `results_released` (322), 8 candidate read-back `res["released"]` (336). Steps 6-8 used to print without asserting; the comments at 267-268, 320-321 and 333-335 record that being fixed. The remaining print-only lines are diagnostics (`llm_state=… result=… score=…`, `RESULT … marks=…`).

**Payload keys, checked directly against `controllers/api/candidate.py`:**

| What `e2e_exam.py` sends/reads | Where | What the route actually does | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `selected_option_ids` for `mcq`/`msq`/`image_ab` | 246 | `_selected_option_lines` reads `id_list_arg("selected_option_ids")` (`candidate.py:616`) | **Match.** The in-code comment cites `candidate.py:616` and it is still correct |
| `justification` for everything else | 252 | `str_arg("justification", max_len=…)` (`candidate.py::justification`) | **Match** |
| `label_%d` fields (`label_1`, `label_2`, …) for `image_label` | | `_collect_label_answers()` reads **`label_answers`**, and requires it to be a `dict` (`candidate.py:596-598`); anything else yields `{}` | **MISMATCH.** `label_1…n` is never read. With no `justification` either, `_record_response` hits `if subjective and not justification: return False` (`candidate.py:660`) and the route answers 422 `incomplete_answer` (`candidate.py:261`). Any `image_label*` question in the bank makes this harness `die("answering")` |
| `item.get("label_slots")` to size the label loop | 248 | The serializer emits **`label_boxes`**, not `label_slots` (`serializers.py:481`) | **MISMATCH.** Always falls back to the hardcoded `or 3` |
| `{"force": True}` on submit | 274 | `bool_arg("force")` (`candidate.py:343`) | **Match** |
| `state.get("question_order")` to get the list of question ids | 218 | `exam_state_envelope` emits `outcome`, `assessment`, `attempt`, `rules` plus gate extras (`serializers.py:491-522`); `question_order` appears nowhere in `controllers/api/` output - only as a stored column read server-side (`candidate.py:422, 466, 646`) | **MISMATCH, and it is the load-bearing one.** `order` is always `[]`, so the answer loop body never runs, `answered` stays 0, and the guard `if answered < len(order)` is `0 < 0` - false. The harness prints `answered 0/0`, does not die, and submits an empty paper |
| `/exam/<t>/state?question_id=<qid>` as a query string | 224 | `body()` is `request.params` and `json2` reads only the body, never the query string (`common.py:37-39, 211-213`); the state route's only positional selector is `arg("q")`, a 1-based **index** (`candidate.py:208`) | **MISMATCH.** Both the query-string transport and the key name are wrong; the route serves the resume position regardless |
| `ev.get("llm_state")` when waiting for the grader | 296, 300 | `evaluator_admin_row` puts it at `subjective.state`, not top level (`serializers.py::state`) | **MISMATCH.** The `in ("scored","error","not_needed")` break can never fire, so the `while` runs to its 420 s deadline and the `else:` clause calls `die("grading did not settle within 420s")` (`e2e_exam.py::die`) |
| `ev.get("score_marks_display")` / `ev.get("score")` | 298, 318 | The row key is `score_marks` (`serializers.py:736`) | Mismatch, print-only |
| `ev.get("applicant_name")`, `cand.get("email")` | 187, 195 | The row nests these under `candidate` (`serializers.py:726`, `applicant_brief` at `serializers.py::applicant_brief`) | Mismatch. `email` falls back to `_env.CANDIDATE_LOGIN`, so it degrades safely; `applicant_name` prints `None` |
| `cand.get("access_token")`, else `/attempts/{id}` detail | 180-184 | List rows omit the token; the detail route adds it for a Manager (`serializers.py:769-771`, `admin.py:895-897`) | **Match** - the fallback is the correct path |
| `state.get("deadline")` | 219-220 | Lives at `attempt.deadline` (`serializers.py:513`) | Mismatch, print-only |
| `/api/v1/scoring/queue` with `assessment_id` | 281 | `int_arg("assessment_id")` (`admin.py::assessment_id`) | **Match** |
| `/assessments/{id}/release` with no body | 309 | An absent `evaluator_ids` releases the whole submitted cohort (`admin.py::assessment_release`); `[]` or `null` would be 422 `invalid` | **Match** - and that is deliberate here |
| `code == "attempt_locked"` on a re-run | 205 | UNKNOWN: I did not locate the `_write_guard` error code; not read in this pass | **UNKNOWN** |

Net: `e2e_exam.py` in its current form cannot complete. On a bank with no `image_label` questions it will answer nothing (empty `question_order`), submit an empty paper, and then die at step 6 after 420 s of polling a key that the response does not contain. `e2e_pipeline.py` does not share these bugs - it reads `question` objects out of `/begin` and `/answer` and counts via `/api/v1/responses`.

#### Things that look wrong, dead, or contradictory

1. **`contract_audit.py`'s exit-2 contract does not work** (verified: exit code 1). Documented above; it inverts `verify.sh`'s SKIP into a FAIL. This is the highest-impact defect in the tooling.
2. **`e2e_exam.py` reads `question_order` from `/exam/<t>/state`, which never returns it** - the answer loop is dead code and the harness submits an empty paper without complaining. Its own comment block at lines 267-271 says the assert exists so a harness "can[not] record zero answers and still exit 0"; the assert is `0 < 0` and does not fire.
3. **`e2e_exam.py`'s scoring wait can never break** - it polls `llm_state` at the top level of a row that nests it under `subjective.state`, so it always falls through to `die("grading did not settle within 420s")`.
4. **`e2e_exam.py` sends `label_1..n` where the route reads a `label_answers` dict**, and reads `label_slots` where the serializer emits `label_boxes`. Exactly the class of bug the whole tooling directory exists to catch, in the harness itself.
5. **`e2e_exam.py` sends its question selector as a query string** (`?question_id=`), which `json2` never reads (`common.py:37-39`).
6. **`tools/e2e_loop.py` does not exist**, but `e2e_exam.py:107` tells the operator to "run e2e_loop.py first", and the module docstring calls itself "Part 2".
7. **`e2e_pipeline.py:10` points at `tool/pipeline_cleanup.py`**; the file is `tools/e2e_cleanup.py`.
8. **Hardcoded paths to a checkout that is not here.** `e2e_exam.py:56, 75` and `check_no_real_key.py:70` reference `/Users/cj/Developer/ops-ethara-backend`, which does not exist on this machine (`ops-ethara-frontend` does). `check_no_real_key.py` with no argv therefore scans one real repo and one missing one - `pathlib.rglob` on a missing directory yields nothing rather than raising, so it reports `CHECKED 2 repo(s) … leaks 0` while having scanned one.
9. **Database-name contradiction.** `_env.py:26-30` states plainly that `ethara_ops` is the *deleted* private checkout's database and that `etp_assessment_pro` cannot load there against this repo's manifest - yet `e2e_exam.py:57, 76`, `vertex_setup.py:5`, `vertex_probe.py:4` and `vertex_media_probe.py:4` all still instruct `-d ethara_ops`.
10. **RESOLVED since 11 August.** The `vertex_*` tools used to import `odoo.addons.etp_assessment_pro.services.{vertex,secret_store}` from a directory inside `assessments_be_v2`. They now import this addon's own services and write this addon's own `assessments_be_v2.*` keys, so the file location and the dependency direction finally agree. `tools/` gained four scripts in this cycle: `backfill_final_marks.py`, `backfill_rating_schemes.py`, `check_scoring_prompt.py` and `response_audit.py` (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: `check_scoring_prompt.py` was deleted with the stored scoring-prompt override it checked; `calibration/` and `profile_mismatch_report.py` were added).
11. **`vertex_setup.py::token` reads a module-global `token` that is assigned at line 112, after `usable()` is defined.** It works because `usable()` is only called at 119 and 133, but the function is not self-contained and would raise `NameError` if reused.
12. **`vertex_probe.py` and `vertex_media_probe.py` set no exit status** - they print `MINT failed` / `CALL failed` / `IMAGE broken` and end normally, so they cannot gate anything. `prove_answer_key.py` likewise always exits 0 on the happy path.
13. **`e2e_cleanup.py` swallows every unlink error** (line 61) and still commits, so a blocked sweep reports as a normal run; the `AFTER:` counts are the only signal.
14. **`e2e_cleanup.py` depends on relative paths** (`sys.path.insert(0, "src")`, `-c odoo.conf`) unlike every other tool, which resolve paths from `__file__`. It only runs from the checkout root.
15. **RESOLVED: `contract_probe.py`'s `subjective_threshold: 71.0` and `write.py` now agree.** The field is on a 0-100 percentage-point scale (1.5, write path item 12). The probe no longer sends the retired `same_questions_for_all` (19.0.3.23.0).
16. **`verify.sh:15` documents an overridable `DB`** that the script never uses.
17. The test module docstring says "four" tests/invariants; the file has 12 methods and a fourth class outside those four invariants.

# Part 2 - The business layer this addon owns (`assessments_be_v2`)

**Retitled and reframed on 25 August 2026.** This part used to be called "What the API wraps
(`etp_assessment_pro`)" and documented a separate upstream module that Part 1 merely called
into. Since the fork it documents the business layer THIS addon owns outright: the models, the
generation pipeline, the scoring rules, the crons. Read it before changing anything in Part 1 -
the API's behaviour is this layer's behaviour, and the two now live in the same addon.

Three things to carry in from Part 1 before reading on:

- **Model names are `assessments.be.*` and tables are `assessments_be_*`.** Every `_pro` name
  in the 11 August edition was rewritten here. Where an explicit
  `custom_addons/etp_assessment_pro/...` path survives it is a historical reference and nothing
  in this addon reaches it.
- **Line numbers were STRIPPED from this part, not updated.** The files it cites grew by
  thousands of lines since 11 August, so every number was wrong. A citation now names the FILE
  and, wherever the claim is non-obvious, the SYMBOL. `grep -n` the symbol. A few numbers
  survive inside code blocks where they were part of a traced sequence; treat those as
  approximate.
- **The unit of scoring is the COMPONENT, not the question.** Section 2.2's "Scoring and
  grading" states the rule in full. If you opened this part to answer "how is a mark reached",
  start there rather than here.

## 2.1 Data model

Paths below are relative to `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/` unless they start with
`custom_addons/`. Module version `19.0.3.23.0` (`__manifest__.py`). What 19.0.3.23.0 changed
and why, item by item, is in `docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 0 (§0.2 fixes, §0.4 feature
inventory, §0.5 deploy note); this part describes the result.

### The data model

#### 1. Model inventory

Unique on `key` (`models.Constraint`). Written only by `services/grading_cache.py`, on a short cursor of its own. `models/scoring_cache.py` |

CSV and harness JSON land as review DRAFTS; only a native export (the `assessments_be_bank` sentinel) restores into the live bank. One Download Template with a flavour picker. The shape predicates `harness_payload` / `native_payload` are shared with `POST /api/v1/bank/import`. `models/bank_import_wizard.py` |

A cap of 0 reads "no limit" (`daily_cap_set`), not "used up". `models/llm_dashboard.py` |

Both the dialog and the write read `_releasable_evaluators`, so the numbers agreed to are the numbers written. `models/release_wizard.py` |

Read-only in Odoo (the console's Form Studio edits it); Publish is repeatable, each press making a new draft assessment, and `publish_question_count` shows how many questions it will mint. `models/studio_form.py` |

| - | `assessments.be.evaluator`, `assessments.be.response` | (re-opened) | Model | `models/release_wizard.py` - `assessment_scoring_phase`, related to the paper's `scoring_phase`, so the attempt and answer forms hide their re-score buttons while a Kill is `stopping` |

That is **30** models declared with `_name` (29 `assessments.be.*` plus `etp.studio.form`) and
nine `_inherit`-only classes (two each in `assessment_api.py` and `release_wizard.py`), across
27 model files. The manifest's `description` still says "27 models across 22 model files" - the
fork-point numbers; do not quote them.

#### 2. `assessments.be` (assessment)

`_order = "create_date desc"`, mail.thread audit via `_log_activity` (`models/assessment.py`).

| Field | Type | Values / default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | Char | required | |
| `active` | Boolean | `True` | Archiving is the sanctioned alternative to deletion |
| `state` | Selection | `draft` (default, required), `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled` | |
| `generator_id` | M2o `assessments.be.prompt` | `ondelete="restrict"` | |
| `question_limit` | Integer | `0` = all | |
| `same_questions_for_all` | Boolean | `True` | **Retired in 19.0.3.23.0 and read by nothing** (W7, `docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` §4.3). Launch always draws ONE shared set for the whole paper, the ORDER still shuffled per candidate unless `preserve_question_order`; the late-add provisioner (`controllers/api/admin.py::_provision_late_candidates`) gives a late candidate that same set, and refuses one when a question the cohort sat has since gone. The field is off the API, both forms and Form Studio publish. The column stays and no row was rewritten, so old rows still hold whatever they held |
| `preserve_question_order` | Boolean | `False` | Serve the authored sequence instead of shuffling per candidate. Set `True` by a Form Studio publish, where the author grouped items into sections deliberately. **Exposed over the API, in the Flutter console AND now on the Odoo form as its inverse, `shuffle_questions`** (serializers.py, the alias hook in write.py, and since 19.0.3.22.0 a computed NON-STORED mirror field with an inverse setter, `assessment.py::_compute_shuffle_questions` / `_inverse_shuffle_questions`) - there is still no `shuffle_questions` column, and this stored negative remains the single source of truth that `action_start`, the late-add provisioner and Form Studio's publish all branch on. The column was deliberately NOT relabelled: a checkbox reading "Shuffle Questions" that ticks to mean "do not shuffle" would be worse than the inconsistency |
| `scoring_cancel_requested` | Boolean | `False`, `copy=False` | The Kill Scoring Process flag, also raised by Archive. Every billable grading lane for this assessment reads it back on a FRESH cursor before its next call (`services/vertex._check_scoring_cancelled`) and refuses. Held raised only while a RUNNING lane holds one of the paper's candidates (`_being_graded`, §2.2 3.3a). Lowered by `_settle_scoring_cancelled` when nothing is held, by `_clear_finished_scoring_kills` at the end of the holding lane's tick, by `_withdraw_scoring_kill` when scoring is asked for again (never while a lane is still stopping), and directly by restore from archive |

##### `_paper_component_totals` - the denominator, and why it is the PAPER

`evaluator._paper_component_totals()` returns `(marks, raw_marks)`: what the DRAWN paper is
worth, summed question by question over `question_order`, the candidate's frozen draw. It
counts every question they were given whether or not they opened it, so abandoning a question
scores 0 out of its marks rather than quietly leaving the total.

That is not a refinement, it is a defect fix that predates the component change and survives
it. The source names the case: attempt 740 was an 8-question paper scored out of 3 and reported
100% PASS. Counting from the draw is what stops that; moving to per-component marks does not
change it, only makes the numbers finer. When no draw was ever recorded - a row created but
never launched - it falls back to the response rows, the same fallback the old question-count
denominator used.

All of `score_percent`, `score_marks_display` and `raw_result`/`raw_percent` read it, so the
marks view and the percentage view can never disagree about what the paper was worth.

**PII anonymization** (`_anonymize_pii`): rewrites `response.justification` to the sentinel `[anonymized]` (`_PII_ANONYMIZED_TAG`) - it MUST stay truthy or `needs_llm` flips False and the answer silently leaves the scoring denominator - and clears `llm_feedback`, `llm_reasoning`, `llm_verdict`, `llm_reference_answer`, `llm_result_json`, `llm_deductions_json`, `llm_credit_json` plus `violation_reason`. Numeric scores are retained.
It also drops any queued `rescore_request_key` and lowers `scoring_requested`; an attempt a lane is
grading right now (`llm_state = scoring`) is set to `cancelled` with "Grading stopped: this
attempt's data was erased." (round 3, RV1-01), so it is never stranded in `scoring` and the deploy
gate stays open, and a parallel lane's `_llm_score_finish` re-reads `pii_anonymized` and stores
nothing on an erased attempt. Every
scoring entry point refuses (re-score: 409 `erased`) or skips an erased attempt, because a
re-grade would pay the grader to mark the literal `[anonymized]` and replace the kept mark.

#### 4. `assessments.be.response` / `.response.line`

`_order = "create_date desc"`. **This is where the component scoring rule lands, and this
whole subsection was rewritten on 25 August 2026.** Read `_compute_final_marks`,
`_compute_subjective_marks` and `_dimension_marks` in `models/assessment.py` alongside it, and
`docs/ETP_KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md (4.6 Scoring, in engineering terms)` before changing any of it.

Identity/answer fields: `assessment_id` (required, cascade), `assessment_evaluator_id` (cascade,
indexed), `evaluator_id` (M2o `hr.applicant`, required), `question_id` (required, cascade,
indexed), `justification` (Text), `auto_submitted` (Boolean, `False`), `cleared` (Boolean,
`False`, no index, 19.0.3.27.0: the candidate emptied the answer; the row is draft with no lines
and no text, so it is neither graded nor counted; a real answer sets it back to `False`; at
settlement the row becomes the question's placeholder in place, keeping `cleared`), `line_ids` (O2m),
`state` (Selection `draft` default / `submitted`). `_is_answered()` is the one definition of
"answered" (see `answered_count` above). Non-stored relateds for the answer form
(19.0.3.23.0): `attempt_state` (the attempt's `state` - answers are submitted one by one during
the exam, this says whether the candidate has handed in), `attempt_released` (drives the
confirming variant of "Re-score This Answer" on a released attempt) and
`assessment_scoring_phase`.

##### The rule in one paragraph

**THE UNIT OF SCORING IS THE COMPONENT, NOT THE QUESTION.** A question is worth the SUM of its
components and each component is worth exactly 1: one mark per KEYED dimension (a dimension
with at least one `is_correct` option - the same rule for mcq, for msq and for every `image_ab`
verdict axis), one mark for the LLM-graded free-text answer, one mark for a labelling box set
taken as a whole. So `final_mark` is `0..N`, not `0/1`, and `final_max` says what the N is -
read them as a pair, never alone. A 3-sub-question MCQ is worth 3; an `image_ab` with four
verdict axes plus a justification is worth 5.

Each component is won or lost on its OWN. There is no partial credit inside a component and no
conjunction across them: an `image_ab` candidate who calls three of four verdicts right and
writes a weak justification scores 3 - not 0, and not 3.75.

##### Which component decides which mark

| Component | Present when | Earned iff |
|---|---|---|
| One per keyed dimension | The dimension has ≥ 1 `is_correct` option | The selected option set equals the key set **EXACTLY**. One missing or one extra option scores THAT dimension 0; the siblings are untouched. `_dimension_marks` |
| The graded free-text answer | `question_type in SUBJECTIVE_COMPONENT_TYPES` = `{subjective_rubric, image_prompt, video_prompt, image_ab}` | `llm_state == "scored"` and `llm_raw_100 >= _subjective_threshold()` |
| The labelling box set | `question_type in LABELLING_COMPONENT_TYPES` = `{image_label}` | Each box is thresholded on its OWN raw; `fraction = cleared / N`; the single mark is 1 iff `fraction * 100 >= threshold`. `_label_marks` |

A **KEYLESS** dimension - one where the author never ticked a correct option - is not a
component and counts in NEITHER the numerator nor the denominator (`_keyed_dimension_count` on
the question). Counting it would mark every candidate wrong on a sub-question nothing can
satisfy, which reads as a candidate failure rather than the authoring fault it is.

`image_label` is deliberately excluded from `SUBJECTIVE_COMPONENT_TYPES` even though it is
LLM-graded: its per-box answers live in the SAME `justification` column a free-text answer
would, so counting it in both sets would charge one answer two marks.

##### The raw, and why objective components have none

`raw_score` / `raw_max` cover the **LLM-graded components alone**. Objective components carry
no raw and are excluded from the raw's numerator AND its denominator - they are not scored 0 in
it. Two reasons, both in the source:

- An objective raw would only restate the mark sitting beside it, so it adds no information.
- Leaving objective components in the raw's DENOMINATOR would make the raw read lower the more
  multiple-choice a paper contained, which is a property of the paper and not of the candidate.

A wholly objective question therefore has `raw_max` 0 and drops out of the raw score entirely.
A wholly objective paper has no raw score rather than a raw of zero.

##### The mark and raw fields

All computed and stored, all `readonly=True, copy=False`, all from `_compute_final_marks`
unless noted.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `final_mark` | Float | What this question earned: `dim_earned + llm_score`. 0 to `final_max` |
| `final_max` | Integer | What this question is worth. Read off the QUESTION via `_component_counts`, so an unanswered question still occupies its marks in the paper's denominator |
| `mcq_mark` | Float | **A COUNT, not a percentage.** How many keyed sub-questions were exactly right |
| `objective_marks_max` | Integer | How many keyed sub-questions this question has. A keyless dimension counts 0 |
| `raw_score` | Float, 4dp | Ungated quality over the LLM-graded components, each contributing 0.0-1.0 |
| `raw_max` | Integer | How many LLM-graded components this question has (0 for a purely objective one) |
| `label_fraction` | Float, 4dp, from `_compute_subjective_marks` | Share of this question's labelling boxes whose graded raw cleared the threshold. This is the figure the labelling mark's own threshold test uses |
| `label_box_scores_json` | Text, written by `services/scoring.py::_apply_image_label_boxes` | The grader's raw 0-100 for EACH box, keyed by box number. Immutable truth: per-box pass/fail, the fraction and the mark are all derived from it live, so moving the threshold re-decides a labelling question with no LLM call |

`score` / `max_score` (`_compute_score`) are the objective tally **in the same currency** -
each keyed sub-question is worth 1, identical to `_dimension_marks`. They used to be their own
all-or-nothing rule out of 1, which disagreed with `final_mark` the day the unit became the
component: a candidate who got two of three sub-questions right earned 2 here and 0 out of 1
there, and the candidate review reads THESE columns for its Correct/Incorrect label, so it
called that answer "Incorrect". There is one rule now. `objective_score` / `objective_max` are
stored `related` duplicates of the pair.

`has_objective` and `needs_llm` come from `_compute_scoring_kind`: `has_objective = qtype in
(mcq, msq)`; `needs_llm` = for `image_ab` `bool(line_ids) and not placeholder`, otherwise
`qtype in (subjective_rubric, image_prompt, image_label, video_prompt) and bool(justification)
and not placeholder`.

##### The subjective and audit fields

All `readonly=True, copy=False` unless noted.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `llm_raw_100` | Float | The immutable 0-100 grader score. Everything else is derived from it and the threshold, so a threshold edit re-decides pass/fail without re-scoring |
| `llm_raw_score` | Float compute stored | `llm_raw_100/100`, 4dp. For a labelling answer this is instead the ungated MEAN of the box raws |
| `llm_passed` | Boolean compute stored | `llm_state == "scored" and raw100 >= threshold`; for labelling, `bool(mark)` |
| `llm_score` / `llm_max_score` | Integer compute stored | The LLM-graded component's mark: 1 or 0, and 1. For a labelling question `llm_score` is the labelling component's mark |
| `llm_state` | Selection | `not_needed` (default), `pending`, `queued`, `scored`, `failed`, `error` |
| `llm_attempts` | Integer | `0` |
| `llm_scored_hash` | Char | `_graded_answer_hash()`: sha256 of the graded justification, plus the A/B picks on an `image_ab` (round 3, A-257); blocks re-queueing an unchanged answer (H-16) |
| `llm_judge_model` | Char | The exact Vertex model that produced the score. Empty for gated/verdict-only answers that never called the model |
| `llm_prompt_version` | Char | `bundled:<first 8 hex of sha256>` of the grading instructions that produced the score (`scoring.scoring_prompt_version`); 19.0.3.23.0 ships `bundled:785826a5`. Empty on scores stored before versioning, never back-filled. Older rows may read `override:...`. The candidate verdict gate compares it with `current_scoring_prompt_version()` (§2.1 #13) |
| `rescore_request_key` | Char, readonly, `copy=False` | A queued RE-SCORE request (19.0.3.23.0): one random key per admin click. The lane grades keyed answers first, each click's answers in calls of their own. Cleared when the answer is graded, errors out for good, fails a re-grade (the old mark stays), is erased, or scoring is killed. Partial index `assessments_be_response_rescore_idx` on `(assessment_evaluator_id) WHERE rescore_request_key IS NOT NULL`, built in `init()`. §2.2 3.3a |
| `llm_gate` | Char | Platform gate string (`empty_answer`, `injection_attempt`, `key_drift`), or `none`. The judge gates (`unscorable:*`) appear only on answers graded by older prompts: the current `prompts/scoring.md` asks for no gate. Vocabulary in `constants.py` |
| `llm_rubric_source` | Char | `supplied` / `generated` on older rows only; `deterministic_verdict` on the verdict-only lane; empty on answers the current prompt graded |
| `llm_feedback`, `llm_reasoning`, `llm_reference_answer`, `llm_verdict`, `llm_profile`, `llm_clarity`, `llm_ai_confidence`, `llm_verdict_consistency` | Text/Char | Grader prose + the v10 axes. `llm_profile` is the rules the CODE graded by (`scoring._grading_rules`, chosen by question type), never the model's echo |
| `llm_key_closeness`, `llm_sop_coverage` | Float | The generic subjective rubric lanes, weights 0.60 / 0.25 per the help text; legacy v10 fields the current prompt does not fill. **Unrelated to the removed `image_ab` blend** |
| `llm_flags_json`, `llm_result_json`, `llm_deductions_json`, `llm_credit_json`, `llm_golden_claims_json` | Text | Audit JSON. `llm_flags_json` can carry `profile_mismatch` (the SOP title claims rules the question type does not allow) and `no_answer_key` (graded against the task alone) |
| `integrity_alert` | Boolean compute stored | From `llm_gate` / `llm_flags_json` / `llm_result_json`. Display and filter only; never affects a score |
| `ab_mcq_pct` | Float compute (not stored) | `image_ab`: the verdict axes as a percentage, for DISPLAY. The MARK is `_dimension_marks` |
| `ab_final_pct` | Float compute (not stored) | `image_ab` RAW 0-100: the grader's score for the WRITTEN JUSTIFICATION and nothing else, read straight off `llm_raw_100`. **Nothing is blended into this any more.** The `ceil()` in `_compute_ab_scores` is a display fallback for an answer the grader has not reached; the stored mark is never rounded up |
| `ab_verdict_pct`, `ab_justification_pct` | Float compute (not stored) | Read out of the stored audit; display only |
| `label_coverage_pct` | Float compute (not stored) | Share of boxes the candidate attempted. **Coverage is now a REPORTING figure only** - an unattempted box scores 0 on its own rather than ceilinging the whole answer |
| `label_correctness_pct` | Float compute (not stored) | Mean of the per-box raws, ungated. The MARK comes from how many boxes individually cleared the threshold, not from this |
| `subjective_score` | Integer `related=llm_score` | The earned equal-marks subjective mark |
| `subjective_result` | Selection compute stored | `pass` / `fail` / False |
| `subjective_reasoning` | Text `related=llm_feedback` | |
| `question_type` | Selection `related=question_id.question_type` | |
| `answer_summary`, `correct_summary` | Char compute (not stored) | `_compute_answer_summary` reads via `sudo` - `correct_summary` IS the answer key |

##### What was REMOVED, and must not be described as current

Everything in this list was live on 11 August and is gone. If you find any of it in a comment,
a doc or a dashboard, that artefact is stale.

| Gone | What replaced it |
|---|---|
| "Every question is worth 1 mark" | Every COMPONENT is worth 1 mark |
| All-or-nothing across a whole question | All-or-nothing WITHIN one sub-question, and nowhere else |
| The `image_ab` 0.75-verdict / 0.25-justification blend, its two weight constants and the helper that applied it | Verdict axes are keyed sub-questions worth 1 mark each; the justification is its own component worth 1. Nothing is weighted against anything else |
| The hard cap at 60 when the OVERALL (OC) preference was wrong | The Overall Choice axis is a component of its own and is simply marked wrong. Same penalty, legible |
| The two blended raw columns on the response - one for the objective half, one for the whole question | Deleted with the blend. `mcq_mark` is a COUNT of sub-questions, and `raw_score` covers the LLM-graded components only |
| The labelling coverage ceiling - the stored ceiling column, its floor and cap constants, and the function that applied them | Each box is thresholded on its own raw and an unattempted box scores 0 directly. That says exactly what the ceiling said approximately, and it closes the advisory-only gap where a candidate who labelled 6 of 10 boxes should have been ceilinged at 60 but in practice only raised a review flag |
| The eighth question type - the two-plate image labelling variant | Retired by `migrations/19.0.3.7.0/pre-migrate.py`, which names the code and repoints every stored copy onto `image_label`. **Seven** question types now |
| The generator's rating-scheme summary field | Removed from the model, the serialiser, the back-office view and the Flutter client. The `tabs.requirements.rating_scheme` JSON blob it summarised is still emitted by `generator_detail` |

**The removed SYMBOL names are deliberately not written out above.** They are recorded where
they belong and where they cannot go stale: the tombstone comment in `constants.py`, and the
docstring of `tests/test_component_marks.py`, which names the file it superseded. Repeating
dead identifiers here would make this document itself match a grep for stale symbols, which is
the check that catches a doc drifting back.

Read the `constants.py` tombstone before anyone proposes reinstating the blend. It records that
the blend was applied TWICE - once in the grader, once again composing the raw, giving an
effective 93.75/6.25 nobody intended - and that a perfect set of verdicts started the raw at 75
before a word of the write-up was read.

**`ondelete="restrict"`**), `selected_option_id` (**`ondelete="restrict"`**). No `_order`.

##### `_component_counts` and `_keyed_dimension_count` - what a question is WORTH

Both live on `assessments.be.question`, and **that placement is the point.** The denominator is
the paper's length, so it has to be computable for a question the candidate never opened -
there may be no response row at all. Deriving it from the answer would shrink the paper to
whatever was attempted and hand an abandoned question a free pass.

```python
_keyed_dimension_count()  ->  how many dimensions have >= 1 is_correct option
_component_counts()       ->  (marks, raw_marks)
    raw_marks = int(qtype in SUBJECTIVE_COMPONENT_TYPES) \
              + int(qtype in LABELLING_COMPONENT_TYPES)
    marks     = _keyed_dimension_count() + raw_marks
```

`SUBJECTIVE_COMPONENT_TYPES = {subjective_rubric, image_prompt, video_prompt, image_ab}` and
`LABELLING_COMPONENT_TYPES = {image_label}`, both in `constants.py`. The sets are keyed on
QUESTION TYPE, never on `needs_llm` - a question has to be priceable before anyone answers it.

Worked: a 3-sub-question MCQ is `(3, 0)`. A `subjective_rubric` is `(1, 1)`. An `image_ab` with
four verdict axes and a justification is `(5, 1)`. An `image_label` is `(1, 1)` however many
boxes it carries - the boxes are normalised to 0-1 INSIDE that single mark, never spread across
the paper.

`question.dimension` (`models/question_dimension.py`): `question_id` (required, cascade), `name` (required), `sequence` (10), `option_line_ids`.
`question.dimension.option`: `question_dimension_id` (required, cascade), `name` (required), `sequence` (10), `is_correct` (Boolean, `False`), `score` (Integer compute stored = 1 if correct else 0).

`question.image` (`models/question_image.py`): `question_id` (required, cascade); `question_type` (**related, store=True** - denormalized so the detect cron can filter); `label` (required); `slot` (Selection required default `single`: `a`, `b`, `single`, `reference`, `output`); `slot_ab` / `slot_text` (compute+inverse UI helpers, not stored); `image` / `annotated_image` (Binary, attachment); `image_url` / `annotated_image_url` (Char); `detections_json` (the labelling answer key - a non-empty value is the detect cron's skip guard); `detection_attempts` (Integer, 0, cap `_DETECT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3`); `source_url`, `dom_manifest_json`, `behavioural_key_json`, `capture_viewport`, `capture_config_json`, `omit_spec_json`, `omitted_element_json`, `label_boxes_json`, `label_application`; `coverage_expected` (Selection `yes`/`no`); `sequence`; `image_admin_url` / `annotated_admin_url` (compute).

`question.video` (`models/question_video.py`): `question_id` (required, cascade), `label`, `slot` (`reference`/`output`/`single`, default `single`), `video_url`, `video` (Binary), `video_filename`, `poster_url`, `duration_s` (Float), `has_audio` (Boolean), `sequence`.

`question.type` (`models/question_type.py`): `code` (required, indexed), `name` (required),
`sequence` (10), `active` (True). `init` re-syncs rows from `GENERATABLE_QUESTION_TYPE_ORDER`
on every install/upgrade and archives any code in `NON_GENERATABLE_QUESTION_TYPES`. **That set
is EMPTY today** - every live type is generatable - so the archive branch cannot currently
fire. It is kept, with its four guard sites, so re-retiring a type is a one-line change. The
retired type's vocabulary row is not archived but DELETED, by the 19.0.3.7.0 pre-migration,
along with its generator allow-list links and its `ir_model_data` row.

#### 9. State machines and transitions

**`assessments.be.state`** - `draft`, `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled`
```
draft --action_start(394)--------------------> in_progress
    guards: has evaluator_ids; has generator_id; >=1 active question with
            required images+videos; question_limit <= pool size; no keyless
            mcq/msq/image_ab; if require_reviewed_rubric, no unreviewed
            subjective question.
    warns (never blocks) in the chatter about questions with no answer
            key: their answers are graded against the task alone and flagged
            `no_answer_key` (`scoring.lacks_answer_key`).
    effects: question_ids := ALL eligible questions; start_date := now;
             ONE shared draw of `question_limit` for everybody (the first N in
             authored order when preserve_question_order, else a random
             sample), shuffled per candidate unless preserve_question_order;
             each applicant's evaluator row gets question_order +
             invite_state='queued'; portal user provisioned. The row is
             usually ALREADY THERE - _sync_roster_rows creates one the moment
             a candidate is assigned - so action_start FILLS it and keeps the
             access_token it was created with. It only creates a row when none
             exists. (Creating unconditionally collided with the
             (assessment_id, applicant_id) unique index and made every
             app-assigned draft impossible to launch.)
in_progress --action_done------------------> done
in_progress --all evaluators submitted-----> done   (_auto_submit_expired)
    NOTE: the all-submitted check lives INSIDE _auto_submit_expired, which the
    candidate submit path delegates to. There is no separate
    _check_assessment_complete - a dead copy of that transition was deleted.
    A no-show never reaches this: deadline_datetime is derived from
    started_at, so a pending evaluator has none and the stale-attempt cron
    skips it forever. end_date drives no transition at all, so an assessment
    with any no-show only reaches done via action_done.
draft|in_progress --action_cancel(495)------> cancelled   (refuses done/cancelled)
    effects: parks `scoring` rows no live lane holds (`_park_unheld_scoring`).
cancelled --action_reset_draft(504)---------> draft
    effects: DELETES all evaluators and responses, clears question_ids,
             start_date, end_date. Refused (409 `released_results`) when a
             candidate's results are released, unless context
             `confirm_released`.
done --> (no outbound transition)
```
`active` is orthogonal to `state`. The back-office Archive (`action_archive`) is refused with a
`UserError` while any attempt is `in_progress`, because archiving does not pause a sitting; the
API route refuses 409 `live_attempts` unless confirmed, and the Delete wizard names the live
count. §2.2 3.11a.

**`assessments.be.evaluator.state`** - `pending`, `in_progress`, `submitted`
```
pending --candidate begins----------------> in_progress
   (controllers/api/candidate.py `/begin` and `/answer` - started_at stamped
    once, idempotent; the QWeb portal path went in 19.0.3.19.0)
in_progress --last response submitted-----> submitted + is_locked=True
   (response._check_all_submitted 2298, under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE)
in_progress --deadline passed-------------> submitted + is_locked=True
   (_auto_submit_expired 1405, fired by portal or _cron_expire_stale_attempts 1463;
    fills placeholder responses with auto_submitted=True, llm_state='not_needed')
any --write(state='submitted')------------> stamps submitted_at once (1058);
   auto-queues grading when assessment.llm_auto_score (1072)
```
No transition back out of `submitted`; there is no `active` field, so an attempt cannot be archived.

**`evaluator.invite_state`** - `none`, `queued`, `sent`, `failed`
```
none --action_start(480)--------------> queued
queued --_cron_send_pending_invitations(1617)--> sent   (batch 25, advisory-locked)
                                       \-------> failed (+ invite_error[:200])
queued|failed|none --action_requeue_invitation(1657)--> queued   (skips 'sent')
```

**`evaluator.llm_state`** - `pending`, `scoring`, `scored`, `partial`, `failed`, `error`, `cancelled`
```
pending --_auto_score_mark_scoring--> scoring   (COMMITTED before the first
                                        judge call, so Kill sees the candidate
                                        as held; `_llm_score_start`)
scoring --> per-response scoring, then
_compute_subjective_rollup:
  no needs_llm responses                        -> scored
  all in (scored, error) and any error          -> error
  all scored                                    -> scored (+ llm_scored_at)
  any failed, some scored/error                 -> partial
  any failed, none scored/error                 -> failed
  any scored/error, rest pending                -> partial
  otherwise                                     -> pending
_llm_score_guarded:
  VertexCancelledError, paper archived          -> pending (scoring_requested kept)
  VertexCancelledError, a kill                  -> cancelled (scoring_requested
                                                   False, re-score keys dropped)
  any other exception                           -> failed (+ llm_error)
action_kill_scoring / drainer settle            -> cancelled, for candidates no
                                                   running lane holds
action_llm_score_all / action_queue_llm_score   -> pending (+ scoring_requested)
action_reset_failed_scoring (Retry Failed)      -> pending (+ scoring_requested)
```
The scoring cron drains `pending, scoring, partial, failed` with `scoring_requested`, on papers
that are active and not cancelled, attempts not erased (`_scoring_shard_evaluators`) - **`error`
is deliberately terminal** and needs Retry Failed Scoring or a re-score. A candidate with a
queued re-score request is drained whatever its `llm_state`.

**`response.llm_state`** - `not_needed`, `pending`, `queued`, `scored`, `failed`, `error`
```
not_needed <- _enqueue_subjective_scoring when no justification / no lines
pending    <- _enqueue_subjective_scoring when needs_llm and text hash changed
scored     <- services/scoring.py::_store_scored
failed     <- services/scoring.py::_store_error  (recoverable, retried)
error      <- services/scoring.py::_store_error  (terminal, after llm_max_attempts)
pending    <- action_reset_failed_scoring (llm_attempts reset to 0)
queued     <- NEVER WRITTEN (see anomalies)
scored     stays scored when a queued RE-GRADE fails (`_is_regrade`): the old mark
           stands, the key is dropped, the reason goes on the attempt's llm_error
pending    stays pending on a deferral (429, rate ceiling, spend cap, full DB pool,
           kill): no attempt is spent
```
`rescore_request_key` rides beside this: set by `action_rescore_individually` (with
`llm_attempts` reset to 0 on a `failed`/`error` answer), cleared by `_store_scored`, by a
terminal `_store_error`, by a failed re-grade, by a kill and by erasure.

**`prompt.state`** - `draft`, `skills_ready`, `generating`, `done`
```
draft --tag extraction completes--> skills_ready  (only from draft; :861, :752)
any   --_action_generate_from_sop(530)--> generating
generating --_finalize_sop_gen_state(704)--> done
```

**`prompt.sop_gen_state`** - `idle`, `queued`, `generating`, `finalizing`, `done`, `failed`
```
idle --_action_generate_from_sop(530)--> queued
queued --cron picks up(626)------------> generating   (committed before the Vertex call)
generating --drafts committed---------> finalizing    (COMMITTED; the drainer does not
                                                       select this state, so a killed
                                                       worker never re-pays Vertex)
finalizing --_finalize_sop_gen_state--> done
generating --VertexQuotaError---------> queued        (:655)
generating --serialization failure----> queued        (:663)
generating --any other error----------> failed (+ sop_gen_error[:300])
finalizing --cron sweep(594) or action_generate_from_sop(517)--> done
```

**`prompt.tag_extract_state`** - `idle`, `queued`, `generating`, `done`, `failed`
```
idle|done|failed --action_extract_tags--> queued   (`_queue_tag_extract`, which
                                                    also triggers the cron)
queued --_cron_extract_tags--> generating --> done | queued (429) | failed
                                            | cancelled (the generator's kill)
```
Extraction never runs in the web request: the request's REPEATABLE READ snapshot collided
with its own independent-cursor status write (40001). The cron owns its transaction and commits
its own progress under `ADVISORY_LOCK_TAG_EXTRACT`.

**`prompt.question.state`** - `draft` ("Pending"), `approved`, `denied`
```
draft --action_approve(2289)--> approved (+ approved_question_id)
draft --action_deny(2782)-----> denied
```

**`prompt.question.image_state`** - `none`, `pending`, `rendered`, `uploaded`, `failed`
```
pending --_render_all_images(3212) all slots filled--> rendered (attempts reset to 0)
pending --VertexQuotaError--------------------------> pending (partial slots persisted)
pending --incomplete render x3----------------------> failed
any     --action_apply_uploaded_image(3927)---------> uploaded
any     --cron exception(3354)----------------------> failed
```

**`prompt.question.video_state`** - `none`, `pending`, `generating`, `rendered`, `partial`, `failed`
```
pending --_submit_video_ops(3426) all slots submitted OR any in flight--> generating
pending --all slots failed past cap, none staged----------------------> failed
pending --all slots failed past cap, some clip staged-----------------> partial
generating --_poll_video_ops(3515) all ops done-----------------------> rendered
generating --any failed, none in flight, some staged------------------> partial
generating --any failed, none in flight, none staged------------------> failed
failed|partial --action_retry_video_generation(3751)------------------> pending
                 (drops only the FAILED slots' ops; a done op_name is never
                  cleared, so a generated clip is never re-billed)
```

**`prompt.resource.status`** (compute): `failed` if `extraction_error`; else `ready` if text; else `native` for `pdf/png/jpg/jpeg/webp/gif` (`NATIVE_DOC_EXTENSIONS`); else `pending`.

#### 10. Relationship diagram

```
                      hr.applicant (inherited)
                        | candidate_user_id -> res.users
                        |
          evaluator_ids (M2m, roster)          applicant_id (M2o, restrict)
   assessments.be ---------------------+        |
     |  |  |                               |        |
     |  |  | generator_id (M2o, restrict)  +--> assessments.be.evaluator
     |  |  v                                          |  (unique: assessment_id+applicant_id)
     |  |  assessments.be.prompt   <--------------+  assessment_id (cascade)
     |  |     |  |  |  |  |                           |
     |  |     |  |  |  |  +-- tag_ids (M2m) --> assessments.be.tag
     |  |     |  |  |  +----- allowed_question_type_ids (M2m)
     |  |     |  |  |             --> assessments.be.question.type
     |  |     |  |  +-- resource_ids (O2m) --> ...prompt.resource (cascade)
     |  |     |  +----- similarity_source_ids (O2m) --> ...similarity
     |  |     |            (source_id / target_id both cascade to prompt)
     |  |     +-- question_ids (O2m) --> assessments.be.prompt.question
     |  |                                    | (draft)
     |  |                                    +-- answer_dimension_ids (O2m, cascade)
     |  |                                    |      --> ...prompt.question.dimension
     |  |                                    |            +-- option_line_ids (O2m, cascade)
     |  |                                    |                  --> ...dimension.option
     |  |                                    +-- approved_question_id (M2o, readonly)
     |  |                                            |
     |  | question_ids (M2m)                         v  action_approve creates
     |  +-------------------------------> assessments.be.question
     |                                        |   ^ generator_id (M2o, set null)
     |                                        +-- question_dimension_ids (O2m, cascade)
     |                                        |      --> ...question.dimension
     |                                        |            +-- option_line_ids (O2m, cascade)
     |                                        |                  --> ...dimension.option
     |                                        +-- image_ids (O2m, cascade) --> ...question.image
     |                                        +-- video_ids (O2m, cascade) --> ...question.video
     |
     +-- response_ids (O2m) --> assessments.be.response
                                   |  assessment_id (cascade, required)
                                   |  assessment_evaluator_id (cascade, indexed)
                                   |     (unique: assessment_evaluator_id+question_id)
                                   |  evaluator_id -> hr.applicant (required, NO ondelete)
                                   |  question_id (cascade, required)
                                   +-- line_ids (O2m, cascade) --> ...response.line
                                          question_dimension_id (M2o, RESTRICT)
                                          selected_option_id   (M2o, RESTRICT)

assessments.be.llm.usage --prompt_id--> prompt        (set null)
                             --evaluator_id--> evaluator  (set null)
```

Note the deletion asymmetry: `response.line` holds `restrict` FKs to dimension and option, so a dimension that any candidate ever answered cannot be deleted; but `response.question_id` is `cascade`, so deleting a question destroys the answers. `question.unlink` (`models/question.py`) blocks deletion only while an assessment is `in_progress`.

#### 11. Key `action_*` methods

| Method | Model | What it does | Preconditions | Side effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action_start` `assessment.py` | assessment | Launch | state `draft`; `evaluator_ids`; `generator_id`; ≥1 servable question; `question_limit ≤ pool`; no keyless mcq/msq/image_ab; if `require_reviewed_rubric`, no unreviewed subjective question | Writes `question_ids` (**the whole eligible pool**), `state=in_progress`, `start_date`; provisions a portal `res.users` per applicant; creates one evaluator each with `question_order`, `access_token`, `invite_state='queued'`; posts chatter |
| `action_done` | assessment | Close | state `in_progress` | `state=done`, chatter |
| `action_cancel` | assessment | Cancel | state not in (`done`,`cancelled`) | `state=cancelled`; `_park_unheld_scoring` sets `llm_state = cancelled` ("Grading stopped: the assessment was cancelled.") on `scoring` rows no live lane holds, so a lane that died cannot strand a row and shut the deploy gate (round 3); chatter. Archive does not park (an archived paper with a dead lane's row still needs Kill or unarchive) |
| `action_reset_draft` | assessment | Reset | state `cancelled`; any candidate with `results_released` needs context `confirm_released`, else `RescoreRefused` `released_results` (409 on the API; round 3, A-040). The Odoo button sends it and its confirm names released results | **Deletes** all evaluators and responses; clears `question_ids`/dates; `state=draft` |
| `action_import_candidates_csv` | assessment | Roster import | `candidate_csv_file`; ≤25 MB; ≤5000 rows; header has `name`,`email`; every row passes `candidate_row_error` (strict email, name ≤200 chars) | Checks EVERY row first; any bad row raises one `UserError` listing them and nothing is created (round 3, A-222). Then skips anybody who could never sit (`_be_sit_blockers`, plus a login refused during provisioning, taken back off by `_sync_roster_rows`) and names them in the History, creates/matches `hr.applicant` for the rest, links to `evaluator_ids`, provisions their logins, clears the upload fields; the notification names each skipped person and why. Launch alone keeps the all-or-nothing refusal (`_be_provision_candidates`) |
| `action_download_candidate_template` | assessment | Two-row CSV template | - | Creates an `ir.attachment` |
| `action_llm_score_all` | assessment | Queue whole cohort ("Run Subjective Evaluation") | paper not `cancelled` (`UserError`); no Kill still stopping (`RescoreRefused` `stopping`, 409 on the API); ≥1 submitted, non-erased attempt with an unscored needs_llm answer (one query, `_answers_scored_domain(scored=False)`) | Skips candidates a running lane holds; saves the tally; withdraws a kill only if it queued someone; `scoring_requested=True`, `llm_state='pending'`, chatter. Returns `queue: {queued, skipped}` for the API |
| `action_llm_score_failed` | assessment | Retry Failed Scoring | same two refusals | Delegates to `action_reset_failed_scoring(("failed","error"))` |
| `action_kill_scoring` | assessment | Kill Scoring Process | - | Raises the flag; `_settle_scoring_cancelled` parks every queued/scoring candidate no running lane holds (`cancelled`) and drops the paper's queued re-score requests except a held candidate's (its lane drops those when the kill reaches it); lowers the flag only when nothing is held. Returns `kill: {settled, cleared, held}`; the toast says "N candidate(s) being graded now will stop at their next call". Scores already stored are kept |
| `action_release_all_results` | assessment | Bulk release, step 1 | ≥1 submitted, unreleased evaluator | Opens `assessments.be.release.wizard` (the counted confirm); writes nothing |
| `action_confirm_release` | assessment | Bulk release, the write | the same | Releases every submitted, unreleased attempt EXCEPT those a running lane is grading (released on the next click); refuses when all are held. Warns about any still being graded. Returns `release: {released, skipped}`; called by the dialog, the API and tests |
| `action_export_results` / `action_export_responses` | assessment | Delegates to `services/export.py` | single record | - |
| `action_requeue_all_invitations` | assessment | Re-queue every invite | single record | Delegates to the evaluator action |
| `action_requeue_invitation` | evaluator | Re-queue | skips rows already `sent` | `invite_state='queued'`, clears `invite_error` |
| `_action_llm_score` | evaluator | The SERIAL lane's grading pass - the cron's and nobody else's | every record `submitted` else `UserError` | **Private since 19.0.3.23.0**: the leading underscore is what keeps it off `/web/dataset/call_kw`, where a web worker would sit on a Vertex call and write over the lane that owns the candidate. `_llm_score_start` → `scoring.score_evaluator` inside `_llm_score_guarded` → rollup |
| `action_queue_llm_score` | evaluator | Queue chosen candidates (`POST /scoring/queue` with ids) | all `submitted`; paper not cancelled; no Kill stopping | Skips candidates a lane holds and erased attempts; `scoring_requested=True`, `llm_state='pending'`; returns `queue: {queued, skipped}` |
| `action_reset_failed_scoring` | evaluator | Retry failed/errored answers | same refusals | One search over the answers: `failed`/`error` → `pending`, `llm_attempts=0`, attempt re-queued; skips busy and erased attempts; withdraws a kill only for papers it touched. Returns `reset: {answers, skipped}` |
| `action_reset_errored_scoring` | evaluator | `error` answers only | - | Kept for its narrower contract; no button or route calls it now |
| `action_rescore_individually` | evaluator | Re-score chosen answers of THIS attempt ("Re-score N answer(s)", "Re-score This Answer", `POST /attempts/<id>/rescore`) | refuses, writing nothing (`RescoreRefused`, code → HTTP): `spend_limit` (a daily or per-candidate cap reached; the per-minute limit is not a refusal), `erased`, `archived`, `stopping`, `being_graded`, `released_confirm_required` (released attempt without `confirm_released`), all 409; `not_on_attempt` 422 naming the first 10 ids. A cancelled paper is a plain `UserError` (the API answers 422 `rejected`) | Writes only the chosen answers: one random `rescore_request_key` per click (and `llm_attempts=0` on `failed`/`error`); an answer already queued keeps its key. No grading in the request. Chatter line with each answer's previous mark, model and prompt version. Returns `rescore: {queued, skipped, question_ids}` |
| `action_release_results` | evaluator | Release | - | `results_released=True`, skipping candidates a running lane is grading (warned, sticky); returns `release: {released, skipped}`. Does **not** check `state == submitted`, unlike the assessment-level action |
| `action_erase_candidate_data` | evaluator | On-demand GDPR erasure | - | `_anonymize_pii`, `pii_anonymized=True`, chatter on the assessment |
| `action_export_responses` | evaluator | Per-candidate export | single record | - |
| `action_rescore_this_answer` | response | Odoo's "Re-score This Answer" | the answer belongs to an attempt | `action_rescore_individually(question_ids=[this question])` |
| `action_archive` | assessment | Back-office Archive | no attempt `in_progress` (`UserError` naming the count) | `active=False` through `write`, which suspends the paper's background work (§2.2 3.11a) |
| `action_submit` | response | Submit one answer | not already submitted; evaluator not locked; mcq/msq/image_ab need `line_ids`; subjective types need a justification; image_prompt/label with dimensions need `line_ids` | `state='submitted'`; enqueues subjective scoring; may lock the attempt and flip the assessment to `done` |
| `action_generate_from_sop` | prompt | Queue SOP generation | **Refuses when `sop_gen_state == 'finalizing'`** - finishes the stranded finalize instead and raises, to avoid a duplicate paid run | `sop_gen_state='queued'`, `state='generating'`, chatter |
| `action_extract_tags` | prompt | Queue tag extraction | needs a resource or `source_text` | `tag_extract_state='queued'` and a cron trigger (`_queue_tag_extract`); `_cron_extract_tags` does the paid work. Returns a toast whose `next` reloads the form, so the status badge starts polling |
| `action_new_task_template` / `action_draft_task_template` | prompt | Author a question template for this generator, by hand / from the SOP (one paid call, saves nothing) | Assessment Admin (`AccessError` otherwise) | Opens a template form. The blank one opens with NO name so leaving the page cannot urgent-save an "Untitled task". The Odoo "Draft from SOP" button is hidden in 19.0.3.23.0 (its draft arrives named, so leaving the page saves it) |
| `action_normalize_tags` | prompt | Consolidate the global vocabulary (paid), then re-extract the selected generators onto it | - | Merges tags across the library; re-runs inline extraction per generator |
| `action_backfill_all_tags` (`@api.model`) | prompt | Extract tags for every untagged generator with a SOP | - | Bulk inline extraction |
| `action_compute_similarity_semantic` | prompt | **PAID** hybrid re-rank (0.30 lexical + 0.70 semantic) for the selection, then a free carry-forward refresh of every peer | - | Creates/updates `…similarity` rows |
| `action_view_similar` | prompt | Opens generators above the similarity floor | - | - |
| `action_approve_all_drafts` | prompt | Approve every pending draft, one savepoint each | ≥1 draft | Holds drafts with `has_revealing_option` / `has_source_reference` unless `acknowledge_warnings` is in the context; skips failures and logs both; raises only when nothing got through |
| `action_approve` | draft | Draft → bank question | state `draft`; not a `NON_GENERATABLE_QUESTION_TYPES` type; image types must have `_current_images` unless `skip_image_ready_guard` context | Creates the question; materializes dimensions, images, videos, the authored label key; runs `_assert_no_key_drift` for image_ab; writes `state='approved'` + `approved_question_id`. An unconfirmed planted flaw only WARNS |
| `action_deny` | draft | Reject | state `draft` | `state='denied'`, chatter rollup. Approve and Deny act on `draft` rows only and return a notification saying how many they decided and how many were already decided |
| `action_rebuild_answer_key_from_json` | draft | Rebuild `answer_dimension_ids` from the JSON columns | - | Replaces the relational key wholesale (`(5,0,0)`) |
| `action_retry_video_generation` | draft | Retry only the failed clips | must be a video type; must have briefs; Veo configured; refuses when every slot is already done | Drops failed slots' ops, `video_state='pending'`, clears `video_error` |
| `action_apply_uploaded_image` | draft | Store the uploaded image into a slot | `upload_image` set | Rewrites `images_json`, `image_state='uploaded'`, clears the binary |
| `action_apply_uploaded_video` `question.py` | question | Store an uploaded clip into a slot | `upload_video` set | Unlinks the existing clip in that slot, creates a `question.video`, clears the binary |
| `action_detect_now` `question.py` | question | Force detection on the Single image | type must be `image_label`; a Single image must exist | Delegates to the image row |
| `action_detect_now` `question_image.py` | question.image | Detection on one image | type `image_label`, slot `single`, has image, `detection_attempts < 3` | Writes `detections_json` + annotated image; increments `detection_attempts` on failure |
| `action_capture_url` `question_image.py` | question.image | Live-DOM capture | `source_url` set; Playwright available | Overwrites `image`, `dom_manifest_json`, `behavioural_key_json`, `detections_json`, `capture_viewport`, `annotated_image`, `coverage_expected`, `omitted_element_json` |
| `action_offload_images_s3` `question.py` | question | Push on-record binaries to S3 | - | Sets `image_url` (does not clear the Binary) |
| `action_export_json` / `action_export_csv` / `action_export_native_json` `question.py` | question | Exports; `_export_native` is the lossless round-trip partner of `import_bank_native` | falls back to `search([])` on an empty recordset | CSV cells are prefixed against formula injection |
| `action_merge_tags` `tag.py` | tag | Merge selected tags into the most-used survivor | ≥2 tags | Repoints `prompt.tag_ids`, **unlinks the losers**. No Vertex call |
| `action_import` `bank_import_wizard.py` | wizard | Routes to harness / native / CSV import (in that order, the order `detected_format` sniffs) | file attached | CSV creates a generator with `state='done'` and leaves every row a DRAFT in Pending Approvals, as harness JSON does; only a native export goes straight into the live bank. A failed import keeps nothing (the API rolls back before its 422). Closes the dialog with a notification |
