#### 3. Scoring and grading

**Rewritten from source on 25 August 2026.** The unit of scoring changed from the QUESTION to
the COMPONENT; everything in the 11 August version of this subsection that described a blend,
a weight, or a coverage ceiling was describing code that no longer exists. Section 2.1 #4 has
the marking rule; this section has the machinery that produces the numbers it marks.

##### 3.0 The rule, restated so this section stands alone

Every component is worth exactly 1 mark and is won or lost on its own. A component is a KEYED
dimension, or the LLM-graded free-text answer, or a labelling box set. `earned =
sum(response.final_mark)`; `possible = evaluator._paper_component_totals()[0]`, summed over the
DRAWN questions. Objective components carry no raw and are excluded from the raw's numerator
and denominator alike.

##### 3.1 What makes a response need LLM grading

`needs_llm` is a stored computed field (`_compute_scoring_kind`, `models/assessment.py`):

- `image_ab` -> `bool(line_ids) and not is_placeholder`;
- `subjective_rubric`, `image_prompt`, `image_label`, `video_prompt` -> that type **and** a
  non-empty `justification` **and** not a placeholder;
- everything else -> `False`.

`is_placeholder` = the `auto_submitted` flag, or (legacy rows only) a `justification` starting
`"[Auto-submitted"`. The PII scrubber writes the sentinel `"[anonymized]"` specifically because
an empty string would flip `needs_llm` to `False` and silently drop the answer from the cohort
denominator.

An `image_ab` answer reaches the grader only when `_image_ab_uses_llm` is true, and that is
**no longer a setting.** It used to AND in the assessment's
`require_justification_image_comparison`, so an operator could switch `image_ab` to
verdict-only - which never reached the LLM at all while `needs_llm` stayed true, so the
awaiting-scoring counters and the rescore button kept counting answers the grader had
short-circuited. That flag is gone from the model and from the write allow-lists. What remains
is degenerate, not configured: an answer with nothing written in it has no justification to
mark, and a question with no `official_reasoning` has no standard to mark one against, so both
fall to the verdict-only store rather than paying for an LLM call whose result could not be
trusted.

##### 3.2 Response-level states

`response.llm_state`: `not_needed`, `pending`, `queued`, `scored`, `failed` (recoverable, the
cron retries), `error` (terminal, surfaced - explicitly *not* a silent 0). Beside it,
`response.rescore_request_key` marks an answer an admin asked to have re-graded (§3.3a).
`evaluator.llm_state`: `pending`, `scoring`, `scored`, `partial`, `failed`, `error`, `cancelled`; rolled up
by `_compute_subjective_rollup`. `evaluator.llm_error` says why a candidate is still waiting: a
deferral, a failed re-grade, or a kill.

##### 3.3 Queue mechanism

1. On submit, `_enqueue_subjective_scoring` sets `llm_state="pending"` and, when the
   assessment's `llm_auto_score` toggle is on, sets `evaluator.scoring_requested = True`.
   **Scoring never runs inline on the candidate's submit path.** Verdict-only `image_ab`
   answers are resolved immediately in code.
2. H-16 loop guard: a response already `scored` whose `_graded_answer_hash()` equals the stored
   `llm_scored_hash` is **not** re-queued, closing a candidate-driven cost loop. The hash is the
   sha256 of the justification, plus the A/B picks on an `image_ab`, and since round 3 (A-257)
   an `image_ab` the grader reads goes through the same guard (it used to re-queue on every
   unchanged re-post). One-time effect: an `image_ab` scored before round 3 carries the old
   text-only hash, so its first re-post re-queues once.
3. `evaluator.write` also auto-queues on `state == "submitted"` when `llm_auto_score` is on.
4. Manual entry points, each reached from Odoo and from the API:
   `assessment.action_llm_score_all` (Run Subjective Evaluation / Score All),
   `assessment.action_llm_score_failed` → `evaluator.action_reset_failed_scoring` (Retry Failed
   Scoring: `failed` and `error` answers back to `pending` with `llm_attempts` 0),
   `evaluator.action_queue_llm_score` (`POST /scoring/queue` with ids), and the re-score requests
   of §3.3a.
5. The cron drains evaluators matching `state="submitted"` AND `scoring_requested=True` AND
   `llm_state in ("pending","scoring","partial","failed")`, on an active, not-`cancelled` paper,
   attempt not erased (`_scoring_shard_evaluators`). Candidates with a re-score request come
   first, in any `llm_state`; the queue fills what is left of the tick.

**Every queueing action follows the same rules:**

- **Refused on a cancelled paper** (`_check_scoring_not_cancelled`, a `UserError`): grading
  spends an LLM call per answer. Kill and Archive stay available on a cancelled paper.
- **Refused while a Kill is still stopping** (`_check_scoring_not_stopping`: `RescoreRefused`
  code `stopping`, 409 on the API), checked before anything is written - the lane's next
  checkpoint would otherwise park the new work straight back to `cancelled`.
- **A candidate a running lane holds is skipped, never rewritten** (`_being_graded`, §3.3a): a
  commit into rows a lane holds hands the lane a SerializationFailure, and its paid results are
  rolled back and bought again. The toast says "Skipped N candidate(s) being graded right now";
  the API reply counts them as `skipped`. Both Release actions follow the same rule.
- **The kill is withdrawn only by a click that actually queued or reset something**, and never
  while a lane is still stopping (`_withdraw_scoring_kill`).
- Each saves the paper's last-run tally first (`_remember_scoring_tally`) and returns a `next`
  that reloads the Odoo form, so the status badge starts polling.

`scoring_requested` is written back to `False` by a kill (the candidate is parked `cancelled`)
and by erasure - never by a finished run. A normal run ends because the evaluator's `llm_state`
leaves the drain set.

##### 3.3a Individual re-score, and what "being graded" means

**A re-score is a request, not a grade** (W6). `action_rescore_individually` (the attempt form's
"Re-score N answer(s)", the answer form's "Re-score This Answer", `POST /attempts/<id>/rescore`)
writes one random `rescore_request_key` on each chosen answer - those rows only, never the
candidate's own row, which belongs to the lane - and grades nothing in the request. With no
questions chosen it takes every answer that needs the grader and has no mark; a scored answer may
be chosen. The refusals, each writing nothing, are in §2.1 #11. A released attempt needs an
explicit confirm, because the grader runs at temperature 0.2 and the new mark can differ from the
one the candidate saw.

**The lane grades them first, on their own.** `_scoring_shard_evaluators` deals keyed candidates
ahead of the queue. `begin_evaluator` grades only the chosen answers when the candidate was not
otherwise queued, groups them by key so one click's answers go in calls of their own (noted
`rescore(n)` on the ledger), and never sends them through a question-group cache. A key on an
answer that no longer needs the grader (its question changed type) is dropped instead of heading
every tick.

**The old mark stands until the new one succeeds.** A failed re-grade of a scored answer
(`_is_regrade`) writes nothing on the answer, drops the key, and puts "Re-score of <question>
failed, its previous mark was kept: <reason>" on the attempt's `llm_error`. Key drift on an
`image_ab` re-grade keeps the mark the same way, and so does a labelling re-grade whose reply
left an answered box unscored: it is never scored from the boxes that survived. The chatter
records who asked, for which answers, and each answer's previous mark, model and prompt version.

**`_being_graded` is the one definition of "a lane holds this candidate".** `llm_state =
"scoring"` alone is not proof - a lane that died leaves it behind, and such a row is nobody's.
The candidate's lane (`evaluator id % scoring_shards`) must also hold its advisory lock right now,
read from `pg_locks`, which takes no lock (`_live_lane_shards`); a lock whose session has been
silent for over 60 minutes (`LANE_LOCK_SILENCE_LIMIT`) does not count. Kill, both Releases, Score
All, queue, reset, re-score, the threshold edit and `_clear_finished_scoring_kills` all ask it. A
Kill parks a `scoring` row whose lane is dead; a poll does not pay for the `pg_locks` read, so
such a row reads as running until its lane is back or a Kill parks it.

##### 3.4 Sharding

`_scoring_shard_count` reads `assessments_be_v2.scoring_shards` (default `"1"`) and clamps to
`[1, MAX_SCORING_SHARDS]` where `MAX_SCORING_SHARDS = 4` (`constants.py`).
`_cron_llm_auto_score(shard=N)` returns immediately if `shard >= shard_count` - **before**
taking any lock - so shards 1-3 are pure no-ops at the default setting even though their cron
records are `active=True`. Shard 0 keeps `ADVISORY_LOCK_AUTOSCORE`; shards >= 1 use
`ADVISORY_LOCK_AUTOSCORE_SHARD_BASE + shard` (`_lane_lock`). A lane holds its lock for the whole
tick, which is how `_live_lane_shards` can tell a running lane from a dead one.

Slicing is `id % shard_count == shard`, applied in Python after an ordered `search`, which
keeps the per-shard limit exact without ORM-version-specific raw SQL. Per-tick throughput is
`assessments_be_v2.scoring_tick_limit` (default 20, per shard; a value < 1 falls back to 20,
`_scoring_tick_limit`). `res_config_settings._check_be_llm_limits` refuses an out-of-range
`scoring_shards` at the WRITE path rather than clamping silently, because a silently-ignored
`shards=8` is worse to operate than a refusal.

`constants.py` states the invariant explicitly: `MAX_SCORING_SHARDS` must equal the number of
shard cron records in `data/cron.xml`, or evaluators in an unserved shard would never be
scored. Currently both are 4 (shards 0-3).

**Calls in flight per lane** (W5). A lane spends nearly all its time waiting on Vertex, so it
keeps up to `scoring_parallel_calls` candidates' judge calls on the wire at once
(`_drain_in_parallel`; default 4, range 1-8 in `constants.SETTING_RANGES`; 1 is the serial loop).
The worker pool only ever holds CALLS. Each candidate is planned on the lane's cursor
(`scoring.begin_evaluator` with `parallel_dispatch`); each call runs on a cursor of its own that
only reads (settings, the budget and rate gates, the kill flag - its ledger row goes through
`_write_ledger_row`'s own committed cursor); every mark is stored back on the lane's cursor, one
candidate per savepoint (`finish_evaluator`). The lane keeps exactly one writer. Once the window
is full, the FIRST candidate whose calls are all back is stored (`_pop_first_ready`), so one slow
call cannot idle the other slots. A tick that dies cancels the calls not yet sent.

`_scoring_parallel_calls` lowers the setting to what the database pool allows. Each call holds
about 2 connections, and all lanes together may take at most half of `db_maxconn` (HTTP requests
draw on the same pool), less 2 per lane for its own cursors: `(db_maxconn / 2 - 2 x lanes) /
(2 x lanes)`, at least 1 and at most the setting. Odoo's default pool of 64 gives 3 per lane at 4
shards; prod's 600 gives the full setting. Odoo Settings shows the result beside the box as "In use per shard"; `/api/v1/settings` as `scoring.parallel_calls_effective`.
The test cursor cannot share commits with worker cursors, so tests take the serial path
(`vertex._side_cursor_is_safe`).

**One lane tick, in order** (`_cron_llm_auto_score`):
1. The daily spend cap ends the tick before anyone is planned: one `SPEND_CAP daily` WARNING per
   lane, instead of a refusal per candidate deep in the call.
2. Plan up to `scoring_tick_limit` candidates (`_scoring_shard_evaluators`).
3. Per candidate: `_auto_score_eligible` (skip an archived or cancelled paper first, before the
   re-score shortcut, so a Cancel mid-tick stops grading and billing for the rest of the tick -
   round 3, RV1-02; settle a killed one; a re-score request is its own ask), then `_auto_score_mark_scoring` COMMITS `llm_state = "scoring"` before
   any call is sent. That is what Kill reads as "held"; committed with the grading transaction it
   would land after the call, and a Kill in between would park the row and let the call through.
4. A candidate that fails is logged. After a serialization failure the cursor is rolled back, so
   the next candidate gets a fresh snapshot instead of failing the same way after paying for its
   call (`_auto_score_failed`).
5. `_clear_finished_scoring_kills` lowers any kill flag whose held candidates have all been let go
   (archived papers are skipped: their flag is the suspension).
6. A tick that was full AND stored at least one mark re-triggers its own cron at once
   (`_trigger_scoring_lane`); a 704-candidate paper at 20 a tick otherwise spent about 35 minutes
   waiting for the clock. A tick in which every call was deferred (429, a cap, a full pool) waits
   for the clock instead of spinning.

##### 3.5 Batching and the grading call

`begin_evaluator` selects `needs_llm` answers in `llm_state in ("not_needed","pending",
"queued","failed")` (`_BULK_STATES`) - `error` is **excluded**, so a terminally errored answer is
retried only by Retry Failed Scoring or a re-score - plus the answers carrying a re-score key
(§3.3a). Verdict-only `image_ab` items are peeled off and resolved first, free. The calls:

- each re-score click's answers, in chunks of `scoring_batch_size`, never cached;
- fresh bulk answers (`llm_attempts == 0`) in chunks of `assessments_be_v2.scoring_batch_size`
  (default 8, clamped 1-32 at the settings write path), or one call per question group when a
  cache plan applies (§3.5a);
- previously-attempted answers **one at a time** - a retried answer never rides in a batch with
  fresh ones.

The serial lane makes and stores each call in turn (`score_evaluator`); a parallel lane prepares
every call before sending any, so a preparation that raises has not already paid for a call.

`_prepare_submission` per call:

- **Three deterministic pre-passes, each of which skips Vertex entirely.**
  (a) the verdict-only lane, when an `image_ab` justification is blank or the question has no
  `official_reasoning` to mark it against (`_image_ab_uses_llm`);
  (b) `_ab_key_drift` - stored `is_correct` verdicts vs `flaw_plan_json`'s `construction_keys` -
  which scores 0 with `gate="key_drift"` (a re-grade keeps its mark instead);
  (c) `gates_svc.evaluate_gates`, which resolves `empty_answer` or `injection_attempt` to raw 0
  locally (`services/gates.py`, with NFKC normalisation, zero-width stripping and
  Cyrillic/Greek homoglyph folding). If nothing survives the pre-passes there is no Vertex call
  at all.
- **Cost attribution:** a single evaluator id, or `min(ev_ids)` with a warning on a mixed batch.
  Never `False`, which would drop the per-candidate spend cap.
- **The item is TEXT ONLY** (W12). No image, screenshot or clip is attached to any grading call:
  the keys were written from that media and are the complete truth about it, and the prompt says
  so. `_build_item` is the answer `id`, `question_id`, the question's material
  (`_question_material`, per type, empty values left out) and the worker's part - `answer` (a
  labelling answer as its `{box: label}` map) and `picks` on `image_ab`. The material per type:
  `subjective_rubric` and any unlisted type - `task`, `rubric`, `golden_answer`; `image_ab` -
  `task`, `axes` (each axis with its official choice), `official_reasoning`; `image_prompt` /
  `video_prompt` - `task`, `required_elements`, `penalties`, `reference_prompt`, `scoring_guide`;
  `image_label` - `boxes`, `decoys`, and `markers_hidden` when the candidate saw no numbered
  markers (§3.7). `task` is the question's prompt plus its description (Form Studio keeps the
  scenario in the description). The user text is one compact JSON object, `{"items": [...]}`.
- **Rules by type, never by SOP title** (`_grading_rules`): `subjective_rubric` GENERAL,
  `image_ab` P1, `image_label` P3 (UI labelling) or P2 (defect annotation, decided by the
  question's own `detection_mode` and key), `image_prompt` P4, `video_prompt` P5. The SOP title is
  read only as a claim; one pointing at rules the type does not allow adds the flag
  `profile_mismatch`. An item with no key field (`golden_answer`, `rubric`, `official_reasoning`,
  `boxes`, `required_elements`, `reference_prompt`) is flagged `no_answer_key` and graded against
  its task alone (`lacks_answer_key` is the same test, used by the launch warning). The code's
  rules, not the model's echo, are stored in `llm_profile` (`_with_rules`).
- **The call:** `max_tokens = min(64000, max(16000, (6000 if video_prompt else 4000) + 2500 *
  items))`. No call gets less than 16,000: thinking counts toward the limit, small calls were
  being cut off and paid for twice, and only used tokens are billed. `temperature=0.2`,
  `thinking` on when any item is `video_prompt`, `response_json=True`, `json_retry=False`. A
  genuine MAX_TOKENS is retried once with `min(2 x the first ask, the model's max_out)`
  (`_retry_output_tokens`).
- **Re-ask and split** (`_grade_job`): a reply that does not parse is re-asked ONCE
  (`_parse_results` is caught so the re-ask can fire; its error text carries the reply's length,
  never an excerpt). When a reply was cut off (MAX_TOKENS) and left answers out, those answers are
  re-sent at once in two halves (`_regrade_what_did_not_fit`; one split, never more; a failure
  there falls back to the retry path). A cut-off or salvaged reply logs one `REPLY CUT OFF`
  WARNING with ids.
- **Deferrals spend no attempt** (`_store_submission`, then `_settle_submission` for the note): a spend cap (`VertexBudgetError`), a 429
  from Vertex or the local `vertex_max_rpm` ceiling (`VertexQuotaError`), and a full DB pool
  (`PoolError`, or Postgres "too many clients" / "remaining connection slots", turned into a
  `VertexQuotaError` by `_deferred_if_pool_full`) leave the answers `pending` with their whole
  attempt budget, log a WARNING tagged `SPEND_CAP`, `GRADING_QUOTA` or `GRADING_POOL_FULL`, and
  write "Waiting to be graded, no attempt used: <reason>" on the attempt's `llm_error`. A kill
  (`VertexCancelledError`) logs `SCORING_STOPPED` and is raised only after every dispatched
  outcome is stored, so a call that got through keeps its marks. Any other error spends an attempt
  on every answer of the call (`_store_error`) and logs at ERROR with ids.
- **Dispatch:** `judge_model = served_models[-1] if served_models else scoring_model`, so
  `llm_judge_model` stays honest when the fallback model rescued the call. `image_label` results
  go through `_apply_image_label_boxes` before `_store_scored`; a labelling result is judged by
  its `box_scores`, not by its top-level `score`.
- **No write to the paper row.** `finish_evaluator` writes only the candidate's own rows. The
  cohort outlier pass finds its papers from the data (§4, the recompute cron), because a write to
  the one row every lane shares, flushed after a Vertex call, loses serialization races and throws
  billed marks away.

##### 3.5a Question-group caches (W13, ON by default)

Bulk calls repeat the same instructions and question material for every candidate, so a question
group can sit in one Vertex context cache and each call send only the candidate's part. **The
switch is `assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache`: unset means `groups` (`SCORING_CACHE_DEFAULT`);
`0`/`false`/`no`/`off` sends everything inline.** It is on because it only engages where it pays:

- **The plan** (`_cache_plan`, per candidate) exists only when some candidate's paper holds every
  question of the cohort (one shared set; old per-person papers share no groups). The groups are
  the cohort's graded questions (`image_ab` only with `official_reasoning`) by id, `batch` at a
  time, so the shuffle has no effect. **A group under the model's cache minimum is left out**
  (`model_catalog.cache_min_tokens`: 4,096 tokens on Gemini 3.x, 2,048 on 2.x; estimated at about
  4 characters a token); with no group left the candidate is batched exactly as with the cache
  off, which is what today's papers get.
- **The cache** holds the instructions plus ONE block of the group's question material keyed by
  question id - never an answer, pick, name or answer id. Its key is a sha256 over project,
  location, model, prompt version, layout version (`_CACHE_LAYOUT = "questions-v1"`, bumped with
  any change to what a cache holds) and the block, so an edited question gets a new cache. A
  cached call sends only `id`, `question_id`, `answer` and `picks` per item.
- **Create and keep-alive** (`services/grading_cache.py`) run on a short READ COMMITTED cursor of
  their own, never in a candidate's marks transaction. A group's cache is created only when at
  least 2 queued answers need it, by the lane that wins a two-key
  `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(827600, <from the key>)`; a loser uses a live cache or goes inline.
  TTL 900 s, extended back to the full 15 minutes when under 5 are left; within 60 s of expiry a
  cache counts as gone. The spend caps and the kill flag are checked before a create.
- **A cache problem never blocks grading.** `resolve` returns None instead of raising (only a
  spend cap, a kill or a 429 propagate) and the call goes inline. A failed create is not retried
  for its key for 10 minutes (`failed_until`). A cache Vertex no longer has
  (`VertexCacheMissError`) is forgotten and the call resent inline at once, no attempt spent; one
  rejected while still live gets the same 10-minute backoff, so a refused key is not recreated
  once per candidate. API-key auth never caches. A retried answer may use its group's live cache
  but never creates one; a re-score request never uses one.
- **Cost:** creates and refreshes are booked as `scoring_cache_create` / `scoring_cache_refresh`
  with no candidate (input tokens at the model's rate plus storage); cached input on each call
  bills at 10% (`cached_tokens`, §1.6).

##### 3.6 The grading instructions: one shipped text, fingerprinted

`_get_scoring_prompt()` returns the shipped `prompts/scoring.md`, always; if the file cannot be
read, `DEFAULT_SCORING_PROMPT` in `services/scoring.py` holds the same text (a test keeps the two
identical). **There is no override.** A value already stored under
`assessments_be_v2.scoring_system_prompt` is left in place and never read, and the Settings
fields that uploaded one are gone.

19.0.3.23.0 ships the text-only instructions (8,451 characters) with the fingerprint
**`bundled:785826a5`** (`scoring_prompt_version`: `bundled:` plus the first 8 hex of a sha256
over the stripped text). Every grade stores it in `llm_prompt_version`; scores stored before
versioning keep an empty value, never a guess. `current_scoring_prompt_version()` recomputes it
from the file on every call, never cached, so it cannot disagree with what the grader stamps; the
candidate verdict gate compares against it (§2.1 #13). Any edit to `prompts/scoring.md` is a new
fingerprint: every verdict graded before it is withheld from candidates while the gate is on.

What the text asks for, in short:
- grade only against the keys and the task - the media is left out on purpose, and a claim about
  it that the key neither confirms nor contradicts earns nothing and costs nothing;
- the per-type rules §3.5 lists (for `image_ab`, the written answer alone, in bands; for prompt
  writing, `100 x hits / elements` minus keyed penalties);
- score accounting that starts at 100, itemises every lost point as a deduction, and keeps
  `100 + sum(points) = score`;
- `box_scores` per box on `image_label` only; `verdict_consistency` and `checklist_zero_count` on
  every other type; `fabrication_count` on all. The PLATFORM turns those counts into the integrity
  ceilings (§3.9); the prompt applies no cap itself, and asks for no gate;
- plain words in everything the worker reads (`verdict`, `feedback`, deduction and credit
  reasons): no weights, thresholds or arithmetic, and never "rubric", "golden", "official",
  "keyed" or "the key".

The paid synthetic check behind this text (old vs new prompt on made-up answers, three runs) and
the release guard - the first paper graded under it is held until an admin spot-checks about 10
answers - are in `docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` §0.1 and Part 5 §5.6.10.

##### 3.7 Per-box image labelling - `_apply_image_label_boxes`

**THE UNIT IS THE BOX.** The judge returns `box_scores`, one 0-100 per box in the golden key,
and the platform stores every box's raw in `label_box_scores_json`. Nothing here decides pass
or fail: the mark is decided downstream, per box, against the assessment's threshold, so moving
the threshold re-decides a labelling question with **no LLM call**.

What the platform enforces over the judge:

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| A box the candidate never attempted scores 0 whatever the judge said | Judges reward a plausible-looking blank surprisingly often, and a box with nothing in it cannot have been answered well. "Attempted" needs >= 2 non-space characters (`_label_attempted_box_numbers`), or a worker farms coverage by typing "x" in every box |
| A box outside the golden key is dropped | The judge does not get to invent boxes and score them |
| A box the judge omitted scores 0, and still counts | **The denominator is the question's own box count** (`_label_total_boxes`), so a judge that returns one box out of twenty cannot make a one-box answer look complete |
| A reply that left an ATTEMPTED box unscored is not scored yet | A cut-off per-box reply reads exactly like wrong labels. `_store_error` leaves the answer `failed` for a whole re-grade while attempts remain - a reply with no `box_scores` at all included; only the last attempt scores the partial reply, because an answer that never scores strands the paper. A re-grade of a scored answer is never scored partially: it fails and keeps its old mark (§3.3a) |

**What the judge is sent** (`_label_boxes`): `boxes`, box number -> what a correct label says,
from the first source that has any - the behavioural key (a UI control and its action), else the
detections (the element or defect, with its description), else an authored `ideal_labels` map.
Free text or a list names no numbered box, so such a question counts as having no key.
`_label_total_boxes` counts exactly these boxes, so the denominator is what the judge was sent.
`decoys` are things that must not be flagged; a flagged decoy or a defect keyed for another box
scores near 0, below a blank box.

**`markers_hidden`** (`_label_markers_hidden`) goes with the item when the candidate saw no
numbered markers: detections exist, there is no behavioural key, the question is not a UI
screenshot (a UI `detection_mode` or a live-DOM capture), and not every detection carries a
drawable `box_2d`. The judge then matches each label to a different keyed box by meaning, in any
order, and reports `box_scores` under the worker's own numbers. Otherwise a label counts only for
the box number it was written under.

The item's own 0-100 becomes the MEAN of the box raws (`composed_raw_100`), so every consumer
that reads `llm_raw_100` as "how good was this answer" - the outlier detector, the progress
rollup, the CSV export - keeps working. The MARK is never taken from it.

Downstream, `response._label_marks(threshold)` returns `(mark, raw, fraction)`: each box is
thresholded on its own raw, `fraction` is the share that cleared, and the component's single
mark is that fraction tested against the same bar. 18 of 20 boxes at a 60% bar is 0.9, which
clears; 11 of 20 is 0.55, which does not. `raw` is the ungated twin, the mean of the box raws
as 0.0-1.0. A question with no answer key at all returns `(0, 0, 0)` - it still costs its mark,
because an authoring fault is not a candidate failure to hide.

**The old coverage ceiling is gone and is not missed.** It clamped a whole-item score to
`100 * attempted/total`, which was only ever a proxy for "you cannot score on boxes you never
addressed". Scoring those boxes 0 directly says the same thing exactly rather than
approximately, and it removes the advisory-only gap where a candidate who labelled 6 of 10
boxes should have been ceilinged at 60 but in practice only raised a review flag.

##### 3.8 The `image_ab` lanes, after the blend

The judge scores only the WRITTEN answer of an `image_ab`, against `official_reasoning`, each
axis's official choice and the worker's own `picks`, in bands (85-100 names the deciding
difference concretely and agrees with the picks; 1-29 contradicts them). The picks themselves
are marked by the platform.

`_store_ab_verdict_only` settles an `image_ab` whose justification box was left empty, or whose
question has no `official_reasoning` to mark it against. **The
verdicts are not scored on this lane any more** - each verdict axis is its own keyed dimension,
marked deterministically by `_dimension_marks` on the answer, so folding them into a 0-100 raw
here would score them twice. What the lane still has to do is CLOSE the subjective component:
the candidate wrote nothing, so the written answer scores 0 and the attempt stops waiting on
it. Leaving `llm_state` unscored would hold the whole result at "pending" forever.
`_score_ab_verdicts` still runs, but its number is recorded for audit only.

`_ab_scores_audit(verdict_score, justification_score, blend)` keeps its three-key shape so
stored history stays readable, but there are **no weights any more** and `blend` now carries
the justification alone.

The 60-point overall-wrong cap went with the blend. It existed to punish a wrong OVERALL (OC)
preference through a number that no longer exists; the Overall Choice axis is now a component
of its own and is simply marked wrong, which is both the same penalty and a legible one.
`_ab_overall_correct` survives as the P1 deciding-dimension check for the audit.

##### 3.9 Trust-but-verify scoring math

- `_strip_platform_keys` removes `composed_raw_100`, `ab_scores`, `label_scores`, `recomputed`
  and `recompute_note` from every judge result before use. A hallucinated or injected
  `"composed_raw_100": 100` would otherwise short-circuit the recompute gate and score a wrong
  answer perfect.
- `_recompute_deductions` re-derives `score = 100 + sum(deduction points)`. An empty deductions
  array is trusted as 100 only if the judge also emitted >= 99.5.
- `_recompute_v10` is the legacy weighted recompute (key-closeness 0.60 / SOP-coverage 0.25 /
  clarity 0.15). The current prompt emits no `golden_claims` / `elements` / `clarity`, so it
  returns `(None, None)` for today's replies and `_verified_judge_100` has no caller. Note that those two weights are the **generic
  subjective rubric lanes** and have nothing to do with the removed `image_ab` blend; do not
  read `weight 0.60` in a UI and conclude the blend is back.
- Integrity ceilings (`_apply_ceilings`, from `SCORE_CEILINGS` in `constants.py`):
  `verdict_contradiction` -> 25, `multi_checklist_zero` (>= 2) -> 55, `fabrication` (count >= 1
  or a `fabricat*`/`hallucinat*` flag) -> 25. The prompt reports the counts
  (`verdict_consistency`, `checklist_zero_count`, `fabrication_count`) and never applies a cap
  itself; only the platform does. `multi_checklist_zero` is not applied to `image_prompt` /
  `video_prompt`, whose score is already `100 x hits / elements`.
- A positive deduction is read as its magnitude (an ordinary LLM sign error would otherwise score
  a deficient answer 100); the WARNING names the answer id, never the reason, which quotes the
  worker.
- `llm_profile` is stamped from the code's own choice of rules (`_with_rules`), never from the
  model's echo, with the review flags that came with it (`profile_mismatch`, `no_answer_key`).
- **`_store_scored` never writes pass/fail or the earned mark.** Both are derived live from
  `llm_raw_100` (or the per-box raws) and the subjective threshold by `_compute_subjective_marks`,
  and the attempt's Pass/Fail from the marks and the pass threshold by `_compute_result`, so a
  change to either threshold re-decides results without re-scoring. This is the single property that
  makes threshold tuning cheap, and it is easy to break by "helpfully" storing a mark.
- Candidate-facing feedback is `it["feedback"] or it["verdict"]` and **never** `reasoning`.
  The labelling lane and the integrity-ceiling path append internal scoring math to `reasoning`
  (`"[image_label per-box: 20 box(es) in the key, ...]"`), which is admin-only and must not
  reach a candidate's Review Answers screen.

##### 3.10 Attempt counting and failure recording

`_store_error`:

- `attempts = (llm_attempts or 0) + 1`;
- if `attempts >= _max_attempts(env)` -> `llm_state="error"`, `llm_raw_100=0.0`, feedback
  suffixed `" (surfaced as a scoring error after N attempts)"`;
- else -> `llm_state="failed"` (inside the cron's re-selection domain, so it retries);
- a queued RE-GRADE of a scored answer is the exception: nothing is written on the answer, the
  key is dropped and the reason goes on the attempt's `llm_error` (§3.3a);
- every branch logs with ids: `answer failed ... attempt=n/N` at WARNING, `ANSWER TERMINAL` at
  ERROR (the one event that needs a human), `RE-GRADE FAILED` at WARNING. A terminal error also
  drops a queued re-score key. Grading and provisioning log lines carry ids, never a candidate's
  name, email or answer text (`services/audit.py`); a parse or refusal error states the reply's
  length, not an excerpt.

The write rides the candidate's savepoint, which the lane commits after each candidate, so the
counter persists and an answer cannot be re-picked and re-billed forever.

An exhausted response resolves to a surfaced `error`, never a silent scored-0 - which would be
indistinguishable from a genuine low score.

`_max_attempts` reads `assessments_be_v2.llm_max_attempts`, default 3, coercing a
non-positive/unparseable value back to 3. The settings form clamps it to 1-5.

`_store_gated` synthesises a full result dict and hands it to `_store_scored`, so a gated answer
lands in exactly the same shape as a graded one - with no `_judge_model_version`, so
`llm_judge_model` ends up empty for a path that never called the model.

**Only a real LLM call spends an attempt** (round 3, A-262). `_store_scored(resp, it,
count_attempt=True)` adds 1 to `llm_attempts`; the three stores that make no call pass
`count_attempt=False`: the verdict-only A/B lane (`_store_ab_verdict_only`), the platform gates
(`_store_gated`) and the A/B key-drift settle (`_store_ab_key_drift`). `_store_error` still counts.

Higher levels: the lane wraps each candidate in its own savepoint, and `_llm_score_guarded`
records `llm_state="failed"` + `llm_error` on failure (or `cancelled` on a kill, `pending` on an
archive), so one bad answer cannot take down a cohort. The cron catches, logs and `continue`s.

##### 3.11 There is no per-type scoring code, and there must not be

`services/scoring.py` ends with back-compat aliases:

```python
_score_image_ab_items = _score_image_prompt_items \
    = _score_image_label_items = _score_subjective_items
```

Every subjective lane funnels through the SAME `_prepare_submission` / `_store_submission`
path. The differences that do exist are data - the per-type question material, the rules table
(`_TYPE_RULES`), the per-box post-pass - not branches in the scoring flow. Do not add type-specific logic here.

##### 3.11a What ARCHIVING an assessment actually does (19.0.3.22.0)

`active` used to be pure visibility. It now **suspends the cost-intensive and queued
work, reversibly** - and nothing else. Caught in `assessments.be.write()` rather than in
`action_archive`, because the Flutter console archives by writing `active` directly while
the back office calls the action, and only `write` is on both paths.

**What archive DOES:**

- Three crons stop selecting the paper's candidates, each through an explicit
  `("assessment_id.active", "=", True)` term: `_cron_llm_auto_score`,
  `_cron_send_pending_invitations`, `_cron_expire_stale_attempts`. The term is written
  out because `assessments.be.evaluator` has **no `active` column of its own**, so Odoo's
  `active_test` never reached it - an archived paper went on being graded by Vertex, went
  on emailing invitations, and went on auto-submitting sittings.
- `_suspend_scoring_for_archive()` raises `scoring_cancel_requested`, which the grading
  lane reads back on a fresh cursor before its **next** billable call. That is the only
  way to reach the one candidate a worker is already holding. The single call already on
  the wire completes and is billed.
- Nothing is snapshotted. `scoring_requested`, `llm_state`, `invite_state` and
  `threshold_recompute_pending` are left exactly as they were, so the untouched rows ARE
  the saved state and `_resume_scoring_from_archive()` needs no replay step. Restore lowers
  the flag DIRECTLY, not through `_withdraw_scoring_kill`: that one keeps the flag up while a
  lane holds a candidate, and a restored paper with the flag up reads as a Kill - the lane
  would park its whole queue `cancelled`. An archive is not a kill.

**What archive DOES NOT do - and any doc that says otherwise is wrong:**

- **It does not pause a sitting and it does not stop the clock.** `deadline_datetime` is
  `started_at + duration_minutes`, an absolute wall-clock instant, and archiving never
  touches it. Nothing gives a candidate time back on restore.
- **It does not close the exam.** Every candidate gate - `exam_state`, `exam_begin`,
  `exam_answer`, `exam_submit` - tests `assessment_id.state != "in_progress"`, not
  `active`. An archived but still `in_progress` paper is fully sittable, and
  `/api/v1/exam/<token>/answer` still auto-submits each candidate at their ORIGINAL
  deadline. The one thing suspended is `_cron_expire_stale_attempts`, the safety net for
  people who closed the tab.
- Because of that, `POST .../archive` refuses with `live_attempts` (409) when anyone is
  `in_progress`, and names the count, unless `confirm_live_attempts` is sent
  (`write.py::_live_attempt_refusal`). The back-office Archive (`action_archive`) refuses
  outright with a `UserError` naming the count (19.0.3.23.0). The Odoo delete wizard has no
  second round trip to refuse in, so it states `live_count` on the one dialog instead.
- **The PII retention sweep is deliberately NOT suspended** (`_cron_purge_stale_pii` has
  no `active` term, and the omission is commented as intentional). Retention is a legal
  duty with its own clock; pausing it would make Archive a one-click way to park PII
  indefinitely. It scrubs free text and keeps the numeric result, so nothing an unarchive
  needs is destroyed.
- `scoring_phase` reads **`idle`** on an archived paper, not `stopping`, even though
  `scoring_cancel_requested` stays raised while it is filed away. See §3.11b.
- **Archive does not park a dead lane's `scoring` row; Cancel does** (round 3). `action_cancel`
  runs `_park_unheld_scoring`, which sets `llm_state = cancelled` on `scoring` rows no live lane
  holds, so a crashed lane cannot keep the deploy gate shut on a cancelled paper. Archive keeps
  `llm_state` as it is (an archive/unarchive round trip must resume exactly), so an archived paper
  with a dead lane's row still needs Kill or an unarchive.

##### 3.11b `scoring_phase` is a total function

`assessments.be.scoring_phase` (non-stored compute, `_compute_scoring_progress`) resolves
in this order, and every input is something ACTUALLY IN FLIGHT rather than a flag:

| test | phase |
|---|---|
| `not active` | `idle` |
| `scoring_cancel_requested` **and (`running` or `queued`)** | `stopping` |
| `running` | `scoring` |
| `queued`, paper not `cancelled`, and `_scoring_drainer_health()["blocked"]` | `stalled` |
| `queued`, paper not `cancelled` | `queued` |
| else | `idle` |

A cancelled paper's queue never moves - the lanes skip cancelled papers - so it reads `idle`
rather than `queued` or `stalled`.

**`stopping` cannot latch, and the `(running or queued)` conjunction is why.**
`action_kill_scoring` deliberately leaves `scoring_cancel_requested` raised while a lane
is mid-call, and the lane that consumes the kill parks itself without lowering it; the flag
comes down only when that lane's tick ends (`_clear_finished_scoring_kills`). Read off the flag
alone the phase would say `stopping` with nothing running and nothing queued: the Kill
button offering to stop a run that has already stopped, and the header badge polling every 3s
for a change that is not coming. The archive branch above avoids
the same trap, because archive leaves that flag raised for as long as the paper is filed
away. **A state with no exit cannot be entered.**

`queued` is `scoring_requested = True` and `llm_state in (pending, partial, failed)` -
the drainer's own selection predicate - plus candidates with a queued re-score request not
already counted as queued or running. `running` is `llm_state = "scoring"` - the same
predicate the kill uses. `awaiting_scoring_count` is a DIFFERENT question ("work
remaining") and is the wrong gate for the Kill button: `llm_state` defaults to `pending`,
so a candidate who was never queued is indistinguishable from one who is first in line.

`_scoring_drainer_health()` (`@api.model`) is the ONE definition of "the grader is dead",
shared by this compute and by `GET /api/v1/scoring`'s `drainer.stalled`; it was worked out
inline in the route, which is why the console had a stalled banner and the Odoo header had
none. It scopes by `model_id.model = "assessments.be"` (the decommissioned
`etp_assessment_pro` crons carry the same method name) **and only counts the shards that
are supposed to run** - shard 0 always runs, shards 1-3 return at their first line until
`scoring_shards` is raised, so counting every record flat made one legitimately-disabled
higher shard enough to declare the grader dead at the shipped default. Missing records
count as blocked: a shard with no cron to drive it drains nobody. **A tick still running is not
overdue**: Odoo advances `nextcall` only when a run ends, and one tick can take past 15 minutes,
so a lane holding its lock (`_running_cron_ids`, read from `pg_locks`) is left out of `overdue`.
`GET /api/v1/scoring` passes its verdict in the context (`be_drainer_health`) so the phase
compute does not ask twice.
**A lane that is not moving is blocked too** (W4 P0 b): a shard whose oldest queued row
(`write_date`) is past 15 minutes, with nothing of that shard stored (`llm_scored_at`) or picked
up since, lands in `health["stuck"]` (`{shard: queued}`) and the console `reason` names it
("grading shard 2 has stored nothing in 15 minutes ..."). A tick that skips because its lane's
lock is held logs `SCORING_LANE_BLOCKED shard=N queued=M` when that shard has queued work, and
nothing when it does not. Pinned by `tests/test_a_blocked_lane_is_visible.py`.

**The tally line.** `scoring_summary` and "Scored N/M on <date>" come from the same compute.
Scored is counted by ANSWERS (`_answers_scored_domain`: submitted, and no answer that needs the
grader is left unscored), so an objective-only candidate - never graded, never `scored` - counts.
While a run is live the tally saved when it started (`_remember_scoring_tally`) stays on screen;
the live count replaces it only once it is newer and has caught up (a forced re-grade resets
marks, and the tally must not count backwards).

##### 3.12 Backfilling after the rule change

`final_mark` is a STORED compute, and Odoo recomputes a stored compute when one of its
DEPENDENCIES moves - not when the method that produces it is edited. Every row written under
the old rule therefore still holds the old number, and stale rows are not frozen: they flip one
at a time the next time a rescore or a threshold edit happens to touch a dependency, so the
same attempt reads differently on two different days for no visible reason.

`tools/backfill_final_marks.py` recomputes them. Two things it deliberately cannot do:

- **It recomputes; it does not re-grade.** An `image_label` answer scored before the per-box
  contract has no per-box raws on disk, and an `image_ab` answer's stored `llm_raw_100` is the
  old blend rather than the justification alone. Those need a real rescore.
- **Scores move in BOTH directions.** A candidate who got two of three parts right gains; one
  who cleared a low bar on a question whose parts were mostly wrong can lose. Expect most rows
  to move, not a few.

##### 3.13 Removed from grading in 19.0.3.23.0 (history)

Each line is a claim earlier editions of this section made; the current behaviour is above.

- The stored scoring-prompt override. (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: `assessments_be_v2.scoring_system_prompt` is never read, its Settings upload fields are gone, `tools/check_scoring_prompt.py` is deleted, and `llm_prompt_version` is always `bundled:...` - §3.6.)
- Media on grading calls. (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: no image, screenshot or clip is attached; `_media_parts_for`, `constants.MEDIA_QUESTION_TYPES` and the "NO MEDIA AVAILABLE ... media_unseen" note are gone, and `thinking` keys on `video_prompt` answers rather than an attached clip - §3.5.)
- Picking the scoring profile from the SOP title (`detect_project`). (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: the question type picks the rules; the title is only checked, and a mismatch is flagged `profile_mismatch` - §3.5.)
- The per-call preamble with `judge_model` / `pass_threshold` / `item_id` and the coverage-gate constraint on labelling items. (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: the reply is `{"results": [...]}` echoing `id`; labelling items carry `boxes` and `decoys`.)
- `max_tokens = min(64000, (6000 if has_video else 4000) + 2500 * items)` with a 16,000 retry ceiling. (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: a 16,000 floor, and a grading retry of twice the first ask capped at the model's `max_out` - §3.5.)
- A 429 or a spend cap spending grading attempts. (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: a 429, the local rate ceiling and a full DB pool now defer like a spend cap - answers stay `pending`, no attempt spent, the reason on the attempt's `llm_error` - §3.5.)
- `evaluator.action_llm_score` as a public "grade now" action, and `scoring_requested` "never written back to False". (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: `_action_llm_score` is private to the lane, and a kill and erasure lower `scoring_requested` - §3.3.)
- Grading raising `score_outlier_stale` on the paper row after each candidate. (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: no lane writes the paper row; staleness is derived from `score_outlier_checked_at` - §4.)

#### 5. Concurrency

##### 5.1 Advisory locks

All keys are defined in `constants.py` with the comment that they must stay mutually unique module-wide.

| Key | Constant | Taken by | Type | Behaviour when not acquired |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 827393 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_AUTOSCORE` | `_cron_llm_auto_score(shard=0)` `assessment.py` | session `pg_try_advisory_lock`, held for the whole tick | silent `return` |
| 827451/2/3 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_AUTOSCORE_SHARD_BASE` (827450) `+ shard` | shard crons 1-3, same call site (`_lane_lock`) | session try, whole tick | silent `return` |
| 827394 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_IMAGE_RENDER` | `_cron_render_pending_images` `prompt.py` | session try | silent `return` |
| 827395 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_IMAGE_DETECT` | `_cron_detect_image_labels` `question_image.py` | session try | silent `return` |
| 827396 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_VIDEO_POLL` | `_cron_poll_video_ops` `prompt.py` | session try | silent `return` |
| 827397 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_EXPIRE_ATTEMPTS` | `_cron_expire_stale_attempts` `assessment.py` | session try | silent `return` |
| 827398 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_INVITE_SEND` | `_cron_send_pending_invitations` `assessment.py` | session try | silent `return` (prevents duplicate invite emails) |
| 827399 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_PII_PURGE` | `_cron_purge_expired_pii` `assessment.py` | session try | silent `return` |
| 827400 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_SKILL_EXTRACT` | **nothing** - imported at `prompt.py`, never used | - | dead constant |
| 827401 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_QUESTION_GEN` | `_cron_generate_from_sop` `prompt.py` | session try | silent `return` |
| 827402 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_TAG_EXTRACT` | `_cron_extract_tags` `prompt.py` (the button only queues) | session try | silent `return` |
| 827500 | `ADVISORY_LOCK_VERTEX_BEARER` | `_minted_bearer` `vertex.py`, on its own short cursor (§1.3) | **transaction** `pg_advisory_xact_lock` (blocking) | waits, then re-reads the cache |
| 827600 + a key from the cache key | `ADVISORY_LOCK_SCORING_CACHE` (19.0.3.23.0) | `grading_cache._try_lock`, before a cache create or extend, on its own short cursor | **transaction** two-key `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(ns, key)`; two-key locks never collide with the one-key locks above | the call uses a live cache as it is, or goes inline |

Session locks must stay session-level: an xact lock would be released by the first per-record `commit` and let a second worker double-process (`prompt.py`, `question_image.py`).

**A lane's lock doubles as its heartbeat.** `_live_lane_shards` reads the granted advisory locks
from `pg_locks` (joined to `pg_stat_activity`), and the live lease rows in lease mode
(`_held_cron_locks`), taking no lock itself, to tell a running lane
from a dead one (`_being_graded`, §3.3a) and a running tick from an overdue cron
(`_running_cron_ids`). A lock whose session has been silent for over 60 minutes does not count,
so one leaked onto a pooled connection cannot hide a dead grader for ever.

**One door: `services/locks.cron_lock`** (W4 P0 a). The nine session locks above are taken and
released only there (a static sweep in `test_every_cron_takes_its_lock_through_one_door`). A busy
tick with work waiting logs `CRON_LOCK_BUSY name=.. key=.. queued=N` once (the scoring lane keeps
`SCORING_LANE_BLOCKED`), so "silent `return`" above means an empty queue only. Release is per key;
a tick that died on a DB error has its aborted transaction rolled back first, so the unlock runs.
An unlock that returns false logs `CRON_LOCK_UNLOCK_FALSE name=.. key=..`. A busy count that fails
(the lane's included) logs `queued count failed, read as 0` and the tick still returns.
**What this removed:** the four `assessment.py` takers began with `pg_advisory_unlock_all`, which
drops every advisory lock on the backend, so on a shared server connection it could release
ANOTHER lane's lock.
**What it did not fix: PgBouncer.** Prod's main database connection already goes through PgBouncer
and its pool mode is UNCONFIRMED. Under transaction pooling session advisory locks are unsafe
today: the lock and its unlock can land on different server connections, and the unlock then
logs `CRON_LOCK_UNLOCK_FALSE`. That line is evidence of transaction pooling; its absence is not
proof of session pooling (an unlock can land on the same server connection by chance). With
`pg_advisory_unlock_all` gone a leaked level no longer heals on the next tick; it persists until
PgBouncer closes that server connection and shows as `CRON_LOCK_BUSY` / `SCORING_LANE_BLOCKED` on
every tick that has work waiting. **Runbook:** Settings > Shards = 1 to drain scoring, then find
the holder in THIS database (another ETP database on the same server can hold the same key):
`SELECT l.pid, (l.classid::bigint << 32) | l.objid::bigint AS key, s.state, s.state_change FROM pg_locks l JOIN pg_stat_activity s ON s.pid = l.pid WHERE l.locktype = 'advisory' AND l.granted AND l.objsubid = 1 AND l.database = (SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database());`
then `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(<pid>);`. A wrong guess kills a live tick's connection (the tick
fails with a closed cursor and its remaining rows are retried next tick), so only terminate a
backend that is `idle` with `state_change` older than the longest tick.
**A normal overlap logs the same busy line as a leak.** All eight counted crons count rows the
running tick has not finished (a `generating` prompt or video, a `pending` image draft mid-render,
the current batch's candidates, invites and images until each commits), so a long tick that
overlaps the next one logs `CRON_LOCK_BUSY` too. A leak is the line repeating long past the
longest tick, with an idle holder in the query above.
**Lease mode, the switch for transaction pooling** (built OFF, W3 R4). Setting
`assessments_be_v2.cron_lock_mode` (Settings > Scoring > "Background job lock", and the settings API,
checked by `write.py::_SETTING_CHOICES`): `advisory` (the default; unset means the same) is everything
above, unchanged; `lease` makes `cron_lock` hold a row in `assessments_be_cron_lease` (`key bigint
primary key, holder text, acquired_at timestamptz, expires_at timestamptz`, created by `-u` through the
model `assessments.be.cron.lease`, `_auto = False`, read-only ACL for Settings admins, no menu)
instead of a session lock, so no server connection carries it and transaction pooling cannot leak it.
The mode is read with one plain select on every call, so a change applies on each cron's next tick; an
unknown value runs advisory and logs `unknown assessments_be_v2.cron_lock_mode ..., using advisory`
once per value per worker process, not once per tick.
Take = ONE statement, `INSERT .. ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE .. WHERE expires_at < now() RETURNING
holder`, won iff our holder (`host:pid:uuid4`) comes back; drop = `UPDATE .. SET expires_at = now()
WHERE key AND holder`. Both commit the tick's cursor (the ticks already commit per record); a tick
that raised is rolled back before the drop, so the drop never commits half a record. A drop whose
commit fails (it flushes the tick's last writes, which can lose a race) logs `tick tail rolled back
so the lease could be dropped`, rolls that tail back and drops again, so the lane is never left held.
**Renewal:** `cron_lock` yields a `CronLock`, true exactly when held; all nine crons call
`got.renew()` immediately before each per-record commit (the video poll before each of its two
helpers, whose loops commit). In lease mode it starts a new term (`acquired_at = clock_timestamp(),
expires_at = clock_timestamp() + TTL`) inside that transaction, so the record's commit saves it.
Advisory mode: no SQL, True. `CRON_LEASE_TTL` = 20 minutes therefore bounds ONE record (a scoring
candidate's worst case is about 9 minutes of Vertex retries), not a tick; a crashed worker holds its
lane at most 20 minutes. A renew that finds the lease gone returns False and logs
`CRON_LEASE_LOST name=.. key=..` once per tick; the scoring lane then stops before its next
candidate (calls already out are stored). Lines: busy is the same `CRON_LOCK_BUSY`;
`CRON_LEASE_TAKEOVER name=.. key=.. previous=<holder> expired_for=Ns` when a lapsed lease is taken
over; `CRON_LEASE_LOST` also when a tick's drop finds another holder; `CRON_LEASE_OVERRUN name=..
key=.. over=Ns` when a drop finds its own lease already expired (a record outran the TTL and nobody
took the lane), which explains the next tick's takeover line: it is not a dead worker.
Odoo cursors are REPEATABLE READ: a take or a renew that meets a row changed since the tick's
snapshot gets a serialization failure, read as busy or lost. **Switching modes:** in a quiet
window: Settings > Shards = 1, then wait until the CURRENT mode's holder query shows nobody (the
`pg_locks` query above for advisory, the lease query below for lease), then switch. **Deploy:**
`-u assessments_be_v2` must run before pods take traffic even with the switch off, because the
heartbeat below reads `assessments_be_cron_lease` on every scoring poll and Kill. The lane heartbeat `_held_cron_locks` (renamed from
`_held_advisory_locks`; behind `_being_graded`, so Kill and the being-graded refusals,
`_running_cron_ids`, so the overdue verdict, and the generation progress route) reads `pg_locks`
UNION the live lease keys (`expires_at > now()`) in one statement, so a lane holding a lease reads
as running and a lapsed lease does not. **Runbook, who holds a lane:** `select * from assessments_be_cron_lease where expires_at >
now();` (a stuck holder clears itself at `expires_at`, or `update assessments_be_cron_lease set
expires_at = now() where key = <key>;`). Pinned by the lease class in
`test_every_cron_takes_its_lock_through_one_door`.

`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`: exactly one, on the evaluator row in `_check_all_submitted` (`assessment.py`), serializing two racing "last submit" workers before the `is_locked` transition.

##### 5.2 Savepoints

| Site | Protects | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| `vertex._cache_param` `vertex.py` | bearer-token cache write | warn, continue - the token is already minted, a lost cache costs one extra exchange |
| `vertex._remember_durations` `vertex.py` | learned Veo duration enum write | debug log; the clip is already submitted and billing, so a poisoned transaction here would lose `video_op_json` and cause a re-pay |
| `prompt._cron_generate_from_sop` `prompt.py` | one stranded `finalizing` row | log + `continue`; one permanently unfinalizable generator must not abort the tick forever |
| `prompt._finalize_tag_extract_state` `prompt.py` | `_auto_rank_after_mapping` (commit / rollback, not a savepoint) | warn; tags are already committed, ranking is re-runnable |
| `prompt.action_approve_all_drafts` `prompt.py` | one draft's approval | record the failure, `invalidate_recordset`, continue with the rest |
| `prompt._auto_rank_after_mapping` `prompt.py`, `1394`, `1405` | self-rank, lexical retry, each peer refresh | needed because `assessments.be.similarity` has a `unique(source_id, target_id)` - catching in Python alone leaves the transaction aborted and 500s the serializer |
| `prompt._detect_label_on_render` `prompt.py` | render-time detection | log; the image stays keyless for the detect cron |
| `prompt._cron_render_pending_images` `prompt.py` | one draft's render | rollback, set `image_state="failed"`, commit, continue |
| `prompt._submit_pending_video_ops` `prompt.py` / `_poll_generating_video_ops` `prompt.py` | one draft's Veo submit/poll | see §5.3 |
| `assessment._auto_score_mark_scoring` / `_auto_score_begin` / `_auto_score_finish` / the serial loop in `_cron_llm_auto_score` `assessment.py` | marking one candidate `scoring` (committed before its calls), planning it, storing it | `_auto_score_failed`: log, roll back after a serialization failure, continue with the next candidate |
| `assessment._auto_submit_expired` `assessment.py` | one placeholder response create | swallow `IntegrityError`, continue |
| `assessment._cron_expire_stale_attempts` `assessment.py` / `_cron_purge_expired_pii` `assessment.py` / `_cron_send_pending_invitations` `assessment.py`, `1641` | one record | log, continue |
| `question_image._detect_inline` `question_image.py` / `_cron_detect_image_labels` `question_image.py` | one image | never fail the render / bump `detection_attempts` |

##### 5.3 Serialization-failure handling

`prompt.py` imports `PG_CONCURRENCY_EXCEPTIONS_TO_RETRY` from `odoo.service.model` as `_TRANSIENT_DB_ERRORS`, falling back to `(SerializationFailure, DeadlockDetected, LockNotAvailable)`.

| Site | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `_submit_pending_video_ops` `prompt.py` / `_poll_generating_video_ops` `prompt.py` | Rollback and **leave state untouched** for the next tick. The comment records the live symptom this fixed: both Veo ops came back `done` with clips staged, yet the draft showed *"Could not check the clip generation status: could not serialize access due to concurrent update"* |
| `_cron_generate_from_sop` `prompt.py` | Detects `SerializationFailure` / pgcode 40001, rolls back, and **re-queues** (`sop_gen_state="queued"`) instead of surfacing `failed`. Any other `OperationalError` falls through to `failed` + `sop_gen_error` |
| `_finalize_sop_gen_state` `prompt.py` | Up to `_SOP_GEN_FINALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5`; rollback + `invalidate_recordset` + `time.sleep(0.1 * (attempt+1))`; re-raises on a non-serialization error or on the last attempt. **Never re-queues** - the drainer cannot distinguish "needs generation" from "needs finalization" and would re-run Vertex against already-committed drafts |
| `_finalize_tag_extract_state` `prompt.py` | Same shape, `_TAG_EXTRACT_FINALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5` |
| `_cron_llm_auto_score` (`_auto_score_failed`) | After a `TransactionRollbackError` / `InFailedSqlTransaction`, `cr.rollback()` so the next candidate gets a fresh snapshot; without it every later candidate of the tick failed the same way, each after paying for its call |
| Grading writers vs a running lane | Nothing a web request does rewrites a candidate a lane holds (`_being_graded`, §3.3); no grading lane writes the paper row (outlier staleness is derived, §4); `_llm_score_start` rewrites the evaluator only on a real change, so it does not hold the row's lock through a Vertex call. A threshold edit while a lane grades the paper goes to `threshold_recompute_pending` for the cron instead of rewriting up to 500 answers inline |
| `_vertex_bearer_until` `vertex.py` | A serialization failure while minting is retried once on a fresh READ COMMITTED cursor; a second is a `VertexQuotaError` deferral |
| `_recompute_cohort_outliers` `assessment.py` | Reads the stored flags first so only rows whose flag flips are written - a candidate mid-grade no longer collides with an unchanged rewrite |
| Every other cron | Broad `except Exception` → rollback → record a failure state → `continue` |

The root cause the two finalizers exist for is stated at `prompt.py`: the SOP-gen cron and the tag-extract path hold **different** advisory locks and can therefore write the same prompt row concurrently.

---

#### 6. Budget and spend controls

| Parameter | Default | Constant | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assessments_be_v2.daily_llm_cap_usd` | `100.0` | `DEFAULT_DAILY_LLM_CAP_USD` `constants.py`, resolved by `vertex.spend_cap` | Refuse any guarded call once same-UTC-day recorded spend reaches it. `0` disables |
| `assessments_be_v2.per_evaluator_llm_cap_usd` | `5.0` | `DEFAULT_PER_EVALUATOR_LLM_CAP_USD` `constants.py`, resolved by `vertex.spend_cap` | Refuse once one candidate's lifetime recorded spend reaches it. `0` disables. Only applies when `usage_ctx["evaluator_id"]` is set |
| `assessments_be_v2.llm_max_attempts` | `3` | - | Scoring attempts before terminal `error`; settings clamp 1-5 |
| `assessments_be_v2.scoring_batch_size` | `8` | - | Answers per Vertex call; settings clamp 1-32 |
| `assessments_be_v2.scoring_tick_limit` | `20` | - | Candidates one lane tick plans. A full tick that stored a mark re-triggers at once, so this is per tick, not per minute; raise it with parallel calls (about 5x) |
| `assessments_be_v2.scoring_shards` | `1` | `MAX_SCORING_SHARDS = 4` | Parallel scoring lanes |
| `assessments_be_v2.answers_flush_seconds` | `60` | `SETTING_RANGES` 15-300; 0 = default | Answer batch interval: seconds the exam client waits before sending its unsent answers in one batch; advertised on `/state` and `/begin`. Longer = fewer requests, more typing at risk if the device dies |
| `assessments_be_v2.paper_prefetch` | unset = off | `candidate.PAPER_PREFETCH_PARAM`; Settings "Send the whole paper at start" | Whole-paper prefetch: `/state` and `/begin` say `paper_prefetch: true` and `/paper` answers; the client fetches every question once and moves with no request. Off = one request per question move, and `/paper` is 404. Reported on `GET /api/v1/settings` as `exam.paper_prefetch` (the same reader, `candidate._paper_prefetch`) |
| `assessments_be_v2.scoring_parallel_calls` | `4` | `MAX_SCORING_PARALLEL_CALLS = 8`, `SETTING_RANGES` 1-8 | Judge calls one lane keeps in flight; lowered at runtime to fit `db_maxconn` (§3.4). 1 grades serially |
| `assessments_be_v2.vertex_max_rpm` | `0` = no limit | - | Local calls-per-minute ceiling (`_check_rate`); a refusal is a 429-style deferral |
| `assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache` | unset = `groups` | `SCORING_CACHE_DEFAULT` | Question-group caches (§3.5a); `0`/`false`/`no`/`off` = off. Not on the Settings screen |
| `assessments_be_v2.verdict_requires_current_prompt` | unset = on | `serializers.VERDICT_GATE_PARAM` | Candidates see only verdicts graded under the current instructions (§2.1 #13). Not on the Settings screen |

How to flip each switch, and what prod runs, is the switch table in
`docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` §0.5 J.

`_check_budget` (`vertex.py`) is `_check_rate` (the per-minute ceiling) then `_check_spend` (the
two money caps); `_check_spend` alone is what a re-score request and a lane tick ask (§3.3a,
§3.4), because a rate limit clears within the minute and must not refuse them. `_check_spend`
sums `cost_usd` from the **persisted** `assessments.be.llm.usage` ledger via a single `_read_group` (`_spend_since`, `vertex.py` - `_read_group`, not the Odoo-19-deprecated `read_group`, because this runs on every billable call). The daily window is UTC midnight from `create_date`.

Enforcement points - the gate is called **before** the HTTP request in:
- `_call_vertex_single` (`vertex.py`) - covers scoring, generation, tag extraction, detection, verification, `locate_defect`, similarity, vocabulary consolidation;
- `generate_image` (`vertex.py`);
- `edit_image` (`vertex.py`);
- `submit_video_op` (`vertex.py`);
- `grading_cache._resolve`, before a cache create.

`fetch_video_op` (a poll of a clip already paid for) is not checked. Veo spend is recorded to the ledger per second of output, so it counts against the cap for every other call.

At the cap, `VertexBudgetError` (a `RuntimeError` subclass, `vertex.py`) is raised with:
- `Daily LLM spend cap $%.2f reached ($%.2f used today). Raise assessments_be_v2.daily_llm_cap_usd or wait for the daily reset.`
- `Per-candidate LLM spend cap $%.2f reached for evaluator %s ($%.2f used). Raise assessments_be_v2.per_evaluator_llm_cap_usd if this candidate legitimately needs more grading.`

It is deliberately excluded from `_call_vertex`'s fallback retry (`vertex.py` catches only `VertexQuotaError` and `LLMRefusalError`), so it propagates. Downstream:

| Caller | Outcome at the cap |
|---|---|
| Grading lane tick | The daily cap ends the tick before anyone is planned: one `SPEND_CAP daily` WARNING per lane per tick |
| `scoring._store_submission` | A DEFERRAL, not a failure: the answers stay `pending` with their attempt budget untouched, a `SPEND_CAP` WARNING is logged, and "Waiting to be graded, no attempt used: <cap message>" goes on the attempt's `llm_error`. The next tick after the cap resets (UTC midnight) or is raised grades them normally |
| `action_rescore_individually` | Refused before anything is written: `RescoreRefused` `spend_limit` (409 on the API) |
| `prompt._cron_generate_from_sop` | Generic handler → `sop_gen_state="failed"`, `sop_gen_error` = the cap message truncated to 300 chars |
| `prompt._render_all_images` → `vertex.render_draft_images` | Swallowed **per slot** by the broad `except Exception` (`vertex.py`) and logged as `"image render failed"`. The render looks merely incomplete, so `image_render_attempts` increments and the draft flips to `image_state="failed"` after 3 ticks - the budget cause is only visible in the log |
| `prompt._cron_extract_tags` | Generic handler → `tag_extract_state="failed"`, `tag_extract_error` = the message truncated to 300 chars |

The Odoo LLM Budget screen shows today's spend against both caps through `vertex.spend_cap` and
the same UTC day (`assessments.be.llm.dashboard`), so it cannot disagree with the gate.

Related non-budget cost defences: the retry ceiling `_RETRY_OUTPUT_TOKENS_CEILING = 16000` (`vertex.py`; grading doubles its own first ask instead, capped at the model's `max_out`), the output clamp to the model's `max_out`, deferrals that spend no attempt (429, rate ceiling, full DB pool), no paid grading on a cancelled paper or an erased attempt, the H-16 identical-answer hash guard (`assessment.py`), the `op_name` idempotency handle preventing Veo double-submission (`prompt.py`), and `render_draft_images` returning already-paid slots on `VertexQuotaError.partial` so a retry re-renders only what is missing (`vertex.py`).

# Part 3 - The Flutter client (`ethara-assessment-fe`)

Branch `main`. The operator console and the candidate exam runner. The facts marked for 19.0.3.23.0 describe the app working tree that ships with backend 19.0.3.23.0 (prod runs app `48e8434`); the plan item ids quoted with them (M1, S1, Q12, FU7, G1-23, ...) are defined in `ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 0 §0.2, and "row N" is a row of its §0.4 feature inventory.


## 3.1 Bootstrap, session, and platform services

Everything below was read from source under `/Users/cj/Developer/ethara/ethara-assessment-fe`. Paths are relative to that root. `dart analyze lib/` reports "No issues found", so nothing here is a compile break.

#### 1. Startup sequence, main() to first frame

| # | What happens | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The browser loads `web/index.html`. Before `flutter_bootstrap.js`, an inline script unregisters every existing service worker, deletes all Cache Storage keys, and reloads the page once if any registration was found. Builds pass `--pwa-strategy=none`, so nothing new is registered; the script only evicts what an older build left. | `web/index.html:36-71`, `Makefile:31` |
| 2 | `main()` is one expression: `runApp(const EtharaAssessmentApp())`. No `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()`, no async setup, no URL-strategy configuration, no error-zone install. | `lib/main.dart:12` |
| 3 | Field initializers run: `Session()` is constructed, which constructs `ApiClient()`; the client's `base` is `kApiBaseUrl` with trailing slashes stripped. | `lib/main.dart:28`, `lib/session.dart:18`, `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:108-111` |
| 4 | `_examToken = examTokenFrom(Uri.base)` is evaluated once, as a `final` field, deliberately not per build (the comment states re-reading `Uri.base` would drag a finished candidate back into the runner). | `lib/main.dart:30-35` |
| 5 | `initState`: subscribes `_rebuild` to the session, calls `unawaited(_session.restore())`, sets `PortalTokens.overrideBrightness = Brightness.dark`. | `lib/main.dart:41-54` |
| 6 | `restore()` runs synchronously until its first `await`. `api.restoreTokens()` reads the token store; if it returns false, `restore()` returns immediately with `_restoring` never set, so the login form is the first frame. If it returns true, `_restoring = true` plus `notifyListeners()` happen before the first build, so the first frame is the `_Resuming` spinner. | `lib/session.dart:61-66`, `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:124-133` |
| 7 | `build` returns a `MaterialApp`: `title: kAppName`, `debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false`, `themeMode: _mode` (dark initially), and two `ThemeData`s that set only `brightness`, `scaffoldBackgroundColor` (`PortalTokens.light/dark.bgApp`) and `useMaterial3: true`. No `textTheme`, no `colorScheme`. | `lib/main.dart:76-93` |
| 8 | `home` is a switch on `(signedIn, restoring)`: `(true, _)` → `AppShell` keyed `ValueKey(session.uid)`; `(false, true)` → `_Resuming` (a bare 22x22 `CircularProgressIndicator`); `(false, false)` → `LoginScreen`. | `lib/main.dart:94-110`, `lib/main.dart:120-133` |
| 9 | `AppShell.initState` builds `AppStore(api: session.api)` and calls `store.adoptSession(orgRole: session.role, name:, uid:)`. `adoptSession` maps the role to a `Portal`, sets `source = DataSource.live` unconditionally, notifies, and fires `refresh()` without awaiting. The store is disposed by `AppShell`, not by `AssessmentSection`. | `lib/app_shell.dart:43-74`, `lib/assessment/state/app_store.dart:203-212` |
