The 224px sidebar is drawn by `AppShell` but built through a callback the section invokes, so route state stays in the section. | `lib/app_shell.dart:76-115`, `lib/app_shell.dart:117-270` |
| 11 | `AssessmentSection._openEntry` gives the deep-link token priority: a non-empty `examToken` does `_nav.reset(Exam(token))` and returns; otherwise the entry enum selects the landing route (`console` and `analytics` both land on `Analytics`). | `lib/assessment/assessment_section.dart:127-180` |

Theme toggling is owned by `_EtharaAppState._toggleTheme`, passed down to the sidebar icon button. It flips `_mode` and mirrors the value into `PortalTokens.overrideBrightness`. There is no toggle on the login screen, so the sign-in page is always dark on a cold load.
Evidence: `lib/main.dart:67-74`, `lib/app_shell.dart:181-185`.

#### 2. Configuration

Every `fromEnvironment` in `lib/` (verified by grep - there are exactly three):

| Define | Declared | Type and default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `API_BASE_URL` | `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:35-38` | `String`, default `''` | Becomes `ApiClient.base` with trailing `/` stripped (`:256`). Empty means every request URI is relative (`Uri.parse('$base$path')`, `:93`), i.e. same-origin. Also drives `hasBackend` (`:46`) and `resolveMediaUrl`, which leaves relative media paths untouched when empty (`:108-113`). |
| `API_DB` | `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:42` | `String`, default `''` | Sent as the `db` field, and only on the Odoo cookie login path, only when non-empty (`:317-322`). The gateway/bearer path never sends it. |
| `PROCTOR_SIM` | `lib/assessment/screens/exam/exam_screen.dart:761-762` | `bool`, **default `true`** | When true the `ProctorRig` overlay is rendered inside the exam chrome (`:411-424`). |

Non-environment compile-time constants in scope:

| Constant | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `kAppName` | `'ETP Assessment Pro'` - header text, `MaterialApp.title`, login footer | `lib/config.dart::kAppName`; used at `lib/main.dart:79`, `lib/app_shell.dart:176`, `lib/login_screen.dart:224` |
| `_kBearer` / `_kRefresh` | `'etp.bearer'` / `'etp.refresh'` sessionStorage keys | `lib/services/token_store_web.dart::_kBearer` |
| `_kOpenKey` / `_kWidthKey` | `'etp.dock.open'` / `'etp.dock.width'` localStorage keys | `lib/assessment/widgets/dock.dart::_kOpenKey` |

`PROCTOR_SIM` specifically: the default is **on**. `Makefile:26-31` builds with only `API_BASE_URL`, `API_DB` and `--pwa-strategy=none`, so `make build` and `make serve` both ship the simulator. Turning it off requires an explicit `--dart-define=PROCTOR_SIM=false`, which no build target in the repo passes. The source comment at `exam_screen.dart:756-760` states the reason for the switch ("It drives the real violation route, so it must not reach a live candidate") and that the default stayed true "because every existing build and every test expects it present".

Contradictions in the configuration documentation:

- `lib/config.dart:11-12` says leaving `API_BASE_URL` empty "makes the app run on its bundled seed data". `README.md:34-40` says empty means same-origin production. The code agrees with the README: empty just means relative URLs (`api_client.dart:183`). Seed mode is unreachable from the real app - `AppShell` always constructs `AppStore(api: widget.session.api)` (`app_shell.dart:54`) and `AppStore`'s constructor sets `source = live` whenever `api != null` (`app_store.dart:53`); `adoptSession` sets it to `live` again (`app_store.dart:207`); and `AppShell` is only reachable after a successful server sign-in (`main.dart:94-96`). Seed data is reachable only from tests that construct `AppStore` with no `api`.
- `lib/config.dart:7-9` and `README.md:19-20` document `API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:7070` / `API_DB=ethara_ops`. `Makefile:14-24` states plainly that those defaults are wrong (the Odoo checkout they came from was deleted, and `etp_assessment_pro` cannot load in `ethara_ops`) and uses `http://localhost:8069` / `etp_local`. Three files, two answers.

#### 3. Session and auth

Ownership: `Session extends ChangeNotifier` and holds the one long-lived `ApiClient` (`lib/session.dart:17-22`). It exposes `busy`, `error`, `name`, `uid`, `role`, `signedIn`, `restoring`. It stores no role logic - `role` is whatever `/api/v1/auth/me` returned.

| Concern | Behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Where the token lives at runtime | `ApiClient._bearer` / `_refresh` (gateway path) or `ApiClient._session` (Odoo cookie string, parsed out of `set-cookie` on 2xx responses only) | `api_client.dart:95-106`, `:245-259` |
| Where it survives reload | `sessionStorage` under `etp.bearer` / `etp.refresh`, written by `_persistTokens()` after gateway login, refresh and logout. `sessionStorage` and not `localStorage` is a stated choice: a shared machine must not open already signed in | `token_store_web.dart:7-13`, `:22-47`, `api_client.dart:136-143` |
| Cookie path persistence | None. `_loginModule` never calls `_persistTokens`, so a cookie-authenticated deployment loses its session on refresh and falls back to the login form | `api_client.dart:317-322` |
| Restore on boot | `Session.restore()`: `api.restoreTokens()` (sessionStorage, else a bearer injected via the constructor) → `_restoring = true` → `/api/v1/auth/me` → on failure one `refreshSession()` then `/auth/me` again → on failure `logout()` and return false. Any thrown exception (unreachable server) returns false, so the user lands on the login form rather than a console whose calls all fail | `session.dart:61-81`, `api_client.dart:124-133` |
| Role adoption | `_adoptWhoAmI` reads `me['user']`, requires a non-empty `role`, and only then sets `_signedIn = true`. Both sign-in and restore go through this single function | `session.dart:84-105` |
| Sign-in | `api.login()` then `_adoptWhoAmI()`. `login()` tries `/api/v1/auth_token` (gateway, bearer) first; only a 404 falls through to `/api/v1/auth/session` (cookie), so a wrong password is not replayed against a second endpoint. When `/auth/me` itself refuses, `_adoptWhoAmI` keeps that `ApiError` (`_whoAmIError`) and the form says "Signed in, but the server refused the session: <server message>" instead of the old blanket "this account has no assessment role"; the role sentence is kept for a real empty role (19.0.3.23.0, row 61) | `session.dart::signIn`, `session.dart::_adoptWhoAmI`, `api_client.dart:280-322` |
| Deliberate non-use of `user_role` | The token response's `user_role` is ignored; `/auth/me` decides the portal. Stated reason: the gateway's ORG role would hand a portal candidate the operator console | `session.dart:107-115` |
| Expiry, cold | Detected only by the server refusing `/auth/me`; there is no client-side expiry timestamp anywhere | `session.dart:67-71` |
| Expiry, warm | `_send` retries once on HTTP 401 when `allowRetry`, a refresh token exists, and the path does not start with the `auth` prefixes. The replay passes `allowRetry: false`. **One renewal per expiry** (19.0.3.23.0, row 63): `_send` remembers the bearer it sent with (`sentWith`); if another call renewed the token while this one was on the wire it just replays with the new bearer, otherwise it awaits the shared `refreshSession()` | `api_client.dart::_send`, `test/assessment/one_refresh_serves_every_expired_call_test.dart` |
| Refresh | `POST /api/v1/refresh_token` (`kGatewayPrefix`) through `_send(allowRetry: false)`, so a refused refresh cannot re-enter the 401 hook; adopts a rotated refresh token when present; persists; on `ApiError` clears both tokens and the store and returns false. **Single-flight**: `refreshSession()` returns the in-flight `_renewing` future when one exists, so parallel 401s share one renewal - the gateway rotates the token on every refresh, and a second refresh used to kill the token the first had just handed out, logging the user out | `api_client.dart::refreshSession`, `api_client.dart::_renew` |
| Sign-out | `/api/v1/auth_token_unlink` when a bearer is held, else `/api/v1/auth/logout`; the `finally` clears `_session`, `_bearer`, `_refresh` and wipes storage regardless of outcome. `Session.signOut` swallows `ApiError` and clears local state either way. A sign-out raised INSIDE the portal (the account card's "Sign In Again", the exam gate's "Sign in" / "Switch account") calls `AppStore.signOut`, which ends the API session and then calls `onSignedOut`; `AppShell` sets that to `session.signOut`, so the app really returns to the login form (19.0.3.23.0; before, the person was left on a shell with no token) | `api_client.dart:369-384`, `session.dart::signOut`, `app_store.dart::signOut`, `app_shell.dart::initState` |
| Switching users | `AppShell` is keyed `ValueKey(session.uid)`, so a different user builds a new shell and therefore a new `AppStore` | `main.dart:94-99` |

Observations that look wrong:

- The 401-refresh retry sits *after* `jsonDecode` (`api_client.dart:193-222`). A 401 with a non-JSON body (Odoo's HTML login redirect, which the comment at `:197-199` says is the expected shape of that failure) throws "Your session has expired. Sign in again." before the retry is ever considered. The automatic renewal therefore only covers JSON 401s.
- On web the cookie path is doubtful: `_headers` sets a literal `Cookie:` header (`api_client.dart:150`) and `_captureSession` reads `set-cookie` off the response (`:255`). Both are forbidden header names for browser fetch/XHR, so neither is expected to work in the browser this app targets. `package:http`'s browser client also does not set `withCredentials`. UNKNOWN: whether the cookie path was ever exercised from the web build.
- `Session.signOut()` clears name/uid/role/`_signedIn` but not `_error`, so an error from a previous failed sign-in is still rendered on the login screen after signing out (`session.dart::signOut`, consumed at `login_screen.dart:181-184`).

#### 4. Deep links

`examTokenFrom(Uri)` is a pure function over a `Uri`, called exactly once with `Uri.base` (`lib/main.dart:35`). Accepted shapes, in the order they are tested:

| Input | Result | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `/?token=abc123` | `abc123` | `queryParameters['token']`, trimmed, checked first as unambiguous (`deep_link.dart:25-26`) |
| `/exam/abc123` | `abc123` | path segment scan (`:30-41`) |
| `/exam/abc123/` | `abc123` | trailing slash produces no extra non-empty segment |
| `/#/exam/abc123` | `abc123` | `Uri.parse(uri.fragment).pathSegments` is concatenated onto `uri.pathSegments`, covering Flutter web hash routing |
| `/pro_assessment/abc123` | `abc123` | the legacy Odoo portal path is accepted verbatim |
| `/exam/abc123/review` | `abc123` | the scan takes the segment after the first `exam`/`pro_assessment` marker and ignores the rest |
| anything else, or `/exam` with no following segment | `null` | loop bound is `segments.length - 1`, and an empty token is rejected |

Routing of the token: `main.dart:95-104` passes it to `AppShell`, which passes it to `AssessmentSection` (`app_shell.dart:90-92`), whose `_openEntry` does `_nav.reset(Exam(token))` and skips the entry switch entirely (`assessment_section.dart:144-148`). Two consequences visible in the code:

- The exam runner is only reached after sign-in. An unauthenticated candidate clicking the emailed link sees `LoginScreen` first (`main.dart:94-110`); the token survives because it was captured before the first frame.
- The token is applied regardless of role. An admin who opens a URL containing `/exam/<token>` lands in the exam runner rather than Analytics.
- `AssessmentNav` is an in-memory stack (`lib/assessment/nav.dart:184-236`), not a Router. Nothing writes back to the address bar - `nav.dart:216-217` says so explicitly ("the host owns the address bar"), which in this standalone app means the URL never changes after load. The sub-routes below `/exam/<token>` (`/review`, `/answers`, question index) are therefore reachable only through in-app navigation, never by URL, even though `examTokenFrom` tolerates them in the incoming link.

Test coverage for this file: `test/deep_link_test.dart` covers all six accepted shapes plus the negative cases.

#### 5. The conditional-import pattern

The exact idiom, and every pair in the repo (grep for `if (dart.library`):

```dart
import 'download_stub.dart' if (dart.library.js_interop) 'download_web.dart';
```

`lib/services/csv_export.dart:3`. Multi-line variants are identical in meaning, for example `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:30-31`:

```dart
import '../../services/token_store_stub.dart'
    if (dart.library.js_interop) '../../services/token_store_web.dart';
```

The condition is `dart.library.js_interop`, true only when compiling to JS/wasm, so the VM (and `flutter test` without `--platform chrome`) always gets the stub. Where the pair shares a type, the web half re-exports it from the stub so both halves expose one declaration: `export 'file_pick_stub.dart' show PickedFile;` (`file_pick_web.dart:9`), `export 'token_store_stub.dart' show StoredSession;` (`token_store_web.dart:5`), `export 'proctor_stub.dart' show ProctorRules, ProctorWatch;` (`proctor_web.dart:26`).

| Pair | Contract | Web half does | Stub does on non-web | Import sites |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `download_stub.dart` / `download_web.dart` | `void saveTextFile(String filename, String content, String mimeType)` | Builds a `Blob`, `URL.createObjectURL`, hidden `<a download>`, click, remove, `revokeObjectURL` immediately. Blob rather than a `data:` URI because Chrome caps data URIs near 2 MB | Empty body, no-op | `lib/services/csv_export.dart:3` |
| `file_pick_stub.dart` / `file_pick_web.dart` | `class PickedFile(name, bytes)`, `Future<PickedFile?> pickFile({String accept})` | Hidden `<input type=file>`, `FileReader.readAsArrayBuffer`, completes with raw bytes; `null` on empty selection, on read error, and on the `cancel` event where supported | Returns `null` always (`file_pick_stub.dart:16`) | `chatter.dart:7`, `import_sheet.dart:17`, `new_generator_screen.dart:14`, `generator_detail_screen.dart:16`, `assessment_detail_screen.dart:17`, `review_queue_screen.dart:20` *(new_generator_screen.dart: removed since 19.0.3.12.0)* |
| `prefs_stub.dart` / `prefs_web.dart` | `String? readPref(String)`, `void writePref(String, String)` | `window.localStorage`, both calls wrapped in `try/catch` (Safari private mode, blocked site data, quota); empty string is normalised to `null` | `readPref` returns `null`, `writePref` is a no-op | `lib/assessment/widgets/dock.dart:17` (chatter dock open state and width) |
| `proctor_stub.dart` / `proctor_web.dart` | `ProctorRules`, `abstract class ProctorWatch`, `ProctorWatch createProctorWatch()` | Real `_WebProctorWatch` (section 6) | `_NoopProctorWatch`: `start`/`stop`/`requestFullscreen` empty, `isFullscreen` false (`proctor_stub.dart:66-83`) | `lib/assessment/screens/exam/exam_screen.dart:23-24` |
| `token_store_stub.dart` / `token_store_web.dart` | `class StoredSession(bearer, refresh)`, `StoredSession? loadSession()`, `void saveSession(String, String)`, `void clearSession()` | `sessionStorage` under `etp.bearer` / `etp.refresh`; `loadSession` returns `null` unless the bearer is non-empty; `saveSession` removes rather than stores an empty value | `loadSession` returns `null`, the writers are no-ops | `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:30-31` |
| `video_plate_stub.dart` / `video_plate_web.dart` | UNKNOWN (contents not read - outside this section's scope) | - | - | `lib/assessment/screens/exam/video_plate.dart:8-9`, which uses `export ... if (...)` rather than `import`, the only file that does |

Note the `prefs` / `token_store` split is deliberate and documented on both sides: credentials go to `sessionStorage` so they die with the tab, layout preferences go to `localStorage` so they do not (`prefs_web.dart:3-8`, `token_store_web.dart:7-13`).

`csv_export.dart` itself is platform-neutral: `buildCsv` (RFC 4180 escaping), `downloadCsv` (prepends a UTF-8 BOM for Excel), `exportCsv`, `csvName`, `debugCsvCell` (exposed for tests), and `csvToDataUrl` (base64 `data:` URL, documented as "used by the stub path and tests", though the stub path never calls it - `download_stub.saveTextFile` is an empty function).

#### 6. Proctoring

`proctor_web.dart` implements `ProctorWatch` against `package:web`. `start()` is idempotent via `_running` (`:66-68`), records `_baseDpr` at attach time, and registers only the listeners the passed `ProctorRules` enable. Every listener is kept in a `_listeners` record list so `stop()` can remove all of them plus cancel the devtools timer (`:162-172`).

| Rule | Mechanism | Reason string sent to the server |
|---|---|---|
| `rightClick` | `contextmenu` on document, `preventDefault()` | `Right-click attempted` |
| `copyPaste` | `copy`, `cut`, `paste` on document, `preventDefault()` | `Clipboard action: <type>` |
| `tabSwitch` | `visibilitychange`; ignored when the `fullscreen` rule is on and the document is not fullscreen; ignored unless `document.hidden`; debounced at 1500 ms | `Tab switched / window hidden` |
| `devtools` | 2 s `Timer.periodic`; `zoom = devicePixelRatio / _baseDpr`; flags when `outerWidth - innerWidth * zoom > 300` or the same for height; fires at most once (`_devtoolsReported`) | `Developer tools detected` |
| `screenshot` | `keyup` where `key == 'PrintScreen'` | `Screenshot key pressed` |
| `fullscreen` | `fullscreenchange`; entering sets `_everEnteredFullscreen`; leaving fires only if it had been entered | `Exited fullscreen` |

`requestFullscreen()` calls `document.documentElement.requestFullscreen()` inside a `try/catch` (`:151-159`). It is invoked from exactly one place, the Begin button handler, before navigation so the user gesture is still in scope (`exam_screen.dart:301-317`). The file header documents three fixes carried over from the Odoo portal's inline script rather than re-derived: the fullscreen guard on tab-switch, DPR normalisation of the devtools width, and the "only after having entered" fullscreen rule (`proctor_web.dart:1-17`).

Wiring and the server route:

- `ExamScreen` creates the watcher as `widget.proctor ?? createProctorWatch()` (the `proctor` parameter is a test seam) and calls `_proctor.stop()` in `dispose` and at time-up (`exam_screen.dart::_timeUp`, round 3, MT3-01), so an Escape or a tab switch under the time-up overlay is no longer counted.
- `_ensureProctoring(asm, ev)` is called from `_buildChrome` (`:346`), not `initState`, because the rules arrive with the attempt. It returns early if already started, if the attempt is locked or submitted, or if `rules.any` is false. It maps `asm.rules[ProctorRule.*]` onto `ProctorRules` (`:132-153`).
- Every violation, real or simulated, goes through `_violate` (`:326-332`): toast, `store.recordViolation(ev.id, reason)`, and navigation to the completion screen if that returned true.
- `AppStore.recordViolation` increments the local count, then, **when `source == DataSource.live`**, fires `_reconcileViolation` (`_api.examViolation(ev.token, reason)`) without awaiting, then ends the sitting only if `violationAction.isAuto && count >= cap` where `cap = maxViolations > 0 ? maxViolations : 1` - so cap 0 under Auto-submit is the first violation, and Log only never ends it at any cap (`app_store.dart::recordViolation`). `_reconcileViolation` adopts the reply's `violation_count` and `violation_limit_breached` (the limit reached, in either mode: a label; under Log only the exam goes on), ends the sitting on `attempt_ended`, and on a 409 `time_expired` (a violation after the deadline) first awaits `flushAnswers()` - the flushed `/answer` meets the deadline itself and says whether it was kept - then, unless that reply already told the candidate, raises the time-up message ("saved" only if every pending save was kept) and moves to the completion screen, instead of a proctoring auto-submit; other errors are dropped (round 3, A-074, MT3-01).
- The route is `POST /api/v1/exam/<token>/violation` with body `{"reason": "..."}` (`api_client.dart:481-485`).
- `webcam` opens the camera with `getUserMedia` from `start()`: a refused camera blocks the exam (not a violation), one turned off after being granted fires `Webcam turned off / lost` (`proctor_web.dart`).
- `ai_proctor` (server contract, Week 2; needs `webcam`): AI detections are posted to the same route with reasons prefixed `AI: ` (`AI: phone detected`, `AI: no face for 5s`, `AI: more than one face`, `AI: left the frame`), and each snapshot is POSTed as `<epoch_ms>_<rule>.jpg` (JPEG, at most 400000 bytes) with the `evidence_upload` policy that comes with every question served and with the instructions screen (`url` + `fields` + the file as multipart). The client keeps the last policy until its `expires_at`, so turning the rule off mid-sitting stops uploads only when that policy expires (deadline + 30 min). The admin reads them back from `GET /api/v1/attempts/<id>/evidence` (see "Proctoring / violations").

Does the simulator drive the real route: **yes.** `ProctorRig`'s `onViolate` is bound to `_violate` (`exam_screen.dart::_violate`), which is the same function `ProctorWatch.onViolation` calls (`:1194`). Both reach `recordViolation` and therefore the same POST, and both can trip the auto-submit cap. The comment block at `:400-410` says this explicitly, and adds that the rig was previously rendered unconditionally. With `PROCTOR_SIM` defaulting to true and no build target setting it to false, a released bundle built from this repo's `Makefile` still contains it.

#### 7. Theme

Two files are the source of truth, both under `lib/core/theme/`, with `lib/assessment/theme.dart` acting as a rename adapter over them.

`PortalTokens` (`portal_tokens.dart::PortalTokens`) is an `@immutable` class with two `static const` instances, `light` (`:191`) and `dark` (`:252`). It is deliberately not a `ThemeExtension` (`:15-16`). Token groups, as the file itself sections them:

| Group | Members |
|---|---|
| Brand / accent | `primary`, `primaryHover`, `primarySubtle`, `selected` |
| Surfaces | `bgApp`, `bgMuted`, `bgSubtle`, `bgBase`, `bgHover` (translucent, meant to be composited) |
| Lines | `border`, `borderSubtle`, `borderHover` (the only magenta-tinted line), `zebra` |
| Text | `textPrimary`, `textSecondary`, `textMuted` |
| Semantic status | four symmetrical families - `success*`, `info*`, `warn*`, `dest*`, each with `Text` / `Bg` / `Dot` |
| Floor-plan canvas | `canvas`, `canvasGrid`, `tableBg`, `tableBorder`, `seatEmpty`, `seatEmptyText` |
| Chrome | `ring`, `skeleton`, `scrollbar`, `scrim` |
| Elevation | `shadowS1`..`shadowS5`, each a ready-made `List<BoxShadow>`, with a boosted dark scale rather than the light one reused |
| Flag | `isDark` |

Non-color scales live in the same file as `abstract final class` holders: `Space` (`:317-332`), `Radii` (doubles plus `BorderRadius` constants, `:348-360`), `Sizes` (`:350-375`), `Layout` (page caps, padding, breakpoints, `:392-429`), `Motion` (durations, curves, `reducedMotion(context)`, `:471-486`).

Light/dark resolution, two paths:

1. `PortalTokens.of(context)` returns `dark` when `Theme.of(context).brightness == Brightness.dark`, else `light` (`:191-192`). Because `MaterialApp` is given both a light and a dark `ThemeData` and a `themeMode`, setting `themeMode` alone switches every token (`main.dart:82-93`).
2. `PortalTokens.current` is the context-free fallback: `overrideBrightness ?? PlatformDispatcher.instance.platformBrightness` (`:188-194`). `main.dart` writes `overrideBrightness` at startup and on every toggle to keep it in step.

`lib/assessment/theme.dart` maps the portal system onto the names the assessment screens use: `typedef AppTokens = PortalTokens` (`:26`), `context.tokens` → `PortalTokens.of(this)` (`:34`), `context.type` → `AssessmentTypeRamp(PortalTokens.of(this))` (`:37`). The ramp defines no sizes of its own; every getter delegates to a `PortalType` style and picks the token color for that role (`:52-103`). It also adds `Radii` as `BorderRadius` constants (`:111-123`), `Color.o(alpha)` (`:127-129`), and an `AssessmentCharts` extension giving `seq1..seq3` and `c1..c5` derived from the accent and the semantic dots plus a `shadow` tint and `hoverA` opacity (`:140-165`).

`PortalType` (`portal_type.dart::PortalType`) is a static style factory over two families: `'Plus Jakarta Sans'` for all interface text and `'DM Mono'` for every numeral a human reads as data. `ui()` pushes the weight through both `fontWeight` and `FontVariation('wght', ...)` because the file is a variable font (`:48-64`). Named UI scale: `headingXl/Lg/Md`, `titleLg/Md/Sm`, `bodyMd/Sm/Xs`, `label`, `labelSm`, `button`, `eyebrow`. Named mono scale: `dataXl/Lg/Md/Sm/Xs`. Sizes are literal, with a documented refusal to apply the older Ethara design system's global 0.9 scale (`:26-34`).

Problems found in the theme layer:

- **The two typefaces are not shipped.** `portal_type.dart:16-19` states both families "ship as assets in `assets/fonts/` and are declared in `pubspec.yaml`". `pubspec.yaml` has no `fonts:` section at all (only `assets: - assets/`), `assets/` contains exactly one file (`ethara-mark.svg`), and the last built `build/flutter_assets/FontManifest.json` lists only `MaterialIcons`. Every `fontFamily: 'Plus Jakarta Sans'` / `'DM Mono'` therefore falls back to the platform default, and the mono/tabular-figures behaviour the file argues for does not happen.
- **`PortalTokens.current` has no readers.** `main.dart:50-53` sets `overrideBrightness` to keep it correct "because the chart painters and cell builders read `PortalTokens.current`", and `portal_tokens.dart:181` names `scoreColor` and `flagColor` as the callers. Grep finds no `PortalTokens.current` and no `scoreColor`/`flagColor` anywhere in `lib/`. The getter and the override are currently dead.
- **Two `Radii` classes.** `lib/assessment/theme.dart` re-exports `portal_tokens.dart` (which declares `Radii` with `sm/md/lg/xl/full` doubles) and also declares its own `Radii` with `BorderRadius` members. The local declaration is what consumers get (`app_shell.dart::badge` uses `Radii.badge`, which only the local one has), and `dart analyze` is clean, but the name is doubly defined across one import surface. Grep finds zero uses of the portal `Radii.md`/`rMd` form anywhere in `lib/`.
- The re-export paths in `lib/assessment/theme.dart:22-23` are written as `'../../core/theme/...'` while the imports two lines above are `'../core/theme/...'`. Both resolve to the same file only because URI resolution clamps at the package root. It works, but the two spellings of the same target are inconsistent.
- Several token groups are unused by this app: `seatEmpty`, `seatEmptyText`, `canvas`, `canvasGrid`, `tableBg`, `tableBorder` (the Seat Allocation set), `skeleton`, `scrollbar`, `scrim`, `bgBase`, and all five `shadowS*` lists have zero references outside the theme files. So do `Space.*`, `Sizes.*` and `Motion.*`; `Layout` is referenced once, at `login_screen.dart:58`. The chart ramp is partly used (`seq1-3`, `c1`, `c2`) and partly not (`c3`, `c4`, `c5`).

#### 8. Other files in scope

- `lib/login_screen.dart` - two-pane above `Layout.twoColumn` (1024), single column below (`:56-94`). Brand pane is a radial magenta wash at 10% dark / 6% light over `bgSubtle` (`:102-116`). The form is wrapped in `ListenableBuilder(listenable: session)` so `busy` and `error` drive it (`:164-231`); errors render as `Notice(tone: Tone.bad, text: session.error!)`. `_submit` refuses when busy or when either field is empty, and the sign-in call is `session.signIn(login.trim(), password)` (`:58-62`). Email field submits into the password focus node; password submits the form. A private `_Input` reimplements the app's field shape rather than using Material defaults (`:237-299`).
- `lib/widgets/ethara_mark.dart` - `SvgPicture.asset('assets/ethara-mark.svg')` with an optional `ColorFilter.mode(color, BlendMode.srcIn)` tint; sized 96 on the wide login pane, 40 compact (`login_screen.dart:118-128`). This is the only use of the `flutter_svg` dependency.
- `lib/app_shell.dart` - `initState` sets `_store.onSignedOut = widget.session.signOut`, the one link from a store-raised sign-out to the login form (see Session and auth above). The sidebar renders a group heading only when `entries[i].group` differs from the previous entry's (`:199-212`), badges render only when `> 0` (`:325-337`), and the account row's role label is derived from `_store.portal == Portal.admin` and printed as `'Admin'` or `'Candidate'` (`:79`, `:107`) rather than from `session.role`, so any other server role string is displayed as "Candidate".


## 3.2 AppStore: the single source of UI state

`lib/assessment/state/app_store.dart` (3676 lines when this section was written; 8,186 in 19.0.3.23.0, so treat a bare `:N` below as approximate and search for the member name). Everything below was read from the file; line numbers are `app_store.dart:N` unless another path is given.

#### The pattern in one paragraph

`AppStore extends ChangeNotifier` (app_store.dart:45). There is no Provider, no InheritedWidget and no service locator in this module: the store is constructed once in `_AppShellState.initState` (`lib/app_shell.dart::initState`) and passed down as a plain constructor argument - `AssessmentSection(store: _store)` (`lib/app_shell.dart:87`), then `DashboardScreen(store: _store)`, `GeneratorDetailScreen(store: _store, ...)` and so on for every route (`lib/assessment/assessment_section.dart::AssessmentSection`). Subscription is manual and coarse: exactly two widgets call `addListener` - `_AppShellState` (`lib/app_shell.dart::_AppShellState`) and `_AssessmentSectionState` (`lib/assessment/assessment_section.dart::_AssessmentSectionState`) - and both listeners are `void _rebuild() { if (mounted) setState(() {}); }`. So a single `notifyListeners()` rebuilds the whole section subtree; there is no selective subscription anywhere. Ownership is split deliberately: `AppShell` builds and disposes the store, `AssessmentSection` only listens and explicitly does not dispose it (`lib/assessment/assessment_section.dart:196-203`). Mutation is by whole-list replacement (`generators = generators.map(...).toList()`) rather than in-place edit, so identity comparison is not usable for change detection.

#### Public fields and getters

"Screens" are files under `lib/assessment/`; `NONE` means no non-test reader was found anywhere in `lib/`.

| Name | Type | Holds | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|

| `api` (getter, :72) | `ApiClient?` | The client, **null in seed mode**. Escape hatch for leaf panels that fetch their own detail | `widgets/chatter.dart:168,222,297`, `widgets/emails_panel.dart:120` |
| `source` (:82) | `DataSource` | `seed` or `live`. Set in ctor, by `adoptSession`, `signOut` (the store's `signIn` was removed in round 3, A-105) | not read directly outside the store; surfaced via `isLive` |

The public field `DataSource source` and `LoadState loadState` are both plain mutable fields, not getters - any holder of the store can write them.

#### Public methods

Every method that goes through `_act` (:1103) is marked "`_act`". `_act`'s contract: seed mode runs `ifSeed` and returns without touching the network (:1110-1113); live mode runs `optimistic`, calls, toasts `okMessage` or the error (a failure first runs `rollback`, and an `asks` hook can take an `ApiError` over as a question for the screen, with no toast - round 3), and **always** ends with `await refresh(background: true)` in a `finally` (:1132-1136) - including after a failure.

| `refresh({bool background = false})` :242 | see load architecture below | every entity list | is the refresh |
| `setPortal(Portal p)` :3657 | none | `portal` | no. **No caller anywhere - dead** |

The store has no `signIn` any more (the dead, fail-open `AppStore.signIn`, `_portalFromServer` and `Portal.parse` were removed in round 3, A-105); the app signs in through `Session` (`lib/session.dart:116,142`) and adopts the result via `adoptSession`. `signOut` is called from the account card ("Sign In Again", `screens/account/account_screen.dart`) and from the exam gate's "Sign in" / "Switch account" (`exam_screen.dart` passes `onSignOut: s.signOut` to `GateScreen`), and reaches the login form through `onSignedOut`.

All six `load*` hydrators return early in seed mode (`if (!_live) return;`), catch `ApiError` into `toaster.bad`, and route anything else to `_hydrationFailed` (:1857), which `debugPrint`s the stack and warns "Could not load the full record - showing partial data".

#### Load and refresh architecture

**On construction.** If `source == DataSource.seed` the constructor calls `_load()` (fixtures) and sets `loadState = ready` synchronously (:57-60). If live, nothing loads - the ctor comment says the API scopes every response to the caller, so it waits for a session.

**On boot.** `_AppShellState.initState` builds `AppStore(api: widget.session.api)` and immediately calls `adoptSession(...)` (`lib/app_shell.dart::initState`), which sets `portal`/`meName`/`meId`, forces `source = live`, notifies, then fires `refresh()` **unawaited** (:211) - `initState` cannot await, and the banner reads `loadState` instead.

**`refresh({background})`** (:242-277):
1. Returns immediately if `source != live` (:243). In seed mode `refresh` is a no-op, which also makes the failure banner's Retry button inert there.
2. Unless `background`, sets `loadState = loading` and notifies. Background refreshes leave the screen alone - this is what stops `pollGeneration` (every 2 s) and `_act` (every mutation) from tearing the page down to a skeleton.
3. Clears `loadError`.
4. Branches on `portal == Portal.admin` -> `_loadAdmin()`, else `_loadCandidate()`.
5. Catches `ApiError` -> `loadError = e.message`; catches **everything else** -> `'Could not read the response from the server. $e'` (:261-273). The broad catch is deliberate: a `TypeError` inside a `fromJson` used to escape and leave `loadState` stuck on `loading` forever.
6. `finally { notifyListeners(); }`.

**`_loadAdmin` order** (:279-342). Nine calls issued **concurrently** via `Future.wait`, then one sequential call:

| Index | Call | Paged? | Assigned to |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `assessments(limit, offset)` | yes | `assessments` |
| 1 | `bank(limit, offset)` | yes | `bank` |
| 2 | `tags(limit, offset)` | yes | `tags` |
| 3 | `generators(limit, offset)` | yes | `generators` **via `_mergeGenerators`** |
| 4 | `drafts(limit, offset)` | yes | `drafts` |
| 5 | `settings()` | no | `settings` (unwraps `['data']`) |
| 6 | `responses(limit, offset)` | yes | `responseRows` (raw maps) |
| 7 | `ledger(limit, offset)` | yes | `ledger` |
| 8 | `budget()` | no | `budget` (unwraps `['data']`) |

Then `await _loadAttempts()` (:341), which is a single paged `/api/v1/attempts` sweep, not one call per assessment (:435-446), and which also builds `people` from the embedded `candidate` objects. Every result is read by **positional index** (`rows(0)`, `res[5]`, `res[8]`); the comment at :292-294 warns that inserting a call in the middle silently hands each list its neighbour's payload.

`_allPages` (:364-387) drives paging: `pageSize = 200`, reads `total` and `hasMore` out of `meta` (not the top level, not inside `data`), and breaks on `rows.isEmpty || (!hasMore && out.length >= total)`. So a single admin refresh is at minimum 10 requests and grows by one per extra 200-row page on any of the seven paged lists.

**`_loadCandidate`** (:464-481) is one call: `myAssessments()`, whose bucketed payload is flattened into a single `attempts` list. A candidate session therefore never populates `assessments`, `bank`, `drafts`, `generators`, `tags`, `people`, `ledger`, `budget`, `settings` or `responseRows`. Both member screens are written knowing this (`my_performance_screen.dart:114-117`, `my_assessments_screen.dart:72-75`).

**On navigation.** Detail screens hydrate themselves from `initState`, all inside `addPostFrameCallback` except `attempt_detail`:
- `assessment_detail_screen.dart:64` -> `loadAssessment(asmId)`
- `generator_detail_screen.dart:66` -> `loadGenerator(genId)`
- `attempt_detail_screen.dart:52` -> `loadAttempt(id)`
- `response_detail_screen.dart:48` -> `loadResponse(attemptId, questionId)`
- `review_queue_screen.dart:96` -> `loadDraft(d.id)` when a card is opened
- `assessment_detail_screen.dart:1461-1462` -> `loadDraft` or `loadQuestion` for the preview sheet
- `scoring_screen.dart:43` -> `loadScoring()` *(scoring_screen.dart: removed since 19.0.3.12.0)*
- `exam_screen.dart:102` -> `loadExamByToken(token)` only when `attemptByToken` misses; `exam_screen.dart:293` -> `loadExamReview(token)`

**After a mutation.** Every `_act` call ends with a full background `refresh()`. Nine methods stack a second read on top of that: `inviteMany`, `inviteByEmail`, `saveBankQuestion` (a second `refresh(background:)`), `setQuestionCount`, `saveExtraInstructions`, `setAllowedTypes`, `uploadResource`, `removeResource`, `saveDraft`, and the three media methods (`detectNow`, `captureUrl`, `applyVideo`) via `.then(loadQuestion)`.

**During generation.** `pollGeneration` (:3309-3337) loops up to `maxTicks = 90` at 2 s, calling `refresh(background: true)` each tick and comparing a `id:sopGenState` fingerprint. It returns as soon as no generator `isBusy`. Guarded by `_polling` against a parallel poll and by `_disposed` after each await. Worst case that is ~90 full admin refreshes, i.e. roughly 900 requests over three minutes.

#### Merge semantics: `_mergeGenerators`

`_mergeGenerators(List<Generator> current, List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows)` (:394-427) is the only place in the store where a list refresh does not overwrite what is held. It exists because **a `/generators` LIST row is a strict subset of a `/generators/<id>` DETAIL row** (:312-325): the list carries no `resources`, `allowed_types`, `select_all_types`, `sop_question_count`, `question_count_mode` or `similar`.

The mechanism:

```dart
final Map<String, Generator> held = { for (final g in current) g.id: g };   // :398-400
return rows.map((row) {
  final Generator fresh = Generator.fromJson(row);
  final Generator? old = held[fresh.id];
  if (old == null) return fresh;                                            // :404
  return fresh.copyWith(
    resources:  fresh.resources.isEmpty ? old.resources : fresh.resources,  // :408
    allowedTypes: row.containsKey('allowed_types') || row.containsKey('allowedTypes')
        ? fresh.allowedTypes : old.allowedTypes,                            // :409-412
    sopQuestionCount: row.containsKey('sop_question_count') || row.containsKey('sopQuestionCount')
        ? fresh.sopQuestionCount : old.sopQuestionCount,                    // :413-417
    questionCountMode: row.containsKey('question_count_mode') || row.containsKey('questionCountMode')
        ? fresh.questionCountMode : old.questionCountMode,                  // :418-422
    similar: fresh.similar.isEmpty ? old.similar : fresh.similar,           // :423
    meta:    fresh.meta.isEmpty    ? old.meta    : fresh.meta,              // :424
  );
}).toList();
```

Two different preservation tests are used, and the difference is load-bearing:

- **Key-presence** (`row.containsKey`, on the *raw* JSON map, checking both snake and camel spellings) for `allowedTypes`, `sopQuestionCount`, `questionCountMode`. This distinguishes "the list route did not send this field" from "the server genuinely sent an empty allow-list". Without it, clearing the allow-list on the server could never be reflected.
- **Value-emptiness** (`.isEmpty` on the parsed object) for `resources`, `similar`, `meta`. This **cannot** distinguish absent from genuinely-empty, so deleting the last resource on the server is invisible to a list refresh. That is exactly why `removeResource` and `uploadResource` both follow their `_act` with an explicit `loadGenerator(genId)` - the comment at :3494-3498 states it directly: the merge "preserves what was already held" and "cannot invent the change either".

Records the list no longer returns are **dropped** (the result is built from `rows`, not from `held`), so an archive takes effect; a generator not yet hydrated is taken as-is (:1097).

**What breaks without it.** The store's mutation path is: optimistic local edit -> server call -> `refresh(background: true)` in `_act`'s `finally`. With a plain `generators = rows(3).map(Generator.fromJson).toList()`, that background refresh overwrites every hydrated detail field with the list's thin version. Per the comment at :312-325, this produced both reported generator bugs: upload an SOP and the toast said "attached" while the corpus grid emptied a moment later (`resources` wiped); tick a question type and the chip lit, the server saved it, then the chip un-ticked (`allowedTypes` wiped) - indistinguishable from a broken checkbox. It also reverted the question count to Auto after any unrelated action, and `pollGeneration` re-wiped both every two seconds during a run.

**Gaps in the merge.** `Generator.copyWith` only exposes `sopQuestionCount`, `questionCountMode` and `sourceText` among the detail-only fields (`domain/models.dart:1156-1174`); everything else is carried through from `fresh`. So `sourceText`, `plannedCount`, `structureCount`, `selectedStructureCount`, `structureMode`, `sopGenError`, `tagExtractError`, `tagExtractLastRun`, `lastExtractSummary`, `ratingSchemeSummary`, `resourceCount`, `approvedCount`, `similarCount` and `active` are **not** protected - `_mergeGenerators` never passes `sourceText:`, so `fresh.sourceText` wins unconditionally. If the list route omits `source_text`, a saved "extra instructions" value is erased by the next background refresh; `saveExtraInstructions` happens to re-hydrate via `loadGenerator` (:3115), but any *other* action's `_act` refresh would wipe it again until a detail fetch runs. **UNKNOWN: which of these fields the `/api/v1/generators` list route actually sends** - that is server-side and not determinable from this repository.

No other entity has a merge. `bank`, `drafts`, `assessments`, `tags` and `attempts` are all assigned wholesale from list rows (:309-334), so a `loadQuestion`/`loadDraft`/`loadAssessment`/`loadAttempt` hydration is discarded by the next `refresh()`. Screens re-hydrate from `initState`, so this is normally invisible - but a background refresh triggered by any `_act` while a detail screen is open will thin that screen's record back to its list row, with no re-fetch.

**No test covers `_mergeGenerators`.** Greps across `test/` for merge-related assertions found nothing.

#### Error handling

| Site | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `refresh` :258-273 | `ApiError` -> `loadError = e.message`; **any other exception** -> `loadError = 'Could not read the response from the server. $e'`. Both set `loadState = failed`. Surfaced as a `Notice(tone: bad)` with a Retry button at `assessment_section.dart:240-252` |
| `_act` :1121-1131 | `ApiError` -> `toaster.bad(e.message)` (the module's own words); anything else -> `toaster.bad('$label failed. $e')`. Then `finally` refreshes regardless, so the server's version replaces the optimistic edit |
| `_hydrationFailed` :1857-1860 | `debugPrint` of exception + stack, plus `toaster.warn('Could not load the full record - showing partial data')`. Used by all six hydrators |
| Hydrators, `ApiError` branch | `toaster.bad(e.message)` |
| `_download` :2368-2372 | `ApiError` -> message; other -> `'$label failed: $e'`; empty/missing `content` -> `'$label returned nothing'` |
| `addAssessment` :1630, `importBank` :2949-2957, `createGeneratorWithSop` :1729-1735 | catch and toast, return `null` rather than throwing |
| `createGeneratorWithSop` upload failure :1713-1724 | Refreshes, then toasts `'$name was created but the file did not attach: ...'` and **still returns the id**, so the user can attach from the corpus tab |
| `finishExam` :2827-2845 | `attempt_locked` is treated as **success** (the server settled it first); any other `ApiError` rolls the local attempt back and toasts "Your exam was NOT submitted" |

**Swallowed on purpose, with a stated reason:**
- `signOut` :219 - a failed `logout` still ends the local session.
- `loadExamByToken` :2024-2026 - a dead token leaves the cache untouched so the exam screen shows its own gate.
- `loadExamReview` :2662-2665 - a failed checklist fetch must not block submitting.
- `beginExam` :2447 and `recordViolation` :2730 - fire-and-forget; the violation report (`_reconcileViolation`) drops every error except 409 `time_expired`, which raises the time-up message and moves to the completion screen (round 3, MT3-01).
- `_syncAnswer` :2684-2697 - autosave failures are `debugPrint`ed, because `finishExam` re-sends everything; a failure other than `attempt_locked`, a 409 or `incomplete_answer` raises the once-per-sitting `_warnAutosaveFailing` connectivity warning. `incomplete_answer` is exempt (19.0.3.23.0): the server holds a half-finished answer as a draft, so the refusal is silent on autosave - an A/B answer written verdicts-first met it on every save and read as data loss. `time_expired` raises the time-up message and moves to the completion screen.

**Swallowed with no reason given:** `loadScoring` :3001-3003 catches `ApiError` and toasts, but has no general `catch` - a parse error there escapes into an unawaited future.

#### Loading and busy flags

Three independent mechanisms:

1. **`loadState` / `loadError`** - page level. `assessment_section.dart:238` shows a 2 px `LinearProgressIndicator` while loading; `:240-252` shows the error `Notice`; `:417-432` shows a full `ListScreenSkeleton` only when `loadState == loading && isEmpty` **and** the current route is one of the ten list-shaped routes, so the skeleton never paints over the exam runner, a detail page or a form.
2. **`_busy` / `isBusy(key)` / `withBusy`** (:92-107) - per-action, keyed `verb:recordId`, cleared in a `finally`. Keys actually set: `count:<gen>`, `approveall:<gen>`, `tags:<gen>`, `scoring`, `scoring:queue`, `draft:<id>`, `bank:<id>`, `instructions:<gen>`, `types:<gen>`, `archive:<gen>`, `similarity:<gen>`, `image:<draft>`, `settings`, `normalizetags`, and `submit:<attempt>` (held by `finishExam` for the whole live submit, read by the exam's Submit button; round 3).
3. **`_hydrating` / `isHydrating(kind, id)`** (:558-576) - per-record detail fetch, keyed `kind:id`, used so a detail screen can tell "still arriving" from "genuinely not here" instead of claiming a deletion. Read at `attempt_detail_screen.dart:67`, `generator_detail_screen.dart:134`, `assessment_detail_screen.dart:79`, `response_detail_screen.dart:71`.

Mismatches found:
- `scoring_screen.dart:189` reads `s.isBusy('requeue')`, but **`requeueErrored` never sets that key** (:2252 goes straight to `_act` with no `withBusy`). That spinner can never appear. *(scoring_screen.dart: removed since 19.0.3.12.0)*
- `types:<gen>` (:3127) and `instructions:<gen>` (:3105) are set but read by no screen.
- `withBusy` is public but has no caller outside the store.

#### Seed mode

`DataSource.seed` (:38) is a complete offline fixture set. It is selected in exactly one place - the constructor initialiser `source = (api != null || hasBackend) ? DataSource.live : DataSource.seed` (:53) - where `hasBackend` is `kApiBaseUrl.isNotEmpty` and `kApiBaseUrl` comes from `String.fromEnvironment('API_BASE_URL', defaultValue: '')` (`data/api_client.dart:35-46`). The explicit `api != null` clause exists because a test binary has no `--dart-define`, so without it a test would fall back to fixtures and report itself signed in.

When selected, the constructor calls `_load()` (:652-663), which copies `SeedData.build()` into `generators`, `drafts`, `bank`, `assessments`, `attempts`, `people`, `jobs`, `ledger`, `tags`, and sets `loadState = ready` synchronously. The fixtures (`state/seed_data.dart`, 1546 lines) are 10 people, 4 generators, 10 bank questions, 12 drafts, 5 assessments spanning all four `AsmState` values (:966-1050), attempts, 3 jobs, a ledger built from generators + the first 12 attempts + 2 unattributed rows (:1449-1520), and 15 tags of which 3 are deliberate near-duplicates carrying `mergeInto` (:1536-1545). Everything that varies is derived from `stableHash` (FNV-1a, 32-bit) in `util/seed.dart:25-55` rather than from a random source, so the same input always gives the same output on both the VM and the web - the split 16-bit multiply at `seed.dart:32` exists specifically because `0xFFFFFFFF * 0x01000193` exceeds 2^53 and would produce different hashes in compiled JavaScript.

Behaviour in seed mode: `refresh()` returns immediately (:243); `api` is `null` (:72); `isAuthenticated` is unconditionally `true` (:117-118); `_act` runs `ifSeed` and never touches the network (:1110-1113); every `load*` hydrator returns early; `answerSheet` builds the sheet from fixtures through the same `AnswerSheet.fromJson` parser (:687-707); `gradeOne` runs the seeded subjective grader (:2134-2144); `advanceJobs`/`_startJobTicker` animate a fake generation queue. Roughly twenty methods respond with an info toast instead - "Editing runs against a live server", "Uploads need a live backend", "Bulk approve needs a live backend", and so on.

**Risk of masking a broken server.** In the shipped app this is currently not reachable: the only `AppStore` construction in `lib/` is `AppStore(api: widget.session.api)` (`lib/app_shell.dart:54`), and `Session.api` is non-null by construction (`lib/session.dart::api`), so `source` is always `live`. The exposure is elsewhere:

- **Tests.** Every widget test that writes `AppStore()` gets a fully populated store with `loadState == ready` and no network at all. A screen assertion like "the console lists five assessments" passes identically whether the live payload parsing works or not, because a screen "never asks which one it is looking at" (:36-37). Only tests that inject a spy client exercise the wire.
- **A build without `--dart-define=API_BASE_URL`.** `hasBackend` is false and `resolveMediaUrl` also degrades silently (`api_client.dart:64`). If a future code path ever constructs `AppStore()` without an api, the app boots into a self-consistent world with `isAuthenticated == true`, no login gate, and no way for any screen to tell.
- **Failure looks like success.** Seed mode's refusals are `toaster.info(...)` - the same neutral tone used for "Nothing pending" - not errors. And `refresh()` returning early means the error `Notice` and its Retry button in `assessment_section.dart:240-252` are permanently inert, so the one surface that would report a broken backend cannot fire.
- **The one honest signal is unused.** `backendLabel` (:122) exists to print "Demo data - no backend configured" under the login title. Nothing in `lib/` or `test/` reads it.

#### Stateful things that look fragile

- **`AppStore.dispose()` closes a client it does not own.** `dispose` calls `_api.close()` (:525), but `_api` is the `Session`'s long-lived `ApiClient` (`lib/app_shell.dart:54`, `lib/session.dart:18-22`), and `close()` is `_http.close()` (`api_client.dart::close`). `Session.signOut` notifies -> `main.dart:93-107` switches `home` to `LoginScreen` -> `AppShell` unmounts -> `_store.dispose()` -> the session's HTTP client is closed. The same happens on a uid change, because `AppShell` is keyed on `_session.uid` (`main.dart:96`). A subsequent `signIn` on that `Session` would then use a closed `http.Client`. I read this statically and did not execute it, but I can find nothing that reopens or replaces the client.
- **`_clear()` is incomplete** (:502-514). It resets nine entity lists and `meName`, but leaves `settings`, `responseRows`, `scoring`, `budget`'s companions, `examByToken`, `examReviewByToken`, `acknowledged`, `lastDecision`, `meId`, `portal`, `_busy`, `_hydrating` and `loadError` untouched. It is also only reachable from `AppStore.signOut`, which the app never calls - so in production the store is thrown away rather than cleared, which happens to be safer.
- **`decideDraft` double-toasts in live mode.** It toasts `'Approved - ${d.name} is in the bank'` at :961, then passes an `okMessage` returning the identical string to `_act` at :980. `Toaster.show` has no dedupe (`widgets/feedback.dart::show`), so two identical toasts stack.
- **`undoDecision` (:991-1010) never contacts the server.** `decideDraft` persists the approval through `_act`; `undoDecision` only reverses `drafts` and `bank` locally. The next `refresh()` - which `_act` fires after every subsequent action - restores the server's approved state, so the undo silently expires.
- **`signRubric` (:1017-1039) flips `rubricReviewed` in both `drafts` and `bank`** with the same `flip` closure. A question approved out of the review queue keeps its id, so if it exists in both lists both copies toggle from one press. `nowReviewed` is computed from `bankById(...) ?? draftById(...)` (:1020-1023), so the value sent to the server is the bank copy's when both exist.
- **`refresh()` has no re-entrancy guard.** `_act`'s `finally` refresh, `pollGeneration`'s 2 s tick, an `initState` hydration and the boot refresh can all be in flight simultaneously. `_loadAdmin` assigns fields positionally after a `Future.wait`, so two overlapping runs interleave arbitrarily and the later-finishing one wins per field. `_mergeGenerators` reads the `generators` field at the moment it runs, so an overlapping refresh can merge onto a list another refresh is about to replace.
- **`_allPages` (:364-387) has no iteration cap.** It breaks only on `rows.isEmpty` or `!hasMore && out.length >= total`. A server that reports `hasMore: true` on every page loops forever with no timeout and no tick limit.
- **`_loadAdmin`'s positional indexing** (:306-339). `rows(0)`..`rows(4)`, `res[5]`, `rows(6)`, `rows(7)`, `res[8]`. The file warns "APPEND, never insert" (:292-294); the invariant is enforced only by that comment.
- **Detail screens hydrate in `initState` only.** None of `assessment_detail_screen`, `generator_detail_screen`, `attempt_detail_screen` or `response_detail_screen` implements `didUpdateWidget`. `_page()` (`assessment_section.dart::_page`) builds them without keys, so navigating from one record of a kind straight to another record of the same kind at the same tree position reuses the `State` and never re-hydrates. Going list -> detail -> back -> detail unmounts and is safe; a direct detail-to-detail link is not.
- **`allResponses()` runs on every frame.** `_sectionEntries()` calls it to compute the responses badge (`assessment_section.dart:337-343`), and `_sectionEntries()` is called from `build`. Every `notifyListeners()` - including one per keystroke path, per busy toggle and per hydration start/stop - re-flattens the entire response set. `scoringErrorCount` (:908) does the same again.
- **`attemptsForPerson` matches on `employeeId.isEmpty`** (:840). The rationale (:833-839) is that a candidate's self-scoped endpoint omits the candidate object. But the predicate is unconditional: if an admin-loaded attempt ever arrives without an `employeeId`, it is attributed to whichever person is asked about. Only member screens call this today.
- **`_answerSync` is keyed by `questionId` alone** (:2486, :2670). Two attempts open on the same question id would share a debounce slot. `_syncAnswer` also captures `ev` at scheduling time and sends `ev.token` a second later.
- **`dispose` cancels pending autosaves rather than flushing them** (:521-524), so up to one second of typing is dropped. `finishExam` re-sends everything, which covers the normal path but not an unmount without submitting.
- **`examByToken` and `examReviewByToken` are never evicted.** They grow for the lifetime of the store and survive `_clear()`.
- **`fixResource` (:3501-3520) has no `_live` guard** and no server call. Against a real backend it marks a failed resource `ready` and invents `pages: 14` purely in memory, until the next `refresh` or `loadGenerator` contradicts it.
- **`retryJob` (:3430-3444) likewise has no `_live` guard**, and mutates the fixture-only `jobs` list.
- **`meId` defaults to the fixture literal `'P-1'`** (:635) and is only overwritten by `adoptSession` (:206). `Person get me` (:815) falls back to `people.first`, which throws on an empty roster - unused today, but it is a live landmine.
- **`portal` defaults to `Portal.admin`** (:614). Only `adoptSession` sets it, through `Portal.fromOrgRole` (an unknown role is `member`); `_portalFromServer` and `Portal.parse` were removed in round 3 (A-105). The field default itself is the opposite direction.
- **A background refresh that fails still flips `loadState` to `failed`** (:259), so the red banner appears over a screen that already holds good data - including on a `pollGeneration` tick or after any `_act`.
- **Misplaced doc comments.** The block at :344-363 documents `_loadAttempts` but sits above `_allPages`; the block at :1955-1964 documents `loadExamByToken` but sits above the `examByToken` field; the block at :2499-2517 documents `_syncAnswer` but sits above `approveAllDrafts`. The generated API docs will attach each to the wrong member.
- **`SeedData.metaFor(Generator g)` and `tagsFor(Generator g)` ignore their argument** (`seed_data.dart:329-337`), always returning `_meta1` and one fixed tag list. `_meta2` is used only by the literal generator at `seed_data.dart:205`.
- The class doc-comment at :9-17 enumerates "the four invariants this file is responsible for" and then lists numbers 1, 3 and 5. Invariants 2 and 4 are referenced elsewhere in the file (:1250, :1285) but never listed in the header.


## 3.3 ApiClient: every call the app can make

Source: `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart` (1291 lines when this section was written, 2,527 in 19.0.3.23.0; one class `ApiClient` + top-level symbols), `lib/assessment/data/bank_payload.dart` (131 lines, three top-level functions, no class).

#### Transport

| Concern | Behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Base URL | `String.fromEnvironment('API_BASE_URL', defaultValue: '')`, i.e. a `--dart-define` at build time. Constructor arg `baseUrl` overrides it. Trailing slashes stripped with `replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '')`. | `api_client.dart:35-38`, `:108-111` |
| "Is there a backend" | `hasBackend` is just `kApiBaseUrl.isNotEmpty`. When false the app runs on bundled seed data. | `api_client.dart:46`; consumed at `lib/assessment/state/app_store.dart:53,123,223-225` |
| DB name | `kApiDb` from `--dart-define=API_DB`. Sent on exactly one call - `_loginModule`, and only when non-empty. | `api_client.dart:42`, `:319` |
| HTTP verb | **Every call is POST.** There is one `_http.post` and no other verb anywhere in the file, including reads and paged lists. Filters/paging ride in the JSON body. | `api_client.dart:186`; rationale at `:154-161` (Odoo `json2` reads only the body) |
| Headers | `Content-Type: application/json` always; `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when `_bearer != null`; `Cookie: session_id=<id>` when `_session != null`. No `Accept`, no CSRF token, no custom headers. Both auth headers are sent together if both happen to be set. | `api_client.dart:147-151` |
| Credentials held | Three nullable fields: `_session` (Odoo cookie), `_bearer` (gateway access token), `_refresh` (gateway refresh token). Instance state, not global. | `api_client.dart:95-106` |
| Credential persistence | `_persistTokens()` writes bearer+refresh to `sessionStorage` keys `etp.bearer` / `etp.refresh` on web, or no-ops on the stub. `_session` (the cookie) is **never** persisted. | `api_client.dart:136-143`; `lib/services/token_store_web.dart:14-47`; `lib/services/token_store_stub.dart:21-25` |
| Cookie capture | Regex `session_id=([^;]+)` over the `set-cookie` response header, and only on a 2xx. | `api_client.dart:245-259` |
| Timeouts | **None.** No `.timeout()`, no `Client` configured with one. A hung socket hangs the call forever. | grep for `timeout` in the file returns only unrelated identifiers (`retryVideo`, prose) |
| Retry | Exactly one, and only for HTTP 401: refresh the bearer and replay once. Guards: `allowRetry:false` on the replay, `_refresh` must be non-null, and paths starting `/api/v1/auth` are excluded. No backoff, no retry on 5xx or network failure. Since 19.0.3.23.0 the refresh is shared: a call whose bearer was renewed while it was in flight replays without refreshing, and concurrent 401s await one `refreshSession()` (see 3.1 Session and auth). | `api_client.dart::_send`, `api_client.dart::refreshSession` |
| Transport failure | Any `Exception` from `post` becomes `ApiError('Could not reach $uri: $e')` with `isDomain:false`, `status:null`. | `api_client.dart:185-189` |

#### Envelope unwrapping

`_send` is the single funnel (`api_client.dart:178-243`). Order of operations:

1. POST, catching `Exception` → transport `ApiError`.
2. `_captureSession(res)` - 2xx only.
3. `jsonDecode(res.body) as Map<String, dynamic>`. A `FormatException` (non-JSON body) becomes `ApiError` with the message `"Your session has expired. Sign in again."` for 401/403, otherwise `"Unexpected response from $path"`, carrying `status`. `api_client.dart:193-205`
4. **401 refresh-and-replay**, before any error is raised. `api_client.dart:215-222`
5. Failure test is `body['ok'] == false || res.statusCode >= 400`. The message is taken from `error.message`, then top-level `message`, then `error` itself if it is a String, then the literal `'Request failed'`. `code` is `error.code ?? body['code']`. `isDomain` is true only when `body['ok'] == false` - a 4xx with no `ok:false` is reported as non-domain. `api_client.dart:224-239`
6. Success: `return body['data'] is Map<String,dynamic> ? body['data'] : body;` - so **when `data` is a List (or absent), callers get the whole envelope including `ok` and `meta`**. `api_client.dart:241-242`

That last line is load-bearing for paging: `app_store.dart:374-382` relies on it to reach `meta.total` / `meta.hasMore`, which are only visible because list routes put a List in `data`. For routes whose `data` is a Map, any top-level `meta` is discarded and unreachable.

`ApiError` (`api_client.dart::ApiError`) carries `message`, `isDomain`, `status`, `code`; `toString()` returns the message.

#### The parsing helpers

`jget` / `jval` / `jid` / `jobj` / `jtags` are **not in either scoped file**. They live in `lib/assessment/domain/models.dart:22-100` and are used by the model `fromJson` constructors and by `app_store.dart`, `widgets/chatter.dart`, `widgets/emails_panel.dart`. `api_client.dart` itself does no field parsing beyond the envelope - it hands raw maps upward.

| Helper | Signature | Behaviour | Silent-default risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jget` `models.dart::jget` | `Object? jget(Map<String,dynamic> j, String camel)` | Returns `j[camel]` if the key is **present** (`containsKey`, so an explicit `null` value wins over the snake fallback). Otherwise converts camelCase→snake_case by `replaceAllMapped(RegExp(r'[A-Z]'), '_' + lowercase)` and returns `j[snake]`. | Returns `null` for a missing key - no error. Conversion is one-way and naive: `raw100` stays `raw100`, `sopCoverage` → `sop_coverage`. An acronym like `httpURL` becomes `http_u_r_l`. |
| `jval<T>` `models.dart:49-56` | `T jval<T>(Map, String camel, T fallback)` | `null` → fallback. **Double check runs first**: `fallback is double && v is num` → `v.toDouble()`. Then `fallback is int && v is num` → `v.toInt()`. Then `v is T` → `v`. Else fallback. | **Every type mismatch silently yields the fallback.** A String `"12"` where an `int` is expected returns the fallback, not 12 and not an error. The double-first ordering is deliberate and documented at `:44-48`: in compiled JS `0.0 is int` is true, so int-first truncated currency values in the browser while VM tests passed. |
| `jid` `models.dart::jid` | `String jid(Object? v)` | `null` → `''`, otherwise `v.toString()`. Normalises Odoo integer ids and fixture string ids (`A-1`) to one `String id`. | A missing id becomes `''` rather than failing; downstream lookups then miss silently. |
| `jobj` `models.dart::jobj` | `Map<String,dynamic> jobj(Map, String camel)` | Returns the value when it is a `Map<String,dynamic>`, else `const {}`. | A nested group that arrives as a List or a scalar degrades to `{}` - every field read from it then takes its own fallback. |
| `jtags` `models.dart::jtags+` | `List<String> jtags(Map)` | Reads `tags`, maps non-map entries via `'$t'`, and for map entries prefers `display`, then `label`, then `name` with any `facet:` prefix stripped. | Casts `jget(j,'tags') ?? []` to `List<dynamic>` unguarded - a non-list `tags` value would throw a `TypeError`. |

Net effect: **a malformed payload almost never produces an error.** `jval` and `jobj` degrade to defaults, so an entirely wrong response shape parses "successfully" into an object of zeros and empty strings. The header comment at `models.dart:13-21` states this was itself the fix for an earlier bug (camelCase-only reads made live payloads render as rows of zeros), so the failure mode was traded, not removed.

#### bank_payload.dart

Pure, dependency-free (only `dart:convert`), tested by `test/assessment/import_test.dart`. Only consumer in the app is `lib/assessment/widgets/import_sheet.dart:206,222`.

**`payloadFromText(String text, String fileName) → Map<String,dynamic>`** (`bank_payload.dart:22-42`) - builds the *import* payload: *(bank_payload.dart: removed since 19.0.3.12.0)*

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| empty / whitespace-only | throws `const FormatException('The file is empty.')` |
| text starting `{` | `jsonDecode` then `Map<String,dynamic>.from(parsed as Map<String,dynamic>)` |
| text starting `[` | `{'question_bank': <the list>}` |
| anything else | treated as CSV: `{'question_bank': rowsFromCsv(text)}` |
| all cases | `payload['project'] ??= {'name': stemOf(fileName)}` - only fills in when absent |

Output shape is therefore `{project: {name: ...}, question_bank: [...]}`, matching what `ApiClient.importBank` sends under its `payload` key (`api_client.dart:752-762`). There is **no export side in this file** - it only parses in. The native-export round trip referenced by `importBank(native: true)` is server-produced; nothing here builds it. CSV export lives elsewhere (`lib/services/csv_export.dart`).

**`stemOf(String)`** `:45-48` - substring before the last `.`, but only when `dot > 0`, so `.gitignore` returns unchanged.

**`rowsFromCsv(String) → List<Map<String,dynamic>>`** `:56-131` - hand-rolled RFC 4180 subset: quoted fields, doubled `""` escapes, embedded commas, `\r` discarded, `\n` ends a row. Header row lower-cased and trimmed. Rows where every cell is blank are skipped. Returns `const []` when fewer than 2 physical rows exist (header-only file yields no rows and no error).

Per-row output keys and their column sources:

| Output key | Column | Default when the column is absent |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `name` | `''` |
| `question_type` | `type` | `'mcq'` |
| `difficulty` | `difficulty` | `'medium'` |
| `prompt` | `prompt` | `''` |
| `options` | `options`, split on `\|`, trimmed, blanks dropped | key omitted entirely when the list is empty |
| `options[].is_correct` | `o.toLowerCase() == answer_key.toLowerCase()` | all `false` when `answer_key` is absent or matches nothing |

Notes on this parser:
- Columns not in the list above (any extra CSV column) are read into `r` but **dropped**; only the six keys above are emitted.
- If a data line has fewer cells than the header, the loop `i < head.length && i < line.length` leaves the trailing columns unset, so they take their defaults. Extra cells beyond the header are dropped.
- An `answer_key` that matches no option produces a question with **no correct option and no error**. Whether the server rejects that is server-side; nothing here checks.
- Duplicate header names silently overwrite each other in `r`.
- The `\r` handling is a blanket `c != '\r'` discard in the unquoted branch only; inside quotes a `\r` is written into the cell.

#### Things that look wrong, dead, contradictory, or half-finished

1. **`createAssessment` sends proctoring-rule keys the server does not accept.** `_ruleBody` emits `e.key.wire` (`api_client.dart::_ruleBody`), and `ProctorRule.wire` values are the bare names (`tab_switch`, `copy_paste`, ...), while `ASSESSMENT_FIELDS` allow-lists the `rule_block_*` spellings. The docstring immediately above `_ruleBody` claims the keys are "`rule_block_tab_switch` and friends" - they are not. `updateAssessment` sends the `rule_block_*` / `rule_*` spellings (`:1152-1159`). The server allow-list is `rule_block_tab_switch`, `rule_block_screenshot`, `rule_block_copy_paste`, `rule_block_right_click`, `rule_block_devtools`, `rule_watermark`, `rule_fullscreen`, `rule_webcam` (`ethara-etp/custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/write.py:383-394`), and `_picked` drops any key not named there without error (`write.py:69-80`). The live caller passes `rules: a.rules.asMap` (`lib/assessment/state/app_store.dart:1610`), so **creating an assessment from this app silently applies the server's default proctoring rules regardless of the eight switches the operator set** - the exact failure mode the comment at `api_client.dart:1070-1075` says was fixed. No test covers it.
2. **FIXED - `refreshSession` could recurse without a base case.** The renewal now posts through `_send(..., allowRetry: false)` (`api_client.dart::_renew`, whose comment records 195 consecutive 401s and a crashed tab), and since 19.0.3.23.0 concurrent renewals share one future. The original finding, kept for the record: `refreshSession` called `_call('/api/v1/refresh_token', ...)` (`:339-342`), i.e. `allowRetry: true`. The 401 guard excludes only paths starting `/api/v1/auth` (`:218`); `/api/v1/refresh_token` does not match. So a 401 from the refresh route re-enters `refreshSession` → `_call` → 401 → `refreshSession` … with `_refresh` still set, and the `on ApiError` clearing at `:362-364` is never reached because nothing throws. Depends on the server answering 401 (rather than 400/422) for a spent refresh token - UNKNOWN which it returns; the risk is in the client either way.
3. **A JSON body that is not an object throws an uncaught `TypeError`.** `jsonDecode(res.body) as Map<String, dynamic>` (`:195`) is guarded by `on FormatException` only. A valid JSON array or scalar response casts-fails with a `TypeError`, which is an `Error`, not an `Exception`, so it escapes `_send` entirely and callers' `on ApiError catch` blocks miss it.
4. **`code` is cast, not coerced.** `(detail['code'] ?? body['code']) as String?` (`:237`). A numeric or object `code` throws `TypeError` from inside the error path, replacing the domain refusal with a crash. Contrast `message`, which is defensively `.toString()`d on the line above.
5. **`leaderboard` puts `limit` in the query string** (`:819`) while the file's own transport note says `json2` "reads only the BODY and ignores the query string" (`:159-161`). By that note the parameter is ignored. The method is dead, so this has no runtime effect today.
6. **`leaderboard` depends on the envelope-unwrap fall-through.** It reads `r['data']` (`:821`), which only works because `_send` returns the whole body when `data` is not a Map (`:241-242`). If the route ever returned `data` as an object, this silently returns `const []`.
7. **`importBank` coerces a non-numeric generator id to `0`**: `int.tryParse(generatorId) ?? 0` (`:760`). A seed-style id such as `G-1` becomes generator 0 with no error.
8. **`login` returns two different shapes** - `{'user': ...}` from the gateway (`:313`) versus the raw data map from the module (`:317-322`). The one call site left, `lib/session.dart:86-91`, defends against this (the store's `signIn`, the other one, was removed in round 3), but the method's own type signature says nothing about it.
9. **Cookie auth cannot work on a web build.** `_captureSession` reads `res.headers['set-cookie']` (`:255`); `Set-Cookie` is a forbidden response header for browser fetch/XHR, so on the web target (`package:web`, `token_store_web.dart`, `*_web.dart` conditional imports throughout) `_session` will never be set and the `/api/v1/auth/session` fallback path is effectively bearer-only. No comment in the file acknowledges this.
10. **The file header points at a module that does not exist at the stated path.** `api_client.dart:3-4` names `../../odoo_addon/etp_assessment_api`; there is no `etp_assessment_api` under `/Users/cj/Developer/ethara/ethara-etp`. The API routes are in `ethara-etp/custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers/api/`, alongside the model addon `custom_addons/etp_assessment_pro`.
11. **Misplaced and duplicated doc comments.** The envelope-shape explanation at `:206-214` sits above the 401-retry block, not above the error block at `:224` that it describes. `_call`'s doc `:154-172` is two unrelated comments concatenated (json2 rationale + retry rationale). `draft(id)` at `:1023` carries a stray first line "The approved pool. Only what is in here can be served to a candidate." (`:1017`) that belongs to `bank()`. `postChatter` `:974-988` has two competing summary lines ("Add to a record's audit trail." and "Add a line to a record's history.").
12. **Section placement.** `emails()` `:458` is defined inside the "Candidate" block between `examAnswer` and `examReview`, though its own docstring describes it as an admin/manager-scoped route.
13. **No timeout on any request** (see Transport). During an exam this means a stalled `examSubmit` never resolves and never surfaces an error.
14. **`detectNow` passes `<String, dynamic>{}` explicitly** (`:791`) where every other zero-body method relies on `_call`'s default - harmless inconsistency.


## 3.4 Domain models, enums, gates, and navigation

Scope: `lib/assessment/domain/models.dart` (2861 lines when written; 6,560 in 19.0.3.23.0), `domain/enums.dart` (742; now 1,279), `domain/gates.dart` (213; now 217), `domain/nav_entries.dart` (115), `nav.dart` (236), `assessment_section.dart` (546; now 853). All read in full at the time; bare line numbers below are from that reading. Line citations are relative to `/Users/cj/Developer/ethara/ethara-assessment-fe/`.

#### 1. Parsing substrate (models.dart top)

Every `fromJson` in the layer goes through five helpers rather than raw map reads. The reason is stated at `lib/assessment/domain/models.dart:13-29`: the Odoo API speaks snake_case and sends integer ids, while the seed fixtures speak camelCase with string ids, and both must land in the same object.

| Helper | Where | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `jget(j, camel)` | 22 | Reads `camel`; if absent, lowers each capital to `_x` and reads that. So `questionLimit` also matches `question_limit`. This is why the per-class tables below list only the aliases that are *not* mechanical case conversions. |
| `humanBytes(int)` | 35 | Byte count to `B` / `KB` / `MB`. Returns `''` for `<= 0`. |
| `jval<T>(j, camel, fallback)` | 49 | `jget` plus a default. The `double` branch is checked **before** `int` deliberately: on the JS runtime `0.0 is int` is true, so an int-first order truncated every double to zero on web only. The *runtime type of the fallback* selects the coercion, so passing `0` where a double is wanted silently truncates (see `LedgerRow.cost`, `:5348`). |
| `jid(v)` | 63 | `v.toString()`, `''` for null. Normalises integer Odoo ids to `String id`. |
| `jobj(j, camel)` | 71 | A nested map, or `{}` when the key is absent or not a map. Lets a parser read a group (`candidate`, `flags`, `result`, `subjective`) then fall back to the flat fixture spelling. |
| `jtags(j)` | 91 | Tag names out of `tags`. Prefers `display`, then `label`, then `name` with any `facet:` prefix stripped. Accepts bare strings (fixtures) and objects (API). |

Private normalisers: `_correctAnswers` (`:579`, string-or-list to list), `_rubricLines` (`:649`, flattens a map-of-lists or a list to display lines), `_labelBoxNumbers` (`:676`, accepts `[1,2,5]` from the exam route and `[{number:1,...}]` from the draft route, sorted ascending), `_assetsWithBoxes` (`:699`, attaches `label_boxes` regions to the **first** image only), `_marksPart` (`:1984`, splits a server `"N / M"` string), `_labels` (`:5103`, strings-or-note-objects to display strings), `_kindTone` (`:5117`, server `kind` to `Tone`, unrecognised stays `inert`).

#### 2. Model classes

##### The marks contract, client side - **added 25 August**

The server's unit of scoring is the COMPONENT, and the client was brought into line with it in
this cycle. Four things to know before reading any marks code in `lib/`:

- **`Response` carries the server's numbers and prefers them.** `finalMark`, `finalMax`,
  `mcqMark`, `objectiveMarksMax`, `rawScore` and `rawMax` are all parsed off the response row.
  `Response.mark` is `finalMark?.round() ?? (hasObjective ? score : llmScore)` - the server
  wins, and the old two-half reading is only a pre-field fallback. `Response.markOutOf` treats
  a `finalMax` of **0 as "not stated"**, not as zero marks, and falls back the same way.
  `Response.hasRaw` is `(rawMax ?? 0) > 0`, which is how a purely objective question drops out
  of the raw display rather than rendering a 0.
- **`Question.componentCount`** = keyed dimensions plus one if subjective, floored at 1. It is
  the client's local mirror of the server's `_component_counts`, and it is what
  `Attempt.maxMarks` sums when the server sends no total. That fallback used to be
  `totalQuestions`; the two have parted company, and a screen that still divides by the
  question count is wrong.
- **`Attempt.maxMarks` is `serverTotal ?? sum(componentCount)`** - summed over the questions this attempt drew (`questionOrder`), the whole pool only when that is empty (seed data; round 3, A-104) - and `Attempt.earnedMarks` sums
  `r.mark`, not `r.score`. `Attempt.rawOutOf` sums `rawMax` and returns **null** when no answer
  states one - a list route sends no per-question rows - so the caller prints the raw bare
  rather than over a guessed denominator.
- **`AnswerSheetRow.marksAvailable` defaults to 1, never 0**, because it is used as a divisor.
  `marksEarned` is parsed **only when `released`** and is null otherwise; `category_scores.dart`
  therefore uses `marksEarned != null` plus a non-inert tone to decide a row counts at all,
  since an ungraded row still arrives as `marks_earned: 0.0`.

Two server fields are **not** consumed by the client at all: `label_fraction` and
`label_box_scores_json`. Neither is serialised (section 1.7), and no spelling of either appears
in `lib/` or `test/`. `Subscores` carries only `labelCoveragePct` and `labelCorrectnessPct`,
both marked in the source as reporting-only.

Read the wire keys through `jget(j, camelKey)`, which tries the camelCase key and then lowers
each capital to `_x`. That is why a snake_case grep over `lib/` finds almost nothing.
