#### The member/candidate-facing side

**What a candidate can reach.** `Portal.member` gets a two-entry sidebar - "My assessments" (`mine`) and "My performance" (`performance`) - from `memberNav()` (`domain/nav_entries.dart::memberNav`), selected in `assessment_section.dart:338`. The exam runner is a third surface reached only from a card, or directly from an invitation deep link: `_openEntry` resets to `Exam(token)` before considering the entry when `widget.examToken` is non-empty (`assessment_section.dart:137-147`).

**What they see.**

*My assessments* (`my_assessments_screen.dart`): one card per attempt, in an `AutoGrid(minWidth: 288)`. Bucketing is `_bucketOf` (`:44-61`): `isDone` -> `completed` wins over everything; with no assessment record loaded (the normal candidate case), `inProgress` state -> `inProgress`, everything else -> `available`; with an assessment loaded, `inProgress`+`inProgress` -> `inProgress`, `AsmState.inProgress` -> `available`, `AsmState.draft` -> `upcoming`, otherwise `closed`. Filter chips render `All` plus only the buckets with a non-zero count (`:107-114`). Each card shows title, question count and duration (or "No time limit"), a state pill, and:

| Bucket | Middle of card | Call to action |
|---|---|---|
| available | - | `Btn.primary('Start assessment')` -> `nav.exam(token)` |
| inProgress | progress bar + "N of M answered" | `Btn.primary('Resume')` -> `nav.examQuestion(token, firstUnanswered)` |
| completed, not released | "Awaiting release..." sentence | `Btn('See my submission')` -> `nav.examComplete(token)` |
| completed, released | `Pill.state(result)` + `ThresholdBar` + `Marks(earned, total)` in the header row | `Btn('See my answers')` -> `nav.examAnswers(token)` |
| upcoming | - | plain text "Opens <IST timestamp>." (or "Opens once it is scheduled."); a plain `d/m/yyyy` date before 19.0.3.23.0 |
| closed | - | plain text "This assessment closed without a submission from you." |

A proctoring violation count, when > 0, prints "N proctoring violation(s) recorded." in warn colour (`:294-300`). Since 19.0.3.23.0 a completed card also carries: on a released result whose written answers are still queued, `ev.pendingMarkingNote` ("N written answers have not been marked yet - your total may rise when they are.") under the grey "Pending" pill, which otherwise reads as a fail (N11); and "Ended on the clock. Time used: 38 of 45 min." (the first sentence only when `endedOnClock`) from `timeUsed` (Q12). Below 720px the rail is a drawer, so the cards get the full width (row 49).

*My performance* (`my_performance_screen.dart`): four KPIs (Best result as marks, Passed of released, Completed, Awaiting release), two `ScoreRing`s (Pass rate = passed/released; Marks earned = pooled earned/available), a `DataGrid` breakdown with columns Assessment / Submitted / Score / Against pass mark / Result, and - only when `released.length >= 2` - a "Your marks over time" panel with a `Sparkline` plus a `BarChart` (`:213-218`, `:438-475`). Changed in 19.0.3.23.0: the per-sitting category (strengths and weaknesses) panels judge each category against `ev.passMarkPercent(asm)` - the pass mark the server applied, the same one the breakdown's `ThresholdBar` uses - instead of `asm?.passThreshold ?? 70`, which a candidate (who cannot load the assessment) always got as 70, filing 60-69% categories as weaknesses on a 60% paper (row 57); the "Time Taken" panel's column is "Time used" ("38 of 45 min" from `timeUsed`, with "Ended on the clock" under the name when it did); dates print as IST (`istShortDate`); and the two rings' captions are `Flexible` so the pair no longer overflows a phone panel.

**The two invariants the candidate side enforces, and where:**
- **Invariant 3 - no figure before release.** The gate is `ev.resultsReleased`, spelled identically in all three places: `my_assessments_screen.dart:251`, `:273`, `:279`, `:467`, `:476`; `my_performance_screen.dart:131-133`, `:290`. In the performance breakdown a candidate's own unreleased row shows `-` for score, **no threshold bar at all** (`:303-322`, with the comment that a bar would disclose roughly where the score landed), and a `Pill('Awaiting release', Tone.inert)`. An admin opening the page for someone else (the dashboard leaderboard's `CandidatePerformance` route) sees a held row's marks and bar too - they decide the release - while the pill still says held and the totals stay released-only (`_breakdown`: `showMarks = released || !isSelf`; round 3, A-133). Unreleased sittings contribute to no ring, no total and no KPI - `_Performance.fromStore` computes every aggregate from `released`, never `completed` (`:130-148`). A `_heldNotice` explains why the figures look low when `awaiting > 0` (`:432-440`).
- **Invariant 2 - marks, never a percentage.** Everything rendered is `Marks(earned, total)` or `X / Y`. The internal ratio exists (`_ratio`, `:63-66`) and is used only to rank "best" and to shape the sparkline; the comment at `:437-441` calls out the trend line as exactly the place a percentage would leak.

**What a candidate cannot do.** No writes from either screen. No access to the answer key, other candidates, the ledger, budget, settings or Docs by way of the rail. Marks and verdict on a candidate's own list come from the server (`serverEarned` / `serverTotal` / `serverPassed`, `my_assessments_screen.dart:209-217`, `my_performance_screen.dart:40-50`) because the candidate endpoint sends no per-question responses to recompute from. The pass threshold now travels with the verdict: `candidate_result` and `exam_state_envelope` both emit `pass_threshold`, and `Attempt.passMarkPercent` (read by the strengths and weaknesses panels too since 19.0.3.23.0) reads that first, the loaded assessment second, and only then the literal `70` (`DEFAULT_SUBJECTIVE_THRESHOLD`) as a last resort. Before that key existed the app went straight to the `70` default, which re-derived a released 6 / 10 judged against a 60% bar as a FAIL, and told a candidate sitting a 60% paper on the instructions page that they needed 7 of 10.

**Gap worth flagging:** portal only selects the *sidebar*. `AssessmentSection._page()` (`assessment_section.dart::_page`) switches purely on the route and has no `Portal.member` guard - nothing in it refuses `BudgetAdmin`, `SettingsAdmin` or `ResponsesList` if such a route were ever set while `portal == Portal.member`. In practice the member rail never offers those keys, and `_loadCandidate` never fetches their data, so the screens would render empty rather than leak - but the enforcement is by navigation reachability and by what the server sends, not by an explicit client-side check.


## 3.8 Exam runner

Scope: `lib/assessment/screens/exam/` - the seven files a candidate's browser actually runs. Supporting facts are cited from `lib/assessment/state/app_store.dart`, `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart`, `lib/assessment/domain/models.dart`, `lib/assessment/domain/enums.dart` and `lib/services/proctor_*.dart` where the runner delegates.

#### Entry and route resolution

One widget, `ExamScreen`, serves five stages. The section host maps the route to a sub-stage (`lib/assessment/assessment_section.dart:479-489`): `ExamStage.gate -> ExamSub.instructions`, `question`, `answers`, `review`, `complete`. The token arrives from `lib/deep_link.dart` (`examTokenFrom`), which accepts `/exam/<t>`, `/exam/<t>/`, `/#/exam/<t>`, `?token=<t>` and `/pro_assessment/<t>`. In-app navigation does not change the address bar (`lib/assessment/nav.dart:1-18`).

`initState` hydrates the sitting only when the store has no attempt for that token, then holds a `_resolving` flag so the "link does not work" gate is not shown mid-flight (`exam_screen.dart::initState`).

`build` resolves in a fixed order (`exam_screen.dart::build`):

| # | Condition | Result | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `attempt == null` and `_resolving` | bare `CircularProgressIndicator` | 171-174 |
| 0b | `attempt == null`, resolve finished | `GateScreen(kind: GateKind.parse(view?.outcome), onSignOut: s.signOut)` - the server's own outcome (`login_required`, `wrong_candidate`, `closed`, ...), `invalid` only when it gave none the client can place | 175 |
| 1 | `sub == answers` | `_AnswerReview` - resolved *before* the assessment lookup | 187-189 |
| 2 | `assessment == null` | the same outcome-driven `GateScreen` | 193 |
| 3 | `attempt.isDone` (submitted or locked) | `_Complete` | 201 |
| 4 | `asm.state != inProgress` | `GateScreen(closed)` | 204-206 |
| 5 | `sub == review` | `_Review` inside `_buildChrome` | 209-216 |
| 6 | `attempt.startedAt == null` | `_Instructions` | 219-220 |
| 7 | otherwise | `_QuestionPage` inside `_buildChrome` | 228-263 |

There is no branch for `ExamSub.complete`; the completion screen is reached only via step 3 (`attempt.isDone`). `ExamSub.instructions` likewise has no branch of its own - it is the fall-through at step 6.

#### The journey, screen by screen

1. **Instructions / consent** (`_Instructions`, `exam_screen.dart::_Instructions`). Own `Scaffold`, no exam chrome, no clock, no proctoring listeners. Shows a 4-tile KPI strip: question count (server's `instructions['total_questions']`, then `view.total`, then `asm.questions.length` - 988-992), time (`asm.durationMinutes` or "No limit"), pass mark rendered as `ceil(questions * passThreshold / 100) / questions` marks not a percentage (1020-1024), and a hardcoded `Attempts: 1` (1025). A "What is monitored" panel lists every enabled `ProctorRule` with its `label` and `hint` (1032-1061), then a `Notice` stating the consequence and cap up front from `violationConsequence` (Auto-submit: "The exam auto-submits on violation N.", or "...on the first violation." at cap 0; Log only: "The exam is never ended automatically.", plus, when a cap is set, that reaching it marks the attempt as over the violation limit, shown to the candidate and the organiser; round 3, A-074) (1065-1079), plus a camera notice if the webcam rule is on (1080-1089). The consent paragraph names the candidate from `store.personById` and states that the clock does not pause (1098-1108). Actions: "Start assessment" and "Not now" (back to `MyAssessments`).
2. **Question page** (`_QuestionPage`, 1146-1230), wrapped in `_buildChrome`. A warning `Notice` appears above the card once `violationCount > 0` (1176-1188); under Log only past its cap (`Attempt.limitBreached(asm)`: the server's `violation_limit_breached`, or the same test on the counts - the one rule the admin badges read too) it is replaced by a live-region warn `Notice` "You have reached the violation limit (N)." / "The exam continues, and your violations are reported to the organiser." (round 3, A-074). The card is eyebrow "Question N", prompt, optional description, then `AnswerArea`. Footer: `Previous` (disabled at question 1), `Review & submit`, and a primary button that reads `Save & review` when `number >= total` else `Save & next` (1212-1226).
3. **Pre-submit review** (`_Review`, 1233-1337), also inside the chrome. Rows come from `store.examReviewByToken[token]`, falling back to a locally built list over `asm.questions` (1253-1262). A `Notice` counts unanswered questions (1270-1280). An `AutoGrid` of `_MatrixCell` tiles - green for answered, amber for not, never red (1339-1340) - plus a two-item legend. Actions: "Back to questions" (jumps to index 1) and "Submit assessment", which shows busy while `submit:<attempt>` is held (round 3, A-052).
4. **Completion** (`_Complete`, 1429-1569). Own `Scaffold`. Under the subtitle, "Time used: 38 of 45 min" from `timeUsed` (19.0.3.23.0, Q12). An auto-submit `Notice` when `ev.autoSubmitted` (1475-1484) names the cause: "Auto-submitted: proctoring violation limit reached." for `violation`, **"Ended on the clock."** for `expired` (was "Auto-submitted: your time ran out."), else "This attempt was submitted automatically.". When the limit was reached (`ev.limitBreached(asm)`, either mode) a warn `Notice` "You reached the violation limit (N)." with the body "The exam ended there, and the attempt is marked Violation Limit Breached for the organiser." under Auto-submit or "Your violations are reported to the organiser." under Log only (round 3, A-074). If `!ev.resultsReleased` it shows "Awaiting results" and nothing numeric (1486-1493); otherwise a `ScoreRing`, a result `Pill`, `Marks` and a `ThresholdBar`, preferring `ev.serverEarned`/`ev.serverTotal` over any local recount (1508-1510), plus `ev.pendingMarkingNote` when written answers are still queued (N11). "See my answers" is disabled until `resultsReleased` (1549-1554).
5. **Answer review** (`_AnswerReview`, 1577-1728). Self-fetching via `store.answerSheet(token)` -> `/api/v1/exam/<token>/answers`, with the future created in the field initialiser, not in `build` (1591). Three states: spinner, error, loaded. On error it substitutes `GateScreen(notReleased)` when the cached attempt says the result is unreleased, else an `EmptyState` showing the server's message verbatim (1603-1628). An unreleased sheet also gets `GateScreen(notReleased)` (1635-1637). Loaded: back control, assessment name, KPI strip (score as marks or `-`, result label, answered count, and since 19.0.3.23.0 "Time used" with an "Ended on the clock" sub-line - the sheet carries no times, so it reads the cached attempt), then one `_AnswerCard` per row with prompt, the candidate's answer (a question the clock took away reads "You did not answer this question." - see `_ownWords` in 3.4), the correct answer when the server sent one, and a "judge's verdict" block that opens with the grader's one-line `scoreVerdict` in bold (19.0.3.23.0, row 50: released rows only, and only when the server's verdict gate passes it) followed by feedback plus `+ credit` / `- deduction` lines (1771-1809).

#### The seven question types

Rendered by `AnswerArea` (`answer_layouts.dart::AnswerArea`), a `switch` on `QType`. Wire keys from `lib/assessment/domain/enums.dart:398-414`. Every save goes through `ApiClient.examAnswer` (`lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:434-449`), which always sends `question_id`, `selected_option_ids`, `justification`, `label_answers` and `nav`; the column below lists which keys carry data for that type.

| Wire key | Enum | Widget | How the candidate answers | Payload keys carrying data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mcq` | `QType.mcq` | `_Options(multi: false)` (`answer_layouts.dart::_Options`) | Taps one option per dimension; picking strips every other option id belonging to that dimension before appending (`:200-204`). Marker is a circle. | `selected_option_ids` |
| `msq` | `QType.msq` | `_MsqHint` + `_Options(multi: true)` (`:311-325`) | Taps to toggle; ids accumulate (`:198`). Marker is a 5px-radius square, plus a redundant "Select all that apply" chip (`:144-167`). | `selected_option_ids` |
| `subjective_rubric` | `QType.subjectiveRubric` | `_FreeText`, 8 rows, eyebrow "Your answer" (`:97-106`) | Types prose into one textarea. | `justification` |
| `image_ab` | `QType.imageAb` | `_ImageAbLayout` (`:1419-1480`) | Every `q.images` asset as its own `StimulusPlate` on the left; one legended single-select `_Options` block per `q.dims` entry on the right, separated by rules, then a 5-row justification field labelled "Scored at 25% alongside the verdict". | `selected_option_ids` + `justification` |
| `image_prompt` | `QType.imagePrompt` | `_ImagePromptLayout` (`:1521-1567`) | Stimulus via `mediaFor(q)` (video first, then image, then `MissingStimulus`); single-select options, then a 7-row "Your prompt" field. | `selected_option_ids` + `justification` |
| `video_prompt` | `QType.videoPrompt` | `_VideoPromptLayout` (`:1573-1612`) | Every `q.videos` asset as a `VideoPlate`; one 8-row prompt field. No option controls at all. | `justification` |
| `image_label` | `QType.imageLabel` | `_ImageLabelLayout` (`:1643-1868`) | One annotated plate; one text input per number in `q.labelBoxes`, paginated 8 to a page (`:664`). | `label_answers` (map of box number as string -> text); `justification` when `labelBoxes` is empty |
| any unknown code | `QType.unsupported` (round 3, A-053) | a warn `Notice` "This question type is not supported in this version of the app." / "Please contact your assessment organiser. You can still move on to the next question and submit." | Nothing to answer; Next moves on and the question counts as unanswered | none |

Notes on the labelling layout: `_boxes` reads `q.labelBoxes`, never `q.boxKey`, because `boxKey` is the marking scheme and the exam route does not send it (`:1678`, `models.dart:466-478`). When the asset carries an `annotatedUrl` and boxes exist, the plate is swapped for the server-burned annotated image (`:736-740`). When `labelBoxes` is empty the layout falls back to a single free-text field so the question stays answerable (`:789-807`). The caption under the plate promises "The numbered overlay marks each region you need to name." only when markers are really drawn - a baked annotated image, or client-drawn regions from per-marker geometry; otherwise it says the picture carries no numbered markers and asks for each region the question names (19.0.3.23.0, row 56). The server sends neither for a planted-defect question, where the markers would be the answer key. The "n / m labelled" counter is driven from local state (`:684`, `:700-709`). A "Every page is submitted, not just this one." reassurance appears whenever the pager shows (`:858-863`).

`readOnly` is threaded through every layout; options keep full-strength colour when read-only rather than dimming, deliberately (`:55-60`).

#### Answer persistence

Two write paths, chosen by widget:

- **Option taps** call `store.saveAnswer` (`answer_layouts.dart:205`), which mutates the attempt and notifies listeners (`app_store.dart::saveAnswer`).
- **Every free-text keystroke and every label keystroke** calls `store.saveAnswerQuiet` (`answer_layouts.dart:417-423`, `:703-707`), which writes the same value but deliberately does **not** call `notifyListeners` (`app_store.dart::saveAnswerQuiet`). The stated reason is caret and focus preservation; each field owns its own `TextEditingController` (`answer_layouts.dart:390-392`, `:687-690`).

Both funnel into `_syncAnswer` (`app_store.dart::_syncAnswer`), which is a no-op in seed mode and otherwise debounces per question id at **1 second**, then POSTs `/api/v1/exam/<token>/answer`. Failures go to `debugPrint` (`answer autosave REFUSED for question <id>: <why>`, `answer autosave failed ...`), and the rationale given is that `finishExam` re-sends everything anyway (`:2507-2517`); beyond that the candidate gets at most one connectivity warning per sitting (`_warnAutosaveFailing`). Two refusals never trigger it (19.0.3.23.0): `incomplete_answer`, which is the server holding a half-finished answer as a draft, and `time_expired`, which raises the time-up message (see The timer).

**On navigation**, `_navigate` (`exam_screen.dart::_navigate`) branches on `store.isLive`:
- Seed mode: pure client-side route walk (`prev` -> `number - 1`, `next` -> `number + 1`, `review` -> review route).
- Live: cancels the pending debounce for that question, then calls `store.examAdvance(token, q.id, response, nav:)` (`app_store.dart::examAdvance`). The route's reply *is* the next question: `next` is merged into the cached `ExamView` and `notifyListeners` repaints without a route change. When `next` is null the server's `review` block is adopted and the caller navigates to the review route (`exam_screen.dart:291-295`). An `ApiError` here surfaces to the candidate as a destructive toast in the server's own words (`app_store.dart:2640-2643`), and returns `false`, so the candidate stays put - except `attempt_locked` / a 409, which moves to the completion screen, with the time-up message first when the code is `time_expired`.

`_adoptServerAnswer` (`app_store.dart::_adoptServerAnswer`) seeds a question the store has nothing for from the server's `answer` block (`selected_option_ids`, `justification`, `label_answers`); local edits win. On a resume (`loadExamByToken`) it runs only after the attempt row is in place, so the landing question shows the answer the server already holds, cold or warm (round 3, A-068).

**The submit path** (`store.finishExam`, `app_store.dart::finishExam`), reached from `_Review` -> `onFinish()` or from the deadline overlay -> `_finish(auto: true)` (`exam_screen.dart::_finish`):

0. Returns at once when the attempt is already `isDone` or `submit:<id>` is busy, so a second tap sends nothing; the key is held until the live submit finishes (round 3, A-052).
1. Locally grades every response over `asm.questions`, discarding any that grade to null so a blank reads as unanswered rather than a zero (`:2748-2756`).
2. Optimistically writes `state: submitted`, `isLocked: true`, `autoSubmitted`, `submittedAt` (`:2758-2766`).
3. Seed mode shows the final toast immediately; live mode shows only `Submitting your exam...` (`:2778-2787`).
4. Live: cancels and clears **all** pending debounce timers so a late autosave cannot land after the lock (`:2792-2796`).
5. Re-sends every graded answer in a loop where **each answer has its own `try`** and a refusal only increments a `refused` counter (`:2812-2825`). The comment records the prior bug precisely: one shared `try` meant a single 422 aborted the loop and `examSubmit` was never called, while the candidate had already been told the exam was submitted (`:2799-2811`).
6. Calls `/exam/<token>/submit`. An `ApiError` with code `attempt_locked` is treated as success (the server settled it first). Any other error **reverts the local attempt** and shows: `Your exam was NOT submitted: <message> Your answers are saved - please try Submit again.` (`:2827-2845`).
7. On success, the final toast, plus a warning if `refused > 0`: `N answer(s) could not be re-sent, so the copy already saved on the server was used for them.` (`:2854-2860`). Then `refresh()`, because the server's grades are the ones that count.

Consequence of the revert in step 6: `_finish` has already navigated to `ExamStage.complete` (`exam_screen.dart::_finish`), but the reverted attempt is no longer `isDone`, so step 3 of the route resolution fails and the candidate falls through to the question page with the failure toast on screen. The completion screen is never displayed for a refused submit.

#### The timer

- **Source.** The server's `ev.deadline` first, else `asm.durationMinutes` added to a start time: `initState` from `ev.startedAt` (`exam_screen.dart:111-113`), `_begin` from `DateTime.now() + ev.clockOffset` (`:313-315`), and the expression that drives the bar in `_buildChrome`: `ev.deadline ?? _deadline ?? (ev.startedAt != null && asm.durationMinutes > 0 ? ev.startedAt + duration : null)` (`:373-377`). **Server clock** (round 3): every candidate payload with `deadline` also carries `server_now`; `Attempt.clockOffset` is `server_now` minus the device clock, and `Clock` counts down against device now + that offset, so a device clock that is off does not move the deadline (no `server_now` = zero offset, the old behaviour; an offset under 2 s is treated as zero, `models.dart::_clockOffset`). The comment states the `initState` cache was null forever on resume because the attempt had not loaded yet.
- **Resume after reload.** The deep-link path leaves the attempt null on the first frame, so `Clock` is first built with `deadline: null` and would print "No limit". `Clock.didUpdateWidget` re-arms whenever the deadline value changes, resetting `_fired` (`:964-971`). The comment records that without this a resuming candidate got no countdown and an `onExpire` that never fired.
- **Behaviour.** `Clock` owns a 1-second `Timer.periodic` and rebuilds only itself, never the exam surface (`:544-595`). Display is `mm:ss` clamped at zero; background/border/text switch to warn tokens under 5 minutes (300000 ms) and destructive tokens under 1 minute (60000 ms) (`:609-624`). With no deadline it renders the literal `No limit` (`:606-607`).
- **At zero.** The tick fires `onExpire` once (`_fired` guard), which runs `_timeUp` (round 3): stop the proctor watch (MT3-01), `store.flushAnswers()` - send every pending debounced autosave now and drop the debounce (MT3-02) - then `_block = 'deadline'`. That renders a non-dismissible `BlockOverlay`: "Time is up" / "Time's up - your answers are saved. Questions you did not reach are recorded as unanswered." (`AppStore.timeUpMessage`; before 19.0.3.23.0 it said "Your answers were submitted as they stand", which was not yet true, FU7) / single action "See my submission" (`:441-454`). **The submit does not happen until the candidate presses that button** - `_finish(auto: true)` runs in the button handler (`:452`). The overlay has no backdrop dismissal and no Escape (`:890-893`), and while any blocking overlay is up the paper below the top bar is under `ExcludeFocus` + `ExcludeSemantics`, so Tab cannot reach the answer box behind it; the top bar and clock stay readable, the overlay's heading takes focus, and focus returns when it clears (round 3, MT3-02); apart from that one flush, nothing is sent to the server in the interim.
- The clock only exists inside `_buildChrome`, so it is absent from the instructions, completion and answer-review screens.
- **One time-up message on every path** (19.0.3.23.0, Q12/FU7, row 53). The server keeps an answer that lands within `ANSWER_GRACE_SECONDS` (10 s) of the deadline, refuses a later one unstored, and answers 409 `time_expired` with `answer_saved` (round 3, MT3-02). Whichever path meets that first - Next (`examAdvance`), the debounced autosave, the submit flush in `finishExam`, an auto submit with reason `expired`, or (round 3, MT3-01) a `/violation` sent after the deadline - calls `AppStore._tellTimeUp`, which toasts "Time's up - your answers are saved." once per token (`_timeUpTold`) and, when `answer_saved` is false, adds the neutral warn "Your last change reached us after the deadline, so it may not count." (round 3; `answer_saved: false` covers past-the-grace, incomplete-and-refused and a held draft) - never a red "not saved", because the server still settles and grades a held A/B draft (G2-05). The old buzzer toast that blamed proctoring ("auto-submitted at the violation threshold") is gone for a time-out (G2-04). The completion page then says "Ended on the clock." and "Time used: X of Y min". Tests: `time_up_says_the_answers_are_saved_test.dart`, `the_buzzer_says_whether_the_answer_was_saved_test.dart`, `ended_on_the_clock_is_shown_test.dart`, `a_draft_answer_is_not_an_error_test.dart`, `a_question_the_clock_took_away_is_not_an_answer_test.dart`, and (round 3) `time_up_stops_proctoring_test.dart`, `time_up_overlay_is_modal_test.dart`, `the_clock_counts_on_server_time_test.dart`.

#### stimulus.dart - media rendering

| Path | Condition | Rendering | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Data URL | `asset.url` starts with `data:` | base64-decoded once per URL and handed to `Image.memory(gaplessPlayback: true)`. Decode failure returns `MissingStimulus`. | `stimulus.dart:181-190` |
| Network URL | any other non-empty `asset.url` | `Image.network(resolveMediaUrl(src), gaplessPlayback: true)` - `resolveMediaUrl` prefixes `kApiBaseUrl` for relative paths (`api_client.dart:61-66`). The bearer and the element strategy are decided per ORIGIN by `isOurMediaOrigin`: our own proxies get `mediaAuthHeaders` and `WebHtmlElementStrategy.never`, a third-party host gets no headers and `WebHtmlElementStrategy.fallback`. | `:191-198` |
| Synthetic | `asset.url` null or empty | `CustomPaint(_WarehousePainter)` - a deterministic warehouse frame seeded from `asset.id`, drawing floor, perspective lines, racking, palette-tinted crates, and (when `showRegions`) the numbered boxes itself | `:200-207`, `:237-335` |

**WHY THE ELEMENT STRATEGY IS PER-ORIGIN, and why it is not one setting for everything.** The
Flutter default is `WebHtmlElementStrategy.never`, which fetches the bytes over XHR and decodes
them - so on CanvasKit a host that does not send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` renders NOTHING,
even though a plain `<img>` would have displayed it perfectly (a browser needs CORS to READ an
image's pixels, not to SHOW it). `fallback` tries bytes first and then mounts an `<img>`, which
is what makes a pasted third-party URL work at all. Two constraints pull the other way:

- **Non-empty `headers` disables the `<img>` path outright** (`_network_image_web.dart:157-166`
  routes to `loadViaDecode()` whenever headers are present). Preview used to send
  `mediaAuthHeaders` to EVERY host, which is why it was strictly worse off than the designer.
  Our own `auth="user"` proxies must keep the bearer, so the header set and the strategy are
  chosen together, per origin.
- **`stimulusImageProvider` is deliberately left on the default** (`stimulus.dart:819`), because
  it feeds the annotation editor. Under `fallback` a cross-origin image resolves to a
  `WebImageInfo` whose `.image` getter throws `UnsupportedError`
  (`_web_image_info_web.dart:46`), and `_RegionOverlayImageState._resolve` reads
  `info.image.width` inside a listener whose `onError` swallows everything - so `_aspect` would
  stay null and the region overlay would silently vanish. Guessing an aspect ratio is worse than
  failing there: that widget's contract is "a fraction of the canvas IS a fraction of the
  image", so a wrong aspect mislocates every stored `box_2d`. Annotation genuinely needs pixel
  access, so a CORS-blocked host cannot support it.

**This half cannot be covered by the test suite.** `webHtmlElementStrategy` is inert off-web -
`_network_image_io.dart:29` stores the field and never reads it - and the 37 FE test files that
touch a filesystem or a conditional import carry `@TestOn('vm')`, this area's included. It is
measured instead by a browser probe,
`tool/corsprobe/run.sh` in the FE repo, which reports `never=FAIL fallback=OK` and
`noHeaders=OK withHeaders=FAIL` against a local server that deliberately omits the CORS header.

The decode cache `_decoded` is keyed by the full data URL and capped at `_kMaxDecoded = 24`, evicting the oldest on overflow (`:143-157`). The stated reason is that decoding inside `build` produced a new list each time, a new `Image.memory` cache key, and a dropped frame.

`StimulusPlate` (`:20-129`): uppercase caption eyebrow, `AspectRatio(4/3)` inside a `Flexible` (so a bounded parent shrinks it rather than clipping), `SystemMouseCursors.zoomIn`, a hover-revealed "Zoom" chip at opacity 0/1 over 140 ms, and a tap that opens the lightbox.

Annotated overlays: for a real image, `_withRegions` stacks `_RegionPainter` over the image inside the *same* box the image occupies, because region coordinates are fractional (`:215-230`, `:534-586`). Each region draws a 2px primary-coloured rect plus a filled numbered chip placed above the box, or inside it when there is no room above (`:569-574`). `showRegions` is passed true only from `_ImageLabelLayout`'s marked plate (`answer_layouts.dart:767`, `:775`).

Lightbox (`:386-496`): `showDialog` with a `0xEB0F0B13` barrier; `InteractiveViewer` (scale 1-6) wrapping an `AnimatedScale` driven by a `_zoom` stepped by 0.4 and clamped 1-6; controls are minus / Reset / plus / Close; a full-bleed backdrop `GestureDetector` closes it while the stage does not; caption line reads `<caption> · scroll to zoom · Esc to close` (Escape is handled by the dialog route, not by code in this file).

Fallbacks: `MissingStimulus` - 220px box, `image_not_supported_outlined`, "No image yet for this question." (`:348-379`). `MissingVideo` - identical shape with `videocam_off_outlined` and "No video yet for this question." It is defined **twice**, once in `video_plate_stub.dart::MissingVideo` and again verbatim in `video_plate_web.dart:133-160`.

Video: `video_plate.dart` (103 lines) is a conditional export - the stub on any non-web platform, `video_plate_web.dart` under `dart.library.js_interop` - PLUS the two platform-neutral helpers that decide what a URL is, deliberately placed here rather than in the web half because they touch no web API and non-web callers need the same answer. `publicVideoEmbedRef` (`:25`) resolves a YouTube or Vimeo link to `(kind, id)`; `mediaKindOf` (`:88`) returns `MediaKind.embeddedVideo` / `videoFile` / `image` (`enum` at `:71`), with `isVideoMedia` (`:103`) as the shorthand. THE CLASSIFIER IS SHARED ON PURPOSE: `form_item_editor.dart`, `form_preview.dart` and the server's `_looks_like_video` (`models/studio_form.py::_looks_like_video`) each used to test the extension of the whole URL string in their own copy, so a YouTube link (no extension) and `clip.mp4?sig=abc` (extension behind the query) were classified as IMAGES by all four and handed to `Image.network`, which mounts an element with nothing to decode. `mediaKindOf` checks the embed hosts first, then reads the extension off `Uri.path` so a query or fragment cannot hide it; `image` stays the default, because our own proxy paths carry no extension and are stills. The stub's `VideoPlate.build` always returns `MissingVideo` (`video_plate_stub.dart::MissingVideo`), so video questions are unanswerable outside the browser, which is what makes them untestable under the VM test runner. The web plate registers an `HTMLVideoElement` platform view once per `assetId + url.hashCode` (`video_plate_web.dart::_registered`, guarded by a static `_registered` set), with `controls = true`, `autoplay = false`, `objectFit: contain`, fixed 300px height, and - when `allowDownload` is false, the default - `controlsList=nodownload`, `disablePictureInPicture=true` and a suppressed context menu, explicitly described as an affordance removal and not a security control (`:82-91`). The caption line reads `Video - download disabled`. The comment at `stimulus.dart:337-344` records that this used to be a static mock with a hardcoded "0:12 / 0:35".

#### gate_screen - the pre-exam gates

`GateKind` (`gate_screen.dart::GateKind`) carries the server's `outcome` vocabulary verbatim, with `parse` falling back to `invalid`. All five render the same card: 54px tone-coloured icon tile, title, body, and a `Wrap` of actions (a `Wrap` rather than a `Row` because the two-action gate overflows a narrow viewport - `:95-99`).

| Kind | Wire | Tone | Title | Action(s) | Constructed at |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `invalid` | `invalid` | bad | "This link does not work" | "Go to my assessments" | `exam_screen.dart::build`, via `GateKind.parse(view?.outcome)` (also its fallback) |
| `login` | `login_required` | info | "Sign in to continue" | "Sign in" | same, when the server's outcome is `login_required` |
| `wrong` | `wrong_candidate` | warn | "This link belongs to somebody else" | "Switch account" + "My assessments" | same, when the outcome is `wrong_candidate` |
| `closed` | `closed` | inert | "This assessment is closed" | "Go to my assessments" | `exam_screen.dart:205`, and via the outcome |
| `notReleased` | `not_released` | info | "Results not released yet" | "Go to my assessments" | `exam_screen.dart:1612`, `:1636` |

The primary buttons do what their labels say (19.0.3.23.0, row 59): on `login` and `wrong`, "Sign in" and "Switch account" call `GateScreen.onSignOut` (the runner passes `AppStore.signOut`, which reaches the login form through `onSignedOut`); every other action, and the secondary "My assessments", is `context.nav.reset(const MyAssessments())`. Before, all of them went to My assessments - a list behind the very session the gate reported missing, or somebody else's. Test: `every_gate_button_goes_where_it_says_test.dart`.

**Consents and pre-exam gates other than these screens:** the only explicit consent is the paragraph on the instructions page, accepted by pressing "Start assessment" (`exam_screen.dart:1098-1116`). There is no separate checkbox, no camera permission prompt, and no equipment check. Fullscreen is requested inside the "Start assessment" gesture, before the route change, because browsers only honour the request from a user gesture (`:308-311`).

#### Proctoring from the candidate's side

Rules arrive on the assessment as a `RuleSet` (`models.dart::RuleSet`). Listeners are attached from `_buildChrome`, not `initState`, once per screen life (`_proctorStarted` guard), skipped entirely when the attempt is locked or submitted, and skipped when no rule needs a browser listener (`exam_screen.dart:132-153`). `_proctor.stop()` runs unconditionally in `dispose` (`:140-146`) and at time-up (`_timeUp`, round 3, MT3-01); `_proctorStarted` stays true, so it is not re-attached.

| Rule | Wire | What is actually watched (`lib/services/proctor_web.dart`) | Reason string sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Block tab switching | `tab_switch` | `visibilitychange`; **ignored unless fullscreen** when the fullscreen rule is also on; debounced at 1500 ms (`:88-102`) | `Tab switched / window hidden` |
| Block copy and paste | `copy_paste` | `copy`, `cut`, `paste` on document, each `preventDefault`ed (`:79-86`) | `Clipboard action: copy` / `cut` / `paste` |
| Block right-click | `right_click` | `contextmenu`, `preventDefault`ed (`:72-77`) | `Right-click attempted` |
| Detect developer tools | `devtools` | 2s poll of outer-vs-inner window size, normalised by `devicePixelRatio / baseDpr`, threshold 300px, fires at most once (`:104-120`) | `Developer tools detected` |
| Block screenshot keys | `screenshot` | `keyup` where `key == 'PrintScreen'` (`:122-128`) | `Screenshot key pressed` |
| Require fullscreen | `fullscreen` | `fullscreenchange`; only counts after fullscreen has been *entered* at least once (`:130-142`) | `Exited fullscreen` |
| Require webcam | `webcam` | the camera is opened with `getUserMedia` from `start()`; a refused camera blocks the exam (no violation), one turned off after being granted is a violation (`proctor_web.dart`) | `Webcam turned off / lost` |
| AI proctoring | `ai_proctor` | needs `webcam`; face and phone detection on the camera feed, each hit posted as a violation plus a snapshot uploaded with `evidence_upload` (Week 2, see "Proctoring / violations") | `AI: ...` (`AI: phone detected`, `AI: no face for 5s`, ...) |
| Watermark | `watermark` | not a violation; renders `Watermark` | - |

On every non-web platform `createProctorWatch()` returns a no-op (`lib/services/proctor_stub.dart:66-83`).

What the candidate sees:

- **Before starting**: the full enabled-rule list with hints, and the consequence stated in the same words the exam will use - "The exam auto-submits on violation N." ("...on the first violation." at cap 0) under Auto-submit, or "The exam is never ended automatically." under Log only. The body says, in both modes, that reaching the limit "marks the attempt Violation Limit Breached for the candidate and the organiser" (under Log only only when a cap is set, adding "only Auto-submit ends the exam") (`enums.dart::violationConsequence`, round 3, A-074; `exam_screen.dart:1065-1079`).
- **On a violation**: `_violate` (`:667-673`) shows `ViolationToast` - destructive-toned, its own channel, 4-second life - reading `Proctoring: <reason> - this has been recorded.` (`:155-161`, `:1141-1177`), positioned 78px from the bottom. `store.recordViolation` increments the count, fires `/exam/<token>/violation` immediately rather than batching it with the submission (`app_store.dart:2723-2732`), and returns true only when the action is auto-submit **and** the count reached the cap (cap 0 = the first violation) - in which case it ends the sitting through `_endForViolation` (live: marks it done locally, then re-reads the server's copy only once the `/violation` reply is in - `replyPending` / `_settleLocalEnd`; a re-read fired at once raced the POST, came back `in_progress` and put a live exam back on screen; a failed POST or a server that did not end it also re-reads, so the screen follows the server) and the runner routes to the completion screen (`app_store.dart::_endForViolation`, `exam_screen.dart:331`). Under Log only nothing ends the sitting at any cap (round 3, A-074).
- **Persistently after a violation**: a warn `Notice` at the top of every question page, "Warning: proctoring violation N of M." (Auto-submit) or "Proctoring violation recorded (N)." (Log only) (`:1176-1188`); under Log only past the cap it becomes "You have reached the violation limit (N)." / "The exam continues, and your violations are reported to the organiser.", announced as a live region. The completion page states a reached limit in both modes (round 3, A-074).
- **Watermark**: 60 tiles (6 x 10, 190x60px) of `"<name>  <email>"` at 6% ink, rotated -30 degrees, inside `IgnorePointer` + `OverflowBox` (`:653-710`). Laid out with a `Wrap` rather than a `GridView` because a scrollable inside an unbounded `OverflowBox` throws.
- **Camera-off block**: only reachable from the simulator (`onBlockWebcam`). A non-dismissible `BlockOverlay`: "Your camera is off" / "Only the on-off state is monitored. No video is recorded or stored. The clock keeps running while the camera is off." / "Enable camera", whose handler just clears the overlay and shows an OK toast (`:425-440`).
- **The proctoring simulator** (`ProctorRig`, `:1189-1313`) is a floating panel with one button per *enabled* violation-producing rule, plus camera and time-expiry buttons, and a header reading `Violation N of M - auto-submits at M`. It drives the **real** `/violation` route. It is gated on `const bool kProctorSim = bool.fromEnvironment('PROCTOR_SIM', defaultValue: true)` (`:761-762`) - **default on**, so a candidate build must be produced with `--dart-define=PROCTOR_SIM=false` or the candidate can fabricate violations against themselves, or at cap 1 end their own exam with one click. The file says exactly this at `:400-410`.

#### Accessibility

**True count: 0.** `grep -rn "Semantics\|semanticLabel\|ExcludeSemantics\|MergeSemantics\|excludeSemantics"` over `lib/assessment/screens/exam/` returns no matches in any of the seven files. There are no semantic labels, no live-region announcements, no focus management, and no keyboard handlers anywhere in this directory. *(outdated: `exam_screen.dart` now announces - the Clock's minute milestones and, since round 3, the live-region violation-limit notice - and, while a blocking overlay is up, puts `ExcludeFocus` + `ExcludeSemantics` over the paper below the top bar and moves focus to the overlay's heading and back (round 3, MT3-02).)*

Concrete consequences visible in the code:

- Every interactive control is a bare `GestureDetector` (+ `MouseRegion` for the cursor), not a `Button`/`InkWell` with a semantics role: `_Option` (`answer_layouts.dart::_Option`), `_MatrixCell` (`exam_screen.dart::_MatrixCell`), `_PagerBtn` (`answer_layouts.dart::_PagerBtn`), `_LbBtn` (`stimulus.dart::_LbBtn`), `StimulusPlate` (`stimulus.dart::StimulusPlate`), and the `ProctorRig` header (`exam_screen.dart:809`). None is reachable or actionable by keyboard or by a screen reader.
- Images carry no alternative text. `StimulusArt` passes nothing to `Image.memory`/`Image.network` (`stimulus.dart:188`, `:188-192`), and the `CustomPaint` fallbacks emit no semantics at all, so the numbered regions a labelling question is *about* are invisible to assistive technology.
- The `Clock` never announces; the countdown, the amber threshold, the red threshold and expiry are colour-and-text-only (`exam_screen.dart:604-648`).
- The `ViolationToast` is a plain `Text` in a `Positioned` - not announced (`:1141-1177`).
- `BlockOverlay` is a `Positioned.fill` inside a `Stack`, not a route or a `Dialog`, though it is a semantic modal (`scopesRoute`, live-region title) (`:894-962`). Since round 3 (MT3-02) the paper behind it is under `ExcludeFocus` + `ExcludeSemantics` while it is up, so Tab and screen readers cannot reach it; the top bar and clock stay outside the exclusion and readable. The overlay's heading takes focus when it goes up, and focus goes back where it was when it clears (`exam_screen.dart::_followOverlay`).
- The `Watermark` doc comment claims it is "never announced to assistive technology" (`:653-654`). It is not excluded. On Flutter 3.44.8, `IgnorePointer(ignoring: true)` with `ignoringSemantics` unset only strips pointer *actions* from the subtree and leaves the rest of the semantics intact (`packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/basic.dart:7695-7714`), so 60 copies of the candidate's name and email address are in the semantics tree. `ExcludeSemantics` is what the comment describes and is absent.

#### Things that look wrong, dead or half-finished

1. **The Assessment record is not loaded for a candidate entering from their own list.** For `Portal.member`, `refresh()` runs only `_loadCandidate()`, which populates `attempts` and nothing else (`app_store.dart:464-481`); `assessments` stays empty, and `my_assessments_screen.dart:47-49` says so outright ("`asm` is normally null here"). `loadExamByToken` - the only call that merges the assessment for a candidate (`app_store.dart:2012-2022`) - runs **only when the attempt is not already cached** (`exam_screen.dart:100-105`). Entering from the in-app card therefore reaches `exam_screen.dart:193` with `asm == null` and shows "This link does not work" on a valid attempt. The deep-link path works because nothing is cached yet. Not reproduced against a live server here - UNKNOWN whether `/api/v1/me/assessments` bucket rows carry `token`/`accessToken` (`models.dart::token`), which is what decides whether the cached attempt is found.
2. **Jumping to a specific question does not work in live mode.** `_Review`'s matrix cells (`exam_screen.dart:1296`) and "Back to questions" (`:1324`) change only the route index. The question rendered is `view?.question` - the server's current one - and the header number is `view?.index` (`:229-247`); nothing re-fetches on a route change. The requested index is used only when `view` is null, i.e. seed mode. Same for `Resume` from the candidate list, which computes `firstUnanswered(...)` (`my_assessments_screen.dart:331-334`) and has it ignored.
3. **The debounced autosave sends `nav: 'next'`.** `_syncAnswer` omits `nav` (`app_store.dart:2672-2683`) and `ApiClient.examAnswer` defaults it to `'next'` (`api_client.dart:440`); the same is true of the re-send loop inside `finishExam` (`:2815-2821`). The response is discarded in both cases. Whether the route treats `nav` as a cursor move is UNKNOWN from this repo (the server is not present) - if it does, every keystroke pause advances the server's position while the client's `ExamView` stays put.
4. **FIXED - `GateKind.login` and `GateKind.wrong` were dead.** The runner now builds its dead-end gates from `GateKind.parse(view?.outcome)`, so `login_required` and `wrong_candidate` reach their own gates, and since 19.0.3.23.0 their buttons sign out (see gate_screen above). The original finding: no call site outside `gate_screen.dart`, both states collapsed to `GateKind.invalid`, and `ExamView.outcome` never consulted for gating.
5. **`ExamView.preview`, `canReviewAnswers` and `expired` are parsed and never read.** `preview` is documented as "a manager holding the token may READ the runner and never write to it" (`models.dart:2573-2576`), yet the runner offers every write control unconditionally.
6. **`kProctorSim` defaults to true**, so the default build ships a panel that can auto-submit the candidate's own exam (`exam_screen.dart:400-410`, `:1184-1185`). This is documented, not hidden, but it is an opt-out rather than an opt-in.
7. **FIXED - `ProctorRule.webcam` monitored nothing.** `proctor_web.dart` now opens the camera with `getUserMedia`: refused blocks the exam, turned off after being granted fires `Webcam turned off / lost`. The original finding: no camera API was touched, and the "Your camera is off" overlay was reachable only from the simulator while the instructions said "Your camera stays on."
8. **A refused submit strands the candidate on a question page.** See the submit path above: `_finish` navigates to `complete` before the server has answered, and the revert in `finishExam` (`app_store.dart::finishExam`) makes `isDone` false again, so route resolution falls through to the question page.
9. **Expiry does not submit until the candidate clicks.** `onExpire` only raises the overlay (`exam_screen.dart:378`); `_finish(auto: true)` runs in the overlay's button handler (`:452`). A candidate who leaves the tab open at zero has nothing sent by this client beyond the one flush of pending autosaves at time-up (round 3); the server settles the expired attempt itself (the cron, or the next visit), which is why the overlay can say "your answers are saved" (still true at 19.0.3.23.0).
10. **`Attempt.durationMinutes` exists (`models.dart::durationMinutes`, parsed at `:2366`) and the runner never uses it.** Every deadline computation reads `asm.durationMinutes` (`exam_screen.dart:111-113`, `:313-315`, `:373-377`), while the candidate list already falls back to the attempt's own value (`my_assessments_screen.dart:243`).
11. **`MissingVideo` is duplicated verbatim** in `video_plate_stub.dart::MissingVideo` and `video_plate_web.dart:133-160`.
12. **`answer_layouts.dart`'s header comment is stale**: it says "`answerArea(q, r, ro)` builds all seven" (`:6`) while the switch handles eight types across seven layouts, and the file opens by explaining why it will not state a count (`:3-5`).
13. `_Instructions` renders `Kpi(label: 'Attempts', value: '1')` as a constant (`exam_screen.dart:1025`) - no field is consulted.
14. Minor: stray space in `if (nav == 'review' )` (`exam_screen.dart:274`).


## 3.9 Shared widget library

All paths below are relative to `/Users/cj/Developer/ethara/ethara-assessment-fe/`. Every widget in `lib/assessment/widgets/` paints from `context.tokens` (`AppTokens`) and `context.type` (`AssessmentTypeRamp`), both `BuildContext` extensions declared in `lib/assessment/theme.dart::Radii`; corner radii come from `Radii` (`lib/assessment/theme.dart:111-123`) and alpha from the `Color.o(double)` extension (`lib/assessment/theme.dart:127-129`). No widget in this directory holds a literal colour except fully transparent `Color(0x00000000)` and pure white on the primary button (`buttons.dart:159`).

#### Layout primitives and the composition pattern

The envelope is fixed and stated at `panel.dart:1-5`: crumbs, head, optional KPI strip, one or more panels. There is no hero, banner or coloured page header anywhere in the module.

```
PageBody(children: [
  Crumbs([...])          // omitted on root destinations
  PageHead(title, sub:, actions: [Btn.primary(...)])
  KpiStrip([Kpi(...), Kpi(...)])
  Notice(...)            // optional, only when a condition holds
  Panel(
    flush: true,         // so the table meets the panel edge
    toolbar: Toolbar([SearchField(...), SelectField(...), Spacer(), TagChip('n of m')]),
    footer: Pagination(...),   // only on paged lists
    child: DataGrid(cols: [...], rows: [...], emptyMessage: ..., emptyAction: ...),
  ),
])
```

Real example, `lib/assessment/screens/admin/generator_list_screen.dart:61-183` (abridged; the comments are the file's own):

```dart
return PageBody(
  children: <Widget>[
    // No breadcrumb here: this IS a root destination ...
    PageHead(
      'Generators',
      sub: 'One generator per SOP. Upload the document, extract its '
           'skills, then generate questions from it.',
      actions: <Widget>[
        Btn.primary('New generator', icon: Icons.add,
            onPressed: () => context.nav.go(const NewGenerator())),
      ],
    ),
    KpiStrip(<Widget>[
      Kpi(label: 'Generators', value: '${all.length}', sub: 'one per SOP'),
      Kpi(label: 'Drafts awaiting review', value: '$pending',
          sub: 'human approval gate',
          valueColor: all.isEmpty ? null : (pending > 0 ? t.warnText : t.successText)),
      ...
    ]),
    Panel(
      flush: true,
      toolbar: Toolbar(<Widget>[
        SearchField(value: _search, hint: 'Search generators or tags',
            onChanged: (String v) => setState(() => _search = v)),
        const Spacer(),
        TagChip('${shown.length} of ${all.length}'),
      ]),
      child: DataGrid(
        minWidth: 1080,
        emptyMessage: q.isEmpty ? 'No generators yet. Create one and ...' : 'No generator matches "$_search". ...',
        emptyIcon: Icons.auto_awesome_outlined,
        emptyAction: q.isEmpty ? Btn.primary('New generator', ...) : Btn('Clear search', ...),
        cols: const <Col>[Col('Generator', flex: 3), Col('Questions', width: 86, numeric: true), ...],
        rows: ...,
      ),
    ),
  ],
);
```

Rules the primitives enforce so a call site cannot break them:
- `Toolbar` and `Pagination` are `Row`s, never `Wrap`s, because both need a `Spacer`, and `Spacer extends Expanded` throws outside a Flex - inside a `Wrap` it takes down the whole subtree silently (`panel.dart:255-263`, `data_grid.dart:372-375`).
- `PageHead` uses `Expanded` (not `Flexible`) around the actions `Wrap` so `WrapAlignment.end` reaches the true right edge (`panel.dart:136`); the file says `ui_report_fixes_test` guards this.
- `AutoGrid` never uses `IntrinsicHeight` or `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch` (`panel.dart:464-475`) - a `LayoutBuilder` in a cell cannot be measured intrinsically and the whole screen renders blank.
- `Kpi` is a fixed 100px, a measured number, guarded by `test/assessment/kpi_height_test.dart` (`panel.dart:340-351`).
- `Panel` uses the Dart 3.9 null-aware element `?toolbar` at `panel.dart:233`; the SDK constraint is `^3.9.0` (`pubspec.yaml:9`).

#### chatter.dart in detail

**Model.** `ChatterEntry` (`chatter.dart::ChatterEntry`): `id`, `author` (defaults `'System'`), `text`, `date` (`DateTime?` from `DateTime.tryParse`), `subtype`, `attachments`. `ChatterFile` (`chatter.dart::ChatterFile`) is `{name, url}`. `subtype` is parsed at `chatter.dart::subtype` and **never rendered** - `_Line` (`chatter.dart::_Line`) draws text, attachment names, then `"author · <IST timestamp>"` (`istTimestamp`; a relative "5m ago" / "3d ago" before 19.0.3.23.0).

**Fetch.** `ChatterPanel` fetches itself rather than via the store, deliberately (`chatter.dart:70-72`). `_load` (`chatter.dart::_load`) calls `widget.store.api.chatter(kind, recordId)` → `ApiClient.chatter` (`lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart:961-971`) → HTTP **POST** `/api/v1/chatter/$kind/$recordId` with `{limit: 40, offset: 0}` (every `_call` is a POST with a JSON body, `api_client.dart:186`). Entries with empty `text` are dropped (`chatter.dart::text`). `meta.total` and `meta.has_more` are read into `_total`/`_hasMore`. When `store.api == null` (seed mode) it shows `'History is only available against a live backend.'` rather than an empty list.

**Ordering.** The route returns newest-first; `_visible` (`chatter.dart::_visible`) reverses to **oldest-first, newest at the bottom**, and the composer sits below the timeline (`chatter.dart:372-378`).

**Re-pointing.** `didUpdateWidget` (`chatter.dart::didUpdateWidget`) resets entries, totals, error, composer, search and staged files and reloads when `recordId` or `kind` changes; without it Flutter's element reuse showed the previous record's history.

**Posting.** `_post` (`chatter.dart::_post`) calls `ApiClient.postChatter` (`api_client.dart:989-999`) → POST `/api/v1/chatter/$kind/$recordId/post` with `{body, post_kind: 'note', attachments}`. Attachments are `{name, content}` with base64 content. Empty body plus at least one file posts the literal `'(file attached)'` (`chatter.dart:234`). After a successful post it clears, **reloads** rather than appending locally, toasts `'Note logged'` and re-focuses the composer. There is exactly one verb: the `mail.mt_comment` ("notify followers") button was deliberately removed (`chatter.dart:212-220`, `431-439`). `kind == 'attempt'` is read-only, so no composer at all (`chatter.dart:88-96`).

**Send key.** `Enter` sends, `Shift+Enter` inserts a newline. Implemented as a `Focus.onKeyEvent` that checks `LogicalKeyboardKey.enter || numpadEnter` on `KeyDownEvent`, returns `ignored` when `HardwareKeyboard.instance.isShiftPressed`, otherwise calls `onSend()` and returns `handled` (`chatter.dart:479-489`). The field is `minLines: 2, maxLines: 6`.

**Search.** A toggle in `headActions` (`chatter.dart:306-315`), not a permanent field. It is a **client-side filter over the already-loaded page only** - `_load` never sends a query - matching `text` or `author`, case-insensitively (`chatter.dart:266-273`).

**Emoji.** A hard-coded 12-glyph list (`chatter.dart:464-468`) in a `PopupMenuButton` 214px wide (`chatter.dart:561-601`); picking one splices at the caret and re-focuses (`chatter.dart:389-401`). No package.

**Attachments.** `_attach` (`chatter.dart::_attach`) uses `pickFile()` from the conditional import at `chatter.dart:6-7`, base64-encodes into `_staged` (a list of `({String name, String b64})` records), rendered as deletable `Chip`s (`chatter.dart:523-537`).

**Full screen.** The `open_in_full` head action calls `_openFullScreen` (`chatter.dart::_openFullScreen`), which opens `showSheet(wide: true)` (880px) at 70% viewport height. It passes `composable: false`, so **the full-screen view has no composer** - the mode you would use to read a long trail is the one that cannot add to it.

Problems in this file:
- **FIXED (round 3, A-126) - the chatter search's empty-state string was escaped** (`\${_search.text.trim()}`), so a search with no matches printed the expression verbatim; it now interpolates.
- **No way to reach entries past the first page.** `_hasMore` is set at `chatter.dart:194` and read only in `_countNote` (`chatter.dart::_countNote`); there is no "load more" control and `limit`/`offset` are never passed, so a record with 112 entries shows `"40 of 112 entries"` and the other 72 are unreachable from this UI.
- `_openFullScreen` wraps the body in a `StatefulBuilder` whose `setLocal` is never called (`chatter.dart:418-419`) - dead scaffolding.
- `ChatterEntry` is constructed outside this file only by `test/assessment/charts_chatter_test.dart:219,234,243`.

#### emails_panel.dart

Shows `mail.mail` delivery records for one record: subject (bold, 2 lines max), a `StatusBadge` carrying `stateLabel` in a tone derived from `state` (`sent`/`received` → ok, `exception` → bad, `outgoing` → info, `cancel` and anything unknown → inert, `emails_panel.dart:47-53`), recipient plus an IST timestamp on one line (a relative time before 19.0.3.23.0), and the raw `failure_reason` in destructive text when present - shown inline rather than behind a disclosure (`emails_panel.dart:258-267`).

Differences from `ChatterPanel`:

| | `ChatterPanel` | `EmailsPanel` |
|---|---|---|
| Question answered | what people did to the record | what the mail server did with it |
| Route | POST `/api/v1/chatter/{kind}/{id}` | POST `/api/v1/emails/{kind}/{id}` (`api_client.dart:458-467`) |
| Can write | yes, except `kind == 'attempt'` | no - read only, no composer |
| Order | oldest first (reversed client-side) | newest first, in the server's order (`id desc`); the client-side sort was removed in 19.0.3.23.0 |
| Search / emoji / attach / full screen | yes / yes / yes / yes | none of them; head action is a single `refresh` |
| Loading state | `ChatterSkeleton` | `InlineBusy('Loading delivery history')` |
| Error handling | `catch (e)` on everything, message interpolates the error | `on ApiError catch (e)` only - any other exception propagates |
| Presentation | timeline with rail and dot | flat stacked rows |
| Paging | `meta.total` / `meta.has_more` surfaced in the panel note | since 19.0.3.23.0: note is `'$_total total'` from `meta.total`, and a "Load more (N left)" button fetches the next page at `offset = rows held` (40 a page) |

**One paged call, whatever the kind** (19.0.3.23.0, row 47). An assessment's invitations are filed against its attempts (`evaluator`), never the assessment itself, and the `/api/v1/emails/assessment/<id>` route now includes them server-side, so the panel just pages that one route. It used to fan out instead - its own mail, then one `emails('attempt', id)` per attempt in `store.attempts`, `Future.wait`ed: O(attempts) requests per tab open (652 on a real cohort, up to 832 in the round-1 count), and only for the attempts the console happened to have loaded. A page that arrives for a record the panel no longer shows is dropped. Deploy order matters: an old app on the new backend lists each invite twice until reloaded, and this app on the old backend shows an empty tab (backend first, plan §0.5). Test: `emails_panel_pages_test.dart`.

Both panels are used together in `lib/assessment/assessment_section.dart:520-556`, as two tabs of `_DockTabs` inside `ChatterDock`, explicitly keyed so switching tabs does not hand one panel's `State` to the other. Those `ValueKey` strings carried escaped `\${...}`, so they were constant literals until round 3 (A-126); they now interpolate, so each record gets its own panel `State`.

#### data_grid.dart: what is and is not supported

| Capability | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed-width and flex columns | Supported | `Col.width` / `Col.flex`, resolved by `_cell` (`data_grid.dart::_cell`) |
| Right-aligned numeric columns | Supported, header and body | `data_grid.dart:201`, `data_grid.dart:268-270` |
| Zebra striping | Supported, odd rows take `t.zebra` | `data_grid.dart:127` |
| Row hover tint | Supported, painted as an `IgnorePointer` overlay | `data_grid.dart:293-299` |
| Whole-row navigation | Supported via `GridRow.onTap`; pointer cursor only when tappable | `data_grid.dart:285-289` |
| Horizontal overflow | Supported: when `avail < minWidth` the table scrolls inside the grid, with a 28px non-hit-testable gradient fade on the trailing edge | `data_grid.dart:144-169` |
| Designed empty state | Supported: no headers are drawn, `emptyMessage` is split on the first `". "` into headline and body, and `emptyAction`/`emptyIcon` are passed to `EmptyState` | `data_grid.dart:83-108` |
| Cell-count mismatch | Caught by `assert` in debug; in release extra cells are dropped and missing ones render blank | `data_grid.dart:240-245` |
| **Sorting** | **Not supported.** `Col` has no sort key, no comparator, no direction, no header tap target. Every ordering in the app is fixed in the screen's data prep (for example `lib/assessment/screens/admin/dashboard_screen.dart:451`, `lib/assessment/screens/admin/budget_screen.dart:77`) | `data_grid.dart:24-35` |
| **Filtering** | **Not supported by the grid.** Filtering is `SearchField`/`SelectField` in a `Toolbar`, applied by the screen before it builds `rows` | `lib/assessment/screens/admin/responses_screen.dart:221-268` |
| **Selection** | **Not supported by the grid.** No checkbox column, no selection callback, no selected-row styling. Screens that need it add a `Col('', width: 34)` and their own private checkbox: `_RowCheck` in `lib/assessment/screens/admin/responses_screen.dart:306,329`, with the selected set held in the screen (`responses_screen.dart:62`) | - |
| **Paging** | **Not supported by the grid.** `Pagination` is a separate widget the screen puts in `Panel.footer`; the screen slices its own list and owns `_page`/`_pageSize`. Used in exactly two places: `responses_screen.dart:284` and `ledger_screen.dart:95` | `data_grid.dart:348-402` |
| Cell clipping | Deliberately absent - overflow is allowed to report so a too-narrow column is visible | `data_grid.dart:262-266` |

`Pagination.pageCount` is `total <= 0 ? 1 : ((total - 1) ~/ pageSize) + 1` (`data_grid.dart:366`); the range label is `"$from-$to of $total"`.

#### charts.dart: how charts are drawn

No charting package. `pubspec.yaml:12-29` lists exactly three dependencies (`http`, `web`, `flutter_svg`), and the file header (`charts.dart:7-18`) states the reason: a library would add roughly 400KB to draw rectangles and would bring its own colour defaults that fight `context.tokens`.

Two of the four use `CustomPainter`; two are composed from plain widgets:

| Chart | Technique | Data in |
|---|---|---|
| `DonutChart` | `CustomPaint` + `_DonutPainter` (`charts.dart::_DonutPainter`). Stroke is 16% of width, track drawn as a full circle in `t.border`, slices as arcs starting at `-pi/2` with a 0.02rad gap. Centre text is a `Stack`ed `Column`. | `List<Slice>` plus `centerValue`/`centerLabel` strings the caller formats |
| `BarChart` | Pure widgets: `Row` per bar of a 148px label, a `LayoutBuilder`+`Stack` track/fill, and a 54px right-aligned mono value. Bar width is `math.max(2, c.maxWidth * frac)`, but only drawn when `value > 0` - zero draws nothing (`charts.dart::BarChart`). | `List<Slice>`, optional `maxValue` (else the max of the bars), `valueSuffix` |
| `StackedBar` | Pure widgets inside a `ClipRRect`. Widths computed from the real fraction with a 3px floor, explicitly **not** `Expanded(flex:)`, and `height` is set explicitly because a childless `ColoredBox` laid out at 0x0 (`charts.dart:257-281`). Legend is a `Wrap` of 9px swatches under it. | `List<Slice>`, `height` |
| `Sparkline` | `CustomPaint` + `_SparkPainter` (`charts.dart::_SparkPainter`). Builds a `Path` normalised to min/max, closes a copy to the baseline for a 14%-alpha fill, strokes the line at 1.8px. A flat series draws mid-height rather than dividing by zero (`charts.dart::Sparkline`). | `List<double>` and one `Color`; renders nothing below 2 points |

`Slice` (`charts.dart::Slice`) carries its own `Color`, so colour selection is the caller's job. Production callers: `dashboard_screen.dart:662,693`, `my_performance_screen.dart:464`, plus `budget_screen.dart` slices. The chart ramp itself lives in the `AssessmentCharts` extension on `PortalTokens` (`lib/assessment/theme.dart:140`). `BarChart` is the only one with a written empty state (`'Nothing to chart yet.'`, `charts.dart:155`); `DonutChart` and `StackedBar` draw an empty track when the total is zero, and `Sparkline` returns a blank `SizedBox`.

#### feedback.dart: the toast / banner / dialog conventions

Three channels, distinguished by how long the message needs to live (`feedback.dart:1-10`):

1. **Banner (`Notice`)** - a persistent condition on the surface, stays until the condition does. Tinted from `ToneColors`, 10px radius, warning icon for `bad`/`warn` and info icon otherwise, optional `strong` lead sentence in bold, optional trailing actions.
2. **Check list (`CheckList`)** - a set of gate conditions, all evaluated and shown together, never one at a time. Passing rows get a green tick and state what they found; failing rows get `!`, escalate their explanation to `t.destText` and bullet the offending records (`feedback.dart:182-192`). Fed `List<GateResult>` from `lib/assessment/domain/gates.dart`; used at `new_assessment_screen.dart:393` and `assessment_detail_screen.dart:453`.
3. **Toast (`Toaster` + `ToastLayer` + `ToastHost`)** - an acknowledgement that something happened.

Toast contract, enforced in code:
- One global `Toaster`, reached as `store.toaster`; API is `ok` / `bad` / `warn` / `info`, all delegating to `show(message, tone)` (`feedback.dart::show`).
- Lifetime is exactly **3200ms** (`feedback.dart:229`).
- Dismissal is by **id**, never index, so overlapping toasts cannot remove the wrong one (`feedback.dart:230-232`).
- Bottom-centred, 18px from the bottom, wrapped in `IgnorePointer` - a toast **cannot be clicked and therefore cannot be user-dismissed** (`feedback.dart:248-252`).
- Entry animation is a 200ms fade plus an 8px rise (`feedback.dart:297-308`).
- Mounted once per app by `ToastHost` (`controls.dart::ToastHost`), installed at `lib/assessment/assessment_section.dart:233`.

There is **no Flutter `SnackBar` and no `AlertDialog`** in this directory. Every modal - confirmation, preview, audit, import - goes through `showSheet` (`controls.dart:353-453`): a `showDialog` with barrier `0x8C030213`, a transparent `Dialog`, 640px (or 880px when `wide`), max 88% viewport height, title + optional sub + close button in a bordered head, scrolling body, and a tinted footer whose actions are laid out after a `Spacer` with the affirmative last. Escape closes it (default `showDialog` behaviour).

Long-running work has its own vocabulary rather than a toast: `Btn(busy: true)` for a single in-flight action (16 call sites), `InlineBusy` for a region with no content yet, `BusyOverlay` for a panel that must keep its layout, and `JobCard` for any background pipeline (`feedback.dart:336-340`: "work with no visible state is indistinguishable from work that is not happening").

#### Defined but never used

Grepped across `lib/` and `test/` with `grep -rnw --include='*.dart'`, excluding each symbol's own definition site.

| Symbol | File:line | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `BusyOverlay` | `loaders.dart::BusyOverlay` | **Zero references anywhere**, including its own directory and the test suite. Dead. |
| `Pill.showDot` parameter | `marks.dart::showDot` | Never passed by any caller; every `Pill` in the app renders with the dot. |
| `AutoGrid.intrinsicHeight` | `panel.dart:436,444` | Already `@Deprecated` and explicitly "no longer read"; zero call sites pass it. Dead parameter kept for source compatibility that nothing needs. |
| `ChatterEntry.subtype` | `chatter.dart::subtype` | Parsed from the wire, never rendered by any widget. |
| `Switcher` | `buttons.dart::Switcher` | Used only by `SwitchRow` (`buttons.dart::SwitchRow`). No screen instantiates it directly. Not dead, but not a public entry point in practice. |
| `ToastLayer` | `feedback.dart::ToastLayer` | Used only by `ToastHost` (`controls.dart::ToastHost`). |
| `Spinner` (`feedback.dart::Spinner`) | `feedback.dart:458` | Used only by `JobCard` (`feedback.dart::JobCard`) in the same file. |
| `ChatterFile` | `chatter.dart::ChatterFile` | Used only inside `chatter.dart`. |
| `EmailEntry` | `emails_panel.dart::EmailEntry` | Used only inside `emails_panel.dart`. |
| `kImportColumns` | `import_sheet.dart:31` | Used only inside `import_sheet.dart`, despite the comment saying it is named there so both callers share it - the callers call `showImportSheet`, not the constant. |
| `kDockMin`, `kDockMax`, `kDockDefault`, `kDockCollapseBelow` | `dock.dart::kDockMin` | Public top-level constants read only inside `dock.dart`. |
| `ChatterEntry` (as a constructor) | `chatter.dart::ChatterEntry` | Production code never builds one outside `chatter.dart`; only `test/assessment/charts_chatter_test.dart` does. |

Thin-usage widgets that are not dead but have a single production call site, worth knowing before changing them: `StatusBar` (`assessment_detail_screen.dart:150`), `Sparkline` (`my_performance_screen.dart:464`), `DonutChart` (`dashboard_screen.dart:693`), `StackedBar` (`dashboard_screen.dart:662`), `InlineBusy` (`scoring_screen.dart:119`), `Spinner` from `loaders.dart` used directly once (`exam_screen.dart:1600`), `EmailsPanel` (`assessment_section.dart:538`), `TableSkeleton`/`ChatterSkeleton`/`KpiStripSkeleton` (only referenced from `test/assessment/skeleton_test.dart` and, transitively, from `ListScreenSkeleton`/`DetailScreenSkeleton`). *(scoring_screen.dart: removed since 19.0.3.12.0)*

#### Other things that look wrong or half-finished

- **Two classes named `Spinner`**, `feedback.dart:458` (`size` only, fixed 2px stroke, `t.primary.o(.25)` backdrop) and `loaders.dart::size` (`size` + `color`, stroke scaled `(size/9).clamp(1.5,3.0)`, no backdrop). They render differently. `feedback.dart` does not import `loaders.dart`, so `JobCard` gets one and `Btn`/`exam_screen` get the other. Any file importing both unprefixed would fail to compile.
- **`import_sheet.dart:16-17` conditional import depths disagree**: the stub is `'../../services/file_pick_stub.dart'` (correct) while the web branch is `'../../../services/file_pick_web.dart'` (one `..` too many). It happens to work because RFC 3986 URI normalisation clamps excess `..` at the package root, and `build/web/main.dart.js` (built 2026-08-11 15:05, after the file's last edit) confirms a successful web build. Compare `chatter.dart:6-7`, which uses the correct depth. The same inconsistency exists in three admin screens (`new_generator_screen.dart:14`, `generator_detail_screen.dart:16`, `review_queue_screen.dart:20` all use four `..`). Cosmetic, but it makes the pattern look like it has two valid forms. *(new_generator_screen.dart: removed since 19.0.3.12.0)*
- **`DataGrid`'s empty-message split is naive**: `emptyMessage.indexOf('. ')` (`data_grid.dart:94`) will split on the first abbreviation or decimal followed by a space, putting the wrong text in the headline. No caller currently hits it, but nothing prevents it.
- `emails_panel.dart:174` catches `ApiError` only; `chatter.dart:203` catches everything. Two panels side by side in the same dock behave differently when the server returns something unparseable.
- FIXED in 19.0.3.23.0: `emails_panel.dart`'s `for (final String kind in <String>['assessment'])` loop over a one-element literal went with the fan-out.
- `Panel` renders its header strip when `title != null || headActions.isNotEmpty`, but `note` alone will not produce one (`panel.dart:206`) - a `Panel(note: 'x')` silently drops the note.
- UNKNOWN: whether `ChatterEntry.attachments[].url` is ever meant to be openable. `_Line` prints the filename with a paperclip icon (`chatter.dart:651-660`) and never uses `f.url`; nothing in this directory makes it a link or a download.

#### Platform: what needs `--platform chrome`, and why

No test *requires* Chrome to pass. Chrome is run because compiled to JavaScript there is one numeric type, so `0.0 is int` is true there and false on the VM. Four groups of assertions only have teeth in the Chrome run:

- `ledger_test.dart:132-158` - `jval` tested `fallback is int` before `is double`, so every cost went through `toInt()` and the budget screen summed integer parts ($13.00 against a real $17.4437) while the VM suite stayed green.
- `stimulus_media_test.dart:66-75` - a fractional `box_2d` coordinate would round to 0 and stack every label box at the origin.
- `seed_test.dart:5-11` - `stableHash` must agree across VM and JS or a token minted in a test does not resolve in the browser.
- `parser_safety_test.dart:62-121` guards the same rule statically, but only on the VM.

**95 of the 238 `*_test.dart` files** opt out of Chrome with `@TestOn('vm')` in 19.0.3.23.0 (74 of 207 on 18 Sep 2026). The
breakdown below was taken at the 11 September edition, when there were 14:

| Reason | Files |
|---|---|
| Uses `dart:io` (no filesystem under Chrome; fails with `Unsupported operation: _Namespace`, stated verbatim at e.g. `kpi_tone_test.dart:2-6`) | `envelope_unwrap`, `kpi_sub_length`, `kpi_tone`, `live_payload`, `parser_safety`, `question_types` |
| Documented non-`dart:io` reason (token store is a conditional import whose web half needs a real `sessionStorage`) | `session_restore_test.dart:9-12` |
| **No stated reason and no `dart:io`** | `audit_followups`, `chatter_panel`, `cold_cache_hydration`, `deep_link_hydration`, `exam_deep_link`, `features`, `generator_resources` |

That last row is worth acting on: `exam_deep_link_test` and `generator_resources_test` are pure `fromJson` tests with no platform dependency at all, and they are exactly the class of test the Chrome run exists to catch numeric bugs in. On 18 Sep the Chrome run was 1,276 tests against the VM's 1,826, and nothing compares the two counts.
