#### Invariants the suite genuinely protects

These are the assertions whose failure would be a real regression rather than a cosmetic one.

**Correctness of the result**
1. **Nothing reaches a candidate unreviewed.** A draft with a blocking warning cannot be approved; acknowledging unblocks it; undo reverses both the draft state and the bank row it created; only approved + active + media-complete + keyed questions are `launchReady` (`invariants_test.dart:17-82`).
2. **Marks, never percentages.** Every question is worth 1; the display is `earned / totalQuestions`; the percentage exists only to compare against the threshold (`invariants_test.dart:84-129`). Re-asserted at the UI edge: `answer_review_test.dart:276-277` requires "0 / 3" on screen and no `%` anywhere.
3. **Results are never revealed automatically.** Submitting does not release; release touches only submitted, resolved attempts; there is no un-release; an attempt still being graded is excluded from both the bulk and the single-row release path (`invariants_test.dart:131-193`, `workflows_test.dart:221-269`). An unreleased answer sheet discloses no key, verdict, feedback or marks (`answer_review_test.dart:308-366`).
4. **An unresolved answer holds the whole result on `pending`,** and a terminal LLM error holds rather than fails - an infrastructure failure must never be recorded as a candidate failure (`invariants_test.dart:195-256`).
5. **A terminal error is never retried automatically;** a person re-scoring does clear it (`invariants_test.dart:258-305`, `workflows_test.dart:296-336`).
6. **Advisory flags never change a score,** and erasing PII keeps every mark while blanking justifications (`invariants_test.dart:307-348`).
7. **All seven launch gates are evaluated together,** every gate states its reason, gate 6 names offending questions, and the guard sits in `launch()` itself and not only on the button (`invariants_test.dart:350-425`).
8. **Objective scoring is all-or-nothing;** an empty subjective answer is discarded rather than scored zero; a subjective score is re-decided from the stored raw score when the threshold moves (`invariants_test.dart:427-508`).
9. **The proctoring cap:** `autoSubmit` ends and marks the attempt as automatic at the cap; `logOnly` never ends it (`invariants_test.dart:510-549`).
10. **Two roles only, and the role comes from the server.** `Portal.values.length == 2`; an unknown or empty org role falls to `member` (`invariants_test.dart:551-584`, `auth_test.dart:332-383`).

**Client/server contract** (the class of bug that is silent by construction - the server answers `ok: true` and nothing happens)
11. Assign sends `applicant_ids`, not `person_ids` (`features_test.dart:46-66`, `server_actions_test.dart:89-117`).
12. Launch sends `confirm: true`, not `dry_run` - the route defaults to a dry run (`features_test.dart:322-347`).
13. An exam answer sends `selected_option_ids` and `label_answers` (`features_test.dart:350-388`).
14. Bank filtering sends `question_type`, not `type` (`features_test.dart:390-399`).
15. Every list call sends an explicit `limit > 40`, or rows 41+ vanish silently (`features_test.dart:261-288`).
16. `updateAssessment` sends only what changed: a subjective edit never carries `pass_threshold` (`features_test.dart:137-163`), and a pass-threshold edit carries it alone (`the_pass_threshold_is_editable_test.dart`).
17. **A refused submit is never reported as success.** One 422 on a single answer must not abort the loop before `examSubmit`; a refused submit says "NOT submitted"; `attempt_locked` counts as success and triggers a refresh (`server_actions_test.dart:530-665`). This is the highest-value test in the file - the old behaviour lost the candidate's paper while telling them it was submitted.
18. **Parsers never throw on the wire.** No raw `j['key']` reads, no int fallback on a double field (`parser_safety_test.dart`), and real captured payloads parse (`live_payload_test.dart`). A `TypeError` here used to escape `refresh()` and hang `loadState` on `loading` forever.
19. **A cold cache still hydrates.** Deep links and browser refreshes arrive with nothing loaded; `loadAssessment/Generator/Question/Attempt/Response` must upsert, and a fetch in flight must not read as "not found" (`cold_cache_hydration_test.dart`, `deep_link_hydration_test.dart`, `audit_followups_test.dart:38-104`).
20. **A stored token is verified, not trusted,** and an empty role is not a session (`session_restore_test.dart:64-84`, `:162-180`).
21. **The invitation URL parses** in all six shapes the module and the Odoo portal emit (`deep_link_test.dart`).
22. **Every sidebar destination opens a distinct real screen** (`section_entry_test.dart`). Called out in the file header as the only honest check available: Flutter web renders to canvas, so browser automation cannot click these.

#### `tool/verify.sh`

**What it is.** A single bash script that decides whether the app is sound. Not `set -e`: it uses `set -uo pipefail` (`verify.sh:10`) so every check runs and the tally is printed, and the process exit status comes from `[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]` on the last line (`verify.sh:130`). It prepends `/opt/homebrew/bin` to `PATH` and `cd`s to the repo root (`:11-12`), so it can be invoked from anywhere.

**How to run**

```
bash tool/verify.sh            # everything: static + both test platforms + release build + live
bash tool/verify.sh --quick    # same, minus the release build (step 6 becomes a SKIP)
make verify                    # equivalent to the first form (Makefile:57-58)
```

**Environment variables**

| Variable | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `API` / `ETP_API` | `http://localhost:8069` | Base URL for the live probes, and the fallback bundle URL (`verify.sh:14`) |
| `ETP_ADMIN_LOGIN` / `ETP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | the script's local-dev defaults (see `verify.sh:16-17`) | Operator token for step 7 (`:16-17`) |
| `ETP_CANDIDATE_LOGIN` / `ETP_CANDIDATE_PASSWORD` | empty | Candidate token. Empty means the privilege-boundary half of step 7 is skipped (`:18-19`, `:109-117`) |
| `API_BASE_URL` | falls back to `$API` | Baked into the release bundle (`:65`, `:72`) |
| `API_DB` | `etp_local` | Baked into the release bundle. The comment at `:66-70` records that this used to read `ethara_ops`, a database the module cannot load in |
| `ETP_MODULE_PATH` | unset | Not read by `verify.sh` itself, but by `question_types_test.dart:42` during step 2/3 |

**The seven checks**

| Step | What it does | How it fails |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Static analysis (`:26-28`) | `dart analyze lib/ test/`, counting lines matching `^ +error`. Warnings and infos are ignored | Non-zero error count |
| 2 Tests on the VM (`:30-33`) | `flutter test`, greps the last line for "All tests passed" and echoes the `+N` count | Missing "All tests passed" |
| 3 Tests on Chrome (`:35-41`) | `flutter test --platform chrome`. The comment at `:36-38` records why it is not redundant: the `0.0 is int` numeric difference | Missing "All tests passed" |
| 4 Deep link honoured (`:43-50`) | Greps `examTokenFrom(Uri.base)` in `lib/main.dart` and `loadExamByToken` in `exam_screen.dart`. A text check, not an executed one - it is the only coverage `main.dart` has | Either grep misses |
| 5 Detached from the host portal (`:52-56`) | Counts files in `lib` and `test` referencing `workflow_management_app_v2`, and files in `lib` importing `api_client.dart' as host` | Either count non-zero |
| 6 Release build (`:58-87`) | `flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none` with both `--dart-define`s, then greps `build/web/main.dart.js` for the URL and asserts `flutter_bootstrap.js` contains no `serviceWorkerVersion: "` | Build output lacks "Built", URL not in the bundle, or a service worker is registered. Skipped entirely under `--quick` |
| 7 Live backend (`:89-126`) | POSTs `/api/v1/auth_token` with the admin credentials (5 s timeout). With a token, POSTs `{}` to nine operator routes (`auth/me`, `assessments`, `generators`, `bank`, `drafts`, `tags`, `responses`, `ledger`, `settings`) expecting `ok: true`. With a candidate token, POSTs five of them expecting `ok: false` | A route refuses the admin, or a route answers a candidate. **Skipped, not failed,** when no backend answers (`:93-94`) or no candidate account is configured (`:116-117`) |

**What a pass looks like.** Each check prints `  PASS <detail>`, then a final tally line and exit status 0:

```
1 Static analysis
  PASS 0 errors
2 Tests on the VM
    00:06 +320: All tests passed!
  PASS vm +320
3 Tests on Chrome - the environment that actually ships
    00:29 +239: All tests passed!
  PASS chrome +239
4 An invitation deep link is honoured
  PASS the URL is read at startup and the sitting is fetched by token
5 The app is detached from the host portal it was ported out of
  PASS no host package or client references
6 Release build
  PASS web bundle built
  PASS backend URL baked into the bundle
  PASS no service worker registered
7 Live backend
  SKIP no backend at http://localhost:8069 - static checks above still stand

PASS 8  FAIL 0  SKIP 1
```

The `+320` and `+239` above are the counts measured on this checkout today; steps 1 to 5 were re-run and pass. Step 6 and step 7 were not run here (they mutate `build/` and need a live Odoo respectively), so their output lines are reconstructed from the script's own `echo`/`ok` strings at `:74`, `:78`, `:86`, `:94`.

**Caveats worth knowing.**
- Step 6 leaves `build/web` populated with a bundle pointed at whatever `API_BASE_URL`/`API` was in effect. That is deliberate (`:62-64`) but it means running `verify.sh` changes what `make serve` would serve.
- Nothing compares the VM count with the Chrome count, so a file that acquires `@TestOn('vm')` silently reduces Chrome coverage while both lines still read PASS.
- There is **no format check anywhere** - not in `verify.sh`, not in the `Makefile`. `dart format` is available but unwired.
- There is no coverage step. `flutter test --coverage` is never invoked.
- Step 1 greps `^ +error`; if `dart analyze` ever changes its output prefix the count becomes 0 and the check passes vacuously.

#### The other three scripts in `tool/`

| Script | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `capture_payloads.py` | 214 | Re-captures the 14 JSON fixtures into `test/assessment/payloads/` from a live backend. Credentials come from `ETP_ADMIN_LOGIN/PASSWORD` and `ETP_CANDIDATE_LOGIN/PASSWORD` (`:36-39`); `access_token`, `token`, `candidate_link`, `email`, `email_from` and `login` are redacted before writing (`:41-50`) after a previous capture committed a live token. It deliberately picks a generator that *has* a resource and the assessment with the *most* attempts, because a blank fixture is worse than none (`:116-143`). Run with `python3 tool/capture_payloads.py [base_url]` or `make fixtures` |
| `serve.py` | 47 | Serves `build/web` on 127.0.0.1 with `Cache-Control: no-store`, stripping `If-Modified-Since`/`If-None-Match` *before* the base class sees them so a conditional GET cannot 304 back a stale bundle (`:17-23`). Names the port holder on `EADDRINUSE` rather than printing a traceback (`:37-43`). Invoked by `make serve` from inside `build/web` |
| `dev_server.py` | 179 | Static server plus an `/api`, `/web`, `/odoo`, `/jsonrpc`, `/longpolling` reverse proxy to Odoo, so the app can call its own origin with no CORS. Answers `flutter_service_worker.js` with a real 404 to force the browser to unregister a stale worker (`:73-90`), sends `no-store` on static assets only, relays 4xx/5xx from Odoo verbatim rather than converting them to 502 (`:139-141`), and falls back to `index.html` on any non-proxied 404 for SPA deep links (`:159-165`). **Its default upstream is port 7070** (`dev_server.py:35-36`), which contradicts the `Makefile`'s documented `:8069` and the comment at `Makefile:20-27` saying the `:7070` default came from a deleted checkout. Nothing in `Makefile` or `verify.sh` invokes this script; it appears to be stale |

## 3.11 The Form Studio designer's item card

Scope: `lib/assessment/screens/admin/form_item_editor.dart` (1,906 lines), the ONE item editor
shared by Form Studio (`form_designer_screen.dart`, 681 lines) and the Task Template designer
(`task_template_editor.dart`). It was extracted out of the designer because the two screens each
drew their own version of the same thing - Form Studio had 18 item kinds, help text, descriptions,
duplicate/delete/reorder and the media BLOCKS (`textBlock`, `imageBlock`, `videoBlock`) a
generated question fills in; the template editor had 13 kinds, no blocks and no item chrome at
all. A template is meant to be the SHAPE of a Form Studio form, so anything the designer can
express a template must be able to express too, and two hand-maintained copies could only drift.
(The 18 and 13 are the file's own header comment, recording the state at extraction;
`FormItemKind` is **15** values today - `form_models.dart:34`, ending in `promptWriting`.)
The file's own rule is that it is the designer's code moved verbatim - every comment, padding,
tooltip and hint string is the one Form Studio shipped (`:12-15`).

**Ownership.** The widget edits ONE item. The list it lives in belongs to the parent, so duplicate
and delete are `VoidCallback`s (`:55-56`, `:74-75`) rather than list surgery done here: the
designer inserts into a `FormSection`, the template editor into its own structure, and neither has
to know about the other's container.

#### The four affordances, and what each was fixing

A section card and a question card now carry the same four controls, in a section header's order
and with a section header's icons (`:314-357`).

| Control | Where | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Collapse / expand | 319-323 | **Absent.** A SECTION could collapse and a QUESTION could not | `IconBtn` toggling `_collapsed`, tooltip "Collapse question" / "Expand question" |
| Drag to reorder | 329-337 | present | `ReorderableDragStartListener`, but **only when `showDragHandle`** |
| Duplicate | 347-351 | in a footer below an `Hr()` | in the header, `Icons.copy_outlined`, and it now toasts |
| Delete | 352-356 | in the same footer, **fired on one click** | in the header, behind a confirm sheet |

**Collapse is the one that mattered most.** The two cards otherwise offered the same affordances,
so the missing control read as an oversight rather than a decision - and a 47-item form is
unnavigable when every option list is expanded (`:103-107`). `_collapsed` is view state only,
never persisted, and is held on the STATE rather than lifted into the parent's set: the widget
already owns its other UI-only maps (`_uploadMode`, `_selMarker`, `_goldenSel`, `:97-99`) and
lifting it would make every host screen carry collapse plumbing it does not otherwise need
(`:108-112`).

A collapsed card shows **the question, not nothing** (`:369-372`). `_collapsedSummary` (`:173`)
prints the title plus a one-line shape summary ending in `· collapsed`, mirroring
`form_designer_screen._collapsedSummary`, because the title is the only thing that identifies
which item this is - hiding it would make a collapsed form a stack of anonymous kind pickers.

**The drag handle stands down rather than lying.** A `ReorderableDragStartListener` with no
reorderable ancestor throws the moment it is dragged, and the task template editor draws a plain
flat list, so `showDragHandle: false` removes the handle instead of offering a gesture that
cannot work (`:324-328`).

**Duplicate acknowledges itself.** The copy is the parent's business; `_duplicate` (`:130`) adds
only `toaster.ok('Question duplicated')`. A section's duplicate already said so and a question's
did not - and the new card appears BELOW the original, which on a form long enough to scroll is
off screen, so without a toast the click looked like it had done nothing.

**Delete asks first.** `_confirmDelete` (`:139`) opens a sheet titled "Delete this question?" /
"Delete this block?" with sub "This cannot be undone.", a `Btn.danger` labelled "Delete Question"
/ "Delete Block", and a `!mounted` re-check after the await because the card can be gone by the
time the sheet closes (`:164`). This was **the one destructive control in the designer that fired
on a single click**, while `form_designer_screen._confirmDeleteSection` had asked all along.
Nothing is gated: a section refuses to delete its last one, but a section is allowed to hold no
questions at all.

**Why the controls moved out of the footer** (`:337-346`, the file's own comment): the same two
actions sat in two different places depending on whether the reader was looking at a section or a
question, and on a long question the footer scrolled out of sight - so the controls moved as the
card grew.

The `Required` switch stays in a real footer strip (`:401-420`), a `Container` with a top
`BorderSide` rather than a hand-drawn `Hr()` inside the body, because the hand-drawn rule did not
reach the card's edge where a section's footer rule does. It stands down on a display block that
cannot be answered - an empty strip read as a card that had lost its buttons - and on a collapsed
card, where a section shows its summary and nothing else.

#### Alignment with a section card is measured, not eyeballed

`test/assessment/form_item_parity_test.dart` (387 lines, 13 `testWidgets`) mounts **both cards on
screen at once**, in the nesting the designer draws, and compares geometry: the distance from the
card's right edge to the last control's right edge, and each control's left edge
(`:264-290`). Every icon is looked up as a descendant of its own card, because both cards carry
the same four glyphs and an unscoped `find.byIcon` matches two of each and throws. Two cases:
`the controls sit at a panel header's inset from the edge` (`:291`) and `the controls reach the
edge on a wide card` (`:370`).

The other 11 cases pin the shared contract so a future edit that re-forks the two editors fails
here rather than in a demo: help text is carried (which the template editor lacked), a
`textBlock` asks for body text rather than help text, duplicate and delete are on every card, all
four controls sit in the header above the body, cancel keeps the item, confirming deletes exactly
once and says so, a block is confirmed in its own words, the kind picker is present, every kind
renders with no `FormDef` at all, the branch picker stands down when there is no form, and the
drag handle can be hidden for a flat list.

Ground truth was re-derived from source, not from the readers' text. Two independent passes:

1. `grep -rn "@http.route" custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/controllers custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/models | wc -l` → **84**. Zero hits in `models/` (every `models/ir_http.py` hit for the word "route" is prose inside a docstring or comment: `models/ir_http.py:150,157,323,336,370,373,459,468,470,477,480,482`).
2. An AST pass over every `.py` file in the addon, taking the first positional argument of every decorator call whose function name contains `route` and resolving it with `ast.literal_eval`. This is the authoritative pass, because grep prints only the first physical line: `write.py:680` greps as `"/api/v1/generators/<int:generator_id>/resources/"` and silently drops the implicit string concatenation on `write.py:681` (`"<int:resource_id>/delete"`). Any inventory built from raw grep output alone will have that path truncated.

6. State the counting rule explicitly - 84 decorators, 84 distinct paths, 120 (path, method) pairs - so the recurring bare number "84" is unambiguous.


## 4.2 Configuration, databases, and CI

Two repos are in scope: `ethara-etp` (Odoo 19 backend, `src/odoo/release.py` `version_info = (19, 0, 0, FINAL, 0, '')`) and `ethara-assessment-fe` (Flutter client). All paths below are relative to the repo named in the heading of each subsection.

---

#### 1. `ir.config_parameter` keys the code reads

**Every key in this section was renamed on 25 August 2026.** The prefix moved
`assessments_be_v2.*` -> `assessments_be_v2.*` with the fork, and **nothing migrates them**.
A deployment carrying the old keys runs on defaults: Vertex unconfigured, S3 unconfigured,
CORS closed. Set the new ones by hand.

Fifty keys at the 25 August count, all read through `ir.config_parameter`. `19.0.3.23.0` adds
four - `scoring_parallel_calls`, `scoring_cache`, `verdict_requires_current_prompt`,
`default_pass_threshold` (Q20) - plus the
runtime-only `score_outlier_checks_since`, and stops reading two: `scoring_system_prompt` and
`scoring_prompt_filename`. "Default" is the value the code falls back
to when the row is absent or empty. "Form" means there is a `config_parameter=` field on
`res.config.settings` (`models/res_config_settings.py`); "UI" means that field is actually
rendered by `views/res_config_settings_views.xml` - **the two are not the same**, see the gap
noted at the end.

Two `_param` wrappers exist and behave slightly differently:

- `services/vertex.py::_param` - `get_param(key, default) or default`, then returns `default`
  if the value contains the literal `PLACEHOLDER`.
- `services/s3_service.py::_param` - same `PLACEHOLDER` sentinel, but returns `""` for a
  placeholder rather than the default.

So a stored value containing `PLACEHOLDER` is treated as unset everywhere. That sentinel is
undocumented in the Settings UI.

##### Vertex / model selection

There is no single "the model". Six independent selectors, each with its own key and its own
fallback chain. Read `services/vertex.py`'s `_generation_model`, `_scoring_model`,
`_detection_model`, `_verify_model`, `_vertex_image_model` and `_video_model` together.

| Key (`assessments_be_v2.` prefix) | Default / fallback chain | Controls | Form / UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vertex_project_id` | `""` | GCP project in every Vertex REST URL. Backfilled from the service account's `project_id` on first bearer mint | yes / yes |
| `vertex_location` | `VERTEX_DEFAULT_LOCATION` = `"global"` | Endpoint host. `global` -> `aiplatform.googleapis.com`; anything else -> `<loc>-aiplatform.googleapis.com` | yes / yes |
| `vertex_model` | `VERTEX_DEFAULT_MODEL` = `"gemini-3-pro-image"` | Catch-all for a task with no override. Note the default is an **image** model | yes / yes |
| `generation_model` | -> `GENERATION_DEFAULT_MODEL` = `"gemini-3.1-pro-preview"` | Reads the SOP document and authors questions. Must be document-capable: the image model reads a PDF as opaque binary | yes / yes |
| `scoring_model` | -> `generation_model` -> `GENERATION_DEFAULT_MODEL` | The subjective grading judge. **Never** falls back to `vertex_model`, which is the image model on this deployment | yes / yes |
| `detection_model` | -> `_generation_model(env)` | Detects elements in an `image_label` stimulus for the numbered-box overlay | yes / yes |
| `verify_model` | -> `_detection_model(env)` | Vision model that re-reads a rendered image to confirm planted flaws. Must READ an image | no / no |
| `image_model` | -> `vertex_model` | Renders `image_ab` / `image_prompt` / `image_label` pictures | yes / yes |
| `fallback_model` | `""` = lane disabled | Second TEXT model retried once on a 429 or a no-text refusal, for generation, scoring and detection. Not used for image or Veo calls | yes / yes |
| `video_model` | `VIDEO_DEFAULT_MODEL` = `"veo-3.1-generate-001"` | Veo model for async `video_prompt` clips. Empty means `video_generation_available()` returns False | yes / yes |
| `video_location` | `VIDEO_DEFAULT_LOCATION` = `"us-central1"` | Veo region. **Veo 404s on the `global` location** - never reuse the gemini location here | yes / yes |
| `video_default_duration_s` | `"6"`, snapped into `(4,6,8)` for veo-3.x or `(5,6,7,8)` for veo-2.x | Clip length when a brief omits one | yes / yes (Selection) |
| `video_supported_durations.<model-lowercase>` | absent | **A DYNAMIC KEY SUFFIX.** The per-model duration enum, learned at runtime from Veo's own rejection text and written back, then honoured over the hardcoded tuple | no / no |

##### Vertex credentials

| Key | Default | Controls | Form / UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vertex_api_key` | `""` | Alternative auth. An `AQ.`-prefixed key goes to `aiplatform.googleapis.com`, anything else to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`. **Encrypted at rest** | yes / yes (`password`) |
| `vertex_access_token` | `""` | Pre-minted bearer; short-circuits SA minting entirely. **Encrypted at rest** | yes / yes (`password`) |
| `vertex_service_account_json` | `""` | Service-account JSON. **Encrypted at rest** | yes / **no** - only the Binary upload and a readonly filename render |
| `vertex_service_account_filename` | `""` | Display only | yes / yes (readonly) |
| `vertex_minted_token` | `""` | Cached OAuth bearer, written inside a savepoint so a concurrent first-INSERT race cannot poison the transaction | no / no - runtime cache |
| `vertex_minted_token_expires` | `"0"` | Unix expiry of the above; the cache is treated as stale 300s early | no / no |

`_minted_bearer` takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock(ADVISORY_LOCK_VERTEX_BEARER)` before the
double-checked mint, and **pins the SA JSON's `token_uri`** to `oauth2.googleapis.com`,
`accounts.google.com` or `www.googleapis.com` over https - it refuses to sign an assertion for
anything else. Uploading a new SA blanks both token keys.

##### S3 (question media)

| Key | Default | Controls | Form / UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `s3_bucket` | `""` | Bucket. Also the sole truthiness test for `storage.configured` in the API | yes / yes |
| `s3_region` | `"us-east-1"` | Region for the client and for URL construction | yes / yes |
| `s3_access_key_id` | `""` | Access key (not encrypted) | yes / yes |
| `s3_secret_key` | `""` | Secret key. **Encrypted at rest** | yes / yes (`password`) |
| `s3_folder` | `"etp_assessment"` | Key prefix | yes / yes |
| `s3_cdn_url` | `""` | CDN base substituted for the bucket URL; `rstrip("/")`-ed | yes / yes |
| `s3_max_retries` | `"3"`, floored at 1 | Upload retry count for the retryable error set in `s3_service.py` | yes / yes |
| `media_redirect_to_s3` | `""` = off | When on, the media proxies 302 to S3 instead of streaming bytes | no / no |

**The SECOND, disjoint S3 configuration is GONE - this paragraph used to say otherwise and was
wrong for this edition.** Form Studio's media lane once read `etp_assessment_pro.s3_bucket` /
`.s3_region` and imported `odoo.addons.etp_assessment_pro.services.s3_service`, so configuring
only the `assessments_be_v2.s3_*` keys left Form Studio uploads landing nowhere. All three sites
(`form_media_upload`, `form_media_serve`, `_fetch_s3_object`) now resolve through this addon's own
`services/s3_service.storage_target` (`forms.py:547`, `:597`, `studio_form.py:1008`) and read the
keys in the table above - the ones the Settings screen, the settings API and `tools/s3_setup.py`
actually write. The remaining `etp_assessment_pro` strings in those two files are three prose
comments (`forms.py:573`, `studio_form.py:5`, `:995`), not imports or `get_param` keys; the last
of them records why the switch was made. `forms.py:559` names the `assessments_be_v2.*` keys in
the error message an unconfigured deployment sees. See section 1.1, "The four surviving upstream
references".

##### Scoring throughput and resilience

| Key | Default | Controls | Form / UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llm_max_attempts` | `"3"`; non-numeric or <= 0 -> 3 | Failed scoring attempts before a response resolves as a surfaced `error` rather than being retried | yes / yes, refused outside 1-5 at write |
| `scoring_batch_size` | `"8"`; non-numeric or <= 0 -> 8 | Answers per Vertex grading call | yes / yes, refused outside 1-32 |
| `scoring_tick_limit` | `"20"`; < 1 -> 20 | Candidates drained per cron tick, per shard | yes / yes |
| `scoring_shards` | `"1"`, clamped to `[1, MAX_SCORING_SHARDS]` = `[1, 4]` | Parallel scoring lanes; shard N owns evaluators with `id % shard_count == N`, each under its own advisory lock | yes / yes, refused outside 1-4 |
| `scoring_parallel_calls` | `"4"`; blank, 0 or unparseable -> 4; clamped to `[1, MAX_SCORING_PARALLEL_CALLS]` = `[1, 8]` | Judge calls ONE lane keeps in flight (`_drain_in_parallel`). At run time it is lowered to fit the DB pool: `(db_maxconn // 2 - 2 x shards) // (2 x shards)`, at least 1 (`assessment.py::_scoring_parallel_calls`). Odoo's default pool of 64 at 4 shards gives 3; prod's 600 gives the full 4. `/api/v1/settings` reports both, as `scoring.parallel_calls` (stored) and `scoring.parallel_calls_effective` (in use). New in `19.0.3.23.0` | yes / yes ("Parallel calls", with "In use per shard" beside it), refused outside 1-8 |
| `redis_url` | `""` = question cache off | The Redis the question cache uses when env `REDIS_URL` is unset (production sets the env var; this is for local and stage rigs). `/api/v1/settings` reports `question_cache.{enabled, source, target, reachable}`, target as scheme://host:port/db only, `reachable` a live PING. Saving it answers `true`, never the URL; the Odoo field is masked. See "Question cache" in section 1.7. New in `19.0.3.27.0` | yes / yes ("Question cache Redis URL"), free text |

The bounds are enforced at the WRITE path rather than only clamped on read, because a
silently-ignored `shards=8` is worse to operate than a refusal. **Since 19.0.3.22.0 there is
exactly ONE table of them: `constants.SETTING_RANGES`**, `{key: (low, high, default)}`. All
three enforcers read it - the form constraint, the write API (`write.py::_SETTING_BOUNDS`,
now built from it by comprehension) and the pre-deploy gate
(`tools/check_settings_in_range.py`). They used to be three hand-copies and the gate's copy
had already drifted: it refused a stored `0`, which the constraint coerces to the default and
accepts, so it held deployments back on values that save perfectly well. `0` means "unset, use
the default" on every one of them, which is why the default rides in the tuple.
`19.0.3.23.0` added `scoring_parallel_calls: (1, 8, 4)` to it, and all three enforcers picked
it up with no second copy. `scoring_tick_limit` is not in the table (its default stays 20; prod
stores 5).

The first four keys above gained a Settings field and a UI block in the 2 September cycle; the
11 August edition correctly recorded `scoring_shards` and `scoring_tick_limit` as DB-only, and
that is no longer true.

The form constraint is **`res_config_settings._check_be_llm_limits`**, renamed from
`_check_llm_limits` in the same wave. `etp_assessment_pro` defines a method of the old name on
the same model with no `super()` call, and Odoo composes one class from every installed addon -
so on production, which carries both, v2's constraint was composed away **together with its
`@api.constrains` trigger list**, and none of its checks ran on the Odoo Settings form. The
`be_` prefix is both the fix and the guard. `vertex_max_rpm` was bounded nowhere until this wave
added it to `_SETTING_BOUNDS` (1-10000); it is not in `SETTING_RANGES` because no form
constraint and no pre-deploy gate read it.

> **The same collision hit three more methods, and they are now fixed.**
> `res.config.settings._onchange_vertex_sa_upload`, `_onchange_question_prompt_upload`
> and `_onchange_scoring_prompt_upload` were defined with those exact names in BOTH
> `assessments_be_v2` and `etp_assessment_pro`, on the same model, and neither copy
> called `super()`. Whichever module composed last won and the loser's `@api.onchange`
> trigger went with it, so on a deployment carrying both, one module's three Settings
> upload widgets stopped filling their text box as the file was picked. **Less severe
> than `_check_llm_limits`:** `set_values` decodes the same uploads itself inside the
> Save transaction, so the upload still persisted - only the live in-form feedback was
> lost. They are now `_onchange_be_vertex_sa_upload`,
> `_onchange_be_question_prompt_upload` and `_onchange_be_scoring_prompt_upload`, with
> their `@api.onchange` decorators and field lists unchanged. (`19.0.3.23.0` removed the
> scoring-prompt upload together with the stored override, so only the first two remain.)
> `_decode_upload` collided
> too but harmlessly - both copies are staticmethods with byte-identical bodies,
> verified by AST comparison rather than assumed - and is renamed `_be_decode_upload`
> with them. `get_values` / `set_values` are same-named in both addons and are left
> alone on purpose: they are Odoo's own API, both call `super()`, and they stack as
> intended. `ir.http._adopt_gateway_token` does not collide today. The manifest carries
> the rule: a method added to a model shared with `etp_assessment_pro` must carry
> `_be_`; an override that calls `super()` is exempt, because stacking is the intended
> behaviour there. **The suite cannot see this defect class by running:** a fresh test
> database has `etp_assessment_pro` uninstalled, so only one definition of each name
> exists there. `tests/test_a_shared_model_has_no_shared_method_names.py` therefore
> reads both modules' source instead of relying on installation.
>
> **THE PROCESS FACT BEHIND ALL THREE, WORTH ITS OWN PARAGRAPH BECAUSE IT IS WHAT WILL
> PRODUCE THE NEXT ONE.** `etp_assessment_pro` is installed on **production** and on
> **`etp_local`**, but **uninstalled on every fresh test database**: a `-i assessments_be_v2`
> run builds a registry holding exactly one definition of each method name. So a green
> suite on a fresh database (1,869 tests then) is not evidence that no method collides - it
> is evidence that the suite never composed the two classes together. That is how two
> instances of this defect
> (`_check_llm_limits`, then the three upload onchanges) survived months behind a green
> suite, and it is why the guard above parses SOURCE with `ast` rather than inspecting the
> registry.
>
> **Recommendation, not done yet.** Add a CI database with **both** modules installed and run
> the suite against it as a second job. A static parse catches same-named methods; it cannot
> catch the rest of the shared-registry surface - two `_inherit` definitions of the same field
> name with different types, colliding `_sql_constraints` names, view `xpath`s fighting over
> the same inherited form, or `ir.rule` / `ir.model.access` rows from the two modules
> combining into an access ladder neither module tested alone. Until that job exists, read
> "the suite is green" as a statement about a SINGLE-module registry only.
>
> **One exception, by construction rather than by CI.** The `19.0.3.23.0` gates ran
> `-u assessments_be_v2 --test-tags /assessments_be_v2` on fresh `pg_dump` copies of
> `etp_local`, which carries `etp_assessment_pro` `19.0.1.135.0` installed. So those 2,413
> tests (2,408 before the Q20 follow-ups, 2,391 before Q20) did run on a two-module registry. That is a property of how the gate was run by hand,
> not a CI job, and nothing makes the next run do the same.

##### Governance and cost

| Key | Default | Controls | Form / UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `daily_llm_cap_usd` | `100.0` | Refuse Vertex calls once same-day RECORDED spend reaches it. `0` disables. Window is UTC midnight | yes / yes |
| `per_evaluator_llm_cap_usd` | `5.0` | The same, per candidate. `0` disables | yes / yes |
| `score_outlier_sigma` | `2.0` (`SCORE_OUTLIER_SIGMA_DEFAULT`) | Flag a candidate for human review at this many sigma **above** the cohort mean, min cohort 5. `0` disables. Advisory only - never changes a score | yes / yes |
| `pii_retention_days` | `0` = **disabled** (`PII_RETENTION_DAYS_DEFAULT`) | Daily cron anonymizes free text on submitted attempts older than this. Numeric scores always kept | yes / yes |

Both spend caps are ON by default, so a fresh install is protected without a flag to remember.
The comparison is `>=` on already-recorded spend, so the cap is a "stop once crossed" gate, not
a pre-authorization: the call that crosses the line is paid for, the next one is refused.
A hit cap raises `VertexBudgetError`, which nothing outside `services/vertex.py` catches and
which `_call_vertex` deliberately does NOT retry on the fallback model - retrying would only
spend more.

`19.0.3.23.0` adds no cap and changes neither default (owner rule). What changes is how a
grading lane meets them: a cap hit, a 429 or a Postgres refusal ("too many clients",
"remaining connection slots") now DEFERS the answer to the next tick without spending one of
its `llm_max_attempts`, and the reason (`SPEND_CAP`, `GRADING_QUOTA`, `GRADING_POOL_FULL` in
the logs, tagged in `services/scoring.py`) is shown in both UIs. The Odoo LLM Budget screen
gained a read-only "Today" section: spend against these two caps, UTC day, same resolver as
the spend gate.

##### Prompt overrides

Each falls back to a bundled markdown file in `prompts/`, then to an inline constant.

| Key | Default chain | Read at | Form / UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question_prompt` | `""` -> `prompts/question.md` -> `INLINE_QUESTION_PROMPT` | `vertex.py::_get_question_prompt` | yes / **no** |
| `scoring_system_prompt` | **no longer read** (`19.0.3.23.0`) - see below | - | no / no |
| `tag_prompt` | `""` -> `prompts/tags.md` -> `_TAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FALLBACK` | `vertex.py::_get_tag_prompt` | no / no |
| `mapping_prompt` | `""` -> `prompts/mapping.md` -> `_MAPPING_PROMPT_FALLBACK` | `similarity.py::_get_mapping_prompt` | no / no |
| `question_prompt_filename` | `""` | display only | yes / **no** |

**THE GRADING INSTRUCTIONS CANNOT BE OVERRIDDEN ANY MORE (since `19.0.3.23.0`).**
`scoring.py::_get_scoring_prompt` always returns the shipped `prompts/scoring.md`, falling back
only to the inline `DEFAULT_SCORING_PROMPT` if the file is unreadable. A
`scoring_system_prompt` row already stored is left in place and never read (prod stores none).
The Settings field, its upload and its filename went with it (three transient
`res_config_settings` columns dropped on `-u`), and so did the `box_scores` version check and
`tools/check_scoring_prompt.py`, which existed only to vet a stored override.

Every graded answer records which instructions graded it in `llm_prompt_version`:
`bundled:` plus the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the stripped file
(`scoring.py::scoring_prompt_version`). The release ships **`bundled:785826a5`**; prod's
`19.0.3.22.0` file is `bundled:34c42d2f`. The candidate verdict gate below compares against
that fingerprint, read fresh on each request (`current_scoring_prompt_version`), never cached.
`TestTheInstructionsAreOneShippedText` pins `DEFAULT_SCORING_PROMPT` to the file.

##### Candidate app, CORS and identity

| Key | Default | Controls | Form / UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `candidate_app_base_url` | `""` - **and unset is correct on every known environment**, see 4.2a | An OVERRIDE. Unset, the origin is derived from `web.base.url`: the pairing table for prod/stage, `http://localhost:8200` for a local backend, the Odoo host otherwise | no / no |
| `cors_origins` | `""` | Comma-separated origins allowed to send credentialed API calls. Trailing slashes stripped | yes / yes |

The CORS values are cached in module-level globals because the WSGI preflight wrapper runs
before Odoo builds a request. The refresh opens its own `Registry(dbname)` cursor and **returns
silently when `db_name` resolves to more than one database**, so a multi-database deployment
gets no configured origins at all.

A group is cached only if it reaches the model's cache minimum (4,096 tokens on Gemini 3); smaller groups are left out and batched exactly as with the switch off, which is every prod paper today. Only question material is cached - **answers never are**. The individual re-score path never uses it. New in `19.0.3.23.0` | no / no - engineer switch; change it only when no bulk run is going |
| `default_pass_threshold` | unset, unreadable or outside 1-100 = `DEFAULT_PASS_THRESHOLD` = 70 (`assessments.be._default_pass_threshold`) | Seeds a NEW assessment's `pass_threshold` (`assessments.be.default_get`, and the Flutter New Assessment form's pre-fill). Never touches an existing assessment. Odoo Settings reads a bad stored value as 70. Read over the API as `scoring.default_pass_threshold`, written through `/settings/update` (1-100, else 422). If the check itself fails it withholds and logs one WARNING line. Off shows every stored verdict, including the 1,411 on prod written in an admin's voice before candidates could see them - a product decision, never a deploy step. New in `19.0.3.23.0` | no / no |

Both new switches, and `default_pass_threshold`, are read at use time: flipping one needs no deploy and no restart. How to
flip each, and what devops leaves unset, is the switch table in `ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md`
Part 0 §0.5 J. `score_outlier_checks_since` is NOT a switch: the first run of the outlier
recompute cron writes its own start time there, so historical papers are not recomputed. Do
not set or edit it.

##### NOT config parameters - do not add them to this table

Three values are routinely mistaken for settings and are per-RECORD fields (`default_pass_threshold`, above, is a setting, but it only seeds new assessments):

| Value | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `subjective_threshold` | A Float on `assessments.be`, default `DEFAULT_SUBJECTIVE_THRESHOLD` = 70.0 | The per-answer and per-box bar belongs to one assessment, not to the database |
| `pass_threshold` | A Float on `assessments.be` (Q20), seeded from `default_pass_threshold`; 0 / NULL = follows `subjective_threshold`. The evaluator's `pass_threshold` is a computed per-candidate copy of the effective value | The pass bar belongs to one assessment. `write.py` says so in the settings allow-list's own comment |
| `image_label_count` | An Integer on `assessments.be.prompt`, default `DEFAULT_IMAGE_LABEL_COUNT` = 20 | The box cap belongs to the generator that authored the question. See section 2.2 |
| `image_label_live_capture` | A Boolean on `assessments.be.prompt`, default False (19.0.3.24.0) | Live website screenshots are one project's need (High Res Dense), so the generator decides |

The 11 August edition listed `etp_assessment_pro.pass_threshold` as a writable-but-unread key.
**It has been removed entirely** - it is no longer in the write allow-list and no longer exists
anywhere in the addon. There is no `label_threshold` or `image_label_*` config key of any kind.

##### Odoo core keys read by this code

| Key | Read at | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `web.base.url` | `models/assessment.py::_compute_candidate_link`, `models/assessment_api.py`, `models/studio_form.py`, `controllers/api/admin.py` | Portal invitation link base; returned as `base_url` by `/api/v1/settings` |
| `database.secret` | `services/secret_store.py::_fernet` | PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 100 000 iterations, into a Fernet key |

##### Encryption at rest

`secret_store.SECRET_PARAM_KEYS` is now **four** keys, not the two the 11 August edition
recorded: `s3_secret_key`, `vertex_service_account_json`, `vertex_api_key` and
`vertex_access_token`. Ciphertext is prefixed `enc:v1:`; a value without the prefix is treated
as legacy plaintext and passed through unchanged. If `cryptography` is missing or
`database.secret` is blank, `encrypt` **stores plaintext with a warning** rather than failing -
availability is chosen over confidentiality by design, and the module docstring says so.

Because the key is derived from `database.secret`, restoring a dump onto a new database makes
stored secrets undecryptable. `services/vertex.py` detects that case and raises a message
naming it explicitly. This is also why Vertex configuration set locally never carries to stage.

##### Write paths

| Path | Keys it can write |
|---|---|
| Settings -> Assessments BE v2 form | the `config_parameter=` fields rendered by `views/res_config_settings_views.xml` - **38 of the model's 41** at `19.0.3.23.0` (36 of 41 at `19.0.3.22.0`: the release added "Parallel calls" and "Default pass threshold (%)" and removed the scoring-prompt field and its filename). The three not rendered are the SA JSON (it arrives through the Binary upload) and `question_prompt` / `question_prompt_filename`. Uploads are persisted in `set_values()` **before** `super()`, because an `@api.onchange` cursor is rolled back and the write is silently discarded |
| `POST /api/v1/settings/update` | exactly **38** keys (`write.py::SETTINGS`, AST count; 32 at `19.0.3.22.0`, plus `scoring_parallel_calls` and `default_pass_threshold`, then `answers_flush_seconds`, `redis_url` and `cron_lock_mode`, 37 at `19.0.3.27.0`, then `paper_prefetch`) plus **3** write-only secrets (`write.py::SECRETS`: `vertex_api_key`, `vertex_access_token`, `s3_secret_key`). Manager-gated; every value is validated before the first write, so the call applies all or none. `_MAX_SETTING_CHARS = 64 KiB`; an empty string clears an override. Neither switch in "Feature flags" is on the list |
| `GET /api/v1/settings` | read-only projection; credentials are reported as booleans, never echoed. Since `19.0.3.23.0` its `scoring` block adds `default_pass_threshold` (Q20), `parallel_calls` (the stored value, which the panel posts back on Save), `parallel_calls_effective` (what a lane runs after the pool limit) and `resolved_model` - an object from `model_catalog.describe`: `model`, `price_known`, `capabilities_known`, `max_output_tokens`, `cache_min_tokens`, `cache_storage_per_mtok_hour` |
| `tools/vertex_setup.py` | SA JSON, filename, project id, location, minted-token reset, plus the model keys |
| Runtime self-writes | `vertex_minted_token`, `vertex_minted_token_expires`, `vertex_project_id`, `video_supported_durations.<model>`, and since `19.0.3.23.0` `score_outlier_checks_since` (once, on the first outlier-recompute run) |

### 4.2a Nothing has to be configured per environment

**THE WORKFLOW THIS SERVES.** The same tree is pushed and pulled between local,
stage and production and used as it is. A setting that must be typed in per
environment is a setting that will be missing on one of them - and the two this
addon needed both fail SILENTLY:

- a missing client origin emails every candidate a link to port 8069, which is
  Odoo and not the exam runner;
- a missing CORS entry means the request reaches Odoo, Odoo answers 200, and the
  BROWSER discards the response. Clean server log, empty screen, a CORS line
  buried in the console.

Both are now derived from `web.base.url`, which Odoo maintains itself.

| `web.base.url` | client origin | localhost trusted at CORS |
|---|---|---|
| `https://projects.ethara.ai` | `https://assessment.ethara.ai` | no |
| `https://projects-stage.ethara.ai` | `https://assessment-stage.ethara.ai` | no |
| `http://localhost:<any port>`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` | `http://localhost:8200` | **yes** |
| anything else | the Odoo host itself | no |

`services/app_origins.py` owns the derivation: `paired_app_origin` for the two
deployed environments, `local_app_origin` for a developer's machine,
`is_local_backend` for the CORS half. `models/ir_http.py::_refresh_paired_origin`
reads both facts from the same parameter on the same trip, so a preflight and its
request cannot disagree.

**WHY LOCALHOST IS SPLIT ACROSS TWO FUNCTIONS.** The two callers want different
things from it. CORS has to TRUST an origin and a developer serves many ports, so
`ir_http` admits the whole documented `LOCALHOST_ORIGINS` set rather than guessing
one. A LINK has to NAME one origin and there is no "all of them" answer, so
`local_app_origin` returns `http://localhost:8200` - `LOCAL_PORT` in the front-end
repo's Makefile, which is what `make serve-local` binds `build/web-local` to.

**WHY THIS IS NOT A SECURITY HOLE.** Every branch is a statement about which
server this IS, read from a parameter only a database administrator can write.
Nothing in it reads the request's `Origin`. So a deployment on a real hostname
admits nothing extra however it is called - verified over real HTTP against a
`19.0.3.13.0 -> 19.0.3.19.0` upgrade of a production-shaped database with both
parameters deleted: `https://assessment.ethara.ai` allowed, and localhost, the
stage client and an arbitrary origin all refused.

**THE HOST DECIDES, NOT THE PORT.** `is_local_backend` was an enumerated netloc
set that only knew 8069. Odoo writes `web.base.url` from the first request it
serves, so a fresh install on `--http-port=8199` produced `http://localhost:8199`
and read as a DEPLOYED host - no local client origin, no localhost CORS, on a
developer's own machine. A fresh install caught it; reasoning had not. The check
is on the hostname alone now, and `localhost.evil.com` is still not local because
the match is exact rather than a substring.

**THE PARAMETERS REMAIN, AS OVERRIDES**, and still win when set:

- `candidate_app_base_url` - a deployment serving the client from a vanity domain,
  a path, or Odoo's own origin is a topology no table can describe.
- `cors_allow_localhost` - a shared box on a REAL hostname that front-end work
  points a local build at. Its own `web.base.url` is not localhost, so only the
  opt-in can admit it. This is the case the parameter was written for and still
  owns.

Pinned by `tests/test_a_clone_needs_no_configuration.py`, which asserts the chain
per environment, that no environment emails a link to the backend's own origin,
and that a deployed host trusts no localhost with `_dev_mode` patched off.

`19.0.3.23.0` keeps this property: `scoring_parallel_calls`, `default_pass_threshold` (70)
and the two new switches all default in code, and the deploy note sets none of them (`ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 0
§0.5 I3 and J).

**The gap worth knowing about:** `cors_origins` and `cors_allow_localhost` are writable in the
Odoo form but NOT over the API, and the one prompt override left, `question_prompt`, is
writable over neither - the model carries the field, `views/res_config_settings_views.xml`
renders no upload widget for it, and `write.py::SETTINGS` omits it. Today the only ways in are
`psql` or an Odoo shell. The view's own header comment records that the model carried 41
fields while the file rendered 9, and that the blocks were added to close the gap; the
prompt-upload set was not included. (The scoring-prompt half of this gap closed in
`19.0.3.23.0` by removing the override, not by rendering it.)

##### Why there are no seeded defaults

The retired `data/llm_config_parameters.xml` was removed upstream because `noupdate="1"` rows
**shadow** the code default: `get_param(key, default)` returns the row, so bumping
`GENERATION_DEFAULT_MODEL` in `constants.py` reached no existing deployment. The consequence
for anyone adding a setting: **do not add `default=` to a `config_parameter` field** - the
first Settings save would persist it and recreate the freeze. Several existing fields do carry
`default=` (`vertex_location`, `vertex_model`, `video_model`, `video_location`,
`video_default_duration_s`, `s3_region`, `s3_folder`, `s3_max_retries` and the numeric knobs,
`scoring_parallel_calls` and `default_pass_threshold` included - the first Odoo Settings save
stores 70 for the latter),
which contradicts that guidance and is worth resolving before the next model default moves.

##### `ethara-etp/scripts/`

**Re-checked 24 September 2026: one file.** `scripts/` holds only `build_tron_instances.py`.
`scripts/run_tests.sh` is gone from the checkout, and `git log` has no record of it, so it was
a local, untracked file. The text about it below is kept as a record. The addon's suite is run
by hand, from the repo root, against a throwaway copy of a database (never `etp_local`):

```
env -u PYTHONPATH .venv/bin/python src/odoo-bin -c <conf> -d <throwaway copy> \
  -u assessments_be_v2 --test-enable --test-tags /assessments_be_v2 \
  --stop-after-init --log-level=test
```

The only passing verdict is `0 failed, 0 error(s) of T tests` with T > 0. How to make the copy
and blank its mail and cloud keys is `ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 5 §5.1.

**`scripts/run_tests.sh`** (as of 11 August) - the canonical verify command; `agent/coding_context.py detect_project_facts` auto-detects it. File mode is `0711` (`-rwx--x--x`), which is unusual - not group/world readable.

> **It does not run this addon.** `MODULE="etp_assessment_pro"` is hardcoded, the final command
> passes `-u etp_assessment_pro`, and every tag it builds is `/etp_assessment_pro:...`. So the
> repo's canonical runner exercises the module being DECOMMISSIONED and skips
> `assessments_be_v2`'s 167 test files and 1,869 tests entirely. Nothing else in `scripts/` runs them.
> Until the runner is updated, run them by hand:
>
> ```
> unset PYTHONPATH; LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 .venv/bin/python src/odoo-bin -c odoo.conf \
>   -d etp_ux_test -u assessments_be_v2 --http-port=8071 \
>   --test-enable --test-tags /assessments_be_v2 --stop-after-init --log-level=test
> ```
>
> This is the single highest-value fix in the repo's tooling: a green run of `run_tests.sh`
> currently says nothing at all about the addon that is being shipped.

```
scripts/run_tests.sh                          # whole etp_assessment_pro suite
scripts/run_tests.sh TestGeneratorChatterLog  # one class  -> --test-tags /etp_assessment_pro:TestGeneratorChatterLog
scripts/run_tests.sh :TestAssessmentFeatureBatch   # passed through
scripts/run_tests.sh /some_tag                     # passed through
```

Environment: `ETP_TEST_DB` (default `etp_ux_test`), `ETP_PG_PORT` (default `5433`), `ETP_TEST_HTTP_PORT` (default `8071`, chosen so the suite can run alongside a dev server on 8069, `:27-30`).

Three environment fixes, each documented inline: `unset PYTHONPATH` so a leaked venv does not shadow the project's (`:46-49`); `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` because macOS `postgresql@16` aborts with "postmaster became multithreaded during startup" otherwise (`:51-53`); `OPENSSL_CONF=$REPO_ROOT/openssl-legacy.cnf` for the Vertex TLS handshake path (`:65-67`). It starts Postgres via `pg_ctl -D /opt/homebrew/var/postgresql@16 -o "-p 5433"` if nothing is listening (`:57-61`). Final command:

```
.venv/bin/python src/odoo-bin -c odoo.conf -d "$DB" -u etp_assessment_pro \
  --http-port=8071 --test-enable --test-tags "$TAGS" --stop-after-init --log-level=test
```

Note the `-u etp_assessment_pro` - it upgrades and tests only that module, **never**
`assessments_be_v2`. See the banner above.

**`scripts/build_tron_instances.py`** - unrelated to assessments. Walks a directory of UUID-named harbor task folders, parses `task.toml` + `tests/verifiers.jsonl` + `environment/seeds/*.sql`, and writes a JSON array for the `/tron` dataset viewer.

```
python3 scripts/build_tron_instances.py --src <task-dir> --out <json-path>
```

Defaults: `--src /Users/apple/Downloads/final_30_harbor` (`:16`) - a different person's home directory that will not exist on this machine, so the script exits 2 unless `--src` is given. `--out` defaults to `custom_addons/tron_dashboard/data/tron_instances.json`.

| `tool/capture_payloads.py` (0644) | Captures live API responses into `test/assessment/payloads/*.json` as fixtures for `live_payload_test.dart`. Redacts `access_token`, `token`, `candidate_link`, `email`, `email_from`, `login` recursively (`:48-50`, `:82-89`). Picks a generator that has a resource and the roster with the most attempts, because a blindly-picked empty fixture makes the suite green while checking nothing (`:116-143`) | `python3 tool/capture_payloads.py [base_url]` or `make fixtures` | Env: `ETP_API`, `ETP_ADMIN_LOGIN`/`_PASSWORD`, `ETP_CANDIDATE_LOGIN`/`_PASSWORD`. Captures 7 list routes + settings + the Form Studio import template + generator detail + draft detail + bank detail + candidates + candidate list |
| `tool/corsprobe/` (`run.sh` 0755, 136 lines of Dart) | **The one part of the media fix the suite cannot cover.** `run.sh` serves a 4x4 red PNG with NO `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, builds two release web probes, drives them under headless Chromium and prints their verdicts. `cors_probe.dart` (77 lines) measures `WebHtmlElementStrategy.never` against `.fallback`; `hdr_probe.dart` (59 lines) measures an empty `headers` map against a non-empty one. Both report through `document.title`, not through the DOM - a CanvasKit frame is pixels in a canvas and the `<img>` fallback is a platform view, so neither is findable by a selector | `bash tool/corsprobe/run.sh` | Expects `never=FAIL fallback=OK` and `noHeaders=OK withHeaders=FAIL`. Chromium comes from `../ethara-etp/.venv` (where `services/dom_capture` already uses Playwright); override with `PLAYWRIGHT_PYTHON`. Not in the Makefile and not in `verify.sh` |

`tool/verify.sh` step by step:

| # | Check | Real gate? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `dart analyze lib/ test/`, counts lines matching `^ +error` | Yes, but counts only `error` severity - warnings and infos pass |
| 2 | `flutter test` (VM), greps `All tests passed` in the **last line only** (`tail -1`) | Yes, though a suite that crashes before printing that line is reported as "vm suite red" |
| 3 | `flutter test --platform chrome` | Yes. Rationale at `:36-38`: on JS there is one numeric type, so `0.0 is int` is true on web and false on VM, which once truncated every currency value while VM stayed green |
| 4 | Greps `examTokenFrom(Uri.base)` in `lib/main.dart` and `loadExamByToken` in the exam screen | Yes, but it is a text grep - it proves the strings exist, not that the flow works |
| 5 | No references to the host portal (`workflow_management_app_v2`, `api_client.dart' as host`) | Yes |
| 6 | `flutter build web --release --pwa-strategy=none` with both dart-defines, then greps the URL out of `build/web/main.dart.js` and asserts `serviceWorkerVersion: "` is **absent** from `flutter_bootstrap.js` | Yes. Skipped by `--quick`. The comment at `:66-70` records that this fallback used to say `ethara_ops`, baking the wrong DB into the bundle silently |
| 7 | Live: mints an admin token, probes 9 operator routes for `ok: true`; then, if `ETP_CANDIDATE_PASSWORD` is set, probes 5 of them with a candidate token expecting `ok: false` | Yes when a backend answers; **SKIP** (not FAIL) when it does not (`:93-95`), and the candidate boundary is silently skipped when `ETP_CANDIDATE_PASSWORD` is unset (`:109-117`) |

#### 6. CI

`ethara-assessment-fe` has **no `.github/` directory at all**. Nothing in CI runs `dart analyze`, `flutter test`, or `tool/verify.sh`. The front end is verified only by hand.

`ethara-etp/.github/workflows/` contains exactly one file: `security-scan.yaml`, job `security-scan`, on the self-hosted runner label `ethara-runners` (ARM64 EKS + DinD per the header comment).

**Re-read 24 September 2026. The workflow now targets PRODUCTION, from `main`** - it used to
build a stage image from `stage`. The release does not change the file; the triggers, image
and gitops target below are the current ones, and line numbers are re-read from it.

##### Triggers

- `workflow_dispatch` with one input, `deploy_to_production` (choice `true`/`false`, **default `'true'`**, `:21-24`, described as "Deploy to production after successful build").
- `push` to branch `main` (`:29-31`).

Job-level guard (`:40-42`):

```
github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
(github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'prod:'))
```

So **a push to `main` whose head commit message does not start with `prod:` runs nothing at
all**, and one that does builds and deploys to prod straight away. The local checkout is on
`main`; its HEAD message does not start with `prod:`. This is why the `19.0.3.23.0` deploy note
forbids a `prod:` message and builds by manual dispatch with `deploy_to_production=false`
instead: nothing in the pipeline runs `-u assessments_be_v2`, and the image CMD does not
either (4.2 #2), so a `prod:` push would put new code on the old schema
(`ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 0 §0.5 F; once this release is on `main`, anyone's later
`prod:` commit ships it the same way). The 11 August edition described a `stage` branch and a
`stage:` prefix; neither applies now.

`permissions:` declares `pull-requests: write` (`:35`), but no step touches a pull request.

`env.PATH` is set at job level (`:45-46`) to a fixed seven-entry list, replacing whatever the runner image had.

##### Steps, and which are real gates

GitHub runs each `run:` block with `bash -e`, so an unguarded non-zero exit fails the step and the job.

| # | Step | Where | Can it fail the build? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Checkout Code (`actions/checkout@v4`, depth 1, no submodules) | 49 | **Yes** |
| 2 | Setup Tools (`apt-get install`, download + install AWS CLI v2) | 55 | **Yes** - unguarded |
| 3 | Configure AWS Credentials (`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6`, OIDC into `arn:aws:iam::426628337772:role/GitHubActionsRole`, `ap-south-1`) | 65 | **Yes** |
| 4 | Install Bandit | 71 | **Yes** |
| 5 | Run Bandit | 74 | **No - `\|\| true` (`:75`).** Findings are written to `bandit-report.json` and reported; a HIGH-severity finding does not block anything |
| 6 | Install Trivy | 77 | **Yes** |
| 7 | Run Trivy Dockerfile Scan | 84 | **No - `\|\| true` (`:87`).** Also writes `[]` and skips if no `Dockerfile` (one exists at repo root) |
| 8 | Install Hadolint | 93 | **Yes** - `exit 1` on an unrecognised `uname -m` (`:99`) |
| 9 | Run Hadolint Scan | 105 | **No - `\|\| true` (`:109`).** Sets output `hadolint_issues`, which **nothing in the file ever reads** - a dead output |
| 10 | Run Pytest | 124 | **No, twice over.** The repo has **no root `tests/` directory**, so `:127-131` sets `tests_passed=true` and `exit 0`. Even with one, `set +e` captures the exit code and only converts it to an output (`:135-146`); the step itself always succeeds |
| 11 | Docker Build and Push | 148 | **Yes - the only real code gate.** `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --push` to `426628337772.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/ethara-prod-backend:<github.sha>` (`:161`; it was `ethara-etp-stage-backend` on 11 August). Guarded by `steps.run_tests.outputs.tests_passed == 'true'`, which is unconditionally true today. Exits 0 without building if no `Dockerfile` (`:152-155`) - and `docker_build.outcome` would then still be `success`, so the deploy step downstream would fire on a build that never happened |
| 12 | Update Image Tag in Target Repository | 187 | **Yes.** `actions/github-script@v7` with `secrets.TARGET_PAT`, rewriting `tag:` in `Ethara-Ai/gitops-prod` → **`etp-odoo-backend/values.yaml`** (`:195-197`; it was `stg-etp-odoo-backend` on 11 August) to `github.sha`. `process.exit(1)` on 404, 403 and any other error (`:228`, `:232`, `:310`). Condition (`:188-191`): `docker_build.outcome == 'success' && ((dispatch && deploy_to_production == 'true') \|\| push)` - so a dispatch left at its default `'true'` also rewrites the prod tag. Returns cleanly if the tag already matches |
| 13 | Format Reports | 313 | `if: always()`. jq calls are guarded with `2>/dev/null \|\| echo "0"`, but `TOTAL_ISSUES=$((...))` at `:323` will fail under `bash -e` if any count is non-numeric or multiline. Low risk, not a code-quality gate |
| 14 | Upload Reports to S3 | 519 | `if: always()`. **`aws s3 cp` at `:530` is unguarded, so it can fail the build** - on AWS credentials or bucket permissions, never on code quality |

The 11 August edition's step 12, "Cleanup Untagged ECR Images", is no longer in the file.

##### What this means in practice

- **No test of any kind gates this pipeline.** Neither the addon's Odoo suite (2,413 tests at `19.0.3.23.0`, run by hand only - see 4.2 #4) nor `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/tools/verify.sh` or `contract_audit.py` is invoked. The pytest step is a no-op because there is no root `tests/` folder, and would still be a no-op if there were.
- **All three security scanners are advisory.** Bandit, Trivy and Hadolint all end in `|| true`. The generated report even prints "**Every issue is a risk. Fix before you MERGE!**" (`:377`) - nothing enforces it.
- **The only things that can fail the build** are: infrastructure setup, AWS auth, the Docker build/push itself, the gitops tag rewrite, and the S3 report upload.
- **Nothing in it upgrades a module.** It builds an image and moves the prod tag; the schema upgrade is a separate, manual job (4.2 #2).
- Reports land at `s3://ethara-production-security-reports/security-reports/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/<sha>-report.md` (`:340-341`, `:527-530`).
- Cosmetic contradiction: the report says `DOCKER_MESSAGE="Docker push to ethara-cicd-app-registry"` (`:345`) while the push actually targets `ethara-prod-backend` (`:161`).
- The 11 August edition's closing point - the `deploy_to_production` input described as "Deploy to staging", with no production path in the workflow - is **no longer true**: the input now says "Deploy to production after successful build", and the target is prod's `etp-odoo-backend` values file.

## 5.0a The `19.0.3.24.0` release (30 September 2026)

From the owner's end-to-end production test of 29 September and the fixes that followed.
The reasoning behind each item is in `ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` §6.8. Version: bump
`19.0.3.23.0` to `19.0.3.24.0` at push; no migration script.

| Repo | State (30 Sep) | Change vs git HEAD (prod) |
|---|---|---|
| `ethara-etp` | staged, not committed | 35 tracked files + 18 new, all in `assessments_be_v2` except `src/requirements.txt` (Pillow `10.2.0` to `10.4.0`); 28 test files |
| `ethara-assessment-fe` | staged, not committed | 47 files: 29 under `lib/`, 18 under `test/` |

**Schema:** 6 new nullable columns, all on `assessments_be_prompt`: `sop_gen_started_at`,
`sop_gen_finished_at`, `tag_extract_reply`, `tag_extract_cancel_requested`,
`template_draft_cancelled_at`, `image_label_live_capture`. Nothing removed.

**Rows rewritten on `-u`:** `assessments.be.prompt.resource.init()` renames category `golden`
to `sample`; a post-init pass (`question._repair_generated_text` →
`vertex.repair_generated_question_text`) repairs generated text that disagrees with its key
and logs each id as "generated-text repair".

**Routes: 127 → 133.** New: `/generators/<id>/progress`, `/generators/<id>/retry_failed_images`,
`/generators/<id>/cancel_tag_extract`, `/drafts/<id>/retry_images`,
`/task_templates/cancel_draft`, and the public `/auth/password_policy`.

**What changed**
- **Image labelling.** Pictures are AI-made by default; a live website is screenshotted only
  for a generator with "Screenshot live websites" on (`image_label_live_capture`), and a failed
  or unusable capture (fewer than 3 controls: `dom_capture.unusable_reason`) falls back to the
  AI picture with a draft warning. Every question has ONE box list - the generator's named boxes
  placed on the picture by one vision call (`vertex.locate_label_elements`), or vision's own
  detections when that fails or finds fewer than half - and the drawn boxes, `behavioural_key_json`,
  `label_boxes_json`, rubric `ideal_labels` and golden `solution_json` are all written from it
  (`prompt._apply_label_list`). One overlay on every screen (`services/labelling.label_overlay`,
  `draft_label_overlay`). Approval carries a website URL only when the approved picture is the capture.
- **Generation.** Live run stats with Retry failed images; golden files are sample files (one
  list); generated text never points at the SOP (`_SELF_CONTAINED_RULE`, then one rewrite call,
  `vertex._rewrite_source_references`; options and correct answers are never rewritten); renamed
  `image_ab` ratings keep their construction keys; side-free comparisons are described as Left/Right;
  runs stuck in `finalizing` settle after 15 minutes.
- **Kill switches.** Extract skills (`action_cancel_tag_extract`: the reply of the call in flight
  is not applied) and Draft from SOP (`template_draft_cancelled_at`: no further call, the request
  answers 409 `cancelled`).
- **Candidates.** Invitation email without the pass mark or the proctoring paragraph; no pass mark
  on the start screen; no hint text in any answer box; blank rubric ratings hold the answer as a
  draft; the released answer sheet shows the same numbered picture as the exam.
- **Admin.** The paper's count follows the ticked questions; every page has a URL that survives a
  reload; password rules are published and shown as a checklist.
- **Operations.** Chromium starts under Odoo's prefork memory cap (`dom_capture`); transient DB
  errors are retried in the render, tag, detect and invite crons; zero-token calls are not priced.

**Deploy order.** Before `-u`, every generator read fails (six missing columns) and grading
reads the generator. So: DB snapshot → run `-u assessments_be_v2 --stop-after-init` from the new
image BEFORE rolling the pods (the old code ignores the new nullable columns) → roll the pods →
deploy the app (it calls the new routes) → turn on "Screenshot live websites" for High Res Dense.

**Verified on the shipped tree:** upgrade rehearsal from prod code (exactly the six columns);
Chromium under the memory cap in a `python:3.12-slim-bookworm` container; a real-model candidate
journey (answer, submit, grade, release, answer sheet); backend, Flutter VM and Chrome suites (counts
in 1.8 and 3.10).

The full record - every item id, the owner's decisions Q1-Q20, the test that pins each fix,
what was deliberately left out, the deploy and the rollback - is `ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md`

| `ethara-assessment-fe` | `main` | fully staged, not committed. HEAD is prod's app `48e8434` | **81 files, ~+8.2k / -0.7k**: 35 under `lib/`, 46 under `test/` |

Approximate on purpose, as in 5.1: the docs are part of the diff.

**Schema, from the manifest note** (counted against `19.0.3.22.0`; no migration script, no
business row rewritten, no stored field recomputed on every row): 8 new nullable columns
(`assessments_be.score_outlier_checked_at`, `.scoring_last_scored`,
`.scoring_last_candidates`, `.scoring_last_finished_at`, `.pass_threshold` (Q20);
`assessments_be_response.rescore_request_key` with a partial index;
`assessments_be_prompt.upload_golden_filename`; `assessments_be_llm_usage.cached_tokens`), 11 on
transient tables (Q20's `res_config_settings.assessments_be_default_pass_threshold` included),
1 new system parameter (`default_pass_threshold`), 2 new tables (`assessments_be_scoring_cache`, the transient
`assessments_be_release_wizard`), 3 transient `res_config_settings` columns dropped. `.23.0`
was never released; this bump carries it. The manifest note itself predates Q20 and still
says 7 and 10.

**What ships, by area** (row numbers are §0.4's):

- **Grading lanes.** A lane never writes the shared paper row, rolls back after a
  SerializationFailure, and keeps its Vertex bearer on its own short cursor (rows 1-3). A 429,
  a spend cap or a refused DB connection defers the answer without spending an attempt, with
  the reason shown (row 4). Up to `scoring_parallel_calls` (4) judge calls per lane, lowered
  to fit `db_maxconn`; a lane re-runs at once only after a full tick that stored a mark (rows
  5-6). Paid grading skips cancelled papers and erased attempts (row 29).
- **The grading request.** Text only - no media is sent - and trimmed to what scoring needs;
  the rules follow the question type; a labelling answer tells the grader whether the
  candidate saw numbered markers (rows 8-12). New instructions `bundled:785826a5`; the stored
  override is gone (row 14). A cut-off reply gets a 16k output floor, a doubled retry and a
  split re-grade (row 15). Question-group caching ships ON as `groups`, answers never cached
  (row 16). Model catalog and output clamp, with no model change; temperature stays 0.2 (row
  18).
- **Re-score, Kill, Release.** Per-answer re-score is a key per click, graded first and alone;
  the old mark is replaced only on success (row 25). While a Kill is stopping, every action
  that queues grading gets 409 `stopping` and both UIs disable the buttons; Kill sees the
  candidate a lane holds and reports `held_count` (row 30). Release skips candidates being
  graded and reports `released_count` / `skipped_count`; unreadable ids get 422, never "release
  everyone" (rows 31, 66). Every Odoo Release button now confirms first (the assessment-level one with counts), and
  re-scoring a released result asks first in both UIs and gets 409 from the API without
  `confirm` (rows 27, 32).
- **Candidates.** The grader's verdict on a released answer, only when written under the
  current instructions (row 50). On time-up: "Time's up - your answers are saved", "Ended on
  the clock", time used out of the limit, and no toast blaming proctoring (row 53). A
  timed-out question reads "Not answered", not "Incorrect" (row 51). India dates, a phone
  drawer under 720 px, and sign-in fixes: en-GB browsers, one token refresh for many calls,
  the server's real refusal reason (rows 49, 60-63).
- **Admin screens, Odoo and Flutter.** Scored / Score Pending chips and a "Scored N/M on date
  IST" tally (rows 20, 33); "Same questions for everybody" retired and the question count
  locked after launch (rows 34-35); imports placed where the app has them (rows 36-37); Form
  Studio forms read-only in Odoo and "Published" (row 38); Question Templates on the
  generator in Odoo and a "Model decides" badge (rows 40, 43); Odoo "Draft from SOP" hidden
  (row 41); an Odoo "Today" budget section, and Flutter Budget cards on lifetime totals rather
  than the last 1,000 calls (row 21, Q18); the Emails tab as one paged call (row 47); the
  invitation email rewritten, sent from `no-reply@ethara.ai` with the paper's creator in
  reply-to (row 52).
- **Pass threshold (Q20, row 79).** A per-assessment Pass threshold decides the attempt's
  Pass/Fail; the Subjective threshold decides each answer and box. Editable in the Odoo form
  and the Flutter Config tab, seeded on new assessments from the Settings default
  (`default_pass_threshold`, 70 unless changed). Not set = follows the subjective threshold;
  existing assessments were left unset. The payloads and the invitation's "Pass mark" carry
  the effective value. Follow-ups: both New Assessment forms pre-fill the Settings default
  and the Flutter one sends it; 1-100 is enforced on create and write, API and model, 0
  included; the Flutter threshold fields save on Enter or on leaving the field; the Odoo form
  says "Not set - uses the subjective threshold: N%" on a not-set paper.
- **Round 3 (24 Sep; the owner's A-E list plus A-074, A-133, A-092; same version, no
  migration, no new column).** Our regressions: a native bank export restores only through
  its own button; erasing or cancelling never strands `llm_state = scoring`; the org-wide
  errored sweep skips cancelled papers; a non-number `pass_threshold` is 422. Exam integrity:
  a 10 s answer grace after the deadline, time-up is never a proctoring event, `server_now`
  beside every `deadline`, one submit per sitting, resume shows the saved answer, an unknown
  question type is "not supported". Security: `/emails` and cancel see assessment mail only,
  Reset to Draft asks before erasing released results, every upload is sized before it is
  decoded, typed-in and CSV candidates need a real address, the app's dead fail-open sign-in
  code is gone. Cost: an unchanged A/B re-post is not re-graded, and no attempt is spent
  without an LLM call. Admin: Cancel hidden on Done papers and lifecycle buttons roll back on
  a refusal, per-candidate question counts, three interpolation fixes, the written answer in
  the Responses list, a leaderboard row opens My Performance, Delete on every generator row.
  Proctoring follows the owner's final rule (25 Sep): only Auto-submit ends the paper at the
  limit; Log only never ends it, even at the limit; in both modes a reached limit is labelled
  "Violation Limit Breached" for the admin and the candidate. New papers start at Log only
  with a limit of 5; the Odoo field reads "Violation Limit". The invitation's rule line changes with it
  (`mail_template.xml` is `noupdate="0"`, so `-u` updates it). Record:

- **Tools.** 4.2 #4: `deploy_gate.py` fixed, calibration tools and
  `profile_mismatch_report.py` added, `check_scoring_prompt.py` deleted.

After the final violation rule (25 Sep, so far): Odoo 0 failed of 2,446, Flutter 2,041 passed, `flutter analyze` clean; the final line is in the round 3 bullet at the top of this file (plans file, Round 3 addendum).
