## 5.2 The scoring rewrite, change by change

This is the substance of the cycle. Section 2.1 #4 and section 2.2 §3 document the result; this
is the list of what moved.

| # | Change | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The unit of scoring became the COMPONENT | `models/question.py::_component_counts`, `_keyed_dimension_count` | A candidate who got two of three sub-questions right scored the same as one who got none. The paper could not tell a near-miss from a blank |
| 2 | `_dimension_marks` replaced all-or-nothing across a question | `models/assessment.py` | All-or-nothing now survives WITHIN one sub-question and nowhere else. One missing or one extra option scores THAT dimension 0; its siblings are untouched |
| 3 | A keyless dimension counts in neither numerator nor denominator | `_keyed_dimension_count` | Counting it marked every candidate wrong on a sub-question nothing could satisfy - an authoring fault reported as a candidate failure |
| 4 | The `image_ab` blend, its two weight constants, the helper that applied it and the 60-point overall-wrong cap were all deleted | `services/scoring.py`, `constants.py` | The blend was applied TWICE, giving an effective 93.75/6.25 nobody intended, and a perfect set of verdicts started the raw at 75 before a word was read |
| 5 | Objective components lost their raw, on both sides of the fraction | `_compute_final_marks`, `_compute_raw_result` | An objective raw only restated the mark beside it, and leaving it in the denominator made the raw read lower the more multiple-choice a paper contained |
| 6 | `_compute_score` was brought into the same currency as `final_mark` | `models/assessment.py` | The two disagreed the day the unit changed, and the candidate review reads `score`/`max_score` for its Correct/Incorrect label - so it called a 2-of-3 answer "Incorrect" |
| 7 | Image labelling moved to per-box scoring | `services/scoring.py::_apply_image_label_boxes`, `response._label_marks` | The coverage ceiling was a proxy for "you cannot score on boxes you never addressed"; scoring those boxes 0 says it exactly, and closes the advisory-only gap where the ceiling never actually applied |
| 8 | The scoring prompt became version-checked | `services/scoring.py::_get_scoring_prompt` | A stored prompt predating the `box_scores` contract would have scored EVERY labelling answer 0 with clean logs |
| 9 | The box cap became per-generator and is enforced on every lane | `prompt.image_label_count`, `question_image._label_box_cap`, `services/labelling.py`, the `assessments.be.question.image` create/write backstop | The render path must never offer more "Label N" inputs than the authoring path was allowed to draw boxes for, or a candidate answers a box that was never on the image and is graded on it |
| 10 | `score_marks_display` became two integers again | `_compute_score_marks_display` | It printed `"4.25 / 10"`, which the Flutter client parses with `int.tryParse`: it read null, dropped the server's total and re-derived the score locally |
| 11 | The eighth question type was retired | `constants.QUESTION_TYPE_SELECTION` + the pre-migration | Odoo does not rewrite stored rows when a `Selection` shrinks, so the migration is what stops an invisible row falling silently through every lane |
| 12 | `require_justification_image_comparison` was removed | `models/assessment.py`, `write.py` allow-lists | An operator could switch `image_ab` to verdict-only, which never reached the LLM while `needs_llm` stayed true - so the awaiting-scoring counters kept counting answers the grader had short-circuited |
| 13 | The generator's rating-scheme summary field was removed | model, serialiser, view, Flutter | |

## 5.3 What changed in the Flutter client

The client is **caught up with the server**, verified field by field on 25 August. Specifically:

- `QType` is seven values and its header comment says so; `question_types_test.dart` pins the
  enum against the module's real `constants.py` - and **the path it searches moved with the
  fork**, to `custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/constants.py`, the copy that gets pushed.
- `Response` gained `finalMark`, `finalMax`, `mcqMark`, `objectiveMarksMax`, `rawScore` and
  `rawMax`. `Response.mark` prefers the server's `final_mark` and falls back to the old
  two-half reading only when the field is absent; `Response.markOutOf` treats a `final_max` of
  0 as "not stated" rather than as zero marks.
- `Attempt.maxMarks` falls back to summing `Question.componentCount` - keyed dimensions plus
  one if subjective, floored at 1 - where it used to fall back to `totalQuestions`.
- `AnswerSheetRow` gained `marksEarned` (parsed only when `released`) and `marksAvailable`
  (parsed ungated, **defaulting to 1, never 0**, because it is a divisor). Both feed the
  candidate category breakdown in `category_scores.dart`.
- `answer_layouts.dart` switches on seven types with no `default` arm.
- `response_detail_screen.dart` renders per-component meters and documents the blend as gone.
  The `weight 0.60` / `weight 0.25` notes that remain are the generic subjective rubric lanes,
  not the blend.
- `my_assessments_screen.dart` prefers the server's `score_marks` and keeps the QUESTION count
  separate, with a comment saying the mark total and the question count "have parted company".
- Nothing in `lib/` or `test/` mentions the retired type, the removed raw columns, the coverage
  ceiling or the rating-scheme summary, in either snake_case or camelCase.

Note the client reads scoring keys through `jget(j, camelKey)`, which tries camelCase then
lowers each capital to `_x`. A plain snake_case grep over `lib/` therefore finds only comments;
grep the camelCase spelling.

**Both suites were run for this edition** (`19.0.3.22.0`). The result, kept as history - the
`19.0.3.23.0` gate is in 5.0 (Odoo 2,413, Flutter 1,997; Chrome not run):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Odoo, this addon (`etp_validate`, module `19.0.3.22.0`) | **1,869 tests, 0 failed, 0 errors** (18 Sep 2026) |
| Flutter, VM (`flutter test`) | **1,826 pass**, 0 failed (18 Sep 2026) |
| `tools/verify.sh --quick` | **PASS 7, FAIL 0, SKIP 1** |
| Flutter, Chrome (`flutter test --platform chrome`) | **1,276 pass**, 0 failed (18 Sep 2026). Five consecutive runs, zero harness connection drops; the last three identical at 1,276. Quote it. |
| `flutter analyze` | "No issues found!" |

**CORRECTED 18 Sep 2026. The paragraph that stood here said Chrome was "not a gate" and named
three structurally-failing files. Both halves were stale, and it was re-checked against the tree
rather than re-asserted.**

Of the three files it blamed, only `conditional_imports_resolve_test.dart` imports `dart:io`, and
it now carries `@TestOn('vm')` - so Chrome never loads it. `generator_date_is_created_test.dart`
and `raw_is_a_decimal_test.dart` import no `dart:io` at all; the `Directory.listSync` premise does
not apply to either. 74 of the 207 `*_test.dart` files are `@TestOn('vm')`, which is why the VM
count (1,826) and the Chrome count (1,276) differ by roughly 550 - that gap is deliberate
platform gating, not failures.

The flakiness claim did not reproduce either. Five Chrome runs on this tree, grepped for
`Connection closed` and `Failed to load`: **zero occurrences in all five**. Results were
`+1213 -4`, then `+1265`, `+1276`, `+1276`, `+1276`. The four failures in the first run were REAL
assertion failures in `the_marker_editor_is_offered_only_where_it_works_test.dart` - a harness
defect in the test itself, since fixed - not connection drops. The last three runs are identical
to the test, which is reproducibility. Three of the five ran under load average 18 on 10 cores
with a concurrent Odoo suite - harsher than the load the retired note blamed. Nobody has proven
the drop cannot happen on a different machine or Flutter version; it did not happen in five
attempts under worse load than that note described.

So `make test` (`Makefile:85-90`, the FE repo's) running the Chrome platform is correct behaviour,
not a trap, and Chrome IS a gate. The lesson worth keeping is the one this correction illustrates:
a "known-broken, do not trust" note in a knowledge base outlives the breakage and then quietly
suppresses a real signal. Re-check them before repeating them.

`scripts/run_tests.sh` no longer hardcodes the addon: `MODULE="${ETP_TEST_MODULE:-etp_assessment_pro}"`
(`:34`), so `ETP_TEST_MODULE=assessments_be_v2 scripts/run_tests.sh` runs this suite, and the
script's own comment at `:23-32` says why the default has not moved. *(outdated: the script is
no longer in the checkout; the suite is run by hand, 4.2 #4.)* What remains true is that
**no test of any kind gates CI** - the security-scan workflow's pytest step short-circuits on a
missing root `tests/` and reports green having run nothing. See 4.2.


# Part 6 - Honest status: verified, unverified, and not done

## 6.1 The one thing to read

**Nobody has driven this UI in a browser.** Everything in Parts 1-4 is established by reading
code and by exercising the API and the test suites. The generator screen was rebuilt on the
last day of the cycle and confirmed at route level only.

*(changed in 19.0.3.23.0: that release WAS driven in a real browser. A Playwright
deploy-order matrix walked all four app/backend combinations, with writes, on local copies;
the Odoo status badge's failure to start polling was reproduced and its fix confirmed in a
browser (S15); the Candidates-tab Release dialog was checked by hand, old code against new
(FU5, FU12). `ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 0 §0.1, §0.2. The paragraphs below describe the
2 September cycle.)*

**One narrow exception, added 2 September 2026.** `tool/corsprobe/run.sh` drives a release web
build under headless Chromium and measures ONE thing: whether a cross-origin image renders. It is
not a UI walkthrough - it reports through `document.title` because a CanvasKit frame is pixels in
a canvas - but it is a real browser executing real Flutter, and the media fix rests on it. See
3.10. Everything else in this section stands.

A demo was run during this cycle and it went badly. Three causes, all real:

1. Two defects made the generator screen look broken - see 6.4, items *Generator screen lost
   its own data* and *Bank questions opened the wrong record*. Both were client-side; the
   server had been storing correctly throughout.
2. The app was started against `etp_ux_test`, which has no `cors_allow_localhost` parameter,
   so the browser blocked every call and the app showed "Failed to fetch". The working
   database is `etp_local`. A run command was also given that served the repo root rather
   than `build/web`, which yields a directory listing.
3. The work had been reported as verified on the strength of API and test-suite results. That
   was not the same thing as verifying the product, and the difference is what the demo
   exposed.

That is why this document separates *how* each claim was established rather than presenting
one confidence level for everything.

## 6.4 Defects found and fixed in this cycle

**The three tables below are the SCORING cycle's** (`19.0.3.11.0` and earlier) and are kept
because nothing supersedes them. The 2 September cycle's are listed before them, under their
own heading; Part 5 describes them in full. The `19.0.3.23.0` release's come first, and only the
ones prod users were hitting; every fix, its ids and its test are `ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md`
Part 0 §0.2.

Grouped by whether a user would have seen anything. Evidence markers: **live** = reproduced
against a running system, **unit** = pinned by a test, **traced** = code path read but not
reproduced.

### Fixed in `19.0.3.23.0` (24 September 2026) - defects live on prod

| Defect | Effect | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Grading calls thrown away by collisions | Every lane wrote the one paper row they all share, so concurrent lanes hit serialization failures and one failure cascaded through the rest of the tick. **73% of prod grading calls** (3,800 of 5,178, $190.77) were paid for and discarded (B1-01, B1-03) | live (prod data) + unit |
| Kill did not stop a lane already grading | $2.76 was spent after the paper #44 kill. Kill now sees the candidate a lane holds and settles it at its next call (B2-02, G6-30) | live + unit |
| en-GB browsers were signed out on every call | Prod has only `en_US` installed. A bearer request takes its session language from `Accept-Language` unchecked, `en-GB` raised "Invalid language code" inside `_adopt_gateway_token`, the request stayed anonymous, and every call answered 401 "session expired" - `/auth/me` included, hence "no assessment role". In bursts after each pod restart. The adopter now swaps an uninstalled language for an installed one first (B5-01, G4-04) | live |
| The Flutter Budget cards under-reported spend | They summed the last 1,000 ledger rows: $63.28 shown against $285.67 real (F2-01) | live (prod data) + unit |
| A question the clock took away read "Incorrect" | The auto-submit placeholder was graded as an answer; 27 prod rows. It now reads "Not answered" (G2-07) | live + unit |
| The time-up toast blamed proctoring | Almost every time-out showed a "violation threshold" message; the answers had been saved all along (G2-04). Now "Time's up - your answers are saved" on every path | unit |
| The pass threshold could not be edited | Reported 2026-09-17 ("I am unable to edit Pass Threshold in UI"). Prod shows a read-only "Pass threshold" that only mirrors the subjective threshold, and the app printed its built-in 70% because the payload never sent it. Now a per-assessment setting in both consoles, sent in the payload (Q20) | unit + live (local copy, both consoles) |
| The Odoo generator badge said "0 questions" | On 24 of 26 active prod generators, because Auto mode has no fixed count. Now "Model decides" (S7, B4-24) | live (prod data) + unit |

| Defect | Effect | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A pasted Drive / Dropbox / OneDrive / SharePoint link stored a WEB PAGE as the question's image | These hosts answer **200 with a sign-in or viewer page** rather than 403, so `resp.ok` alone let HTML through. The candidate got an image element with nothing to decode. Now gated on content type, and the importer follows each redirect by hand against an anchored per-hop host allow-list | unit |

| Defect | Effect | Evidence |

| Answer key leaked mid-exam | `/exam/<token>/review` built its rows with the post-release serialiser, which for mcq/msq emits the correct option names and a live Correct/Incorrect verdict - to a candidate who had not submitted | live |
| Per-candidate release published the whole cohort | The Release button sent no evaluator ids and the route treats an empty list as "release everyone" | live |

### Failed silently

| Defect | Effect | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| LLM grading never ran | `llm_auto_score` was off on every assessment, so submits never queued and the cron drained an empty queue every 60 s. One answer sat pending **9 days with zero attempts**, no error anywhere | live |
| First Vertex mint failed on any new system | Search-then-insert race on first creation. Invisible on an old database, fatal on a fresh one - every new deployment would have hit it | live |
| Tag extraction hung forever | Busy state committed on a separate cursor invalidated its own snapshot; the closing write died on a serialization conflict. Also raced its own cron | live |
| Generator screen lost its own data | Every mutation refreshed generators from the *list* route, which omits `resources`, `allowed_types` and the question count. Uploads vanished, type ticks reverted - while the server stored correctly | live |
| Bank questions opened the wrong record | The bank serialiser omitted `state`, so the client parsed every bank question as a draft and fetched `/drafts/<id>` - a different record on a different id sequence | live |
| Scoring screen invented a queue | An all-objective paper has no `not_needed` state at attempt level, so it sat at `pending` and was reported as awaiting grading, permanently, on a healthy system | unit |
| Rescore ignored the grader's lock | The cron holds an advisory lock; the HTTP route called the same method without it. Two paid Vertex calls, two marks, last writer wins | live |
| Restored database blamed the wrong thing | Fernet key derives from `database.secret`; after a restore the app said "Vertex not configured" | live |
| Five crons stopped silently on a leaked lock | Session-level locks stranded on a pooled connection; every later tick took the early return and did nothing | traced |
| Veo clips could be paid for twice | A cache write aborted the transaction after the clip was already billing | traced |
| The contract audit under-checked | Its Dart parser could not handle the trailing comma `dart format` writes and swallowed the next method. It checked **71 call sites where there were 81** and produced one confident false failure | live |

### Mistakes made during this cycle

Recorded because they cost time and are invisible in the diff:

- A best-effort error handler swallowed a Postgres error **without a savepoint**, turning a
  recoverable failure into a 500. Caught in the traceback and corrected.
- A recovery sweeper was added unguarded at the top of a cron loop; one unfixable row would
  have **blocked all generation forever**. Now guarded per row (`prompt.py:572-593`).
- The scoring fix was described with a blast radius it does not have - see 6.2.
- A bad edit duplicated half of a 2,000-line screen file. Caught and repaired.
- A run command served the wrong directory, and the app was started against the wrong
  database. Both cost demo time directly.

# Importing a question bank as JSON

The importer accepts THREE formats through one file box, and works out which it
is holding rather than asking. Whichever surface you drop the file into - the
Odoo wizard (Question Bank > Import) or `POST /api/v1/bank/import` - it is the
same parser, so the same file produces the same records.

## Which format is which

The wizard sniffs in this order (`bank_import_wizard.run_import`):

| Order | Format | Recognised by | Lands as |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **harness** | a top-level list, or an object with `questions`, whose first item has a `fields` key or both `instruction` and `id` (`_try_harness_payload`) | review DRAFTS on a generator, for approval |
| 2 | **native** | an object carrying `assessments_be_bank` AND a `questions` list (`_try_native_payload`) | LIVE questions in the bank, rebuilt as exported |
| 3 | **CSV** | anything else, with a `title` or `prompt` column | approved questions on a generator |

A harness file that omits both `fields` and `id` is not recognised as harness,
falls through to the CSV path, and is refused for having no header row. If an
import reports the wrong format, that fingerprint is why.

Download a filled example of either JSON format from the wizard footer, or from
`GET /api/v1/bank/template/json?flavor=harness` (`flavor=native` for the other).
Both surfaces return the same bytes.

## The harness format

What the authoring harness writes: `questions.json` (a bare list) or
`output.json` (`{questions, solutions}`). Solutions are keyed by the
question's own `id`, which is the ONE field that has to line up between the two
halves.

Imported by `bank_import.import_bank_harness`. Questions arrive as review
drafts, NOT as live bank questions - an admin approves them through the normal
pipeline, and that approval is when any asset URL is actually downloaded.

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `questions[].id` | yes | Stable key. Also the join to `solutions`, and it becomes the draft's `gen_batch` as `harness:<id>`. Defaults to `qNN` by position when omitted, which breaks the solutions join. |
| `questions[].instruction` | yes | The question text. `prompt` is accepted as a fallback. The first 60 characters become the draft's title. |
| `questions[].covers_elements` | no | List of syllabus elements the question covers. Stored verbatim as `covers_elements_json`. |
| `questions[].fields.question_type` | yes | One of the draft model's own codes - `mcq`, `msq`, `subjective_rubric`, `image_ab`, `image_prompt`, `image_label`, `video_prompt`. An unknown code is imported as `subjective_rubric` WITH A WARNING, not refused. |
| `questions[].fields.difficulty` | no | `easy`, `medium` or `hard`. Anything else becomes `medium`. |
| `questions[].fields.options` | no | Required for `mcq` and `msq`; ignored for every other type. |
| `questions[].fields.correct_answer` | no | The answer key for `mcq` / `msq`. A string for one answer, a list for several. |
| `questions[].fields.rubric` | no | Required for `subjective_rubric`; ignored for every other type. A list of `{label, checklist, constraints, pass_condition}`. |
| `questions[].fields.official_reasoning` | no | The model answer shown to a reviewer, never to a candidate. |
| `questions[].assets` | no | `{role: {type, url}}`. ONLY an `http(s)` `url` (or `file`) is auto-attached, as the draft's `images_json`. A local run-folder path is reported in the import warnings for a manual upload, because Odoo cannot read the harness's filesystem. |
| `solutions.<id>.answers` | no | The worked answer, keyed by the question's `id`. Stored as `solution_json`. |
| `solutions.<id>.rationale` | no | Why that answer is right. Stored as `solution_rationale`. |

### Example

```json
{
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q01",
      "instruction": "Which city is the capital of France?",
      "covers_elements": [
        "geography.capitals"
      ],
      "fields": {
        "question_type": "mcq",
        "difficulty": "easy",
        "options": [
          "Paris",
          "London",
          "Berlin",
          "Madrid"
        ],
        "correct_answer": "Paris",
        "official_reasoning": "Paris has been the capital since 1944."
      },
      "assets": {
        "single": {
          "type": "image",
          "url": "https://picsum.photos/seed/capital/512"
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "q02",
      "instruction": "Select ALL prime numbers below.",
      "covers_elements": [
        "maths.number-theory"
      ],
      "fields": {
        "question_type": "msq",
        "difficulty": "medium",
        "options": [
          "2",
          "3",
          "4",
          "9"
        ],
        "correct_answer": [
          "2",
          "3"
        ],
        "official_reasoning": "2 and 3 have no divisors other than 1 and themselves; 4 and 9 are squares."
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "q03",
      "instruction": "Explain what idempotency means for a REST API and why it matters.",
      "covers_elements": [
        "engineering.api-design"
      ],
      "fields": {
        "question_type": "subjective_rubric",
        "difficulty": "hard",
        "rubric": [
          {
            "label": "Idempotency",
            "checklist": [
              "Defines idempotency as same request, same state",
              "Names at least one idempotent method",
              "Says why retries need it"
            ],
            "constraints": [
              "No code required"
            ],
            "pass_condition": "Covers the definition and one concrete retry consequence."
          }
        ],
        "official_reasoning": "A retry must not create a second resource, which is what makes PUT and DELETE safe to repeat."
      }
    }
  ],
  "solutions": {
    "q01": {
      "answers": "Paris",
      "rationale": "The other three are capitals of other countries."
    },
    "q02": {
      "answers": [
        "2",
        "3"
      ],
      "rationale": "4 = 2x2 and 9 = 3x3, so neither is prime."
    },
    "q03": {
      "answers": {
        "Idempotency": "pass"
      },
      "rationale": "A full answer names the property and one retry consequence."
    }
  }
}
```

## The native round-trip format

What `question._export_native` writes and `import_bank_native` reads: a lossless
export, used to move a bank between instances. It writes LIVE questions
directly, so it needs no approval step - and no generator, unless a question
names one.

An `assessments_be_bank` sentinel at the top level is what tells the importer
this is a native file rather than a harness one. Without it, a file with a
`questions` list is read as harness.

Every field below is a key of one entry in `questions`.

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Question title, truncated to 200 characters. |
| `prompt` | yes | The question text. |
| `description` | no | Sub-heading shown under the prompt. |
| `question_type` | yes | Must be one of the live codes. An unknown code is SKIPPED with a warning rather than restamped, because restamping keeps an answer key the new type cannot read. |
| `difficulty` | no | `easy`, `medium` or `hard`; anything else is dropped. |
| `time_minutes` | no | Suggested time. 0 when unset. |
| `sequence` | no | Ordering within the bank. Defaults to 10. |
| `source_ref` | no | Free-text provenance. |
| `official_reasoning` | no | Reviewer-facing model answer. |
| `subjective_rubric_json` | no | Rubric as a JSON STRING (not an object), for subjective types. |
| `grading_json` | no | Grading spec as a JSON string. |
| `meta_json` | no | Arbitrary metadata as a JSON string. |
| `generator` | no | Batch name. Matched by name, and CREATED if no generator has it. |
| `dimensions` | no | `[{name, options: [{name, is_correct}]}]`. A dimension with no options is skipped - that is how an answer key goes missing. |
| `images` | no | `[{slot, label, image_url, image_b64}]`. `image_url` is used as-is; `image_b64` is stored as the binary. |

### Example

The Question Bank list's **Export Native JSON** action emits exactly this shape.
For a filled one-question example, download
`GET /api/v1/bank/template/json?flavor=native`, or use the wizard's
**JSON Template (Native)** button.

## The asset rule, and why a local path is not enough

`_apply_harness_assets` attaches an asset only when it carries an `http(s)`
address in `url` or `file`. Anything else - `assets/q01_a.png`, an absolute path
on the machine that ran the harness - is reported in the import warnings and has
to be uploaded by hand, because Odoo has no access to the harness's filesystem.

The address is only WRITTEN at import time. The download happens later, when the
draft is approved (`prompt._materialize_images` -> `services/image_ingest`),
with a 20-second timeout and no redirect following. So an unreachable URL does
not fail the import; it fails the approval, where it can be corrected.

## Limits

| Limit | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| JSON payload | 50 MB | `bank_import._coerce_json` |
| CSV upload | 25 MB | `bank_import_wizard._MAX_CSV_BYTES` |
| CSV rows | 5000 | `bank_import_wizard._MAX_CSV_ROWS` |

Both JSON paths parse the whole payload into memory in one go and create one
record per question inside a single transaction, so a large file is best split
into batches even where no explicit row cap refuses it.

<!-- END GENERATED: bank-import-json-schema -->

### What 19.0.3.23.0 changed around the importer

Hand-written, so it survives a regeneration (W9, ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md §4.4):

* **Drafts first, with one exemption.** A CSV now lands as review drafts in
  Pending Approvals, exactly like harness JSON; the reviewer's approval is what
  puts a row in the bank. Only a native bank export restores live questions,
  because it round-trips questions already approved here. If the format table
  above still says a CSV lands as approved questions, it predates this - the fix
  belongs in `services/bank_json_template.py`, then regenerate.
* **One rule, two doors.** `bank_import_wizard.harness_payload` and
  `native_payload` decide the lane for the wizard's file and for the JSON
  `payload` of `POST /api/v1/bank/import` alike. The route's `native` flag is
  accepted and ignored, and an unknown JSON shape is 422 `invalid_json_shape`,
  naming both shapes.
* **A failed import writes nothing.** The route rolls back before each 422
  `import_failed` (S12); before, rows made ahead of the failing one stayed.
* **Where the operator meets it.** In Odoo, Import sits beside New on the Question
  Bank and Pending Approvals lists, as in the app. The dialog shows the detected
  format and names its button after the lane - "Import as drafts", or "Restore
  into the bank" with a confirm. The three templates come from ONE Download
  Template control with a CSV / JSON (harness) / JSON (native) picker, not from
  footer buttons. On a successful import the dialog closes and the list reloads.
* **The live bank only through the button that says so** (round 3, RV3-01).
  `question_count` and `detected_format` are `force_save`, so the detected
  format, its count and the "Restore into the bank" button survive any save of
  the wizard (a Download Template click or a failed import used to blank them
  and flip the footer to "Import as drafts" over a native file). And
  `run_import` restores a native export only when the context carries
  `confirm_native_restore`, which only that button sends; otherwise it refuses
  ("This file is a native bank export ... use Restore into the bank."). The API
  file lane sends the flag itself: there the file's shape decides.
* **Sized before decoding.** The API file lane refuses a `content` over 25 MB
  (413 `too_large`) before decoding it, JSON included (round 3). The 50 MB
  `_coerce_json` ceiling above is unchanged.

## 4.1a The Form Studio import template

A DIFFERENT IMPORT ENTIRELY from 4.1 above, and the difference is where the
parser runs. A question bank is POSTed to `/api/v1/bank/import` and read by
Odoo. A **form** is read in the browser: Form Studio's Import button hands the
file to `formFromImportedJson` (`form_models.dart:850`), and only the resulting
draft reaches `/forms/save`. There is no `/forms/import` route and there does
not need to be one.

What the client cannot produce on its own is a FIRST file, which is what
`GET /api/v1/forms/template/json` hands out.

### It is a structure, not a form

The template carries **one empty item of every element kind**, with every slot
an author can write present and blank - no question text, no options, no answer
keys, no media. Filling it in is the author's job.

So it is deliberately **not publishable as downloaded**, and that is the
feature rather than a gap: pressing Publish on an unfilled template answers 422
with a `problems` array naming every slot still blank, item by item, in the
same words the Publish button would have used. The template plugs into a feedback
loop that already existed instead of duplicating it.
`tests/test_form_template.py::TestPublishingAnUnfilledTemplateNamesEveryGap`
pins the message each kind produces, and names the three that correctly say
nothing (`textBlock` is informational; a blank `imageBlock`/`videoBlock` is a
plate with no option label, so it is not yet a question to complain about).

### Generated, never authored

`services/form_json_template.py` renders it from `constants.FORM_ITEM_KINDS` -
the same catalogue `_item_spec` branches on and the back-office item editor
draws its type picker from. Each kind already declares the slots it needs
(`needs`), the switches it offers (`flags`) and a sentence of guidance (`hint`).

It is the **same catalogue** `form_item_editor.js:newItem` reads, not the same
function: the two answer different questions, and the divergences are listed
under "What it names that the Odoo editor's blank item does not" below. `newItem`
seeds what the widget's controls have not written yet; this seeds every key a
person typing JSON can legitimately write.

The `hint` rides in the item's **`_note`**, and `help` is left blank like every
other slot. `help` is not a comment field - it is the CANDIDATE's text:
`_item_spec` publishes it as the question's `description`, and a `textBlock`'s
`help` is folded into the next question's lead text by `_attach_carry`. Seeding
it with authoring guidance shipped sentences written for the author ("Write the
model answer. The judge marks each candidate against it...") to the person
sitting the exam, and Publish could not catch it because `validate_structure`
never inspects `help`. `_note` is read by neither parser - `_item_spec` reads
named keys only, and the Flutter importer ignores item keys it does not know -
so the guidance stays in the file the author edits and reaches nothing else.

A kind added to the catalogue appears in the template with no edit here. A
`needs` token added with no seeder RAISES rather than seeding nothing, because
an item shipped with a slot missing is exactly what no test could otherwise see.

| Guard | Where |
|---|---|
| every catalogue kind is templated or in `SKIPPED_KINDS` | `tests/test_form_template.py` |
| every `needs` token seeds at least one key | same |
| every declared `flag` is seeded `False` or named in `_DEAD_FLAGS` | same |
| no item carries a non-empty `help`, and no hint survives the publish walk | same, `TestPublishingAnUnfilledTemplateNamesEveryGap` |
| an unknown token / an unclaimed family is refused by name | same |
| the route serves exactly the service render, and refuses below Admin | same, `TestTheFormTemplateRoute` |
| no kind is silently degraded by the Flutter importer | `ethara-assessment-fe/test/assessment/form_template_test.dart` |

That last row is the cross-repo guard, and it is the one that matters most.
`FormItemKindX.parse` falls back to `shortAnswer` for a kind it does not know,
**with no warning to anyone**, so a module that learned a new kind would hand
out a template with an element the client quietly turns into a text box. The
client test compares what it parsed against what was written and fails instead.

### What it leaves out, and why

* `date`, `time`, `fileUpload` - `SKIPPED_KINDS`. The first two are retired in
  the Flutter designer (`form_models.dart:129-133`) and would import as a
  `shortAnswer` with no warning; `fileUpload` has role `refused` and one of them
  refuses the whole form.
* `allow_other` - a real flag on the three choice kinds, dropped by publish with
  a warning (`studio_form.py:730`). Naming it would teach a dead field.
* `id`, `published`, `updated_at` - the importer re-mints every id, forces
  `published` false and resets `updated_at`. A key the file cannot influence
  does not belong in a document whose job is to teach the format.
* `scale_golden` / `rating_golden` - the Flutter designer's typed fields, which
  `studio_form` never reads. The template spells the scale key `golden_answer`,
  which is what `_item_spec` actually reads (`studio_form.py:716`).

### What it names that the Odoo editor's blank item does not

`newItem` seeds the keys the editor's own CONTROLS write; a hand-authored file
has no controls, so the template additionally names four things:

* **`media_url_b` and the rating axes on `promptWriting`.** `newItem` tests for
  the tokens `media_b` and `options` exactly, and `promptWriting` declares the
  optional spellings (`media_b_optional`, `options_optional`), so neither seeds
  anything there. Without the second plate named, nothing in the file teaches
  the reference-then-output transform.
* **`media_kind` beside every `media_url`.** The designer stamps it from the
  upload's content type, so the widget never needs it. It is the only way a
  hand-authored file can declare a clip whose URL has no extension and no embed
  host, where `_looks_like_video` would otherwise read it as an image.
* **`regions` on `imageAnnotation`.** `newItem` does seed `annotation_count` and
  `golden_labels`; `regions` is the one the annotation canvas writes, and
  `{n, x, y, w, h}` is not a shape anybody guesses.
* **every declared `flag`, seeded `False`.** `newItem` seeds no flag at all -
  the switch renders from `kind.flags` and the key is written on the first
  toggle - so `multi_select` (`imageBlock`, `videoBlock`) and
  `require_justification` (`comparePair`) exist nowhere in a blank editor item.
  An author reading JSON has no switch to notice one, so it has to be in the
  file to be discoverable. `allow_other` is the exception, above.

It also names **`help`** - blank - which `newItem` seeds too, and **`_note`**,
which `newItem` has no need of because the editor shows the same `hint` beside
the kind in its own UI.

### Where the operator meets it

`showFormImportSheet` (`ethara-assessment-fe/lib/assessment/widgets/form_import_sheet.dart`).
Import opens a sheet rather than the OS file dialog, because going straight to
the picker was right only for an operator who already had a file. The sheet
carries the Download-template button, the fifteen kind chips read off the local
`FormItemKind` enum, and the 512 KB ceiling stated before a file is chosen
rather than as a refusal afterwards. Only in the app: Odoo offers no form import
and no template, because forms are authored in Flutter only (decided; the Form
Studio rows in 4.2).

## 4.2 Odoo / Flutter capability parity

Was `docs/ETP_KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md (4.2 Odoo / Flutter capability parity)`. The inventory of every Flutter admin
capability against its Odoo equivalent, the gaps that were closed on
2026-09-10, what 19.0.3.23.0 moved, and what remains.

Deliverable for spec `assessment-admin-console-defects`, task 19 (defect D3).
Requirements 1.10 and 2.10. Method: `design.md` § 8.

**This file is an inventory, and the rows CJ scheduled have since been implemented.** The
status column below is CURRENT for 19.0.3.23.0: rows closed on 2026-09-10 are marked
`present` with a `CLOSED` note naming what was added, and a row this release changed
says so in its note. Four rows remain `absent`, all of `workaround` severity (see
"Counts by status x severity"). Four Form Studio rows are `n/a` since 19.0.3.23.0:
forms are authored in Flutter only, by decision (ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md §4.6).

### How this was built

- **Left side.** The 23 Flutter admin screens under `lib/assessment/screens/admin/`. For each,
  every user-triggerable capability was extracted as `(screen, action, ApiClient method, route)`.
  `lib/assessment/data/api_client.dart` is the choke point — **117 public methods**, each
  resolving to a `/api/v1` path — so the extraction is mechanical. Only one screen calls
  `ApiClient` directly (`generator_list`); the other 22 go through `AppStore`, so attribution
  walks `screen -> AppStore method -> ApiClient method`.
- **Right side.** The 13 view files under `views/`: **39 views**, **64 `type="object"` button
  occurrences across 44 distinct model methods**, 11 menu items, 14 `ir.actions.act_window`
  records (5 of them on no menu), 3 `ir.actions.server` records, plus list columns, search
  filters and wizards per model.
- **The join is the route or the model, never the screen name.** Odoo has no notion of a Flutter
  screen. Most write routes call the model's own `action_*` method, which makes the join exact:
  the question is whether that same method is reachable from a view. The gap finder is therefore
  mechanical too — **10 of the 57 `action_*` methods defined in `models/` are on no view button**.
- **The console bootstrap fan-out is attributed once, not per screen.** `AppStore._act()` refreshes
  the same 14 routes after nearly every mutation, so a naive call-graph walk credits every screen
  with every list. Those were subtracted before attribution.
- **Out of scope, deliberately:** the `/auth/*` and candidate-facing `/exam/*` and `/me/*` routes.
  D3 is about admin-console parity, and those are neither admin capabilities nor Odoo views.

#### Statuses

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `present` | an Odoo equivalent exists and an operator can reach it |
| `partial` | exists but narrower — fewer fields, no bulk action, different filters, or off-menu |
| `absent` | no Odoo equivalent |
| `n/a` | Flutter-only by design, or Odoo-only |
| `unconfirmed` | could not be confirmed either way — **not** counted as a gap |

#### Severity

| severity | meaning |
|---|---|
| `blocking` | an operator cannot complete a real task in Odoo at all |
| `workaround` | possible through the generic Odoo UI, with collateral or per-record effort |
| `cosmetic` | presentation only |

Developer mode is **not** a workaround here. `group_assessment_manager` (labelled "Admin") implies
`group_assessment_manager_restricted` and `hr_recruitment.group_hr_recruitment_user` only — never
`base.group_system` (`security/etp_assessment_security.xml:97,112`). An assessment Admin cannot
create a server action, so a model method with no view is unreachable for them.

#### Scale and concurrency

Notes marked **Scale:** flag a capability that exists on both surfaces but where one side would not
survive a large cohort. Reference figures measured on stage: 572 candidates per assessment, 2,538
attempts, 31,462 responses. Four patterns are called out — per-candidate iteration without
server-side paging; a long-running or fan-out operation driven from a synchronous request handler
(recorded as *inline* or *queued*, because inline is what pins a worker); polling on a timer; and
serialising an unbounded set. **A gap that only appears at scale is still a gap, and a capability
that would break Odoo at 572 must not be implemented as-is.**

### Counts by status x severity

This is how large D3 actually is.

As first measured (2026-09-08), and as it stands in 19.0.3.23.0 (**now**):

| status | `blocking` | `workaround` | `cosmetic` | — | **total** | **now** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `present` | · | · | · | 72 | **72** | **82** |
| `partial` | · | 13 | 1 | · | **14** | **14** |
| `absent` | 12 | 4 | · | · | **16** | **4** |
| `n/a` | · | · | 1 | 10 | **11** | **16** |
| `unconfirmed` | · | · | · | 2 | **2** | **2** |
| **total** | **12** | **17** | **2** | **84** | **115** | **118** |

**All 12 `absent` + `blocking` rows are closed.** The four rows still marked
`absent` are the `workaround`-severity ones that were never scheduled: a
targeted invitation resend, a retire-impact preview, a tag-backfill shortcut and
a media-URL import wired to a form item.

The inventory grew from 115 to 118 rows: the two Form Studio import rows, and the
Scored / Score Pending split (new in 19.0.3.23.0). What 19.0.3.23.0 moved: the
three import rows now sit where the app has them (tags from `partial` to
`present`); the four Form Studio authoring rows (save, edit an item, import JSON,
download the template) are `n/a`, because forms are read-only in Odoo by decision;
and drafting a task template from a generator is `partial`, because Odoo's Draft
from SOP is hidden for this release.

#### What is still open

**Nothing, of the twelve.** All twelve `absent` + `blocking` rows are closed as of
2026-09-10. The last three were the graphical editors - the labelling annotation
editor, the Form Studio item editor and its media upload - and they are the ones
worth knowing about, because each is a canvas rather than a missing button and
each carries a rule that must not be duplicated (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: the
item editor is read-only on a Studio form, which is authored in Flutter only, and
authors task templates instead, where media upload now lives):

| capability | how it avoids a second copy of the rules |
|---|---|
| Annotation editor | Saves through `apply_studio_annotation_item`, the same model method the API route calls. The geometry transform is not re-derived; `as_studio_annotation_item` remains the only place it lives. |
| Form item editor | Types come from `form_item_kinds()`, validity from `validate_structure()` - which walks the document with the same `_walk_document` that `publish_to_assessment` walks. An editor with its own idea of what is publishable is how a form becomes acceptable in one place and refused in the other. |
| Form media upload | Posts to the existing `/api/v1/forms/media` routes, so the SSRF allow-list and content-type gate are not reimplemented behind the back office. |

Two limits are worth recording rather than discovering later. Markers stored as
`box_px` (the DOM-capture lane) are PIXELS and not comparable with normalised
`box_2d`, so the annotation editor can label them but deliberately will not
redraw them. And a marker carrying neither geometry nor a label cannot be
repaired in the editor - the item shape has nowhere to put it - so the widget
warns that saving will drop it.

### The `absent` + `blocking` rows, as first found

Kept as the original measurement. Ten of the twelve are now closed - see the status
column in the inventory above, where each carries a `CLOSED 2026-09-10` note naming what
was added.

| # | capability | why an operator was stuck |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Re-score only the failed/errored attempts, assessment-wide | The nearest reachable Odoo path is `action_reset_errored_scoring` on the *evaluator form* — one attempt, `error` only. Recovering a cohort-wide grader outage means N form visits. `group_assessment_manager` does not imply `base.group_system` (`security/etp_assessment_security.xml:97,112`), so an operator has no server-action escape hatch. |
| 2 | Edit labelling boxes in an annotation editor | Boxes and labels are reachable in Odoo only as raw JSON on the question form. There is no graphical annotation surface, so correcting a generated labelling question is not a task an operator can do in Odoo. |
| 3 | List Studio forms | Full CRUD in `security/ir.model.access.csv:27` for `group_assessment_manager` and zero views, so the model is writable and unreachable — an operator cannot see that any form exists. |
| 4 | Create and save a Studio form | A form can only be authored through the API. |
| 5 | Delete a Studio form | No list or form view, so there is no record to act on. |
| 6 | Publish a Studio form | The publish state cannot be changed from Odoo. |
| 7 | Edit a form item | Items live inside the form's stored spec; Odoo exposes neither the spec nor an editor. Task 20 should put this to CJ as a Flutter-only decision before scheduling it — reproducing the item editor in OWL is a project, not a gap fix. |
| 8 | Upload form media | No upload widget is wired to a form item. |
| 9 | List task templates | Full CRUD in `security/ir.model.access.csv:28` and zero views, so an operator cannot see the templates that drive generation. |
| 10 | Save a task template | A template can only be written through the API. |
| 11 | Draft a task template from a generator | No button on the generator form reaches it. |
| 12 | Archive a task template | No list or form view, so there is no record to archive. |

They clustered into three groups, which is the shape the work took:

1. **The Studio form surface (6 rows).** `etp.studio.form` has full CRUD access rights and zero
   views. This is 4 Flutter screens; the item editor alone is the largest file in the admin tree.
   Put it to CJ as an explicit Flutter-only decision before scheduling any of it — "build a form
   designer in OWL" is a project, not a defect fix.
2. **Task templates (4 rows).** `assessments.be.task.template` also has no views. Smaller and more
   tractable than the Studio surface: a list, a form and a menu entry would close all four.
3. **Two genuine one-off gaps.** Cohort-wide re-score of failed attempts, and the annotation editor
   for labelling questions. These are the rows worth doing first: both are real recovery and
   correction tasks an operator hits on a live cohort, and neither is a new subsystem.

#### Scale-risk flags

Capabilities that exist on both surfaces where one side would not survive 572 candidates. These are
**not** parity gaps and must not be implemented as-is on the weaker side.

| # | capability | which side | the risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Export cohort responses | both | unbounded serialisation — ~17k rows built in memory in one synchronous request |
| 2 | Release results for the cohort | Odoo | inline `filtered()` over every evaluator reading `response_ids`, then a 572-row write, in the request |
| 3 | Bulk-invite from CSV | Odoo | parses the CSV and creates applicants inline; the heaviest synchronous write on the Odoo side |
| 4 | Launch and invite | Odoo | creates 572 attempts in one transaction — the identical-`create_date` structure behind C1 |
| 5 | Search the roster | Odoo | `candidate_table.js:94` widens the x2many to `list.count` and filters in the browser — all 572 rows per keystroke |
| 6 | Page the roster | Odoo | one shared per-field page size of 10 across three sub-views; 572 candidates is 58 pages |
| 7 | Live scoring status | Odoo | one `orm.read` per busy cell every 3s, unbatched — ~3.3 req/s per open form at 10 rows (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: backs off to 30s while unchanged) |
| 8 | Leaderboard | Flutter | 200 rows fetched inside a 2s poll while a generator runs |
| 9 | Response list | Flutter | walk capped at 2 pages — 400 of 31,462 rows, so the screen shows a sample |
| 10 | LLM spend ledger | Flutter | walk capped at 5 pages on the fastest-growing table on the platform |
| 11 | Approve every draft | Odoo | approves the generator's whole draft set inline |
| 12 | Normalize the tag vocabulary | Odoo | re-extracts every selected generator inline |
| 13 | Console bootstrap | Flutter | 14 concurrent routes per load, re-run every 2s during generation |

Queued rather than inline, and therefore fine: subjective evaluation for the cohort
(`_cron_llm_auto_score`), invitation sending (`_cron_send_pending_invitations`), question generation
(`_cron_generate_from_sop`) and tag extraction (`_cron_extract_tags`).

#### What could not be confirmed

- `/api/v1/emails/<id>/cancel` — the route exists and is manager-gated; no Flutter caller and no Odoo
  view were found for it.
- `/api/v1/generators/<id>/extract_structures` — `controllers/api/write.py` records that
  `action_extract_structures` may belong to a host addon and may not exist. Neither surface exposes it.

Both are `unconfirmed` rather than gaps, because a false gap costs more than a missing row.

#### Orphans found on the way

Not parity rows — neither surface reaches them, so there is nothing to be at parity with. Recorded
because each is a latent capability someone paid to write.

- **Odoo model methods on no view and called by no route:** `action_open_submitted` (the sixth
  dashboard drill-down), `action_regrade_for_component_scoring` (called only by
  `tools/backfill_final_marks.py`), `action_upload_question_image`,
  `action_remove_from_assessment`, `action_reset_errored_scoring`. *(Changed since this list was
  made: `action_llm_score_failed` is now the Odoo "Retry Failed Scoring" button, and
  `action_llm_score` became the lane-private `_action_llm_score` in 19.0.3.23.0.)*
- **`ApiClient` methods with zero call sites in `lib/`:** `extractStructures`, `importCandidates`,
  `myAnalytics`, `myDashboard`. `candidates()` was a fifth until task 10 wired the roster to it —
  the same dead-route pattern that caused D2/D7.

  the tab.
- Re-tick both before moving on.

**4b. Launched, frozen.** Assessments → **VAL Launched - paper is fixed** →
*Selected Questions*.

- PASS: an inert notice **"The paper is fixed."**; four rows; the ticks are
  visible but do not respond to a click.
- FAIL: the ticks being editable, or the tab being disabled. A launched paper
  still has to show what it was launched against.

**4b-bis. The count must never read 0 on a draft nobody has touched.** Create a
fresh assessment (New Assessment → name + generator → Create draft) and open
*Selected Questions*.

- PASS: every row ticked, the badge and sub-header show the generator's full
  count, and **Launch & invite** carries no "(N to fix)".
- FAIL: "0 questions", or a launch gate reading "Asked for 0 but only 0 are
  selected." An empty shortlist means THE WHOLE GENERATOR server-side
  (`action_start`: `if shortlist:` skips the narrowing, then `limit =
  question_limit or len(available_questions)`), so the client must count it the
  same way or it refuses a launch the server would accept.

**4c. Same tab as the Manager.** Sign in as **cj.manager@val.local**, open
either assessment → *Selected Questions*.

- PASS on the draft: an inert notice **"Read-only. Your role can review the
  shortlist but not change it."**, the ticks visible and inert.
- FAIL: editable ticks, or an empty tab.

**4d. The list column agrees.** On the Assessments list, the QUESTIONS column
reads **6** for the draft and **4** for the launched one.

**WHAT THAT COLUMN ACTUALLY SHOWS, because it is not always the paper.** There
are THREE numbers on an assessment and they are allowed to differ:

| Number | Field | Set when |
|---|---|---|
| the POOL | the generator's approved questions | authoring |
| the SHORTLIST | `question_ids` - the *Selected Questions* ticks. Empty means "the whole generator" | any time while draft |
| the CAP | `question_limit` - how many to DRAW per candidate. 0 means "no cap" | any time while draft |

At launch, `action_start` (`assessment.py:1732`) reads
`limit = rec.question_limit or len(available)`, draws ONE shared set of that many
for the whole cohort (the order is still shuffled per candidate unless the
author's order is kept), and freezes it into each `evaluator.question_order`.
**After that the paper is immutable**, and the cap is locked: the server refuses
a changed count on a launched assessment (19.0.3.23.0, W7).

The list route sends no question records, so the QUESTIONS column falls back to
the cap; the detail payload carries the shortlist. So a paper legitimately
configured as "shortlist 4, draw 3" reads **3** on the list and **4** on the
detail, and neither is wrong. Seeded so all three agree, precisely so this check
has one number to look at.

### The pre-deploy gate

Before pushing, on the target database:

```bash
cd /Users/cj/Developer/ethara/ethara-etp/custom_addons/assessments_be_v2
python3 tools/contract_audit.py     # -> FAIL 3 today (see below); OK, 108 call sites, once fixed
ETP_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8069 ETP_DB=etp_validate \
  ETP_LOGIN=cj.admin@val.local ETP_PASSWORD="$VAL_PASSWORD" \
  python3 tools/deploy_gate.py      # -> OK - no sitting or grading is in progress
```

`contract_audit.py` must count `id_list_arg_strict` as a reader of a key, and the
shipped copy does not (`READERS`, `tools/contract_audit.py:43`): it reports
`evaluator_ids` (`/release`, `/scoring/queue`) and `question_ids`
(`/attempts/<id>/rescore`) as unread and exits 1, although all three routes read
them strictly since 19.0.3.23.0. Those 3 are the only failures; with the name
added to `READERS` it prints OK, 108 call sites.

`deploy_gate.py` refuses while anybody is mid-exam or a grading lane is working
(exit 1), pages through every attempt, and needs an assessments Admin login,
because `/api/v1/scoring` is Admin-only (a Manager gets exit 2, "cannot tell").
An upgrade rebuilds the registry, and a sitting that loses its worker mid-answer
loses the answer. The production procedure is ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md §0.5 H3.
