### Nothing has to be configured, on any environment

**There is no per-environment setting to remember.** Both of the parameters this
used to need are derived from `web.base.url`, which Odoo maintains itself:

| `web.base.url` | client origin | localhost trusted at CORS |
|---|---|---|
| `https://projects.ethara.ai` | `https://assessment.ethara.ai` | no |
| `https://projects-stage.ethara.ai` | `https://assessment-stage.ethara.ai` | no |
| `http://localhost:<any port>` | `http://localhost:8200` | yes |
| anything else | the Odoo host itself | no |

Pull the tree, restore a database, run it. Verified with **both parameters
deleted**: the preflight from `127.0.0.1:8200` is allowed, the retired paths
redirect to `localhost:8200`, and a production-shaped `web.base.url` allows only
`https://assessment.ethara.ai` and refuses localhost, stage and everything else.

Why it matters that this is derived rather than documented: both settings fail
**silently**. A missing CORS entry means Odoo answers 200 and the BROWSER discards
it - clean server log, empty screen. A missing client origin means every invited
candidate is emailed a link to port 8069, which is Odoo and not the exam runner.

The two parameters still exist as overrides and still win when set:

- `assessments_be_v2.candidate_app_base_url` - for a deployment serving the client
  from a vanity domain, a path, or Odoo's own origin. No table can describe those.
- `assessments_be_v2.cors_allow_localhost = 1` - for a **shared box on a real
  hostname** that front-end work points a local build at. Its own `web.base.url`
  is not localhost, so only the opt-in can admit it.

The derivation is a statement about which server this **is**, read from a
parameter only a database administrator can write - never about who is calling.
Nothing in it reads the request's `Origin`, which is why a deployment on a real
hostname admits nothing extra however it is called. Pinned by
`tests/test_a_clone_needs_no_configuration.py`.

If you serve the client on a port other than 8200, that is the one case that
still needs `candidate_app_base_url`. `make serve-local` uses 8200.

### Still needing your decision

**70 portal accounts on stage are bound as candidates** - 68 on `@ethara.ai`
addresses, carrying 146 attempts between them. They keep their attempts and their
history; what they cannot do is sign in to the platform, because it is
internal-only. Each one needs either a re-invite on a non-portal address or a
deliberate conversion to an internal account, which is a paid Odoo seat. Nothing
in this change touches them, and a launch will no longer die because one of them
is shaped wrongly - but they will keep being refused until somebody decides.


## 4.4 Vertex setup

Was `docs/ETP_KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md (4.4 Vertex setup)`. Installing the service-account key, picking models, proving generation works, spend caps.

Question generation, image rendering, Veo clips, box detection and subjective
scoring all go through Vertex. Without a working credential the addon installs
and serves, generation and scoring just fail - so this is worth proving once
rather than discovering mid-demo.

The scripts live in `tools/` and are run through the Odoo shell, because the
credential is stored **encrypted** (Fernet, keyed off `database.secret`) via
this addon's own `services/secret_store.py`. A plaintext `INSERT` would put a
live private key into the database and every dump taken from it, and
`_minted_bearer` would fail to decrypt it anyway.

All paths below are relative to the repo root.

### 1. Install the key and pick models

```bash
ETP_SA_JSON=/path/to/service-account.json \
  env -u PYTHONPATH .venv/bin/python src/odoo-bin shell \
  -c odoo.conf -d "$DB" --no-http < custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/tools/vertex_setup.py
```

It stores the key encrypted, derives the project id from it, invalidates any
cached bearer, then probes a list of models and writes the survivors' roles into
`ir.config_parameter`:

* text - strongest first: `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, the 3.x Flash models, then
  `gemini-2.5-pro` and older. The strongest reachable becomes `vertex_model`,
  `generation_model` and `scoring_model`, the cheapest `utility_model` and
  `detection_model`, and the second a `fallback_model`. The judge is never moved
  to a cheaper model by the script; set `scoring_model` by hand once benched.
* image - cheapest first: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image`, `gemini-3.1-flash-image`,
  `gemini-3-pro-image`, then 2.5 and 2.0. Veo is not probed, because a probe
  would render and bill a real clip.

Production grades on `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` at temperature 0.2, and
19.0.3.23.0 does not change the model. What it adds is a model catalog
(`services/model_catalog.py`): `GET /api/v1/settings` returns
`scoring.resolved_model` with `price_known` and `capabilities_known`, and
Flutter Settings shows it as "Scoring model in use", with a warning when the
catalog does not know the model.

Image generation is a **different model family** and is probed separately. An
unset `image_model` does not fall back to something sensible - the code falls
through to the text model and fails with "Multi-modal output is not supported",
an error that names the symptom and hides the cause.

Idempotent. Re-run with no `ETP_SA_JSON` to re-probe and re-point models without
touching the stored key. The key is never printed, never passed as argv, never
echoed; only a path goes in.

### 2. Prove it works

```bash
env -u PYTHONPATH .venv/bin/python src/odoo-bin shell \
  -c odoo.conf -d "$DB" --no-http < custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/tools/vertex_probe.py
```

Read-only. Mints a real bearer and makes one real `generateContent` call through
the module's own path. "It is configured" is not "it works": wrong project, API
disabled, key missing the `aiplatform` role, PyJWT/cryptography absent, model not
entitled - all look identical from the database and only surface on the wire.
Prints token length, never its value, and passes no `usage_ctx`, so a diagnostic
never bills the LLM ledger or pollutes the budget screen.

### 3. If image or video generation fails

```bash
env -u PYTHONPATH .venv/bin/python src/odoo-bin shell \
  -c odoo.conf -d "$DB" --no-http < custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/tools/vertex_media_probe.py
```

Image and video are three families on two endpoint shapes, and a 404 on one says
nothing about the others:

| Family | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| Imagen | `:predict` |
| Gemini | `:generateContent` with `responseModalities: [TEXT, IMAGE]` |
| Veo    | `:predictLongRunning` - and not in every region |

Each is probed on its own path, Veo across regions. "No image or video
entitlement" was once concluded from a single 404 on one default model, and that
was wrong.

Four of the seven question types - `image_ab`, `image_prompt`, `image_label`,
`video_prompt` - cannot be generated without image/video entitlement. Text
generation is unaffected, and so is grading: since 19.0.3.23.0 the grading call
is text-only and sends no media.

### Spend

`assessments_be_v2.daily_llm_cap_usd` and `.per_evaluator_llm_cap_usd` are the
budget guards, enforced in `services/vertex.py`.

**They are on by default.** An unset parameter does not mean uncapped - `vertex.spend_cap`
falls back to `constants.DEFAULT_DAILY_LLM_CAP_USD` / `DEFAULT_PER_EVALUATOR_LLM_CAP_USD`:
**$100/day** and **$5 per candidate**. `0` is what disables a cap, and only a STORED `0`
counts - an absent or blank row is "not configured" and takes the default.

**`vertex.spend_cap` is the ONE resolver, and that is new in 19.0.3.22.0.** It is public
(it was `_spend_cap`) precisely so no surface resolves the key for itself again. The gate
(`vertex._check_budget`), the LLM Budget dashboard (`GET /api/v1/budget`) and the Settings
route (`GET /api/v1/settings`) all read through it. Before, each substituted its own
fallback: with both rows absent the two screens reported `cap_usd: 0, capped: false` while
the gate was refusing every call at $100/day, and the Flutter governance panel posts all
four keys back on any Save - so one Save of a screen prefilled with `0` genuinely disabled
the cap. The `res.config.settings` field defaults read the same constants. `_check_budget` runs at the top of every
`_call_vertex` and `generate_image`, before any billable request, summing the ledger
since UTC midnight. It is a floor check rather than a reservation, so the last call
before the cap can overshoot it.

One nuance: the per-candidate cap only applies when the call carries an
`evaluator_id` in its `usage_ctx`. Question generation does not, so **only the daily
cap gates a generator run**.

A cap never costs a grading answer anything (19.0.3.23.0). A lane tick that finds
the daily cap reached plans nothing and logs `SPEND_CAP daily` once; a cap, a 429
or a full database pool met mid-run leaves the answers `pending` with their
attempt budget untouched, logged at WARNING as `SPEND_CAP`, `GRADING_QUOTA` or
`GRADING_POOL_FULL`, and the next tick picks them up. An individual re-score is
refused at the click, with nothing queued, when either money cap is reached.

Rough cost of one "Generate Questions" click: `gen_selfheal` and `gen_critique` are
both ON by default, so a run is 3-6 calls, each re-sending the whole SOP. On
`gemini-2.5-pro` that is about **$0.30-$1.50**, up to $3-5 for a pathological run, and
roughly 1.5x that on `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. Media is where the real money is: image
render is $0.039-$0.134 per image, and Veo is **$0.40 per second** - a single 6-second
clip costs more than a whole text generation run. Keep the image and video types out of
the allow-list while proving text.

Grading one written answer costs about **$0.016-0.018** on `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`
under the new text-only prompt (two runs; a third, not like-for-like, came to $0.024, against
$0.021-0.023 for the old prompt), measured by the paid synthetic checks of 2026-09-23/24 (ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md §0.1). Bulk runs may also create question-group
context caches (`assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache`, default `groups`, ON): a group is
cached only when it reaches the model's minimum (4,096 tokens on Gemini 3), so today's
papers are sent exactly as with the cache off, and answers are never cached. Cache
creation and refresh are billed and appear on the ledger as `scoring_cache_create` /
`scoring_cache_refresh`; tokens Vertex serves from a cache are recorded in
`cached_tokens` and priced at 10% of the input rate. Switch table: ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md §0.5 J.

Actual spend is on the LLM Budget dashboard and in `assessments.be.llm.usage`. The Odoo
dashboard leads with today against the caps, resolved by `vertex.spend_cap`; the Flutter
Budget cards show the server's lifetime totals (`data.lifetime`), not a sum of the rows
it holds. `_log_usage` never swallows a ledger-write failure silently - it logs "the
Vertex call was billed but NOT recorded" with the estimate, so it can be reconciled
against the invoice.

### Handling the key file

Service-account JSON must never reach git. `.gitignore` covers
`*service-account*.json`, `*serviceaccount*.json` and `*credentials*.json` - note
that gcloud's own default name is `<project>-<keyid>.json`, which matches **none**
of those. Rename the file to include `service-account`, or keep it outside the
repo entirely. `tools/check_no_real_key.py` compares tracked files against the
actual key material at `$ETP_SA_JSON`, so a 4-character test stub passes and a
real leak fails.


## 4.5 Email delivery setup

Was `docs/ETP_KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md (4.5 Email delivery setup)`. How a candidate invitation is actually delivered - mailpit locally, SES on stage and production.

Launching an assessment does not send anything directly. `action_start` writes
`invite_state = 'queued'` on each attempt, and the cron **ETP Assessment: Send
queued candidate invitations** (every minute) drains the queue through
`_deliver_invitation` -> `_send_single_invitation`, which renders
`mail_template_candidate_invitation` and sends it. (The older
`mail_template_single_invitation`, which deep-linked a token, is deleted by
`data/mail_template.xml` — see "The link a candidate receives".)

So an invitation that never arrives has three possible causes, in this order:
the cron is not running, no outgoing mail server is configured, or the mail was
rejected. The first is by far the most common locally - see "Crons" below.

The invitation is sent **From `no-reply@ethara.ai`**, the verified sender, with
the paper's creator in **Reply-To** (19.0.3.23.0, Q11). The body gives the time
limit, the window in IST, the pass mark as a plain number (`%g`: 60 -> "60%",
62.5 -> "62.5%"; the assessment's effective pass threshold, Q20), that the clock starts when the candidate presses Start
Assessment, the proctoring rules the paper actually enforces, and "Sign in with
your Ethara account ... First time? Use Forgot password to set one." The
template is `noupdate="0"`, so an upgrade replaces it: edit
`data/mail_template.xml`, not the copy in the UI.

### The link a candidate receives

The invitation body uses `object.candidate_home_url` — the app's **front door**,
with no token in it — not `candidate_link`. A token URL in an inbox is a bearer
credential: forwardable, logged by mail scanners, and it opens only ONE sitting,
so a candidate with three assessments needed three emails. One sign-in now
reaches all of them.

`candidate_link` still exists and still deep-links (`<app>/exam/<token>`). It is
what the roster's "Copy candidate link" hands an operator, and what the app
resolves for anybody holding an older mail.

Both resolve through `_candidate_app_origin`, which answers in three steps:

| Step | Origin |
|---|---|
| 1 | `assessments_be_v2.candidate_app_base_url`, when an operator set it |
| 2 | `app_origins.PAIRED_APP_ORIGINS[web.base.url]` — `projects.ethara.ai → assessment.ethara.ai` |
| 3 | `web.base.url` itself, for a host in no table |

**There is no longer an Odoo-portal answer.** Every link points at the Flutter
app. The server-rendered exam runner was retired, and its nine paths
(`/pro_assessment/<token>` and friends, `/my/pro_*`) are now redirects into the
app — see `controllers/legacy_redirects.py`. So a link already sitting in an
inbox still works; it just takes one extra hop.

Step 2 was previously forbidden on purpose: the link is emailed and cannot be
recalled, and `/pro_assessment/<token>` answered 200, so deriving would have
silently moved every invitation. That route no longer renders a page, so deriving
is now the accurate answer rather than a risky one.

Set step 1 only where steps 2 and 3 give the wrong answer - a vanity domain, a
path, or a client on a port other than 8200 locally. Leaving it unset is the
normal case: every step already points at the Flutter app.

### Local development: mailpit

Real SMTP is the wrong tool for a laptop. Use a catcher: mail is delivered for
real, nothing leaves the machine, and there is a web inbox to read it in.

```bash
brew install mailpit
mailpit --smtp 127.0.0.1:1025 --listen 127.0.0.1:8025    # inbox at :8025
```

Then one `ir.mail_server` row:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `name` | Local Mailpit (dev catcher) |
| `smtp_host` | `127.0.0.1` |
| `smtp_port` | `1025` |
| `smtp_encryption` | `none` |
| `from_filter` | **empty** |
| `sequence` | `5` |

`from_filter` is deliberately empty. `_find_mail_server` tries to match the
sender against each server's `from_filter` and only falls through to "the first
server with no filter" as a later step - an empty filter is what makes the
catcher apply to everything, which is what a dev environment wants.

Odoo 19 also needs a sender identity, which now lives on **`mail.alias.domain`**
rather than the old `mail.catchall.domain` / `mail.default.from` parameters. One
row with a `name`, `bounce_alias`, `catchall_alias` and `default_from`, linked to
the company via `alias_domain_id`.

### Production and stage: AWS SES

Stage runs this today. Same shape, different row:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `name` | AWS SES |
| `smtp_host` | `email-smtp.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com` |
| `smtp_port` | `587` |
| `smtp_encryption` | `starttls_strict` |
| `smtp_user` | the SES SMTP username (an `AKIA...` key id) |
| `smtp_pass` | the SES SMTP password - **not** the IAM secret key |
| `from_filter` | `no-reply@ethara.ai` |
| `sequence` | `10` |

`from_filter` is set here precisely because it must NOT catch everything: SES
rejects a `MAIL FROM` outside the verified identity, so pinning the filter makes
Odoo pick this server only for mail it can actually send. The invitation's own
From is that identity, so it always matches.

Stage's `mail.catchall.domain` is `ethara.ai` and `web.base.url` is the public
host. `web.base.url` matters beyond cosmetics - it derives the app link (step 2
above) and builds the password-reset link sent with a first invitation.

### Before you point a real relay at a database

**Cancel the failed backlog first.**

```sql
select state, count(*) from mail_mail group by state;
update mail_mail set state='cancel' where state='exception';
```

Failed mail does not resend itself - `process_email_queue` only picks up
`outgoing` - but the Emails list has a one-click Retry, and a dev database is
full of `@example.com` recipients that hard-bounce 100%. Firing a few dozen of
those at a real relay in one burst is a quick way to get the sending domain
throttled.

Check the Digest cron too (`digest.ir_cron_digest_scheduler`). It is active by
default and mails every internal user daily, which on a seeded database means
`admin@example.com`.

### Crons

`--max-cron-threads` defaults to 2 and threaded mode runs them, so crons work on
a plain dev server. The trap is elsewhere: cron threads process
`config['db_name'] or list_dbs()`, and `odoo.conf` here says
`db_name = etp_ux_test`. **Start the server with `-d <your db>` explicitly** or
the invitation queue is drained for a database you are not looking at, while the
UI sits on "queued" forever.

### When "Sent" is not sent

**Sent** on a candidate row means the invitation reached the mail layer, not the
inbox. `_send_single_invitation` returns a reason for every candidate it could
not hand over - no template, or no address - and the drainer writes `failed`
with that reason instead of `sent`; `failed` is requeueable, `sent` is not. A
candidate with no address also gets a cancelled `[NO EMAIL]` mail carrying the
exam link for an operator to pass on by hand, filed against the attempt so the
Emails tab shows it (19.0.3.23.0).

After the hand-over, `send_mail(force_send=True)` runs with Odoo's default
`raise_exception=False`, so an SMTP rejection is recorded on the `mail.mail` as
`state='exception'` and the row still reads **Sent**. The Emails tab is where
delivery shows: it lists each mail's state, and an assessment's tab includes the
mail filed against its attempts, which is where invitations live.


## 4.6 Scoring, in engineering terms

Was `docs/ETP_KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md (4.6 Scoring, in engineering terms)`. How a mark is reached. The unit of scoring is the COMPONENT, not the question.

The arithmetic lives in `models/question.py` (`_component_counts`),
`models/assessment.py` (`_compute_final_marks`, `_compute_subjective_marks`,
`_compute_result`) and `services/scoring.py`. This file exists because the
arithmetic is easy to describe wrongly, and has been.

Checked against `19.0.3.23.0`. That release left the arithmetic (sections 1-7
and 10) alone; it changed how grading is run, stopped, re-run and released
(sections 8-9 and 11-13). Its plan, owner decisions and deploy note are in
`docs/ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 0.

### 1. The unit of scoring is the component, not the question

A question is not worth 1 mark. It is worth the sum of its **components**, and
every component is worth exactly 1.

| Component | There is one per | Found on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keyed dimension (a "sub-question") | dimension carrying at least one `is_correct` option | `mcq`, `msq`, and every `image_ab` verdict axis |
| The LLM-graded free-text answer | question | `SUBJECTIVE_COMPONENT_TYPES` = `subjective_rubric`, `image_prompt`, `video_prompt`, `image_ab` |
| The labelling box set, as a whole | question | `LABELLING_COMPONENT_TYPES` = `image_label` |

So a 3-sub-question MCQ is worth **3** marks, and 2 of 3 right scores **2**. An
`image_ab` with 4 verdict axes plus a justification is worth **5**. An `image_ab`
whose question carries no `official_reasoning` has no justification component:
there is no standard to grade it against, so it is worth its axes alone (4).

`question._component_counts()` returns `(marks, raw_marks)`: what the question is
worth, and how much of that carries a raw score. Two things about it are
load-bearing.

- **It lives on the QUESTION, not on the answer.** The denominator is the
  paper's length, so it has to be computable for a question the candidate never
  opened, where there may be no response row at all. Deriving it from the answer
  would shrink the paper to whatever was attempted and hand an abandoned
  question a free pass.
- **The two sets are keyed on the question TYPE, never on `needs_llm`.**
  `needs_llm` goes false when the candidate wrote nothing, so a denominator that
  read it would let an unanswered subjective cost nothing instead of costing its
  mark.

`image_label` is deliberately outside `SUBJECTIVE_COMPONENT_TYPES` even though it
is LLM-graded. Its per-box answers are stored as JSON in the **same**
`justification` column the free-text answer would use, so counting it in both
sets would charge one answer two marks.

Keyed dimensions are counted by type-agnostic code, so **any** question type can
carry them. That matters: the multiple-choice checks on `image_prompt`,
`image_label` and `video_prompt` questions used to be collected and score
nothing. They are ordinary dimension components now and they count.

### 2. What earns a component's mark

**The rule in one line.** Every component is won or lost on its own. There is no
partial credit inside a component, no weighting between components, and no
conjunction across them.

| Component | Its mark is 1 when | Decided in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keyed dimension | the candidate's selected option set equals the key set **exactly**. One missing or one extra scores 0. | `_dimension_marks` |
| Graded free-text | `llm_raw_100 >= subjective_threshold` | `_compute_subjective_marks` |
| Labelling box set | the share of boxes that individually cleared the threshold, expressed as a percentage, itself clears the threshold | `_label_marks` |

The dimension rule is identical for MCQ, for MSQ and for every `image_ab` verdict
axis, which is why there is one helper and not three.

A dimension with no correct option marked is **keyless**. It is not a component
and appears in neither the numerator nor the denominator. That is an authoring
fault to fix at the source. `action_start` and the API's launch dry run
(`_launch_gates`, gate `answer_keys`) both ask `question._keyless_reason()`, and
refuse a pool holding a question worth 0 marks for every candidate, whatever its
type. They do not refuse a partly keyed axis set, or unkeyed axes on a question
whose graded component still scores.

A separate check, advisory only: a question the grader reads with no usable
answer key (`scoring.lacks_answer_key`) is a launch **warning**, never a block
(gate `grading_keys`, and a chatter line from `action_start`). Its answers are
graded against the task alone and flagged `no_answer_key`.

#### The labelling component, in full

The grader returns a raw **0-100 per box** (`box_scores`), not one score for the
question. The platform then does the marking itself:

1. Each box is thresholded on its **own** raw. A box clears or it does not.
2. `fraction = boxes_that_cleared / N`, where **N is the question's own box
   count**, not the number of boxes the grader happened to return.
3. The component's single mark is 1 when `fraction * 100 >= subjective_threshold`.

Worked example, threshold 60, a 20-box question:

| Boxes clearing 60 | fraction | fraction x 100 | Component mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18 of 20 | 0.90 | 90 | **1** |
| 12 of 20 | 0.60 | 60 | **1** (at the bar counts as clearing it) |
| 11 of 20 | 0.55 | 55 | **0** |

Three enforcements sit above the grader in `_apply_image_label_boxes`, and each
exists because the grader on its own gets it wrong:

- **A box the candidate never attempted scores 0**, whatever the grader said.
  Graders reward a plausible-looking blank surprisingly often.
- **A box outside the golden key is dropped.** The grader does not get to invent
  boxes and score them.
- **A box the grader omitted scores 0 and is still counted.** Otherwise a grader
  returning one box out of twenty would make a one-box answer look complete.

A box counts as attempted only when the candidate typed **at least 2 non-space
characters** into it (`_label_attempted_box_numbers`). Without that floor a
candidate pads boxes with single junk characters to inflate coverage.

**The coverage ceiling is gone.** It used to clamp the whole item to
`100 * attempted / total`, which was only ever a proxy for "you cannot score on
boxes you never addressed". Scoring those boxes 0 directly says exactly the same
thing rather than approximately, and it closes the gap where a candidate who
labelled 6 of 10 boxes should have been ceilinged at 60 but in practice only
raised an advisory review flag.

### 3. Two numbers, different jobs

| Field | Reads | Answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `final_mark` | 0 to `final_max`, whole numbers only | *Which components cleared their bar?* |
| `raw_score` | 0.0 to `raw_max`, continuous | *By how much, on each of them?* |

**Every component carries a raw**, so `raw_max` is always equal to `final_max`
and the two fields are two readings of the same paper. The marks count the
components that cleared their bar; the raw counts how close each one came.

| Component | Its raw contribution |
| --- | --- |
| Keyed dimension | **its own mark** - 1 or 0 |
| Graded free-text | `llm_raw_100 / 100` |
| Labelling box set | the **mean** of the per-box raws, divided by 100 |

A keyed dimension's raw is its mark because there is nothing else it could be:
there is no partial credit inside a dimension, so "how well" and "did it clear"
are the same fact for it. The two numbers therefore diverge only where there is
something to diverge about - a written answer graded 80 against a threshold of
60 earns 1 mark and 0.80 raw.

**This used to work the other way, and the change is deliberate.** Objective
components were excluded from the raw's numerator and denominator alike, on the
argument that an objective raw only restates the mark beside it. It does. The
cost was that the two numbers were quoted out of DIFFERENT denominators on the
same screen - a 5-question paper with three multiple-choice questions read
`Raw score 1.40 / 2` beside a mark of `3 / 5` - and no reader could tell that
apart from a bug. Restating a number is a smaller price than making the headline
unreadable.

Labelling worked example: 20 boxes whose raws sum to 1250 give a mean of 62.5,
so the component contributes **0.625**. That is the ungated twin of the mark: the
same answer can contribute 0.625 to the raw while its mark is 1, or 0, depending
only on how many individual boxes cleared the bar.

Read the raw beside the mark, never instead of it. Only marks decide pass or
fail.

### 4. The fields on a response

| Field | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `final_mark` | Sum of this question's component marks, 0 to `final_max`. |
| `final_max` | What this question is worth. Computed from the QUESTION, so an unanswered question still occupies its marks. |
| `mcq_mark` | How many keyed sub-questions were exactly right. |
| `objective_marks_max` | How many keyed sub-questions this question has. |
| `raw_score` | Ungated quality over ALL of this question's components, 0.0 to `raw_max`. |
| `raw_max` | How many components this question has. The same number as `final_max`. |
| `llm_raw_100` | The grader's raw 0-100 for the free-text answer. Stored, never re-derived. |
| `llm_raw_score` | `llm_raw_100` as a 0-1 fraction, or the labelling mean. |
| `llm_score` / `llm_max_score` / `llm_passed` | The graded component's mark, its max (1), and whether it cleared. |
| `label_fraction` | Share of labelling boxes that cleared, 0-1. |
| `label_box_scores_json` | The grader's raw 0-100 for **each** box, keyed by box number. |
| `llm_prompt_version` | `bundled:<sha8>` of the grading instructions that produced the grade. Empty on answers graded before versioning. Read by the verdict gate (section 12). |
| `rescore_request_key` | Set while a re-score of this answer is queued, one random key per click; cleared when it is graded, errors out for good, or Kill drops it (section 8c). The API shows it as `rescore_requested`. |

The two old per-answer raw fields are gone: the blended whole-question raw, and
the objective partial-credit raw. Neither exists on the model any more.

#### `score` / `max_score` behind the review label

`_compute_score` writes `score` and `max_score` (surfaced as `objective_score` /
`objective_max`) for `mcq` and `msq` only, under the component rule: each keyed
sub-question is worth 1, through the same `_dimension_marks` helper. On those
two types they now agree with `mcq_mark` / `objective_marks_max`.

The candidate's released review (`serializers.released_answer_review_row`) reads
them for its label: "Correct", "Partly correct (2 of 3)" or "Incorrect". An
auto-submitted placeholder reads "Not answered", never "Incorrect" (section
11). Read `final_mark` / `final_max` for the mark: `score` is 0 on every other
type.

### 5. What each question type is worth

There are **seven** types (`QUESTION_TYPE_SELECTION`).

Every component carries a raw, so the "of which carry a raw" column is now the
same number as the marks column for every type. It is kept below only to name
which of a type's components are LLM-graded, because that is what decides
whether the raw and the mark can disagree.

| Type | Marks | Of which are LLM-graded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mcq` | one per keyed dimension | 0 |
| `msq` | one per keyed dimension | 0 |
| `subjective_rubric` | one per keyed dimension, **+ 1** for the written answer | 1 |
| `image_ab` | one per verdict axis, **+ 1** for the justification when the question has `official_reasoning` | 1, or 0 without `official_reasoning` |
| `image_prompt` | one per keyed dimension, **+ 1** for the written prompt | 1 |
| `image_label` | one per keyed dimension, **+ 1** for the box set | 1 |
| `video_prompt` | one per keyed dimension, **+ 1** for the written prompt | 1 |

A purely objective paper therefore has a raw now - it simply equals the marks.

An eighth type, the two-plate labelling variant, was retired. The migration in
`migrations/19.0.3.7.0/` folds existing rows onto `image_label`.

### 6. The `image_ab` case, in full

This is the type people got wrong, and most of what they got wrong no longer
exists.

**Every verdict axis is its own keyed dimension**, marked deterministically by
`_dimension_marks` like any MCQ sub-question. **The justification is its own
component**, graded and thresholded like any other free-text answer. Nothing is
weighted against anything else.

What that removed:

- **The 0.75 / 0.25 blend is gone**, along with its two weight constants and the
  helper that applied it. It was applied twice (once in the grader, once again
  composing the raw), giving an effective 93.75 / 6.25 that nobody intended.
- **"Perfect verdicts start the raw at 75" is gone with it.** Under the blend, any
  threshold at or below 75 meant the justification could not affect the mark at
  all while still appearing to be worth a quarter of the question.
- **The 60-point overall-wrong cap is gone.** It punished a wrong Overall Choice
  through a number that no longer exists. The Overall Choice axis is now a
  component of its own and is simply marked wrong when it is wrong, which is the
  same penalty and a legible one.
- **The all-or-nothing conjunction across the question's halves is gone.** One
  wrong verdict used to cost every mark on the question.

Worked example: 4 verdict axes plus a justification, threshold 70. The candidate
calls 3 axes right and the justification grades 55.

| | Old rule | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Question worth | 1 | 5 |
| Earned | 0 | **3** (3 verdicts; the justification misses its bar) |
| Raw contribution | one blended number | 0.55 out of 1 |

#### When the justification box is left empty

`_image_ab_uses_llm` is false, so no LLM is called. `_store_ab_verdict_only`
settles the answer: the written component scores 0 and `llm_state` closes to
`scored`. Closing it matters, because leaving it unscored would hold the whole
attempt at `pending` forever. `_image_ab_uses_llm` is also false when the
question has no `official_reasoning`; there the component does not exist
(section 1), so nothing is lost.

The verdict axes are **not** folded into a score on that lane. They are already
marked as their own components, so scoring them there would count them twice.

This is no longer a setting. `Require Justification for Image Comparison` was
removed; the trigger is simply whether the candidate wrote anything.

### 7. Attempt totals

```
earned    = sum(response.final_mark)
possible  = sum of component counts over the DRAWN questions
score_percent = earned / possible * 100
result        = pass when score_percent >= pass threshold
pass threshold = assessment.pass_threshold, or subjective_threshold while that is not set
```

`possible` comes from `_paper_component_totals`, which counts over the
evaluator's frozen `question_order` and not over the answers. **The denominator
is the paper, not the answers**, so an unanswered question still costs its marks.
Attempt 740 was an 8-question paper scored out of 3 and reported 100% PASS;
counting from the draw is what stops that, and moving to per-component marks does
not change it, only makes the numbers finer. It falls back to the response rows
when a draw was never recorded.

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `score_marks_display` | `"8 / 11"`. **Two integers, always** - clients parse it with `int.tryParse`, and a fractional value made them drop the server's total and re-derive the score locally. The numbers are **larger** than they used to be, because the denominator is now a component count rather than a question count, but the shape is unchanged. |
| `score_percent` | Internal. Compared against the threshold. |
| `result` | `pass`, `fail`, or `pending`. |
| `raw_result` / `raw_max` / `raw_percent` | The sum of `raw_score`, over the SAME denominator `score_percent` uses. Quality signal, never pass or fail. |

**`raw_percent` and `score_percent` share a denominator.** They used not to,
and that was the single most misread thing on the results screen: `score_percent`
divided by every component on the paper while `raw_percent` divided by the
LLM-graded ones alone, so one attempt was described by `3 / 5` and `1.40 / 2` at
the same time. Both now divide by the paper's component count. What still differs
is the NUMERATOR: the marks count components that cleared the bar, the raw counts
how close each came, and a component that cleared at 61 against a threshold of 60
contributes 1 to one and 0.61 to the other.

The Subjective Pass Threshold does **double** duty: the per-answer bar for a
graded answer, and the per-box bar inside a labelling question. The overall pass
mark for the attempt is the assessment's own **Pass Threshold** (Q20), seeded on a
new assessment from the Settings default `default_pass_threshold` (70 unless
changed). An assessment whose pass threshold is not set - every one made before
Q20, since the upgrade left them unset - uses its subjective threshold there too,
so its results did not change. (changed in 19.0.3.23.0: the subjective threshold
did triple duty, the overall pass mark included.)

#### Worked example: a whole attempt

A drawn paper of 5 questions, subjective threshold 70, pass threshold 70.

| Q | Type | Components | Earned | Raw earned | Raw available |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `mcq`, 1 keyed dimension | 1 | 1 | 1.00 | 1 |
| 2 | `msq`, 3 keyed dimensions, 2 exactly right | 3 | 2 | 2.00 | 3 |
| 3 | `subjective_rubric`, graded 84 | 1 | 1 | 0.84 | 1 |
| 4 | `image_ab`, 4 axes (3 right) + justification graded 55 | 5 | 3 | 3.55 | 5 |
| 5 | `image_label`, 18 of 20 boxes clear, mean box raw 82 | 1 | 1 | 0.82 | 1 |

- `earned` = 8, `possible` = 11. `score_marks_display` = **"8 / 11"**.
- `score_percent` = 8 / 11 x 100 = **72.73**, which is at or above 70, so
  **PASS**.
- `raw_result` = (1) + (2) + 0.84 + (3 + 0.55) + 0.82 = **8.21** over a
  `raw_max` of **11**. The bracketed terms are the keyed dimensions, each
  contributing its own mark.
- `raw_percent` = 8.21 / 11 x 100 = **74.64**.

Note the denominators: 11 and 11. The two numerators are what differ - 8 marks
against 8.21 raw, the gap being the partial credit the marks round away.

### 8. When a result stays pending

`result` is held at `pending` while any subjective answer is unresolved,
including one whose grading hit a terminal error, and one an admin stopped. That
is on purpose. A Vertex outage is not a candidate's failure, so the attempt waits
for an admin to retry it (Odoo "Retry Failed Scoring", Flutter "Score Failed
Candidates (N)" or "Reset & re-score errored (N)", `POST
/api/v1/scoring/requeue_errored`) rather than being finalised as a 0. A killed
answer is held for the same reason and it matters more, not less: it carries no
grade at all, so letting the paper finalise would score it 0 and turn an
operator pressing Kill into that candidate's fail - a decision nobody made about
them.

A **deferred** call is not a failure either. An HTTP 429, the calls-per-minute
ceiling, a spend cap, or Postgres refusing a new connection ("too many
clients") spends no attempt: the answers stay `pending`, the reason goes in the
candidate's `llm_error` (`_settle_submission`), and the next tick tries again.
The Postgres case is new in `19.0.3.23.0` (`_deferred_if_pool_full`).

### 8b. Stopping a run: Kill Scoring Process

Grading runs inside a cron worker, so there is no process to signal and
cancellation is COOPERATIVE. `Kill Scoring Process` raises
`scoring_cancel_requested` on the assessment; every billable grading lane reads
that flag back on a fresh cursor before its next call
(`services/vertex._check_scoring_cancelled`) and refuses. A run therefore stops
within one call rather than at the end of its batch.

What it does and does not do:

- **Scores already stored are kept.** A kill never unwinds a mark.
- **The one request already on the wire completes and is billed.** Everything
  after it is refused. That is the honest boundary, and it is the same boundary
  the generator kill switch has.
- Candidates the drainer had not started are parked in `cancelled` - an outcome
  somebody chose, not a fault, so it is never auto-retried and the retry
  buttons (Retry Failed Scoring, Score Failed Candidates) deliberately skip it.
- **Queued re-score requests are dropped** (`_clear_rescore_requests`),
  including those of the candidate a lane was holding, once its lane parks it
  (`_llm_score_guarded`). Otherwise the next tick would grade and bill them.
- **A candidate a running lane is grading is left to that lane**
  (`_being_graded`: `llm_state = scoring` and the owning lane still holds its
  advisory lock, `_live_lane_shards`). It stops at its next call and lands in
  `cancelled`. A `scoring` row whose lane died is nobody's, and Kill parks it.
- The flag is held raised only while a lane is genuinely mid-call. With nothing
  in flight it is lowered immediately, because the cron only ever revisits
  queued candidates and a kill that emptied the queue would otherwise leave the
  flag up with no tick coming to lower it - refusing the assessment's next
  legitimate run.

**While a lane is still stopping**, the paper's `scoring_phase` reads
`stopping`, and every action that would queue grading is refused before it
writes anything (`_check_scoring_not_stopping`): Score All / Run Subjective
Evaluation, Retry Failed, `/scoring/queue`, `/scoring/requeue_errored`, the
per-answer and per-candidate re-score. The API answers 409 `stopping`; Odoo
hides those buttons and Flutter disables them. Before `19.0.3.23.0` such a click
said "Queued" and the lane then parked it back to `cancelled`.

`POST /api/v1/assessments/<id>/kill_scoring` replies `settled_count` (parked by
this click), `cleared_count` (re-score requests dropped) and `held_count`
(being graded now; each stops at its next call). The Odoo toast says the same.

Archive raises the same flag and means the opposite: the held candidate goes
back to `pending` with `scoring_requested` intact, and restore lowers the flag
directly, so a restored paper resumes. Known gap: Kill, then Archive, then
Restore while a lane still holds a candidate lifts the kill for that candidate
(`ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` §0.2 E).

To resume, press `Score All` once the phase has left `stopping` (or re-queue the
individual candidate). A click that actually queues something withdraws the
kill (`_withdraw_scoring_kill`); one that queues nobody leaves it up.

### 8c. Re-grading something already paid for

The retry buttons (Odoo "Retry Failed Scoring", Flutter "Score Failed Candidates
(N)", both through `action_reset_failed_scoring`) reset only `failed` and
`error` answers, so an answer that already scored is left alone: it has been
paid for, and re-grading it costs another call and can move a mark somebody has
released (the grader runs at temperature 0.2, so a second pass genuinely
differs). Every reset path also skips a candidate a lane is grading right now,
an erased (anonymised) attempt, and a cancelled paper.

Re-grading a paid answer is still possible, two ways.

**One candidate, chosen answers** (`action_rescore_individually`). Odoo
"Re-score N answer(s)" on the attempt and "Re-score This Answer" on the answer
(managers); Flutter per-answer "Re-score", "Re-score N answer(s)" and "Re-score N
selected"; `POST /api/v1/attempts/<id>/rescore` with optional `question_ids`
and `confirm`.

- **Nothing is graded in the request.** The chosen answers get one
  `rescore_request_key` per click; the lane that owns the candidate grades them
  first on its next tick (`scoring.begin_evaluator`), in calls of their own:
  never batched with another click or another candidate, never through a
  question-group cache. The ledger note is `rescore(n)`.
- **A scored answer keeps its mark until the new grade succeeds**
  (`_is_regrade`). A failed or refused re-grade leaves the old mark, and so does
  a reply the platform cannot trust (a labelling reply with no `box_scores`, an
  A/B answer whose key has drifted). A `failed` or `error` answer gets a fresh
  attempt budget.
- **`question_ids` absent** (or null) means every answer that needs the grader
  and has no mark yet. **Present but unreadable** (`[]`, `'abc'`, a list of
  objects) is 422 `invalid`: read as "no ids", it would widen one answer into
  all of them.
- **Refused with nothing written:** 422 `not_on_attempt` (names the first 10
  ids, then "and N more"); 409 `spend_limit`, `being_graded` (with or without
  `question_ids`), `released_confirm_required` (results already released and
  no `confirm: true`; the Odoo buttons ask first), `erased`, `archived`,
  `stopping`; a cancelled paper is 422 `rejected`.
- The chatter records who asked, which answers, and each one's previous mark,
  model and prompt version (`_rescore_audit_line`). Kill drops a queued request
  (section 8b).

**A whole paper, emergency** - a rubric signed off wrong, a whole cohort graded
against it. It has to be asked for explicitly: `POST
/api/v1/scoring/requeue_errored` with `force: true` alongside the state. It
cannot happen as a side effect of a state name in a payload, and when it does
happen the assessment's own log records who did it and to how many candidates.
The reply carries `requeued` (candidates targeted), `answers_reset`, `states`
and `forced`. Unlike the individual path, a forced reset sends each answer back
to `pending`, so its mark counts 0 and the attempt reads `pending` until the new
grade lands.

### 9. Gates and ceilings

**Pre-LLM gates** (`services/gates.py`, `evaluate_gates`) score an answer 0
without ever calling the model. Two fire: `empty_answer`, and
`injection_attempt` for text matching `INTEGRITY_GATE_PATTERNS`. The matcher
normalises NFKC, strips zero-width and bidi characters and folds Cyrillic and
Greek lookalikes first, so disguising the attempt does not help. An injection
gate also raises `integrity_alert` on the attempt.

**The grader's own number is not trusted.** `_recompute_deductions` rebuilds the
score as `100 + sum(deduction points)` from the itemised deductions, and an
empty deduction list is only accepted as a perfect score when the grader's own
headline was already at or above 99.5. A drift of more than 1.5 points flags the
answer `needs_review` and `score_recomputed`.

**Integrity ceilings** (`_apply_ceilings`, from `constants.SCORE_CEILINGS`) then
clamp `llm_raw_100`. Only ceilings strictly below the current raw apply, and the
lowest of those wins.

| Trigger | Cap |
| --- | --- |
| `verdict_contradiction` (the answer contradicts itself) | 25 |
| `fabrication` (fabricated or hallucinated content) | 25 |
| `multi_checklist_zero` (two or more rubric checklists scored zero) | 55, but never on `image_prompt` or `video_prompt` |

Ceilings act on `llm_raw_100`, so they can pull it under the threshold and cost
the graded component its mark. They touch nothing objective. Prompt-writing
answers are exempt from the 55 cap since `19.0.3.23.0`: their score is already
100 x elements hit / elements required, so the cap would cut the same misses
twice. The instructions ask for `verdict_consistency` and
`checklist_zero_count` on every type except `image_label`, where only
`fabrication_count` (text addressed to the grader) is asked for.

**The key-drift guard** exists at two points. At approve time
`_assert_no_key_drift` refuses to publish a draft whose materialized `is_correct`
options no longer match its `construction_keys`. At score time `_ab_key_drift` /
`_store_ab_key_drift` catch an `image_ab` whose key moved anyway, and settle the
answer with `gate = "key_drift"` rather than grade it against a key that no
longer matches what was asked. A re-grade that meets the guard keeps the answer's
old mark rather than storing the guard's 0 (section 8c).

### 10. A threshold change re-decides without re-grading

`llm_raw_100` and `label_box_scores_json` are stored raw and never thresholded at
write time. `_store_scored` writes them; the pass/fail and the earned mark are
computed from them by `_compute_subjective_marks`. Moving an assessment's
threshold therefore re-decides every graded answer live, with **no LLM call**.

Since the per-box raws are stored the same way, this now covers labelling too:
changing the bar re-decides which boxes cleared, the fraction, and the
component's mark, all without re-running the grader.

The pass threshold (Q20) is cheaper still: it moves no mark, only each
candidate's stored `pass_threshold` and `result`, recomputed through
`_compute_result`'s depends. `write()` treats it like a subjective edit
(`threshold_recompute_pending` while a lane is grading).

### 11. Auto-submitted papers

When the clock runs out, or the proctoring cap is reached on an Auto-submit paper
(a Log only paper is never ended by violations; in both modes a reached limit is
labelled "Violation Limit Breached"), the module settles the attempt itself: unanswered questions get a placeholder answer, the attempt locks,
and `auto_submit_reason` records `expired` or `violation`. It stays empty when
the candidate pressed Submit themselves.

Placeholder answers are never sent to the grader and score 0. On the candidate's
released review (`serializers.released_answer_review_row`) the placeholder text
is blanked, so the client shows "You did not answer this question." rather than
the system string, and the row reads **"Not answered"** - for `mcq` / `msq` too,
where a placeholder used to fall through to "Incorrect". A placeholder that
carries picks or labels but no grade reads "No Grade"; an answer still in the
queue reads "Awaiting grading". That is how a reader tells an abandoned
question from a pending one.

On a time-out the candidate is told "Time's up - your answers are saved." on
every path (Next, autosave, the deadline buzzer, manual submit), never a
proctoring message, and their results show "Ended on the clock" and "Time used:
X of Y min". The backend's answer route replies 409 `time_expired` with
`answer_saved` for an answer posted after the deadline: one landing within 10 s
(`ANSWER_GRACE_SECONDS`) is kept, a later one is not stored (round 3). A proctoring
beacon after the deadline is never counted: the attempt ends as `expired`, not
`violation`.

### 12. Nothing is visible until a person releases it

No score, verdict or mark reaches a candidate until an admin releases that
attempt. There is no automatic path (no cron writes `results_released`) and no
un-release: nothing anywhere writes the flag back to `False`.

`action_release_results` is strictly per-record, so releasing one candidate never
releases the cohort as a side effect. Releasing a cohort is a separate, explicit
action: Odoo's header "Release Results" (`action_release_all_results`) opens a
counted confirm dialog (`assessments.be.release.wizard`: submitted, releasing
now, still grading), whose button runs the write, `action_confirm_release`. The
older Odoo Release buttons (attempt form, All Attempts list, Candidates tab)
ask for confirmation too.

**A candidate a lane is grading right now is skipped, not released**, on every
release path: writing that row mid-call would make the lane's paid result
collide and be bought again. The next click, a minute later, releases them with
final marks.

`POST /api/v1/assessments/<id>/release` (`assessment_release`):

- `evaluator_ids` **absent** releases the whole submitted cohort. **Present but
  unreadable** (`[]`, `null`, junk, a list of objects, an id past a float such
  as `1e400`) is 422 `invalid` and releases nobody (`id_list_arg_strict`).
  Before `19.0.3.23.0` the no-ids branch returned 500 and bad ids fell through
  to the whole cohort.
- No submitted candidate to release: 422 `nothing_to_release`.
- Reply: `released_count` and `skipped_count` (from the action),
  `still_grading_count` (released with written answers still to be marked), and
  `candidates` - only those this call released. Any skip adds a warning
  `notice`, which both app builds show in place of "Result released".

**After release, the verdict gate.** A released review row carries the grader's
feedback, deductions and credit for a scored written answer, and its one-line
verdict (`score_verdict`, shown in the app under "The judge's verdict") only when
the answer's `llm_prompt_version` equals the instructions in force
(`serializers._verdict_is_for_current_instructions`). Verdicts written under
older instructions were addressed to admins, so they are sent as `""`. The
switch is the system parameter `assessments_be_v2.verdict_requires_current_prompt`:
unset means ON; `0`/`false`/`no`/`off` shows every verdict. It is a product
decision, never a deploy step. If the check itself fails, the verdict is
withheld and one WARNING line is logged.

### 13. What one grading call carries

How the grade in `llm_raw_100` is obtained. The lane mechanics (shards, ticks,
locks) are in Part 2, section 2.2 of this file; the measurements and decisions behind this are in
`ETP_PLANS_AND_STRATEGY.md` Part 3 §3.7-§3.11.

- **Text only.** No image or video is sent; the answer keys, written from the
  media, are the whole truth. Per answer the call carries the question's
  material (`_question_material`, per type: task, rubric and golden answer;
  A/B axes with the official choice and `official_reasoning`; required
  elements, penalties, reference prompt and scoring guide; labelling box ->
  expected label, decoys, and `markers_hidden` when the candidate saw no
  numbered markers) and the worker's part (`_build_item`: answer id, question
  id, answer, and A/B picks). Nothing is sent twice.
- **One set of instructions**, always the shipped `prompts/scoring.md`; the
  stored override (`assessments_be_v2.scoring_system_prompt`) is no longer
  read. Every graded answer records `llm_prompt_version` = `bundled:` + the
  first 8 hex of `sha256(prompts/scoring.md.strip())`. `19.0.3.23.0` ships
  **`bundled:785826a5`** (prod graded with `bundled:34c42d2f`).
  `DEFAULT_SCORING_PROMPT` in `services/scoring.py` must match the file
  (`TestTheInstructionsAreOneShippedText`). Deduction and credit reasons are
  written for the candidate, in plain words.
- **The rules follow the question type** (`rules_fit_type`), never the SOP
  title; a mismatch is graded by the type's own rules and flagged.
- **Temperature 0.2.** The model is unchanged.
- **Output room:** at least 16,000 output tokens per call, clamped to the
  model's maximum; a reply cut off at the limit is re-asked with double room,
  and what still does not fit is re-graded rather than left unscored.
- **Question-group cache, ON by default** (`assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache`:
  unset means `groups`; `0`/`false`/`no`/`off` turns it off). On a bulk run over
  a shared paper, the cohort's graded questions are cut into groups of the batch
  size and each group's instructions and question material are cached on Vertex
  (`_cache_plan`, `services/grading_cache.py`, table
  `assessments_be_scoring_cache`). **Answers are never cached.** A group under
  the model's cache minimum (4,096 tokens on Gemini 3) is left out, so papers
  prod has run today are batched exactly as with the cache off. A cache is
  created only when at least 2 queued answers need it; a retry may use a live
  one but never creates one; re-scores and the fallback model never use one. A
  cache problem never blocks grading: that call goes uncached.
- **Parallel calls per lane:** `assessments_be_v2.scoring_parallel_calls`,
  default 4 (range 1-8), lowered to what `db_maxconn` allows. Every mark is
  still stored by the lane's own cursor, one candidate per savepoint.
- **Grading never writes the shared paper row.** Outlier staleness is derived
  from the data (`_outlier_stale_papers`, `score_outlier_checked_at`), so two
  lanes grading one paper no longer collide and throw paid marks away.

Line numbers are a convenience only. The **symbol name** is the stable handle;
grep for it if the numbers have drifted.

| The paper's denominator | `models/assessment.py` - `_paper_component_totals` |
